The insured's son was treated for an infected umbilical sinus leading to sepsis. The insurer repudiated the claim under the congenital disease exclusion clause. The Ombudsman noted sepsis originated from the congenital umbilical sinus and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Under a hospital cash policy, a claim for chemotherapy for stage IV colon cancer was repudiated as a pre-existing disease based on medical literature generalisations. The Ombudsman held the insurer failed to prove pre-existence and awarded Rs. 21,000 with 9% interest.

Out of a claim of Rs. 9,832.20, only Rs. 4,383 was initially paid. The insurer conceded during the hearing that the balance was due and instructions had been issued. The Ombudsman awarded the full claimed amount with interest, accounting for previous payment.

Claims for CAD treatment across multiple hospitals were repudiated as pre-existing based on a clinical history noting similar symptoms for a year. The Ombudsman found no conclusive proof that the patient was aware of or treated for CAD prior to the policy and awarded Rs. 9,597 with interest.

Hospitalization for back and neck pain was repudiated due to lack of active treatment and inability to verify the 24-hour stay. The Ombudsman noted the admission was purely for diagnostics and pain killers without active inpatient treatment, and dismissed the complaint.

The insurer disallowed the cost of a CPAP machine during sleep apnoea treatment under a group mediclaim policy. The Ombudsman held that unlike permanent fixtures such as pacemakers, a CPAP is a reusable breathing machine not covered under specific policy terms, dismissing the complaint.

A claim for liver cirrhosis and other ailments was restricted to Rs. 15,000 based on a pre-existing disease cap. The Ombudsman observed active treatment was given for non-pre-existing conditions like liver cirrhosis and ordered the insurer to pay the balance of Rs. 6,410 with interest and costs.

A claim for stroke treatment was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension noted in hospital records. The complainant produced case sheets showing sudden onset without 10-year hypertension history. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and awarded Rs. 29,641 with interest.

Dispute over sum assured slabs and premium calculation upon policy renewal. The insurer conceded the correct sum assured and premium interpolation during proceedings. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to issue the policy with proper sum assured, refund excess collection, and pay costs.

A claim for knee injury hospitalization was repudiated because the stay was solely for an MRI scan without active medical treatment or medicines prescribed. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's exclusion of diagnostic-only admissions and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for CAD treatment was repudiated citing a prior cardiologist consultation. The Ombudsman found the consultation occurred during treatment for a road traffic accident and general checkups proved no prior heart ailment. The insurer was directed to pay Rs. 10,982 with interest.

Delay in settling a personal accident death claim. The insurer admitted liability and stated settlement documents were processed. The Ombudsman awarded the full sum of Rs. 2 lakhs with interest and costs for delayed payment.

A claim for varicose ulcer treatment at an alternative medicine center was repudiated on grounds of unrecognised hospital, unqualified doctor, and unapproved treatment protocol. The Ombudsman ruled the hospital and doctor met policy definitions, awarding Rs. 17,621 with interest.

A claim for accidental injury was repudiated because hospitalization was solely for diagnostic tests (X-ray, CT scan) with minimal medicines and normal reports. The Ombudsman upheld the exclusion of diagnostic-only admissions and dismissed the complaint.

Insured patient was treated for stomach cancer. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing stomach ailment based on a general history statement. Ombudsman found no prior diagnosis or treatment for cancer and set aside the repudiation, awarding Rs. 50000 with 8% interest.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for disc prolapse and treated with bed rest and traction. Insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could be done on OPD basis and complaint was time-barred. Ombudsman held that active treatment requiring bed rest was given and ordered payment of hospital bill of Rs. 7647 with interest and cost.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was admitted following a fall and diagnosed with Sacroiliac strain treated conservatively with bed rest and analgesics. Insurer repudiated stating treatment fell under exclusion and could be managed on OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was treated for lumbar spondylosis. Insurer deducted a portion for pre-existing diabetes mellitus due to a policy break in 2003. Ombudsman upheld the deduction for pre-existing DM but awarded interest and cost due to delay in settlement.

Insured underwent specialized ayurvedic treatment involving herbal and oil massages. Insurer rejected the claim stating it was mere oil massage that could be done on OPD basis and alleged pre-existing illness. Ombudsman found the treatment specialized requiring hospitalization, reversed the rejection, and awarded Rs. 12250 with interest.

Claim for father's hospitalization was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension and lack of policy continuity proof prior to 2001. Complainant provided history details. The text cuts off in the decision section.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for eye treatment was restricted/denied because the eye condition and surgery occurred prior to the individual policy inception, and the insurer treated a second policy as limited for pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman noted non-disclosure of the prior operation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization claim for incisional hernia repair following a past caesarian section was repudiated as pre-existing. Ombudsman held that hernia is a mechanical event arising from an existing scar rather than a pre-existing disease, and directed the insurer to pay the claim.
Claim for cerebral subarachnoid hemorrhage, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion. The text ends abruptly during the facts description.

Claim for son's adenoidectomy and tonsillectomy was rejected under first-year policy exclusion. Ombudsman noted these procedures are not listed among first-year exclusions and directed the insurer to pay the claim.

Insurer restricted a dialysis and chronic renal failure claim to the original sum insured after the policy sum insured was enhanced, citing pre-existing CRF. Ombudsman noted that restriction terms were never communicated or incorporated into the policy and ordered payment of the balance Rs. 12329.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was initially closed/repudiated for non-submission of requested documents following the insured person's death. During the proceedings, documents were submitted and the insurer settled the claim for Rs. 20229.
Claim for acute gastroenteritis was repudiated because the hospital was depanelled without notice to the insured, and there was a delay in intimation. Ombudsman allowed 75% of admissible expenses.

Insurer partially settled a laparoscopic cholecystectomy claim, cutting surgeon and operation theatre fees under the reasonableness clause. Ombudsman found the insurer's cuts mostly reasonable but awarded an additional Rs. 11000 due to emergency nature and comparable cases.

Claim for bilateral cataract operation with premium lens implant was partially disallowed under the reasonableness clause. Ombudsman noted the insurer had settled similar claims in full for other policyholders and directed full settlement.

Insurer deducted room charges and diet charges during ayurvedic treatment for Parkinson's disease. Ombudsman held that essential room-associated services (power, water, sanitation, ward boy) and diet are integral parts of hospitalisation expenses and not legally disallowable.

Claim for lumbar slip disc treatment was partially disallowed on the ground that the last 7 days of hospital stay lacked active treatment. Ombudsman allowed 75% of admissible expenses in view of package billing and hospital clarifications.

insurer: The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for fracture surgery expenses was partially settled by the TPA. During the Ombudsman proceedings, the insurer agreed to settle the full remaining balance of Rs. 25921.

Claim for endovenous laser therapy for varicose veins was repudiated as a pre-existing disease based on hospital records and doctor certificates, despite later contradictory certificates submitted by the insured. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Claim for knee replacement surgery was delayed because implant invoices and stickers were missing. After the insurer sanctioned admissible amounts excluding implants and bulk medicines without receipts, the insured accepted the settlement during proceedings.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: The insured claimed for breast cancer treatment. The insurer rejected it as a pre-existing disease, arguing the policy had been cancelled and re-issued. The Ombudsman noted there was no break in continuity from the original policy date over a year prior, making the claim valid.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for two hospitalizations were rejected: one for lack of 24-hour stay and another for non-necessary hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection for the short stay, but awarded 50% ex-gratia for the second hospitalization given the patient's medical history.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured underwent surgery for Fistula in ano and claimed Rs. 21,968. The insurer paid Rs. 10,000, citing a policy clause capping fistula treatments at 10% of the sum insured. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial payment based on policy terms.

insurer: The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for cardiac treatment was partially rejected because the policy specifically excluded hypertension and related ailments for the insured family member. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cashless pre-authorisation for coronary bypass surgery was cancelled when records indicated a 15-year history of hypertension. Since no formal claim had been filed with the insurer yet, the Ombudsman advised submitting the claim papers with proof of onset.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for a second hospitalization due to chronic liver disease was repudiated as pre-existing based on a doctor's initial certificate. Subsequent clarifications from the treating doctor showed the cirrhosis resulted from an acute infection. The Ombudsman found the rejection unsustainable.

insurer: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for surgery to remove a colloid cyst was initially rejected under the congenital disease exclusion. During the proceedings, the insurer reconsidered, settled the claim for Rs. 1,11,250, and the complaint was closed.

A claim for primary infertility treatment via hystero-laparoscopy was repudiated under the policy exclusion for infertility. The Ombudsman held that hospitalization for evaluation of infertility rather than acute sickness was correctly excluded.

Following surgery for a perianal abscess, the TPA heavily cut surgeon and operation theatre charges using comparative hospital tariffs. The Ombudsman ruled that the policy had no fee caps and the hospital bills were valid, directing full settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for enteric fever was repudiated after investigation revealed the nursing home was closed during the claimed period and another doctor certified treatment on an OPD basis elsewhere. The Ombudsman upheld the denial due to fraud.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: A claim for diagnostic tests regarding dysphagia was repudiated as a pre-existing condition and for being solely for investigation. The Ombudsman found the tests were incidental to diagnosis and treatment, holding the insurer's rejection untennable.
A claim for fistula surgery was partially settled due to billing discrepancies. During proceedings, the TPA paid the remaining balance of Rs. 1,400, and the complaint was closed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured claimed for Ayurvedic treatment of a digestive disorder requiring a 13-day hospital stay. The claim was denied on the grounds that external oil therapies and oral medications did not warrant hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for acute severe cellulitis was repudiated under pre-existing exclusion due to a past history of filariasis. The Ombudsman noted the policy had been active for eight years and the condition did not constitute a pre-existing disease.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The TPA paid part of a varicose vein laser treatment claim based on a network package rate, cutting Rs. 18,000. The Ombudsman found the insurer failed to verify hospital circulars supporting the charged per-leg rate, ruling the deduction unjustified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: An amendment to a previous award adjusting the payable balance to Rs. 16,210 based on the actual remaining sum insured after prior claim settlements during the policy year.

A claim for knee replacement surgery was partially disallowed by applying reasonableness caps to surgeon and assistant fees. The Ombudsman ruled the reasonableness deduction was not sustainable given standard fees in similar cases.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for osteoarthritis and sciatica treatment was entirely repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary for the line of treatment given. The Ombudsman ordered an 80% settlement considering the patient's age and condition.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for gastric motility disorder and depression was rejected under pre-existing and lack of hospitalization necessity clauses. The Ombudsman granted 50% of admissible expenses on an ex-gratia basis given the patient's age and pre-hospitalization condition.

A claim for ventral hernia surgery was rejected because the insurer claimed it resulted from a prior cholecystectomy performed four years earlier. In the absence of previous hospital papers to dispute this, the Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured underwent abdominal hysterectomy. Claim was initially delayed due to pending documents like indoor case papers and bill clarification. Insurer later offered partial settlement which the complainant agreed to during the hearing.

Insured's daughter was hospitalized for calculous cholecystitis. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion clause 4.1 as hospital records and medical history indicated symptoms existed for two years prior to policy inception.

Insured hospitalized for Hepatitis C infection. Claim repudiated for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of past blood transfusion in 1988 considered a predisposing factor. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for obstructive sleep apnea and required a CPAP machine. Insurer rejected claim stating hospitalization was for investigation only, but Ombudsman found the ailment severe and allowed the claim.

Insured hospitalized for gastro-oesophageal ulcer with hiatus hernia. Insurer rejected claim under pre-existing clause citing aspirin use. Ombudsman noted policy was active for 18 years and lack of proof for aspirin being the cause, ruling in favor of complainant.

Insured underwent hernia operation. Claim repudiated due to specific exclusion of hernia in a fresh policy issued after a short break in renewal. Ombudsman ordered ex-gratia settlement based on original sum insured.

Insured hospitalized for prolapsed intervertebral disc shortly after policy inception. Claim repudiated under pre-existing disease clause due to severe symptoms and lack of prior medical papers. Ombudsman upheld insurer decision.

Insured hospitalized for ankle fracture. Insurer deducted amounts from surgeon and anesthetist fees under reasonableness clause. Ombudsman ruled unilateral cuts unjustified since cashless was allowed and directed full payment.

Insured underwent heart surgery during a gap period when renewing and enhancing the policy. Insurer rejected claim due to break in continuity. Settled via Ombudsman recommendation to pay on original sum insured.
Insured hospitalized for acute lumbar disc prolapse. Claim file closed by TPA due to lack of reply regarding late intimation. Settled during Ombudsman proceedings with payment issued to claimant.

Insured hospitalized for coronary angiogram. Claim rejected as a complication of excluded diabetes mellitus. Ombudsman allowed reimbursement of hospitalization expenses excluding diabetes treatment on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured underwent CABG surgery. Claim repudiated under pre-existing clause alleging diabetes since 1997. Ombudsman noted lack of exact proof regarding diabetes onset before policy inception and favored the complainant.

Insured underwent knee replacement surgery. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause due to a short renewal delay after 11 years of continuous coverage. Ombudsman directed payment of 80% of the admissible claim.
Insured hospitalized for mandibular cyst. Claim rejected under pre-existing disease clause as he had similar mandible infection 10 years prior. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claims for two hospitalizations were rejected under pre-existing clause. First hospitalization was for observation only, making rejection tenable. Second hospitalization for chronic renal failure and MI was directed to be paid as similar past claims were settled.

Insured hospitalized for ureteric calculi and cystoscopy. TPA partially settled surgeon fees invoking reasonableness clause based on super deluxe room tariffs. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as expected behavior of a prudent person.

Insured hospitalized for heart surgery. Claim initially rejected as a complication of excluded diabetes, later partially paid by TPA. Insured sought full settlement. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision while noting already sanctioned amounts should not be recovered.

Insured hospitalized for cardiac and diabetic conditions. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause citing long-standing diabetes. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage since 1989 and previous claim payments, directing settlement.

Insured underwent CABG surgery. Claim rejected under pre-existing clause as heart ailment was considered a complication of excluded diabetes. Ombudsman directed settlement for 80% of admissible expenses on original sum insured.

Insured hospitalized for liver cirrhosis and later expired due to complications. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8 as medical evidence confirmed the cirrhosis was due to alcohol. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured claimed for cerebral ataxia and vomiting. Insurer rejected under pre-existing diabetes clause. Ombudsman noted diabetes was not necessarily the sole cause and policy was in its second year, directing 50% settlement.

Child hospitalized for undescended testes. Insurer rejected claim citing congenital anomaly exclusion. Ombudsman noted the anomaly went undetected and was not clearly an external defect, ruling in favor of complainant.

Claim for chronic renal failure and dialysis rejected because an earlier hospitalization in 2001 for hypertension and cardiomyopathy was not disclosed in the proposal form. Insurer's decision was upheld.

Claimant underwent bypass surgery and sought balance payment after partial settlement. Insurer rejected based on hospital records showing history of hypertension prior to sum insured enhancement. Ombudsman dismissed due to jurisdictional limits on resolving medical record contradictions.

Claim for lumbar canal stenosis surgery rejected due to non-disclosure of a laminectomy performed 20 years prior. As the past surgery had no recent complications, the Ombudsman ordered 80% settlement with a 20% penalty for non-disclosure.

Claim for acute pancreatitis leading to death was rejected under alcohol abuse exclusion. Hospital records confirmed alcohol consumption and a previous pancreatitis attack. Insurer's rejection was upheld.

Claim for kidney transplant recipient hospitalized for headache and giddiness rejected as hospitalization was unwarranted since only oral medicines and OPD investigations were administered. Insurer's decision upheld.

Insured disputed quantum for bilateral cataract surgeries. Insurer settled according to group policy MOU limits and 30-day cataract waiting period rules after sum insured enhancement. Insurer's partial payment upheld.

Claim for ceacal ulcers following emergency caesarean section rejected as a pregnancy complication. Ombudsman obtained independent medical opinions favoring complainant and reverted the case back to insurer.

TPA disallowed part of surgeon fees during cashless hospitalization. Ombudsman held that network hospital and TPA issues should not burden the insured and directed reimbursement of the extra amount paid.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for pulmonary and cardiac conditions rejected due to pre-existing illness within five months of policy inception. Although telemarketing involved no proposal form, medical records proved chronic prior symptoms. Insurer's decision sustained.

Claim for tuberculosis hospitalization and death rejected because symptoms existed prior to policy inception and hospitalization occurred on the second day of coverage, violating pre-existing and 30-day exclusion clauses.

Cashless facility was denied and claim rejected on grounds that hospitalization for backache and joint pain was for observation/investigation and lacked emergency. Ombudsman awarded 50% on an ex-gratia basis due to patient suffering.
Claim for child heart surgery rejected due to late submission while waiting for primary insurer to process papers. During Ombudsman proceedings, insurer agreed to reopen and process the claim.

Claim for spinal surgery rejected due to non-submission of older consultation notes from 2005. As the insured passed away, family could not produce them. Ombudsman directed the company to properly investigate and resolve the matter.

Insurer paid claim only up to initial sum insured, refusing enhanced sum insured for PTCA heart surgery because the enhancement carried a specific diabetes exclusion, and blood tests confirmed uncontrolled diabetes.

Claim for foot amputation due to diabetes complications rejected due to policy exclusion. Insurer later admitted the exclusion appeared due to a system error, issued a corrective endorsement, and instructed TPA to process the claim.

Claim for malaria treatment was partially cut by TPA for vitamins, unrelated lab tests, and diabetic consultation. Ombudsman ordered reimbursement of prescribed recovery vitamins/tonics but upheld deductions for unrelated stress tests and diabetic consultation.

CABG claim rejected due to 15-year pre-existing diabetes history despite disclosure in proposal. Ombudsman upheld the pre-existing exclusion clause supremacy but ordered 75% ex-gratia settlement given 7 claim-free years.

Claim for heart ailment rejected under pre-existing clause because insured had CABG in 1988. Complainant argued disclosure at 1997 inception and lack of exclusions. Ombudsman held that current policy terms and pre-existing exclusions apply.

Insured was admitted for gout and treated with oral medication and investigations. The insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.10 stating hospitalization was unnecessary. During the hearing, the insurer reviewed the case and settled the claim.

Insured was admitted for acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease. The claim was rejected as pre-existing since bronchitis and asthma were excluded under the policy and considered related lung conditions. The insurer's decision was upheld.

Insured's son underwent subcutaneous mastectomy for gynaecomastia. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.5 for cosmetic surgery. The ombudsman set aside the repudiation noting the surgery was due to pain and enlargement from hormonal imbalance, not purely cosmetic.

Insured hospitalized for acute renal failure. Claim rejected because renal failure was linked to long-standing diabetes mellitus and hypertension as pre-existing conditions. The company's decision was upheld, but they were directed to pay 50% ex-gratia.

Insured claimed reimbursement for treatment of bilateral osteoarthritis received at a healthcare centre on an OPD basis involving daily exposure for 21 days without hospital admission. The claim was rightly refused as it did not fulfill the 24-hour hospitalization requirement.

Insured hospitalized for tenosynovitis and dilated cardiomyopathy. Claims were delayed and questioned over diabetes history. Following forum intervention and document review, the company settled the claim for Rs. 71,213 as full and final payment.

Insured hospitalized for generalized weakness and shortness of breath, diagnosed with HIV infection and opportunistic infections. The insurer rejected the claim as HIV/AIDS treatments are excluded under the policy. The forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent CAG and PTCA for chest discomfort. Insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of diabetes since 6-7 years. Although telemarketing lacked proposal forms, the long-standing diabetes was a major risk factor for heart ailments making repudiation tenable.

Insured's father treated for sub foveal choroidal neovascular membrane (macular degeneration). Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing age-related issues worsened by diabetes and that treatment was a day-care procedure not needing hospitalization. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured underwent vitrectomy and lens removal for complications from a cataract surgery done 10 years prior. Insurer rejected the claim due to missing past records. Given the long continuous policy and charitable hospital origin of past records, benefit of doubt was given and claim allowed.

Complainant was hospitalized for varicocele, phimosis, and frenuloplasty, alongside primary infertility. The insurer invoked clause 4.8 to reject the varicocelectomy due to infertility exclusions. The phimosis and frenuloplasty procedures were allowed and held payable.

Claim for urinary tract infection (UTI) treatment was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause 4.1. The ombudsman noted that an infection is recurrent and temporary, not a continuous pre-existing disease. The respondent was directed to pay the claim.

Claim for road accident fracture treatment and subsequent wire removal was rejected due to alleged 7-day delay in lodgment. The ombudsman found no delay in intimation and directed the respondent to process the validly supported claim papers.

Expenses for myomectomy surgery were refused by TPA for late submission beyond 7 days. Facts showed papers were submitted promptly after final medical fitness certificate. The respondent was directed to call for papers and process the claim.

Claim for renal pelvic stone treatment was initially repudiated under pre-existing disease clause 4.1. Since the continuous policy started in 1998, the ailment became covered after 4 years. The insurer admitted TPA error and settled the claim prior to the hearing.

Claim for right knee operation was refused by TPA for late submission. Verification showed follow-up visits extended until fitness was declared, making the lodgment timely within the post-hospitalization window. The respondent was ordered to decide the claim.

Claim papers were refused for a 14-day delay after post-hospitalization completion, caused by a family bereavement. The ombudsman held that the TPA's outright refusal was unfair and directed the respondent to condone the delay and process the claim.

Claim was repudiated because the insured was suffering from tongue cancer since 1998, prior to the policy inception in 1999, and the fact was not disclosed. Medical referee reports confirmed pre-existence. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for hospitalization due to suicidal depression (alprazolam overdose) was rejected under exclusion 4.8 for intentional self-injury. The respondent failed to prove suicidal intent or police involvement, so rejection was unjustified. The respondent was directed to settle the claim.

Complainant contested the disallowance of post-hospitalization expenses under a mediclaim policy. The insurer established that they had already paid out an amount exceeding the maximum effective sum insured limit due to an oversight. The case was dismissed.

Claim was lodged under a mediclaim policy. The insurer imposed an unexplained restriction of Rs. 2.5 Lakh without justification or notice to the complainant. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to set aside the restriction and settle the claim.

Claim was repudiated for lack of hospitalization and non-submission of discharge summary. The complainant provided a hospital certificate instead. The insurer did not submit documents or attend the hearing. The Ombudsman directed the case to be reopened upon submission of required papers.

Claim for inguinal hernia surgery was rejected under clause 4.8 as a congenital condition. Independent medical opinion established that inguinal hernia may develop at any age. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to settle the claim.

Claim for Folicular Carcinoma of Thyroid was repudiated due to non-disclosure and pre-existing condition, as records showed the ailment existed for 10 years prior to policy inception. The case was dismissed.
Hospitalization claim for Fistula in Ano was repudiated because Ayurvedic treatment was not taken in a government medical college as required by clause 2.1. The case was dismissed.

Claim following an accident was disputed on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Considering injuries and doctor's advice, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim based on facts.

Claim for Acute Ulcerative Colitis was rejected for late submission exceeding 7 days, though policy terms allowed 30 days. The Ombudsman condoned the delay and directed the insurer to process the claim.

Claim for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia was settled for Rs. 50,000 against a claim of Rs. 63,015. The sum insured was enhanced from Rs. 50k to Rs. 1 lakh when the pre-existing ailment arose. The deduction was upheld.
Claim was lodged for malaria and respiratory infection, but records showed treatment was for a pre-existing knee injury explicitly excluded from the cover. The case was dismissed as false.
Claim was settled for Rs. 50,000 based on the pre-enhancement sum insured because the ailment was pre-existing when the sum insured was raised from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 Lakh.

Claim for Neurogenic Bladder was repudiated under clause 4.1 due to alleged pre-existing frequent urination since childhood. The insurer did not submit documents. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered payment.
Claim for recurrent urine infection, hydrocele, and phimosis was repudiated under clause 4.8 as a congenital external ailment. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the case.
Claim for burn injuries resulting in death was repudiated as police records and inquest papers pointed towards suicide due to old illness. The complaint failed and the case was dismissed.
Claim for post-discharge treatment of Chronic Osteomyelitis exceeding the 60-day policy limit and submitted past the deadline was dismissed.
Claim for Yag Laser Capsulotomy performed as an outpatient procedure following cataract surgery was repudiated because it is not payable outside hospitalization. The case was dismissed.

Claim for Fistula in Ano operation performed by an Ayurvedic surgeon in a private nursing home was rejected under clause 2.1 requiring inpatient treatment in a government hospital. The case was dismissed.
Claim for dental treatment expenses resulting from an accident was repudiated because the policy strictly restricts payments to treatments involving hospitalization. The case was dismissed.
Claim involving diabetic laser treatment was repudiated because medical documents proved diabetes pre-existed the policy inception. The case was dismissed.

Claim for hospitalization to perform coronary angiography for chest pain was repudiated because the admission was deemed purely for diagnostic purposes rather than active treatment. The case was dismissed.
Claim for bronchitis and respiratory tract infection was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 as a pre-existing condition known for 10 years. The case was dismissed.
Claim was repudiated due to alleged pre-existing hypertension leading to chronic renal failure. Evidence did not categorically prove hypertension was pre-existing, so the insurer was directed to pay.

Claim for CAD and TVD was rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion. The past myocardial infarction occurred approximately 6 years prior after policy inception, hence not pre-existing. Insurer directed to pay.

Claim for Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) treated via overnight polysomnography was rejected as diagnostic. The ombudsman noted OSA requires overnight admission and can cause severe complications, making repudiation unjustified.

Claim for finger injury debridement and suturing under local anesthesia was repudiated because hospitalization was unnecessary. Lack of pre/post-operative x-rays also supported the insurer's decision. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for LSCS operation and complications including pulmonary edema was rejected under pregnancy and childbirth exclusion clause. Independent medical opinion supported the insurer's view, and the complaint was dismissed.
Claim was rejected citing pre-existing difficulty in walking. Medical records showed first consultation after policy inception and history did not go back to inception. Insurer directed to pay claim.
Claim for diabetes mellitus was repudiated due to pre-existing condition dating back before policy inception with a gap in renewal history. Complaint failed and was dismissed.

Heart disease claim repudiated for suppressed pre-existing hypertension and past angioplasties. Conflicting hospital records and affidavits created factual disputes beyond the forum's limited infrastructure, so the complaint was disposed.
Claim for incisional hernia operation was rejected because it arose from previous LSCS with ligation done prior to policy inception, amounting to material concealment. Complaint dismissed.

Dental treatment claim for fractured teeth was treated on an OPD basis with hospitalization period lower than the minimum stipulated requirement, invoking corrective/cosmetic exclusion. Case dismissed.
Claim for finger fracture surgery under local anesthesia was rejected due to lack of required hospitalization. During mediation, parties agreed to a compromise settlement of Rs. 4,000.

Claim for laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery for morbid obesity was rejected as cosmetic surgery. Evidence showed it was life-saving to prevent high-risk complications rather than cosmetic fat removal. Complaint succeeded.
Dispute over short-settled scald burns hospitalizations due to TPA being unaware of cumulative bonus. Through forum mediation, parties mutually agreed to a final settlement amount.

Meniscus tear surgery claim was repudiated due to a 116-day delay in submission. As a goodwill gesture, the insurer offered an ex-gratia settlement of 60% of the admissible claim, which was approved by the forum.

Claim rejected on grounds that admission was for physiotherapy only. Since the patient was actually admitted for myasthenia gravis and hemiplegia following doctor's advice, hospitalization was valid. Insurer directed to pay up to sum insured.
Claim for varicose veins was repudiated as a pre-existing disease. Insurer failed to submit evidence establishing pre-existence given continuous renewals since 1997. Complaint succeeded.

Claim for acute pancreatitis with septicemia was repudiated as hospital records failed to prove standard investigations like sonography or CT scans were performed, raising doubts. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for torn earlobe treated under local anesthesia was rejected because it was handled as an OPD process without required hospital bed admission. Complaint dismissed.
Dental treatment claim following an accident was rejected under exclusion clauses because treatment occurred in a dental clinic on an OPD basis without 24 hours hospitalization. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for oral chemotherapy for breast cancer was rejected because it did not involve 24 hours hospitalization. Due to medical advancements allowing oral administration without hospital stay, the insurer was directed to settle.

Claim for cataract surgery hospitalization was repudiated for delayed submission. The treatment lasted until 28-09-2007 and papers were submitted on 21-09-2007, making the delay clause inoperative. Insurer was directed to settle.

Individual mediclaim for hip pain hospitalization was rejected due to alleged pre-existing disease based on an undated doctor note mentioning symptoms for over 3 months. The ombudsman noted pain is a symptom, not a disease. Complaint succeeded.

Mediclaim was repudiated under clause 1.1 as expenses were incurred solely for pathological exams and medicines without hospitalization. Document analysis showed prescriptions and reports related to diagnostic tests only. Case dismissed.

Mediclaim for acute psychosis hospitalization was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8 for psychiatric treatment. Medical records confirmed the diagnosis of psychiatric disorder which is expressly excluded. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for viral infection and hypertension hospitalization was repudiated due to inordinate delay in submission (lodged after nearly 6 months without prior intimation). Repudiation under late submission clause was correct. Case dismissed.

Hospitalization claim for train accident injuries was rejected on grounds of diagnosis-only admission. Following forum mediation, parties mutually agreed to a settlement of 75% of the claim, and the case was disposed.

Hernia surgery claim was repudiated for pre-existing disease due to a policy break caused by a bank strike during renewal. The delay of a few days was beyond control and shouldn't constitute a break. Complaint succeeded.

Claim for severe knee injury hospitalization was rejected as treatment could be done on OPD basis. Through forum mediation, parties mutually agreed to an amount of Rs. 3007 for full and final settlement.

Hospitalization claim for accelerated hypertension was rejected as admission was for diagnosis. Documents proved admission was required for dosage adjustment. Insurer offered Rs. 20,000 in full settlement, which the complainant accepted.

Claim for breast lump treatment was rejected as pre-existing and under exclusion for uterine fibroid hysterectomy. Medical history did not predate policy, and no hysterectomy was performed. Complaint succeeded with full payment ordered.

Group mediclaim was rejected for a 14-day delay in submission because papers were routed through the employer. The delay was minor and warranted condonation for a PSU group scheme. Complaint succeeded.

Claim for diabetes and hypertension hospitalization was not settled because the complainant failed to submit hospital records, offering a hospital letter instead. Mandatory submission of papers not met, so case was dismissed with liberty to submit.
Mediguard claim for diabetes and hypertension was rejected on grounds of unnecessary hospitalization. During hearing, parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement of Rs. 10,000.

Claim for TURP, orchiectomy, and herniplasty was rejected for pre-existing disease. Records showed only the hernia was pre-existing since 1997, while other conditions were not. Insurer directed to settle claims for TURP and orchiectomy.

Claim for ischemic heart disease and angioplasty was rejected under pre-existing clause since the policy excluded diabetes and related disorders, and the insured had long-standing diabetes acting as a high risk factor. Case dismissed.

Hospitalization claim was rejected for late submission beyond 30 days. During proceedings, the insurer agreed to revoke repudiation and settle if the complaint was withdrawn, resolving the dispute mutually.
Claim for chest pain hospitalization was rejected under clause 4.10. Considering the 13-year continuous policy renewal and first claim, the insurer agreed to settle upon mediation.

Claim for viral hepatitis and hemolytic anemia was rejected as pre-existing due to congenital G6PD disorder. Insurer could not establish connection to viral hepatitis. Complaint awarded for viral hepatitis treatment while rest upheld.

Critical illness claim for CABG was rejected because symptoms occurred within 180 days of policy reinstatement, violating the waiting period clause for critical illnesses after reinstatement. Case dismissed.
Claim for adhesiolysis operation was repudiated, but through forum mediation the insurer offered Rs. 6,595 as full and final settlement, which the complainant accepted.

Claim for ischemic heart disease was repudiated because medical records indicated symptoms existed 5-6 months prior, falling within 180 days of policy inception and representing non-disclosure of pre-existing health information.

A claim for nose surgery was repudiated invoking clause 4.3. Following forum mediation, the insurer agreed to settle the claim as per rules after verifying the policy was active for 3 years without a break.

Hospitalization for meniscus tear was repudiated as a pre-existing condition under clause 4.1 based on a medical referee's opinion. The forum found the policy was renewed continuously and the insurer's plea was invalid, directing settlement.

A claim was rejected on the grounds that hospital admission was solely for diagnostic purposes rather than treatment. Through forum mediation, the insurer agreed to settle 75 percent of the claimed amount.

Hospitalization for Urinary Tract Infection was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion clause 4.1. Medical records showed consultations and symptoms occurring just prior to policy inception. The complaint was dismissed.
A claim for breast abscess was repudiated under pregnancy and childbirth exclusions. Following forum mediation, the insurer agreed to settle the claim by mutual understanding.

A claim for prolapsed piles was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8 due to an underlying liver cirrhosis condition. During forum mediation, the insurer agreed to pay 8,500 rupees in full and final settlement.

A claim for fistula and piles treatment was rejected because the procedure was performed in a private Ayurvedic hospital rather than a government hospital, violating policy conditions. The complaint was dismissed.

A claim for major depressive disorder was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8. Records confirmed treatment for severe mental depression following a family mishap, justifying the insurer's rejection under policy exclusions.

A claim for high blood pressure and brain hemorrhage was repudiated as pre-existing based on a neurologist's note. The forum noted the policy had been active since 1998 without breaks, making the pre-existing clause inoperative. Repudiation was set aside.

A claim for viral hepatitis was rejected due to lack of timely intimation and missing papers with the third-party administrator. Through forum mediation, the insurer agreed to open the file and settle admissible amounts.

A claim for intestinal obstruction surgery was rejected under pre-existing ailment clauses due to medical history dating back several years. Following forum mediation confirming policy inception since 1992, the insurer agreed to settle for 81,868 rupees.

A reimbursement claim for dental injury was repudiated under dental treatment exclusion clause 4.7. Records confirmed the periodontal condition did not require hospitalization, leading to the dismissal of the complaint.

A claim for bipolar disorder and acid ingestion was repudiated under pre-existing disease and run-down condition clauses. Records proved a psychiatric history spanning seven years, justifying the rejection.
A claim for bipolar disorder treatment was rejected under mental treatment exclusion clause 4.8. Documents confirmed the diagnosis of a mental disorder, upholding the insurer's repudiation.
A claim for renal disorder and pleural effusion was repudiated due to an inordinate delay of 11 months in submitting claim documents without requesting condonation of delay, violating clause 5.4.

A claim for back pain was rejected because diagnostic tests like an MRI were performed after discharge and no active treatment or injectables were administered during hospitalization, confirming it was an outpatient procedure.

A claim for acute chest syndrome and respiratory tract infection was repudiated invoking clause 4.3. The forum noted that the treating doctor's opinion takes precedence over medical referees and the patient had no past hypertension history. Repudiation was set aside.

A claim for balanoposthitis surgery was repudiated under congenital disease exclusion clause 4.8. The forum noted the condition was pathological and occurred across wide age ranges, making the exclusion unjustified. Settlement of 7,203 rupees was ordered.

A complaint was filed regarding inordinate delay in settling a hospital package claim. As the insurer failed to provide valid reasons for withholding payment and no lapse was found on the complainant, the insurer was ordered to pay the sum insured of 75,000 rupees with interest.

Complainant lodged a claim under five Bhavishya Arogya policies. The insurer agreed to pay for three policies but rejected two policies incepted after the claim. Both parties resolved the matter mutually.

Mediclaim for Rs. 66,672 was partially disallowed by Rs. 5,295 for non-medical administrative charges like surcharge, admission fee, HIV test, and certificate charge. The ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the amount as they could not be clearly classified as non-medical expenses.

Insurer partially disallowed a claim for Alzheimer's treatment, cutting expenses for items like diapers and nebulizer kits, as well as an unsupported Echo report bill. The ombudsman upheld the cut for external items but ordered payment of Rs. 500 for the Echo report.

The insurer imposed an unjustifiable excess/deductible of Rs. 10,000 on a continuously renewed policy without prior intimation or reason. The ombudsman ruled in favor of the complainant and ordered full settlement.

Claim for post-surgery BCG therapy was partially disallowed under the premise that 24-hour hospitalization was not required for BCG. The insurer agreed to consider the case upon submission of proof of treatment, leading to an order to process the claim.

Insured underwent a hysterectomy. The insurer arbitrarily deducted expenses relying on an opinion from a medical referee who was not a gynecologist. The ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the disallowed portion.
A hospitalization claim was partially settled with deductions. Through the mediation of the forum, both parties agreed to resolve the dispute on a mutual basis with the insurer paying the difference.

The insurer partially settled a reimbursement claim after altering terms and capping individual expense heads. Following mediation, the insurer agreed to pay the full cashless amount of Rs. 61,500 in full and final settlement.
Insurer partially settled an Inguinal Hernia surgery claim invoking clause 4.7. Upon mediation, the insurer agreed to settle the balance amount and resolve the dispute.

Claim for breast lump treatment was settled for 70% of the sum insured because the policy was newly incepted and treated as a fresh insurance restricting major surgeries during the initial period. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for knee pain and swelling was repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary and treatment could be done on an OPD basis. The ombudsman held that the treating doctor is the best judge and ordered full payment.

Claim for surgery of an ingrowing toenail was rejected under exclusion 4.10 for lack of necessity of hospitalization. The ombudsman ruled that the attending doctor's decision on hospitalization must be respected and ordered claim settlement.

Claim for urinary tract infection with diabetes was repudiated stating treatment could be managed as an outpatient. The ombudsman held the attending doctor as the proper judge of hospitalization necessity and ordered payment.

Claim for respiratory issues was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing pulmonary tuberculosis from 8-9 years prior. The ombudsman noted continuous policy renewals since 2001 without complications and ordered full claim settlement.

Claim for nasal wall growth treatment was closed as 'no claim' for want of missing documents despite the insured submitting them. The ombudsman ruled against the arbitrary closure and ordered claim processing.

Claim for threatened abortion resulting in excess bleeding was repudiated under standard policy exclusion for pregnancy and childbirth-related treatments. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for para-umbilical hernia was rejected citing a past hysterectomy as a pre-existing condition. The ombudsman found no concrete evidence linking the hernia to the prior surgery and ordered claim settlement.

Claim for LASIK surgery to correct vision and save eyesight was rejected under exclusions for cosmetic surgery or correction of eyesight. The ombudsman noted the surgery was medically necessary to save vision and ordered settlement.

Claim for drug reaction and subsequent eye treatments was rejected because the insured renewed the policy with an enhanced sum insured without disclosing prior ailments. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as claims were already settled up to the original sum insured.

Claim for diabetes mellitus and chest pain was repudiated citing pre-existing conditions without concrete proof. The ombudsman noted lack of evidence from the insurer and ordered full claim settlement.

Insured claimed for two hospitalizations for acute intestinal obstruction. First claim was processed but delayed, and second claim was partially restricted due to enhanced sum insured exclusion rules. Ombudsman ordered settlement of Rs. 15,000 with 9% interest due to unfair delay.

Insured's claim for chronic liver disease was rejected under alcoholism exclusion clause 4.8. Ombudsman held that it was not established beyond doubt that treatment resulted from alcoholism and allowed the claim.

Long-term policyholder underwent bypass surgery and claim was rejected citing pre-existing ischemic heart disease and a renewal break. Ombudsman found no proof of break period proposal formalities and ruled the policy continuous, making the claim payable.
Claim was treated as no-claim due to non-submission of required investigation reports and clarification. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision but advised reopening if documents are provided.

Claim for kidney stone surgery was repudiated because the hospital was removed from the network list. Ombudsman found no streamlined procedure of informing the insured about the change and ordered payment.

Claim for knee treatment was rejected under clause 4.10 for hospitalization primarily for observation and investigation. Ombudsman noted knee aspiration constituted actual treatment and allowed the claim.
Claim for hip surgery was rejected citing pre-existing condition and a policy break. Ombudsman noted lack of prior treatment records for the pain and gave the benefit of doubt to the complainant.

Claim for psychiatric treatment of son's depression was rejected under exclusion clause 4.8. Ombudsman ruled in favor of complainant due to lack of documentary proof that policy terms and conditions were supplied.

Claim for removal of leg rod implanted during previous policy was rejected as pre-existing. Ombudsman held that despite lack of policy terms copy, false declaration on proposal form justified repudiation.

Claim was rejected because hospitalization was for less than 24 hours. Ombudsman noted the total period was 21 hours 45 minutes close to 24 hours and fell under treatments not requiring full 24 hours.

Claim for total knee replacement was restricted to pre-enhancement sum insured of Rs. 3 lakhs for pre-existing disease. Ombudsman upheld the restriction but advised adding cumulative bonus earned up to 2002-2003.
Claim for angiography was rejected under pre-existing exclusion. Ombudsman agreed terms barred it, but due to non-availability of terms and conditions, awarded an ex-gratia amount.

Heart surgery claim was partly paid on presumption of pre-existing disease and branch manager financial limits. Ombudsman ruled the 1 lakh policy document valid and ordered full payment as no prior treatment proof existed.
Claim for heart ailment following sum enhancement was limited to previous sum insured under clause 5.12 for recurrent pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's action.

Claim was rejected under pre-existing clause because discharge summary mentioned pain for 15 years. Ombudsman noted no treatment records existed and complainant led normal life, ordering claim payment.
Claim for PTCA and stenting for CAD was rejected as hospitalization occurred 22 days after policy commencement, violating the 30-day waiting period. Complaint dismissed.

Hysterectomy claim in second year was rejected due to revised policy exclusion of two years. Ombudsman ruled that continuous renewal entitled insured to previous year's waiting period terms and ordered settlement.
Bilateral knee replacement claim in the 3rd year was rejected as pre-existing based on expert medical opinion that osteoarthritic changes developed over a long period prior to policy. Dismissed.
Excimer laser surgery claim for refractive error was rejected because policy excluded refractive errors below power -7 without disease origin. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for atrial septal defect surgery within 3 months of inception was rejected as congenital and pre-existing, supported by history of respiratory infections and prior medical records. Dismissed.

Insured underwent surgery and claimed Rs. 75,000, which was rejected under the pre-existing disease exclusion. The insurer failed to provide clinching evidence of prior acid peptic disease antedating the 2003 proposal where a medical examination was cleared. An ex-gratia amount of Rs. 30,000 was awarded.

Complainant was hospitalized for Cervical Spondylitis and hypertension. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing conditions, though hospital records failed to establish the acute condition pre-dated policy issuance. An ex-gratia sum of Rs. 6,000 was awarded.

Insured was hospitalized for headache and uneasiness following a fall at home after three continuous years of policy coverage. The TPA repudiated the claim for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. Expert opinion confirmed trauma was the proximate cause, making the rejection untenable. The complaint was allowed.

Insured was treated for giddiness and neck pain, but the claim was rejected as a pre-existing condition. The insurer delayed returning original bills by 90 days, causing the insured to lose employer reimbursement. The treating doctor confirmed the condition arose recently, and the insurer's service deficiency warranted allowing the complaint.

Insured claimed Rs. 3,25,000 for angioplasty and subsequent death, but the insurer paid only Rs. 2,00,000 citing policy limits on major surgeries. The ombudsman noted ambiguity in policy wordings should not favor the drafter and awarded an additional Rs. 75,000 as ex-gratia for pre and post-hospitalization expenses.

Spouse of complainant underwent multiple surgeries including hernia repair and hysterectomy. The claim was rejected under clause 4.1 for pre-existing ailment. Since records merely indicated swelling for two years rather than pain and the insurer failed to produce proposal forms or clinching evidence, the complaint was allowed.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for suspected chikungunya and unfortunately passed away from complications including hypoglycemic coma. The claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes. Without exact medical records proving diabetes onset prior to policy inception, an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 30,000 was awarded.

Insured underwent a PET-CT procedure as an out-patient after treatment for Follicular Lymphoma. The claim was rejected because out-patient procedures and diagnostic tests without active treatment do not fulfill the requirement of a minimum 24-hour in-patient hospital stay. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured underwent heart surgery during the policy period, and the claim was rejected on grounds of pre-existing condition. ECG reports from years prior to the policy commencement clearly indicated 'Hypertensive Heart Disease', falling under policy exclusions. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for giddiness, anxiety, and diagnostic tests. The claim was rejected under exclusion of expenses incurred solely for evaluation. Since the patient was diagnosed and administered psychiatric drugs requiring hospitalization under treating doctors' judgment, the rejection was unjustified and the complaint was allowed.

Insured met with an accident resulting in trauma and underwent prolonged treatment. The insurer rejected the claim citing non-submission of documents and misrepresentation regarding suicide or police registration. As the injuries were not disputed and the insurer failed to substantiate grounds, full settlement was ordered.

Insured was hospitalized for Multiple Sclerosis. The insurer rejected the claim citing a pre-existing condition based on past treatment for arthritis symptoms. As multiple sclerosis was only diagnosed recently and the insured was unaware of the exact condition earlier, the complaint was allowed with Rs. 50,000 awarded as ex-gratia.

Insured was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma rectum and hypertension. The claim was rejected due to pre-existing conditions, with medical opinion confirming the advanced cancer required more than 18 months to develop, which predated the policy inception five months prior. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured's daughter underwent LASIK laser surgery for myopia in both eyes. The TPA repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.5 for cosmetic or aesthetic treatment. Medical opinion confirmed high myopia is defined as power exceeding (-) 7, and since the patient's power was below that threshold, the rejection was upheld.

Insured with continuous policy coverage for eight years underwent surgery for Familial Adenomatous Polyposis. The insurer rejected the claim on grounds of pre-existing disease, successfully proving through records that symptoms existed prior to obtaining the policy for the first time. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured received treatment for scar sarcoidosis and steroid-induced myopathy. The insurer rejected the claim on pre-existing condition grounds. Hospital records and indoor case sheets established that the hospitalization related directly to a sarcoidal flare-up on a scar from a past operation. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured preferred claims for treatment taken by his spouse, which were rejected under clause 4.1 for pre-existing diabetes and coronary disease since 1996. The insurer submitted indoor case sheets recording a 15-year history of diabetes, providing irrefutable evidence of pre-proposal illness. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured's mother underwent surgery for piles on the 14th day after policy inception. The insurer rejected the claim under first-year exclusions because the policy had experienced a 9-day break due to a cheque dishonour for insufficient funds, rendering it a fresh contract. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured underwent bypass surgery and claimed Rs. 1,90,000. The claim was repudiated for pre-existing diabetes and non-disclosure, though pre-existing coronary artery disease was not conclusively established. An ex-gratia amount of Rs. 75,000 was awarded, partly allowing the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for chest pain during the third policy year and underwent an angiogram. The insurer rejected the claim based on pre-existing hypertension under clause 4.1. As the complainant failed to produce authentic documents proving the absence of the condition prior to the policy, the rejection was upheld.

Insured claimed total knee replacement expenses up to enhanced sum insured. Insurer restricted payment to pre-enhancement sum insured because major disease was diagnosed within two months of increase and no prior treatment details were furnished. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured underwent Aortic Valve Replacement and claimed Rs 2,42,038. Insurer restricted claim to Rs 2 lacs based on a new Gold Policy condition capping major illnesses without notifying the insured of changes. Ombudsman awarded Rs 20,000 as ex-gratia.

Insured hospitalized for Pituitary Tumor and claimed Rs 1,04,438. Insurer settled for Rs 52,500 based on sum insured prior to revision. Diagnosis occurred when lower sum insured was active and policy schedule bifurcated the sum. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for chest pain and coronary artery disease was repudiated as pre-existing. Discharge summary showed patient was non-diabetic, non-hypertensive with normal blood pressure, establishing no pre-existing disease. Ombudsman ordered full payment of hospitalization expenses.

Insured claimed reimbursement for Dengue treatment. Insurer deducted Rs 10,000 under a compulsory excess clause for pre-existing conditions. Insured contested the clause applicability since dengue is viral and not pre-existing.

Claim for tumor removal of middle finger under general anaesthesia was repudiated because hospital stay was under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted policy exceptions allow day care treatments under general anaesthesia at networked hospitals and directed reconsideration.

Claim for ischaemic stroke and hypertension was repudiated as pre-existing. Insurer's panel doctor observed no documents suggested prior heart disease and no ECG report existed at policy inception. Ombudsman intervened in favor of the insured.

Claim for endometriosis surgery was repudiated as pre-existing because patient was on Danazol from May 2006. Policy inception was February 2006. Ombudsman noted even if treatment started in May 2006 it was within policy coverage and ordered settlement.

Mother of complainant was treated for colon carcinoma and claim was rejected as pre-existing based on lumen obstruction severity. Ombudsman noted lack of prior medical records proving pre-existence and directed insurer to settle the claim.

Ayurvedic treatment claim for spondylitis was repudiated because treatment was taken at a private ayurvedic centre instead of a government or medical college hospital as required by policy terms. Complaint was dismissed.

Mediclaim for biliary duct and liver surgery was repudiated for non-disclosure of past operations from 1980 to 2001. Ombudsman upheld repudiation due to suppression of material facts in proposal form, but awarded Rs 10,000 ex-gratia due to advanced age.

Lasik surgery claim for myopia was rejected as pre-existing and cosmetic. Ombudsman held that vision correction was not cosmetic and older policy conditions did not exclude eye surgeries, rendering repudiation incorrect.

Claim for abdominal pain hospitalization was rejected on grounds that investigations showed normal results and no active treatment was given. Ombudsman noted hospitalization was on doctor's advice following continuous pain and ruled the claim exigible.

Lasik surgery claim was rejected as cosmetic. Ombudsman noted that the policy in force did not exclude eye corrective surgery (which was added later) and patient suffered discomfort from spectacles, meaning it was not purely cosmetic. Insurer directed to pay.

Claim for T.O. Mass was repudiated under exclusions for pregnancy prevention and childbirth. Ombudsman observed patient was not pregnant and minilap was for ligation, making exclusions inapplicable, and directed claim payment.

Complaint filed against delay in settling lumbar canal stenosis claim. Insurer requested past low back pain records and registration certificate. Ombudsman directed complainant to submit documents and insurer to decide on settlement thereafter.

Incision hernia claim was repudiated on the ground of pre-existing surgical scar from prior operations. Ombudsman held that hernia is an anatomical event occurring due to a scar and not a pre-existing disease, directing settlement.
Motor insurance claim for burnt car was repudiated due to electrical breakdown from a non-standard music system. Ombudsman ordered appointment of a new independent surveyor for a conclusive report.

Mediclaim for biliary surgery was repudiated for non-disclosure of past abdominal surgeries. Ombudsman upheld repudiation due to suppression of facts but awarded Rs 10,000 ex-gratia considering advanced age.

Claim for daughter's hospitalization due to fever and rash was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.2 for occurring within 30 days of policy commencement. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to appoint a medical panel to verify if the disease could have been known at proposal, ruling in favor of the insured.

Claim for Hysterectomy due to Menorrhagia was rejected on grounds of pre-existing disease and first-year exclusion. The Ombudsman noted the operation occurred in the second year and there was no irrefutable proof of pre-existence, holding the insurer's reasons untenable.

Claim for PTMC procedure for Rheumatic Heart Disease was rejected as pre-existing. The Ombudsman found no proof that the disease existed prior to the policy inception or that symptoms were known, directing the insurer to settle the claim.

Claim for spine surgery was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion following a 7-day policy renewal break. The Ombudsman condoned the short delay, treated the policy as continuous, and ordered payment as there was no proof of pre-existence.

Bypass surgery claim was rejected on grounds of pre-existing hypertension and chest pain. The Ombudsman held that hypertension is only a symptom and there was no irrefutable proof of manifestation before policy inception, directing the insurer to pay.

Claim for ventral hernia operation was rejected because the insured had a prior hernia operation in 1997. The Ombudsman ruled that an incisional hernia resulting from an internal scar is not a pre-existing disease, especially under a long-standing continuous policy, and ordered payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Incisional hernia claim was rejected due to a prior hysterectomy in 1993. The Ombudsman held that incisional hernia caused by an old scar is not a pre-existing disease, setting aside the repudiation and directing settlement.

Claim for duodenal ulcer and gastritis treatment was rejected on the ground that hospitalization was for investigation only and could be done on OPD basis. The Ombudsman noted that tests successfully diagnosed the underlying condition and ordered settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claims for ACL reconstruction for two sons were rejected due to discrepancies in injury dates mentioned in different prescriptions, interpreted as false statements. The Ombudsman ruled that minor date discrepancies do not forfeit a genuine claim under a long-standing policy and ordered payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for subdural haematoma evacuation was initially rejected under heart disease exclusion, then shifted to hypertension complications. The Ombudsman found no proof of pre-existing hypertension or nexus, directing the insurer to pay the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Root canal treatment claim was rejected because it was performed in a clinic and allegedly not covered. The Ombudsman found treatment was done in a dental hospital due to disease rather than cosmetic reasons, ordering full payment.
Tympanoplasty claim for CSOM was repudiated as pre-existing. Considering the insured's long insurance history, the Ombudsman set aside the insurer's decision and ordered claim settlement.

Two claims involved: wife's back pain hospitalization rejected for investigation-only (allowed by Ombudsman as MRI confirmed degenerative spine), and husband's prostate-related surgery rejected as pre-existing (remanded for independent specialist opinion).

Claim for diabetes and chest pain evaluation was rejected because hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours and was for evaluation purposes. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on policy conditions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for vertigo hospitalization was partially rejected because CT/MRI was not performed. As the insurer agreed to settle part of the expenses during proceedings, the Ombudsman directed payment of the remaining deducted amount.

Coronary artery disease claim for enhanced sum insured was restricted due to non-disclosure of a prior claim when converting from group to individual policy. The Ombudsman directed verification of the original group cover limits and bonus for settlement.
Personal accident claim for death by bus accident was rejected due to delayed submission of documents beyond the 90-day limit. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for back pain hospitalization was rejected on the ground that treatment could be done on OPD basis. The Ombudsman noted the patient was diagnosed with Koch's disease and ordered claim payment.

Syncope hospitalization claim was rejected on grounds of investigation and evaluation only. The Ombudsman held that investigations were necessary to evaluate transient loss of consciousness and directed claim payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Accidental injury claim for wound repair was rejected for hospitalization lasting under 24 hours. Noting subsequent policy amendments covering accidents, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 6,000.

Claim for daughter's hospitalization due to convulsion was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease and investigation purpose only. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation under policy condition 4.10 for tests not indicating any disease.
Claim for L4-L5 Intervertebral Disc Prolapse treatment was rejected because hospitalization was under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted it as a rarest of rare cases and allowed full payment.

Claim for a 1-year-old child hospitalized for fever and convulsion was repudiated as pre-existing. Ombudsman found no proper evidence of pre-existing disease and directed full payment after employer's partial reimbursement.
Wife's discectomy claim was rejected due to pre-existing back pain of 4 years not disclosed in proposal form. Ombudsman upheld repudiation for suppression of material fact.

Claim for surgery of bilateral undescended testis was rejected under exclusion 4.8 for congenital external disease. Ombudsman ordered an independent medical specialist opinion to determine if external or internal.
Claim for coronary artery disease treatment was repudiated due to 7-month delay in submission. Ombudsman condoned the delay and directed insurer to investigate and review the claim.
Claim for appendectomy was rejected as falling within 30 days waiting period. Ombudsman noted surgery occurred after 30 days and directed settlement.
Claim for acute pulmonary oedema was initially repudiated on pre-existing symptom grounds. Insurer later decided to settle, and Ombudsman closed the intervention.
Claim for syncope was rejected due to history of hypertension. Ombudsman ruled hypertension is a symptom and not proven linked to syncope, directing payment.
Pneumonia claim was rejected due to pre-existing DM and HTN. As original proposal forms were missing, Ombudsman gave benefit of doubt to the complainant and ordered payment.
Claim for chemotherapy taken at home was rejected as treatment was not in a hospital. Ombudsman agreed with repudiation but awarded ex-gratia payment.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Heart attack claim was repudiated on pre-existing disease grounds with policy break condoned. Ombudsman found no irrefutable proof of prior disease and directed payment.
Sinus surgery claim was rejected due to policy renewal breaks invoking a two-year exclusion clause. Ombudsman condoned short renewal delays, treated policy as continuous, and ordered payment.
Claim for intradural schwannoma surgery was rejected citing 2-year history of back pain. Ombudsman held that pain is a symptom, not a disease, and directed payment.
Claim for sialoadenitis was rejected for undisclosed previous pain. Ombudsman ruled minor past pain was not material non-disclosure and ordered claim settlement.
Laparoscopic cholecystectomy claim was rejected under 30-day waiting period exclusion. Ombudsman found no proof of disease detection within first 30 days and directed payment.
Prostate surgery claim was rejected because renal allograft history from 2000 was not disclosed in the proposal form. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.
Claim for root canal treatment was rejected because hospitalization was under 24 hours and dental treatments are excluded unless due to accident. Ombudsman dismissed the petition.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Heart treatment claim was rejected under 30-day waiting period clause. Ombudsman noted emergency admission and lack of prior knowledge, directing claim payment.
Cataract surgery claim was rejected due to alleged pre-existing vision dimness of 2 years. Ombudsman upheld the rule but awarded an ex-gratia amount.

Insured claimed reimbursement for cardiac hospitalization under an individual mediclaim policy active since 1992. The insurer delayed settlement and referenced a different claim amount. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the claim if distinct from the other file.

Insured was hospitalized for severe neck and back pain and diagnosed with cervical spondylosis. The insurer initially denied cashless and later repudiated reimbursement under exclusion 4.10 for primary investigation. The Ombudsman held the exclusion inapplicable as tests were for diagnosing an ailment, directing settlement.

Insured was hospitalized for decompensated liver disease. The claim was repudiated under clause 4.8 alleging alcohol consumption based on a doctor's certificate stating occasional drinking. The Ombudsman noted lack of irrefutable proof linking alcohol to the disease and directed full settlement.

Beneficiary of a group mediclaim policy sought reimbursement for an eye operation. The insurer stated the group policy was cancelled prior to the hospitalization date at the bank's request and premium refunded. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint due to lack of policy coverage at the time of occurrence.

Insured's wife underwent pelvic floor repair for cystocele and rectocele. The insurer repudiated the claim as a pre-existing disease assuming the condition could not develop in one month. The Ombudsman found no concrete evidence of pre-existence and directed settlement.

Insured suffered loss of cash in transit and a mobile phone. The insurer insisted on a final police report certified by a local court. The Ombudsman held that an interim police report was sufficient for small losses and directed settlement upon submission of an indemnity bond.

Insured underwent lumbar canal stenosis surgery and sought reimbursement. The insurer delayed and sought past treatment papers due to a past history of low back pain mentioned in the discharge summary. The Ombudsman noted no final decision was taken by the insurer and suggested document compliance.

Insured claimed maternity benefits under a group policy. The insurer rejected it applying a fresh 9-month waiting period after the employer changed insurers. The Ombudsman ruled that continuous coverage under previous policies must be honored and set aside the rejection.
Duplicate record of case bk9-0228 regarding cardiac hospitalization and delayed settlement under a long-standing mediclaim policy. The Ombudsman directed payment of the claim.

Nominee sought death claim under a group personal accident policy after the insured died in a train incident. The insurer repudiated based on police investigation confirming suicide by jumping in front of a train. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured sought reimbursement for maternity hospitalization. The insurer stated payment was already processed and included in a list handed over to the TPA for disbursement. The Ombudsman noted no further intervention was required.
Insured submitted two claims for abscess ulcerated wound and pyoderma gangrenosum. The grievance was satisfactorily redressed during proceedings, requiring no further intervention.

Insured filed a claim for senior citizen mediclaim hospitalization which remained undecided. The insurer agreed to review admissibility. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to immediately decide on settlement or repudiation.

Claim for hospitalization due to hypertension, diabetes, and ischemic heart disease was repudiated. The insurer produced proof of pre-existing IHD dating back to 2001, prior to policy inception in 2003. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insured sought balance amount for a DCR operation claim after partial deduction of inadmissible expenses. As the complainant missed the hearing and a balance cheque was processed, the Ombudsman dismissed the petition.
Insured claimed balance amount after partial settlement of hospitalization expenses. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to finalize and pay the balance amount upon document submission.

Insured contested the deduction of nursing charges from a viral pyrexia claim. Upon submission of a doctor's certificate justifying private nursing, the Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the deducted amount.

Insured contested partial deduction on a dental surgery claim for infected teeth. The insurer agreed to pay X-ray charges. The Ombudsman directed payment of the remaining balance after a minor service charge deduction.

Insured contested partial disallowance of doctor's fees and medicine bills for gastrointestinal bleeding treatment. The Ombudsman ruled that doctor's fees and bills lacking patient names should be honored if matched, directing payment.

Insured contested partial repudiation of an angiogram claim where Cath lab charges and consumables were disallowed. The Ombudsman clarified that Cath lab charges are integral to angiography and directed reimbursement.

Insured contested abnormal and unilateral hike in premium upon renewal of the Mediclaim policy due to adverse claim ratio.
