Ombudsman held that the insurer cannot increase premium unilaterally against an insured who did not make any claim, and directed a refund of excess premium charged for claim-free periods.

Claim for reimbursement of hospital expenses for Ventral Hernia was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing ailment related to prior laparoscopic Caesarian sections. The medical referee opined the hernia was a prior surgical outcome, and the complaint was dismissed.

Hospitalization claim for acute appendicitis was repudiated because it occurred within 30 days of policy inception. Ombudsman noted the insured had no prior history and was medically examined before policy issuance, ruling out pre-existing disease. Complaint succeeded and insurer was directed to settle.

Claim was repudiated for delayed submission under clause 5.4. Examination showed that post-hospitalization papers were submitted within the allowed 60 days. Insurer was directed to settle the claim for Rs. 38,311/-.

Patient was treated for Inguinal Hernia and Stone in Bladder under a single anesthesia. Insurer treated both operations as one. Ombudsman found the insured entitled to prorate reimbursement excluding common expenses, and directed settlement of Rs. 8,220/-.

Hospitalization for acute Gastroenteritis was repudiated as pre-existing irritable bowel syndrome. Insured had 18 claim-free years. Ombudsman held the gastroenteritis was not pre-existing and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Claim for excision of cystic swelling on the left wrist was repudiated on the grounds that it was an OPD procedure not requiring hospitalization. Ombudsman noted surgical procedures correcting deformities qualify under the policy and directed settlement.

Claim for cancer treatment was partially settled by restricting benefits under major surgery clauses. Ombudsman noted chemotherapy alone does not involve surgery and restriction was unjustified, directing settlement of the balance Rs. 2 Lakhs.

Claim for recurrent intra-abdominal liposarcoma was partially settled at 70% of the sum insured as a major disease. Complainant argued it was fat removal, but since liposarcoma is malignant fat, the insurer's restriction was justified and the case was dismissed.

Insurer improperly deducted cumulative bonus beyond the permissible 10% limit of the basic sum insured following a claim exceeding the basic sum insured. Complaint succeeded and insurer was directed to grant cumulative bonus at 40%.

Claim for chemotherapy was partially settled by restricting it under major surgery limits. Ombudsman held that since no surgery was involved, imposing the major surgery clause was incorrect, and directed settlement of the balance amount.

Claim for removal of an upper eyelid sebaceous cyst was repudiated because hospitalization was under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted the cyst was on the eyelid rather than the eye itself and was a minor surgery discharged within 3 hours, upholding the repudiation.

Claim for piles surgery performed by an Ayurvedic practitioner was repudiated on grounds that the doctor provided allopathic treatment without qualification. Ombudsman noted the doctor held a recognized degree and was registered, making the clause misquoted. Insurer was directed to settle.

Claim for emphysematous pyelonephritis with multi-organ failure and diabetes was repudiated due to pre-existing coronary artery bypass graft done in 2001 prior to policy inception in 2002. Repudiation was upheld and the case dismissed.

Claim for piles treatment at a private Ayurvedic hospital was repudiated because Ayurvedic treatment hospitalization is only admissible up to 25% of the sum insured when taken in a Government or Medical College hospital. Repudiation upheld.

Cradle Care policy claim for a newborn treated for preterm care and septicemia was denied because the newborn did not suffer from a covered congenital defect or malformation as required by the policy preamble. Claim was held inadmissible.

Claim for hiatus hernia surgery was partially deducted on pre-existing grounds despite continuous policy renewal since 2002. During forum mediation, the insurer offered Rs. 17,500/-, which was accepted by the complainant as a mutual resolution.

Ear surgery claim was repudiated on pre-existing grounds based on a six-month history of traumatic injury. Tracing back six months fell within the policy risk commencement date, proving the condition was not pre-existing. Insurer was directed to settle.

Claim for knee injury hospitalization was repudiated due to various discrepancies in treatment papers, bills, and intimation dates. Complainant proved through records that the accident occurred during the policy period. Insurer was directed to settle.

Claim for a 2003 hip replacement treatment was lodged late in 2005, violating clause 7.2 requiring claim submission within 30 days of treatment completion. Due to exorbitant delay and lack of justification, the complaint was dismissed.

Claim for surgical removal of teeth under general anesthesia was repudiated citing dental treatment exclusion and lack of requirement with regard to hospitalization. The ombudsman noted surgery required hospitalization and was admissible, but fixed prosthesis charges were not covered, so the complaint partially succeeded.

Hospitalization expenses were repudiated because claim documents were submitted 5 to 6 months late, violating clause 5.4 requiring submission within 30 days of discharge. The complainant provided no convincing reason for the inordinate delay, and the insurer did not condone it. The claim was dismissed.

Hospitalization for Parastomal Hernia was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing disease originating from a previous cancer rectum operation in 2001. The surgeon confirmed the operation repaired a defect at the parastoma site, indicating it was a complication subsequent to the prior cancer operation.

Treatment for dog bite taken on an OPD basis was repudiated under condition 3.11 requiring a minimum hospital stay of 24 hours. Since dog bite treatment does not fall under exempted categories, OPD treatment is not covered and the case was dismissed.

insurer: IFFCO TOKYO Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for Myelodysplastic syndrome with anemia and diarrhea was repudiated for pre-existing conditions and suppression of material facts. History records showed the insured suffered from anemia in 1996 and 2001, prior to the policy inception in 2006, violating the principle of uberrima fides.

Claims for treatment of Hypertension, Diabetes, and related complications resulting in death were repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1 for pre-existing disease. Medical records and referee opinions confirmed the insured was a known case of Type-2 diabetes for 7 years and hypertension for 2 years.

Claim for chest pain, hypertension with IHD, and anemia was repudiated as pre-existing. Although the policy was renewed in 2006, it was not in continuous renewal from its 2002 inception, and records showed a history of disease dating back to 1998.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for vascular headache treatment involving investigations and oral drugs was repudiated under clause 4.19 because hospitalization was solely for observation and investigation. Hospital and discharge records corroborated this, justifying the insurer's decision.

Hospitalization expenses for bilateral otosclerosis were denied as a pre-existing chronic disease based on medical referee opinion. The insurer failed to prove past history or provide documentary evidence of pre-existence. The repudiation was set aside and the insurer was directed to pay the admissible amount of 58148 rupees.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for viral hepatitis was repudiated under policy condition 5.7 for being fraudulent, as the treating doctor confirmed the treatment papers did not contain his signature and consultation dates conflicted with hospitalization. The insurer's decision was upheld.

Life insurance death claim for 5 lakh rupees was repudiated alleging non-disclosure of meager income, occupation, and alcohol/tobacco habits. The insurer failed to submit evidence supporting these allegations or deliberate misstatement. Repudiation was set aside and settlement ordered.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hysterectomy claim was repudiated under condition 4.1 for pre-existing pelvic inflammatory disease based on a medical referee statement. Since the insured was illiterate and the insurer failed to prove previous treatment through evidence, the repudiation was set aside and settlement directed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for osteoarthritis treatment was settled for 50000 rupees based on the old sum insured, while 19950 rupees was disallowed. The complainant sought cumulative bonus of 5000 rupees under the policy. The insurer was advised to pay the unpaid cumulative bonus of 5000 rupees.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hospitalization expenses was repudiated under condition 4.1 as pre-existing hypertension. Hospital discharge summary recorded hypertension history of 40 years while policy incepted in 2002. An affidavit attempting to alter the history to 4 years was rejected, vindicating the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for prolapsed intervertebral disc and lumbar canal stenosis was repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was for investigation only. Hospital records showed the condition required treatment known at admission, proving the investigative excuse invalid. Repudiation was set aside with interest ordered.

Claim for acute C.V. stroke was repudiated under exclusions for alcoholism and drug abuse. Although the claimant admitted occasional alcohol and tobacco use and hypertension, the insurer failed to provide conclusive evidence proving a nexus between alcohol consumption and the illness. Settlement was ordered.

Claim for calculus disease and pancreatitis was repudiated under clause 4.3 for treatments not payable during the first two policy years. Noting treatment was conservative for two ailments, the forum applied the rule of average and directed payment of 50 percent of the admissible amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for urinary tract infection was repudiated because menorrhagia leading to anemia fell under exclusion clause 4.3. Treating records showed treatment for multiple separate conditions including DOB, PID, and UTI. Denying the entire claim was unjustified, so the insurer was directed to pay 50 percent of the claimed amount.

Claim for chronic kidney disease requiring renal replacement therapy was repudiated for pre-existing conditions based on a medical referee's opinion. The insurer failed to produce the proposal form to prove non-disclosure or provide specific dates for hypertension onset. Settlement was ordered.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for primary pulmonary hypertension was repudiated after the TPA demanded various past records, investigation reports, and treatment details. Since the insured had passed away and prior claims for the same condition were already paid, the repudiation reasons were deemed flimsy. Settlement was directed.

Claim for urethral dilation was repudiated due to pre-existing stricture urethra dating back to 1998, prior to policy inception in 1999. The nexus between previous and current treatment was confirmed, and the insurer's decision was upheld.

Claim for total knee replacement was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing knee pain of 15 years duration, while only 1 year was declared in the proposal form. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Claim for laparoscopic operation for ruptured ectopic pregnancy was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 4.12 relating to pregnancy. The insurer's decision was found correct and dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for heart disease treatment was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion. The insured had undergone CABG in 1992 and further treatment in 2001, prior to or closely linked with the policy inception in 1999. The complaint was dismissed.

Hysterectomy claim of Rs. 34,271 was partially settled for Rs. 10,000 as per policy terms restricting expenses to 20% of the sum insured of Rs. 50,000. The insurer's decision was justified and the case dismissed.

Claim was repudiated on the ground that treatment was an OPD procedure. Based on treating doctors' certificates and emergency advice, hospitalization was deemed necessary, and the insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Claim for hospitalization due to schizophrenia-residual was repudiated under clause 4.8 excluding psychiatric disorders. The attending physician confirmed symptoms existed prior to admission, and the case was dismissed.

Claim was repudiated because the disease duration was 8 months, attracting the 30-day initial waiting period exclusion clause. Although policies rolled over since 2001, the specific condition fell under exclusions. Case dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for scrotal swelling operation after an injury while playing was repudiated under congenital external disease exclusion. The forum noted the medical certificate was unsigned and relied on rubber stamps, setting aside the repudiation and ordering settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for major depression treatment was repudiated under clause excluding psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders. The complainant argued continuous renewal since 2002, but revised 2008 rules explicitly excluded psychiatric conditions. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery claim was repudiated due to late submission after original papers were lost in a bus. The forum condoned the delay, recognized the loss of originals, and directed the insurer to consider duplicate papers for payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant claimed Rs. 9,564 for short payment following room and nursing charges deductions under clause 2.1. The forum found the complainant eligible for Rs. 700 as per terms, and the complaint partially succeeded.

Claim was repudiated under the 30-day initial waiting period exclusion based solely on the first consultation date. As there was no conclusive evidence that the disease was contracted within 30 days of inception, the repudiation was set aside.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hospitalization expenses was repudiated as records showed the minimum 24-hour hospitalization requirement was not met. The case was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Dental treatment claim was repudiated because records and certificates proved treatment was taken on an OPD basis, failing hospitalization criteria. Repudiation was justified and the case dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Accidental head injury claim was repudiated for delay in submitting final claim papers beyond the 30-day post-treatment limit. Lacking supporting evidence for prolonged treatment, the insurer's decision was upheld.

Hospitalization claim for kidney treatment was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion, as the insured had undergone kidney surgery prior to policy inception in December 2001. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was repudiated because laboratory tests were linked to a closed lab, and the attending doctor was an RMP using another MBBS doctor's credentials, failing policy qualification criteria. Repudiation upheld.

Oral chemotherapy claim was repudiated due to lack of standard hospitalization. The forum set aside the repudiation, noting medical advancements allow such treatments without confinement, especially for dreaded diseases.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cardiac stroke and hypertension claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing conditions from 1999 under a policy active since 1997. Since the insurer failed to produce the proposal form as conclusive proof, the complaint succeeded.

The claim for treatment of incisional hernia was repudiated because it was considered a complication of a tubal ligation operation performed prior to the policy inception. The complaint was dismissed.

The claim for diabetes and chronic renal failure was rejected as pre-existing based on hospital history, but the patient was admitted unconscious and relatives provided approximate details without conclusive proof from the insurer. The insurer was directed to settle.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The claim for cirrhosis of the liver was repudiated under an exclusion clause due to chronic alcoholism, which was supported by hospital records. The complaint was dismissed.
The claim was rejected due to late submission of documents after four months without a convincing reason. The complaint was dismissed.
The claim for incisional hernia was repudiated as it resulted from a previous LSCS operation done in 1983, which is excluded under policy terms. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Partial repudiation of a kidney transplant claim where the sum insured had been increased over time. Renal disease was diagnosed in 2002 after an initial increase, so the sum insured of Rs. 45,000 at that time was treated as applicable, and the insurer was directed to settle accordingly.

The claim for a hysterectomy was repudiated invoking the pre-existing disease exclusion, as documents and the discharge summary confirmed the ovarian cyst existed prior to the policy inception with the current insurer. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The claim for heart ailment and hemorrhage was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension. However, records showed the hemorrhage was due to an aneurysm rather than hypertension. The complaint succeeded and the insurer was directed to settle.

The claim for piles treatment performed by an Ayurvedic surgeon using K.S. Application under general anesthesia was repudiated. Since the policy did not explicitly exclude this specific treatment method, the insurer was directed to settle the claim.

The claim for radiotherapy was repudiated for late submission beyond 30 days because documents were lost during house shifting. As copies were acceptable, the complaint succeeded and the insurer was directed to settle.

The claim for oral chemotherapy for colon cancer was repudiated due to lack of traditional hospitalization. Because modern medical advancements utilize oral chemotherapy for pain relief and medical management without bed confinement, and the policy does not exclude it, the insurer was directed to settle.

A claim for coronary artery disease was partially repudiated by capping the sum insured at pre-increase levels due to pre-existing conditions. Since the policy was renewed continuously for 10 years without medical checks at the time of sum insured enhancement, the complaint succeeded for the full sum insured of Rs. 2.50 lacs.

insurer: IFFCO TOKYO General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The claim was repudiated on the allegation that the insured's name was missing from the hospital indoor patient register, implying fraud. Discharge cards and treatment papers proved actual admission, so the insurer was directed to settle.

The claim for hypertension treatment following an accidental fall was rejected. Due to a policy break of 16 days and a subsequent endorsement adding parents, the patient was within the initial 30-day lock-in period of the renewed policy, making the repudiation justified.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The claim for cataract surgery was repudiated as a congenital internal disease subject to a two-year waiting period under a policy incepted in 2007. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for acute low back prolapsed disc treatment was rejected on the grounds that it was an OPD case requiring no hospitalization. Since the patient was admitted on doctor's advice involving complete bed rest, traction, and injectables, the complaint succeeded.

A claim for BPH treatment was partially settled after a gap in renewal and a sum insured increase at age 68. The ombudsman ruled that the benefit should apply based on the original sum insured of Rs. 25,000 plus cumulative bonus, and directed settlement accordingly.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: In a telemarketing health insurance case, the complainant alleged disproportionate credit card deductions and unfair refund terms upon policy cancellation. The complaint was dismissed.

A cataract claim was repudiated under a two-year waiting period clause by treating the policy as fresh due to a one-day renewal delay. Since insurers have discretion to condone delays up to 7 days, the ombudsman ordered the insurer to treat it as a continuous policy and settle.
The claim was initially repudiated for a 42-day submission delay against the 7-day limit. Through forum mediation, the parties signed a joint resolution for a full and final settlement of Rs. 3,490.

Claim for myocardial infarction was repudiated due to an exclusion clause regarding hypertension. The policy had been incepted in 2000 and the insured was diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction linked to hypertension. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for stone removal operation was rejected for late submission of papers by 16 days. The forum found that post-hospitalization drainage and dressing continued subsequently, making the final submission of papers well within the time schedule. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Claim was repudiated based on pre-existing disease. Hospital documents proved the insured was previously hospitalized for acute hepatitis right before taking the policy, establishing the ailment as pre-existing. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for LRTI and bronchitis was initially repudiated based on medical history, but settled on 75% of the claim amount through mediation and mutual consent. Another tagged claim for genito-urinary system was dismissed due to the 2-year waiting period exclusion clause, and a third claim for perianal abscess was dismissed due to pre-existing disease rules after switching insurers.

Claim for vaginal hysterectomy due to focal adenomyosis was rejected as pre-existing. The forum noted that prior bleeding and pain were only symptoms and not a known disease prior to inception. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.
Claim for kidney donation surgery (donor nephrectomy) was rejected as not covered under the donor's policy unless charged against the recipient's policy limits. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing anemia of 10 years. The forum held that iron-deficiency anemia is not a disease and had no nexus with anterior wall ischemia. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Claim for carcinoma was repudiated alleging tobacco use caused the cancer. The hospital did not certify the cause, and duration of tobacco use was unproven. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Claim was rejected for delayed document submission. The forum calculated that the submission fell within the condonation period, making the repudiation unjustified. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.
Claim for heart disease treatment was repudiated due to an exclusion clause for pre-declared diabetes and ASD closure. Since exclusions were correctly recorded and informed, the case was dismissed.

Claim for cancer treatment was repudiated under a tobacco-chewing exclusion added recently to a long-standing policy. The forum ruled that continuous renewals protect against newly introduced exclusions without proof of causation. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.
Claim for ischemic heart disease was repudiated due to a long history of myocardial infarction and hypertension predating the policy inception. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for chest pain and high blood pressure was rejected because treatment was oral and hospitalization lasted under 24 hours. As the insurer failed to submit supporting notes or evidence, the rejection was deemed untenable and settlement was ordered.

Claim for accidental injury was partially paid. Upon review, the permissible schedule limit for arthroscopy was found to be slightly higher than paid, leaving a balance amount payable. The insurer was ordered to pay the balance.

Claim for pulmonary koch and typhoid was repudiated for fraud based on vague remarks. The insurer failed to point out specific discrepancies in bills or dates. The insurer was directed to settle the admissible amount.

Claim for umbilical hernia was rejected on the grounds that it was an incisional hernia caused by a past hysterectomy. The operating doctor certified it as an umbilical hernia unrelated to prior surgery. The complaint succeeded and settlement was ordered.

Claim for ventral hernia was repudiated because it resulted from a prior abdominal hysterectomy performed before the policy inception, constituting a pre-existing condition. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for mitral valve prolapse was rejected for pre-existing hypertension based on a letter the complainant allegedly signed under insistence. The insurer failed to prove when medication started, and settlement was ordered.

Claim for diabetes and bronchitis was rejected as pre-existing due to treating the policy as fresh after a port-over from another insurer without break. The insurer was aware of the prior continuous insurance history. Settlement was ordered.

Claim for oral chemotherapy for cancer was rejected due to lack of 24-hour hospitalization. The forum ruled that medical advancements allowing oral chemotherapy should bypass the strict 24-hour hospitalization requirement. The insurer was directed to settle.
Hospitalization claim for a depression episode was repudiated because treatment did not require inpatient admission and lacked qualified medical practitioner advice, as per policy terms.
Hospitalization expenses were settled for a lesser amount based on sum insured capping clauses. Examination showed the insurer correctly reimbursed according to policy limits.

Claim for hospitalization following a scooter fall resulting in a compression fracture was wrongly rejected as diagnostic. The ombudsman directed settlement as accidental hospitalization was essential.
Hospitalization claim was partially settled in accordance with the 20 percent sum insured limit. Payment was correct per policy terms, leading to dismissal of the complaint.
Claim for umbilical hernia mesh repair was rejected as pre-existing due to prior hysterectomy. Surgeon report confirmed the hernia was distinct, making repudiation unjustified.
Claim for accidental fall resulting in leg and wrist fractures was partially settled, disallowing Rs 10,030. Deductions under various heads matched policy schedules.
Claim for cyst surgeries was repudiated under a hysterectomy exclusion clause introduced without notice. The ombudsman set aside the rejection as cysts were distinct from hysterectomy.
Claim for acute renal failure and thrombophlebitis was wrongly rejected under pregnancy exclusions. Nephrologist confirmed the condition had no nexus with pregnancy.
Hospitalization claim for a cystic lesion of the mandible was rejected under dental treatment exclusion. Dental surgeon confirmed it was a non-dental surgical condition, rendering rejection improper.
Claim for ischemic heart disease was rejected because hospital records confirmed pre-existing coronary artery disease, hypertension, and diabetes predating policy inception.
Claim for non-hodgkins lymphoma brain treatment was rejected for 114 days delay in filing. Analysis showed multiple admission spells and filing within prescribed limits after fitness certificate.
Temporary total disability accident claim was rejected because inflammation occurred five months after an incident while performing normal duties, proving injury was not the direct cause.
Hospitalization claim was curtailed under room rent and nursing caps. Insurer applied updated policy terms capping expenses at one percent of sum insured.
Claim for para umbilical hernia surgery was rejected under pregnancy and childbirth exclusion due to a prior caesarean. Attending surgeon confirmed no relation to prior surgery.
Claim for endometriosis treatment was wrongfully rejected under pregnancy exclusions. Medical opinion established endometriosis has no relation to earlier caesarean delivery.
Claim for renal stone treatment was rejected due to a 12-day intimation delay exceeding the 7-day limit. Delay was condoned given remote residence and lack of policy terms notice.
Hospitalization claim for chronic laxative abuse, renal impairment, and malabsorption was validly rejected under policy exclusions relating to general debility and psychiatric disorders.
Claim for intervertebral disc backache treatment under a policy active since 1994 was rejected for pre-existing disease. Repudiation was set aside due to lack of documentary evidence.
Claim for foot abscess surgery was rejected on grounds that 24-hour hospitalization was unnecessary. Insurer's rejection was unjustified as the condition required surgery under general anesthesia.
Claim for acute acalculous cholecystitis with peritonitis was rejected under the gallbladder surgery exclusion clause. Insurer's reliance on policy terms was upheld.

Insured hospitalized for urogenital system disorder during the first year of the policy. Repudiation invoked pre-existing disease and specific waiting period exclusions for conditions like cataract, hernia, and urogenital disorders. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the case.

Claim for head injury with lip laceration requiring stitches was partially settled by the insurer under dental treatment limits. The ombudsman found the dental clause restriction harsh since the injury resulted from an accident requiring wound closure, and directed full settlement.

Claim for prostate cancer chemotherapy was repudiated on the grounds that oral chemotherapy counts as OPD and that treatment did not require hospitalization. Evidence confirmed chemotherapy was administered in clinic under doctor supervision, making repudiation unjustified. Insurer directed to settle.

Claim for accidental hairline fracture of the tibia was rejected based on clause 3.4. The ombudsman found the clause was misquoted as it actually referred to waiver of minimum hospitalization rather than exclusions, making the repudiation based on wrong interpretation. Insurer directed to settle.

Claim for surgery of rhinorrhea (DNS) was rejected because records proved the nasal condition existed for five years prior to policy inception, amounting to a pre-existing disease exclusion. The case was dismissed.

Claim rejected for alleged delay in 24-hour intimation and 15-day claim submission. The insurer failed to prove late intimation, and post-discharge prescription medication extended recovery. Considering a clean prior claim history, the marginal delay was condoned and full settlement ordered.

Claim of Rs. 68,329 for a seizure episode was rejected on grounds of pre-existing polio and hemiparesis. The ombudsman noted hemiparesis is a bodily condition rather than a distinct disease and the seizure was acute, making repudiation unjustified. Settlement was ordered.

Claim for abdominal pain and hysterectomy expenses was left unsettled without requesting requirements or replying to the insured for a long time, on allegations of late submission. The insurer was directed to settle the claim.

Claim repudiated for late submission under clause 5.4 where the complainant lacked proof of acknowledgement of receipt by the TPA. Although the insurer was willing to condone delay upon receipt of original papers, lack of submission proof justified the initial rejection, and the case was disposed.

Claim for severe backache diagnosed as disc annular tear and root compression via MRI was rejected on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. The ombudsman held that treating surgeon's opinion overrides panel doctor's view, making repudiation unjustified and ordering settlement.

Claim for chronic kidney disease stage-5 evaluated for transplant was repudiated under genetic disorder exclusion. The ombudsman noted no genetic abnormality like Alports syndrome was present, and kidney evaluation/transplant is not excluded. Repudiation was set aside.

Claim for cataract surgery and ventral hernia was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.3. There was a one-month break in policy renewal, making waiting period and specific disease exclusions applicable. The insurer's repudiation was upheld and the case dismissed.

Claim for accidental injury was partially settled because certain injury components were excluded under policy terms. The ombudsman confirmed the insurer had already settled beyond terms correctly, and dismissed the complaint.
Claim was repudiated due to a 28-day submission delay against the 7-day limit. The forum noted the delay was not inordinate given reasons provided, and the insurer agreed to settle through mediation.

Claim was partially settled based on sum insured capping rules under various heads. Calculations were largely correct except for a wrongful deduction of Rs. 450 under inward investigation charges, which the insurer was directed to pay.

Claim repudiated because indoor hospital case papers were not provided and appeared overwritten and manipulated. Analysis confirmed lodgment infirmities justified the repudiation, and the case was dismissed.

Claim for infective hepatitis with jaundice amounting to Rs. 12,777 was rejected for non-submission of whole abdomen USG plates and nursing home registration number. The ombudsman ruled that the disease is clinically evident from medical certificates, making USG plates unnecessary, and ordered full payment.

Claim for heart disease treatment costing Rs. 31,195 was cut down to Rs. 8,129 based on a 70% sum insured restriction clause for major angioplasty surgeries. The policy copy provided to the complainant lacked this clause, and neither claim involved an angioplasty. The insurer was ordered to pay the balance of Rs. 22,524.

Reimbursement claim of Rs. 18,355 for sigmoid colon symptoms was disapproved on the ground that the prior year's sum insured was exhausted. The ombudsman noted this was a fresh hospitalization unrelated to prior surgeries, and directed settlement of Rs. 18,093 as payable from bills.

Hospitalization claim of Rs. 30,269 was rejected for want of 2004 claim settlement data concerning a prior heart attack. The ombudsman noted the policy was continuously renewed since 2001 and past data was irrelevant and not under complainant's control. Insurer directed to pay Rs. 29,646 after standard deductibles.

Insured hospitalized for Ischaemic Heart Disease and underwent angioplasty. Claim repudiated for pre-existing heart disorder and alleged pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman noted lack of evidence for prior hypertension or diabetes and allowed the claim.

Complainant hospitalized for heart surgery. Insurer repudiated claim alleging pre-existing hypertension for 7-8 years and non-disclosure. Ombudsman found hospital records ambiguous and insurer failed to produce proposal form, setting aside the repudiation.

Complainant underwent surgery for hernia. Claim denied citing pre-existing illness and first-year exclusion. Ombudsman noted continuous prior health insurance policies since 2005 exempted him from the first-year exclusion and insurer produced no proof of pre-existence.

Renewal premium cheque dishonoured for insufficient funds, leading to policy cancellation. A fresh policy was issued after receiving cash later. Insured suffered heart disease shortly after. Claim rejected due to 30-day waiting period on fresh policy. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

Hospitalized for severe nasal bleeding. Insurer initially sanctioned cashless, then cancelled policies retrospectively alleging non-disclosure and fake claims. Ombudsman found policy was in force during hospitalisation and cancellation notice was sent post-claim, ordering payment.

Wife hospitalized for 15 days. Insurer paid treatment expenses but denied recovery benefit of Rs. 10,000 on grounds that oral medicines did not require prolonged hospital stay. Ombudsman noted policy had no such restriction and allowed the recovery benefit.

Wife hospitalized for uterine fibroid. Claim of Rs. 31,328 partly paid, deducting administrative and service charges. Insurer conceded during hearing that part of the deducted amount was payable, and Ombudsman directed full settlement of admissible balance.
Wife of complainant operated for cataract incurring Rs. 12,509; insurer settled for Rs. 10,000. Ombudsman directed insurer to review and consider the claim afresh.
Wife admitted to clinic; claim rejected on ground of pre-existing ailment. Ombudsman found insufficient grounds for pre-existence and allowed the complaint.

Complainant underwent bypass surgery during policy period. Claim repudiated for pre-existing disease. Insurer failed to produce the proposal form to establish pre-existence; Ombudsman directed settlement.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co Ltd
facts: Hospitalised for chronic renal disorder under hospital cash plan. Claim repudiated for pre-existing disease. Ombudsman held insurer could not establish pre-existence and ordered payment of Rs. 9,000.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co Ltd
facts: Two-year health policy premium charged incorrectly via credit card. Premium refunded after protest, but policy start date was not amended. Ombudsman directed insurer to correct policy effective dates.

Spent Rs. 10,036 for outdoor eye treatment, rejected as outdoor treatment is excluded. Ombudsman noted complainant could have claimed hospital stay if admitted, and awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 4,000.

Hospitalised for chest pain and breathing problem; claim repudiated for pre-existing disease. Ombudsman noted diabetes was disclosed at inception and hypertension was not known, directing claim settlement.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Treated for pneumonia under hospital cash policy. Claim unsettled despite document submission. Insurer produced no investigation report or treating doctor statement to justify non-settlement; Ombudsman ordered settlement.

Wife treated for knee fracture after accident, claimed Rs. 75,450 but paid Rs. 29,028. Insurer absent at hearing. Ombudsman directed insurer to settle full amount or provide detailed reasons for lower settlement.
Wife hospitalized, claimed Rs. 1,65,496, settled for Rs. 1,20,000. Ombudsman found complaint lacked merit considering loading factor and settled amount, dismissing the case.
Partial settlement of mediclaim. Complaint dismissed under RPG Rule 1998 because a consumer dispute forum complaint was already filed for the same subject.
Heart ailment treatment claim repudiated on grounds of congenital internal disease outside policy scope. Ombudsman set aside repudiation and ordered claim settlement based on bills.

Hospitalized for uneasiness in the second year of policy. Claim delayed for two years without communication and recommended for repudiation due to reported hypertension. Ombudsman ruled hypertension is a state rather than a disease, noted discharge summary had no mention of it, and ordered payment.
Insured claimed Rs. 7404 for son's hospitalization. Insurer doubted bonafides because the hospital had been closed. Complaint dismissed.
Wife operated for hernia. Claim rejected as insurer claimed it was related to child birth 5 years ago under exclusion 4.12. Ombudsman held it was unrelated and allowed claim.
Claim for Rs. 31191 rejected because hospital stay was less than 24 hours under policy condition 2.6. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.
Claim rejected because treatment was taken in a hospital not on the insurer's approved list. Ombudsman held terms do not require panel hospitals and allowed the claim.
Claim of Rs. 42578 rejected on grounds of pre-existing diabetes since 1998. Discharge summary had no mention of diabetes history, so Ombudsman ruled in favor of complainant.
Claim of Rs. 2,74,662 for valve replacement rejected as congenital disease under exclusion 4.10. Ombudsman upheld dismissal.

Claim for pacemaker implantation rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman noted no proof of non-disclosure or that conditions necessitated a pacemaker, and allowed the complaint.
Post-hospitalization claim of Rs. 14,541 rejected for non-submission of bills despite opportunities. Ombudsman upheld dismissal.
Claim for EECP therapy rejected as non-invasive and not covered, and discharge summaries appeared manipulated to show hospitalization. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization claim for fever of Rs. 25,695 recovered by hospital from insured after insurer declined due to discharge summary noting 'known wheezier'. Rs. 15,000 awarded as ex-gratia.
Ayurvedic treatment claim rejected under exclusion for Shirodhara. Since Shirodhara was only part of the treatment, Rs. 10,000 awarded as ex-gratia.
Claim for high fever during pregnancy rejected due to maternity exclusion. Ombudsman found hospitalization was for fever, not maternity, awarding Rs. 3,000 as ex-gratia.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: CABG surgery claim rejected due to 20-year pre-existing diabetes contributing to heart condition. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: CABG claim for triple vessel disease within 120 days of policy rejected. Employer paid 1 lakh of the 2 lakh claim; Ombudsman awarded Rs. 50,000 as ex-gratia.

Claim of Rs. 48,785 for bilateral wide excision of fibrocystic breast disease rejected as pre-existing within 10 months of policy. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 25,000 ex-gratia due to lack of medical records proving prior onset.

insurer: The United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs. 1,82,815 for eye treatment rejected due to pre-existing age-related degenerative disorder dating back to 2004. Dismissed.
Claim for hysterectomy and hernia surgery in the first year rejected under specific 2-year waiting period exclusions. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for Rs. 23,188 for uterine fibroids rejected as admission was actually for MTP and family planning, which are excluded. Dismissed.
Claim of Rs. 2,61,591 for bypass surgery rejected because double vessel block existed since 1997 before taking policy in 2002. Dismissed.

Insured claimed Rs 70,574 for hysterectomy and appendectomy. Insurer restricted payment to 20% of sum insured under specific policy exclusion for hysterectomy during the first two years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for left ovarian cyst surgery rejected due to a 1994 cyst history. Insured had disclosed past surgeries in the 2000 proposal form and the insurer did not exclude it. Ombudsman held rejection untenable and awarded Rs 15,000 as ex-gratia.

Claim for osteoarthritis treatment via RFQMR procedure was rejected as an unproven outpatient procedure not recognized by the Medical Council of India. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Hospitalization claim for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and allergic bronchitis. Investigation and expert opinion confirmed pre-existing conditions. Complaint dismissed.

Two claims for hernia repairs in 2006 and 2008 were rejected. Insurer wrongly linked the 2006 hernia to maternity and treated the 2008 renewal as a fresh policy. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage and held rejections unjustified, ordering partial relief.
Claim for hernia surgery rejected on grounds of pre-existing swelling since 1995. Insurer failed to produce clinching documentary evidence. Ombudsman awarded Rs 12,000 as ex-gratia.
Claim for hernia surgery rejected on grounds of pre-existing swelling since 1995. Insurer failed to produce clinching documentary evidence. Ombudsman awarded Rs 12,000 as ex-gratia.
Claim for renal calculi removal rejected as pre-existing due to stone size. Insurer lacked clinching evidence of prior existence. Ombudsman awarded Rs 30,000 as ex-gratia.
Ayurvedic treatment claim rejected because the clinic did not qualify as a hospital and the treatment was an exclusion. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs 8,000.
Claim for Arnald Chiari Malformation surgery rejected as a congenital internal illness under permanent exclusion 3.4(iii). Expert opinion confirmed congenital etiology. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for intra-ocular contact lens implantation to treat myopia and astigmatism rejected under cosmetic/aesthetic treatment exclusion. No medical complication made surgery necessary. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for heart block surgery partially rejected due to pre-existing hypertension. Insurer failed to prove hypertension caused the heart disease. Ombudsman awarded Rs 50,000 as ex-gratia.
Claim for CABG surgery rejected because renewal had a 38-day break, leading the insurer to treat it as a fresh policy subject to pre-existing disease exclusions. Complaint dismissed.

Insurer limited settlement for acute myeloid leukemia treatment to previous sum insured because the condition was pre-existing before the sum insured was enhanced. Ombudsman awarded Rs 25,000 as ex-gratia.
Claim for incisional hernia rejected as a complication of an undisclosed prior laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 2000. Treating doctor disowned the revised discharge summary. Complaint dismissed.

Insurer restricted claims for late husband's multiple ailments due to pre-existing diabetes and enhanced sum insured limits. Ombudsman noted distinct new diagnoses like tubercular Cauda Equina Lesion and awarded Rs 25,000 as ex-gratia.

Ayurvedic treatment claim rejected because treatment was not taken at a government hospital and fell under general exclusions. Ombudsman held private medical colleges are eligible and awarded Rs 25,000 as ex-gratia.

Claim for pulmonary embolism rejected because hospitalization occurred within 30 days of policy inception, which is excluded for non-accidental conditions. Rejection upheld, but full premium refunded.
Claim for chest pain and cardiac treatment rejected due to pre-existing heart ailment, diabetes, and hypertension dating prior to policy inception in 2005. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for high BP and chest pain rejected on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary and due to pre-existing disease. Ombudsman ruled treating doctor's judgment is key and awarded Rs 30,000 as ex-gratia.

Insured underwent cataract surgery and claimed Rs.49,000 for an advanced multifocal lens. Insurer restricted the claim to Rs.14,000 for an ordinary lens. The Ombudsman awarded an additional Rs.15,000 as ex-gratia since the other eye already had a similar advanced lens.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's hospitalization and subsequent claims for multiple chronic conditions like coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, and diabetes were rejected by the insurer under the pre-existing disease exclusion clause. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection due to established adverse medical history.

Claim for Mitral Valve Prolapse Syndrome was partly rejected due to non-submission of prescriptions for ECG tests and medicines exceeding the 60-day post-hospitalisation limit. The Ombudsman found no service deficiency by the insurer and dismissed the complaint.

Insured underwent Lasik surgery for myopia correction in both eyes. Insurer rejected the claim under the policy exclusion. The Ombudsman noted that Lasik is permitted as a therapeutic necessity if correction is -7 or above, which applied to only one eye. An ex-gratia amount of Rs.15,000 was awarded.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent angiogram and PTCA stenting. Cashless facility was withdrawn and claim rejected due to hospital discharge summary mentioning hypertension since 30 years, which the insured claimed was a recording error. The Ombudsman granted benefit of doubt regarding hypertension and awarded Rs.30,000 as ex-gratia.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for severe vertigo, vomiting, and giddiness, revealing mastoiditis on a scan. The TPA repudiated the claim stating no active line of treatment was carried out. The Ombudsman ruled that medication was administered to subside symptoms and directed the insurer to process and settle the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Father of the complainant was hospitalized for chest pain and heart failure. Insurer partly settled only the angiogram expenses, treating the rest as non-payable. The Ombudsman held that the extended hospitalization for stabilization constitutes valid hospitalisation expenses and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Insured underwent aortic valve replacement and the claim was rejected on grounds of pre-existing aortic valve stenosis. As neither party conclusively proved the exact onset date of the disease, the Ombudsman awarded Rs.25,000 as ex-gratia.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent treatment for coronary artery disease. Insurer restricted payment to the original sum insured before enhancement, treating the enhanced sum as a fresh insurance. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's restriction to the pre-enhanced limit and dismissed the complaint.

Insured claimed Rs.1,51,357 for coronary angioplasty after enhancing sum insured from Rs.1,00,000 to Rs.2,00,000. Insurer paid only Rs.1,00,000 applying previous year limits and room rent capping. The Ombudsman held the insurer could not prove the heart ailment pre-dated the sum enhancement and awarded an additional Rs.19,050 after expense capping.

Insured was hospitalized for jaundice and hepatitis B and C. Insurer paid only 50% of the claim, arguing complications from past MVR treatment and pre-existing heart disease. The Ombudsman found no correlation and directed the insurer to pay the remaining 50% of the claim amount.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insured's wife was admitted for planned sinus surgery which was postponed due to low TLC count. Insurer repudiated the claim under congenital exclusion for deviated nasal septum (DNS). The Ombudsman ruled that DNS is not necessarily congenital and could result from trauma, directing the insurer to pay Rs.9,908.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insured underwent bypass surgery within months of taking the policy. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, and depression. The complainant argued clear pre-policy medical diagnostic reports showed no such conditions, and delay in submission was due to a hospital management dispute.
Insured lodged a claim for Rs.42,640 which was rejected by the insurer. The complainant approached the Ombudsman citing favorable consumer court precedents.

Insured was diagnosed with sleep apnea syndrome and purchased a CPAP machine for Rs.42,640. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.16 excluding CPAP machines. The Ombudsman found the revised clause was not applicable to the active policy version and awarded the full claim amount.

Insured claimed reimbursement for facial injuries after falling from stairs. The surveyor concluded the claim was fake after the insured allegedly failed to respond or show injury marks. The Ombudsman noted a violation of natural justice as no proper hearing was given and directed the insurer to dispose of the claim properly.

Insured was admitted for one day for investigations regarding nocturnal seizures and osteoporosis. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.10 for lack of active treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection as discharge records showed no active medical treatment during the brief hospital stay.

Insured underwent Cytotron treatment for osteoarthritis of both knees without overnight hospitalization. Insurer rejected the claim of Rs.1 lakh solely on the ground of non-hospitalization. The complainant cited favorable Ombudsman rulings from other centers treating advanced daycare therapies equivalently.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for abnormal movement of the upper arm and diagnosed with acid peptic disease and anxiety neurosis. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.10 stating treatment could be done on an OPD basis with only investigations performed. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Insured was hospitalized and diagnosed with alcoholic pancreatitis. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.8 disallowing expenses related to alcohol consumption. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as the complainant failed to prove the hospital records were falsified.

Insured died of multi-organ failure. Claim repudiated as pre-existing due to hypertension and CABG. Policy was continuous since 1986 despite a 5-day renewal gap caused by the insurer. Repudiation set aside, claim ordered to be paid.

Insured's daughter treated for multiple viral warts via electrocautery. Claim repudiated as pre-existing based on a prior prescription within policy period. No evidence of pre-existing condition prior to policy inception. Repudiation set aside, insurer directed to settle.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for Avascular Necrosis of right femoral head, a complication of a trochanteric fracture sustained before policy inception. Claim repudiated under policy exclusion clause. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured treated for Irritable Bowel Syndrome. Claim repudiated alleging no active treatment required hospitalization and treatment for depression was excluded. Ombudsman found active hospital treatment was provided and depression was not psychiatric. Insurer directed to pay Rs.3,000 with interest and cost.

Insured treated for CAD. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing acute coronary syndrome from 1998. Ombudsman noted that continuous policy renewals since 2003 provided a claim-free period exceeding 3 years, waiving the pre-existing exclusion. Insurer ordered to pay sum assured of Rs.50,000 with interest and cost.

Insured hospitalized for back pain and underwent an MRI scan. Claim repudiated as admission was solely for diagnostic evaluation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for myocardial infarction a day after sum assured was enhanced. TPA restricted claim to pre-revised sum assured. Ombudsman held insured eligible for enhanced sum assured subject to policy expense caps, awarding Rs.1,05,150 with interest and cost.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured treated for nasal bleeding and growth removal. Claim repudiated as pre-existing based on a vague expert opinion. Ombudsman preferred treating doctor's view that symptoms could develop within policy period. Insurer ordered to pay sum assured of Rs.1,00,000 with interest and cost.

Claim for hysterectomy expenses restricted to 20% of sum assured under revised policy terms. Complainant argued for higher cap without 'whichever is less' clause. Ombudsman held insurer's liability correctly restricted to 20% and dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for hysterectomy. Claim repudiated under two-year waiting period exclusion clause. Complainant cited previous coverage with another insurer, but current policy terms counted inception only from the current insurer. Complaint dismissed.

Insured hospitalized for back pain and discharged the next day. Claim repudiated as admission was solely for investigation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

Wife underwent fibroid surgery. Claim repudiated alleging policy break made surgery fall in the first policy year. Evidence showed renewal cheque was received before expiry. Ombudsman held policy was continuous and awarded Rs.52,526 with interest and cost.

Claim for hysterectomy expenses restricted to 20% of sum assured under revised policy terms. Complainant claimed lack of awareness regarding unilateral changes. Ombudsman noted new policy conditions applied and dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for urge incontinence. Claim repudiated as admission was for evaluation and diagnostic tests without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured treated for viral fever with IV injections. Claim repudiated on grounds treatment could be taken on outpatient basis. Treating certificate confirmed necessity of hospital admission for IV therapy. Insurer ordered to pay Rs.1,478 with interest and cost.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for Ischemic Heart Disease. Claim repudiated as pre-existing diabetes excluded coverage for heart conditions. Ombudsman found blood sugar records confirmed prior diabetes and dismissed the complaint.
Insured hospitalized for hearing loss and underwent MRI and audiological tests. Claim repudiated as admission was strictly for evaluation without active treatment. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized and subsequently expired due to Wegners Granulomatosis with CNS. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing illness dating back to 2005 and polyarthritis since 2002. Ombudsman upheld repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

Insured treated for Chronic Suppurative Otitis Media (CSOM). Claim repudiated as pre-existing disease based on hospital records showing ear discharge symptoms existed for a year prior to policy inception. Complaint dismissed.

Insured's son hospitalized for constipation after ayurvedic treatment failed. Claim repudiated as admission was solely for investigation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

Insured claimed hospital expenses for a disease contracted during the previous policy year, seeking payment from the subsequent renewed policy's sum assured. Insurer rejected this, stating claims must be paid out of the sum assured active when the illness was contracted. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for knee pain, effusion, and aspiration. Insurer repudiated the claim stating treatment could be done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman found hospitalization reasonably required due to painful procedures like aspiration and physiotherapy, directing payment of Rs.1,150 with interest and costs.

Claim for laparoscopic myomectomy for uterine fibroid was repudiated because the policy was treated as a fresh inception due to a break, and genitourinary system treatments are excluded for the first two years. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured made three claims. The insurer settled the first two after delays and disallowed an X-ray deduction and diabetes medicine cost without proof of pre-existence. The third claim was rejected for lack of active treatment, but hospital records proved active medicine purchases on admission. The Ombudsman awarded Rs.9,295 with interest and costs, adjusting prior payments.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent bypass surgery and claimed expenses. Insurer allowed only pre-enhancement sum assured, claiming he was a heart patient at enhancement. Treating doctors confirmed risk factors did not mean established CAD at enhancement. The Ombudsman ruled the exclusion did not apply and awarded the enhanced sum assured of Rs.25,000 with interest and costs.

Claim for idiopathic PAH was repudiated as pre-existing based on a medical history of dyspnoea for 2.5 years. The Ombudsman noted dyspnoea was only a symptom occurring on exertion and gave the insured the benefit of doubt regarding timing, awarding the claimed amount of Rs.19,713 with interest and costs.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's claim for ayurvedic treatment at a private hospital was repudiated because a revised policy condition restricted ayurvedic coverage to government hospitals. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as the specific policy exclusion applied.

Vehicle package policy claim dispute over total loss versus salvage settlement. The insured argued consent was signed while bedridden. The Ombudsman directed payment of the loss assessed after deducting the value of wreck parts not entrusted with the insurer, with interest.

Insured underwent hip surgery and claimed expenses. TPA restricted payment to pre-renewal sum assured and disallowed dual hospital admissions. The Ombudsman held that the secondary hospital admission was at the instance of the primary hospital and the enhanced sum assured applied since the insurer forced the upgrade, awarding a balance of Rs.17,370 with interest and costs.

Claim was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was merely for investigation and lacked active treatment. Hospital records confirmed tests for suspected Crohn’s disease without active treatment. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for urinary calculus treatment was repudiated for lack of immediate notice to the TPA. The Ombudsman condoned the delay given the insured's severe illness and lack of assistance at home, awarding the claimed amount of Rs.4,853 with interest and costs.

Dental flap surgery claims for chronic periodontitis were partly rejected as cosmetic or OPD treatment. The Ombudsman found flap surgery was for an illness condition rather than cosmetic and allowed the claim for the husband, while upholding the rejection for the wife's observation stay. Awarded Rs.6,681 with interest and costs.

Claim for heart disease treatment was repudiated because hospital records mentioned the insured was hypertensive for 8 years. The Ombudsman noted hypertension was a risk factor, not a pre-existing disease for the cardiac treatment received, and awarded the full sum assured of Rs.25,000 with interest and costs.

Insured's daughter was hospitalized, and the insurer reimbursed room and boarding expenses up to the policy cap of 1% of the sum assured per day. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as the insurer had paid the maximum amount eligible under policy conditions.

Claim for excision of biopsy under local anesthesia was repudiated by TPA as an OPD procedure in lieu of hospitalization. Since the insurer directed the TPA to settle as per the doctor's original admission advice, the Ombudsman directed immediate settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for traumatic cataract surgery following an injury was repudiated under first-year cataract exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman ruled that traumatic cataract resulting from an injury is distinct from natural age-related cataract per se and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Delay in settling hospitalization claim due to requests for previous medical records. As the complainant's grievance was satisfactorily redressed during proceedings, no further intervention was required.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for cataract surgery was repudiated invoking a two-year waiting period, treating the policy as fresh due to previous insurer changes. The Ombudsman held that continuous coverage across insurers must be recognized and directed the insurer to pay the claim.

Claim for coronary angiogram and treatment of triple vessel coronary artery disease was delayed and repudiated under untenable internal clauses. The Ombudsman ruled that diagnostics confirming diagnosis and conservative treatment warranted payment, directing the insurer to settle.

Claim for surgery of an infected sebaceous cyst in the arm was repudiated under a first-year exclusion clause for benign growths. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as cysts fall under excluded benign growths during the initial policy period.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for laparoscopic myomectomy for fibroid uterus was repudiated as pre-existing. Ombudsman held that the insurer lacked irrefutable proof that the fibroid existed before policy inception and ordered payment.

Hospitalization claim for acute abdominal pain was rejected on the grounds that treatment was for investigation purposes only. Ombudsman noted that tests and conservative treatment were valid and ordered settlement.

Claim for menopausal bleeding and fibroid uterus was rejected citing pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of a parallel policy. Ombudsman held the policy was continuous and awarded a pro-rata amount.
Claim for epilepticus treatment was repudiated due to pre-existing condition and non-disclosure of prior surgical procedures. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation for suppression of material facts.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Abdominal pain hospitalization claim was rejected for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of previous uterine surgery. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation due to suppression of material facts.
Menorrhagia surgery claim was rejected as it fell within the first-year policy exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for glossectomy due to carcinoma of the tongue was rejected as pre-existing. Ombudsman found no irrefutable proof of pre-existence and directed the insurer to pay the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Dental surgery claim was rejected because the procedure did not require in-house treatment and bills were not from the hospital. Ombudsman gave the complainant benefit of doubt and ordered payment.
Claim for neurological and leg pain hospitalization remained unpaid due to delay and lack of response from the insurer. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle and pay.

Mediclaim was partly settled by disallowing physiotherapy, medicines without prescription, and investigations referred by a homeopathic doctor. Ombudsman directed the insurer to verify and pay admissible amounts.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Angioplasty claim was rejected because it occurred four days after policy inception, with a policy break preventing continuity. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Surgery claim was rejected under initial exclusion periods due to a 4-day policy renewal gap. Ombudsman condoned the short delay, treated the policy as continuous, and ordered settlement.
Hospitalization claim for abdominal distension was rejected due to a policy gap and pre-existing ailments. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to non-disclosure of previous health problems.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Chest pain hospitalization claim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman held that hypertension and symptoms are not proof of pre-existing disease and ordered payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery reimbursement was partly settled by disallowing surgeon fees. Ombudsman awarded the disallowed amount as ex-gratia to meet ends of justice.
Elbow surgery claim was delayed indefinitely due to administrative failures in updating policy numbers. Ombudsman ordered settlement with penal interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Amputation claim was partly disallowed due to classification as intermediate surgery rather than major, and prosthetic finger costs were denied. Ombudsman ordered reimbursement for major surgery expenses.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hysterectomy claim was partially repudiated due to a policy break making it a fresh policy subject to a 2-year exclusion. Ombudsman awarded ex-gratia due to misleading communication from the insurer.
Osteoarthritis treatment claim was rejected because the facility did not qualify as a hospital. Ombudsman awarded ex-gratia due to TPA negligence in responding to prior queries.
Hernia surgery claim was repudiated as a pre-existing condition because the patient was treated for bilateral hernia years earlier. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Insured underwent hospitalization for Left MCA Acute Infarct. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing bypass surgery and associated complications under clause 4.1. The Ombudsman noted the insured's advanced age and long policy history, granting an ex-gratia payment of Rs.30,000.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for severe abdominal pain and later expired due to acute pancreatitis sepsis related multi-organ failure. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.4.6 for chronic alcoholism. The Ombudsman held that although alcoholism was noted, the current treatment was not directly related, and allowed 80 percent of admissible expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured filed a claim for Right Eye Vitreous Hemorrhage surgery. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension based on an OPD letter. The Ombudsman observed that the policy had continued since 1999 with previous claims settled for cataract, making the repudiation untenable.

Complainant sought the balance of a hospitalization claim after the TPA lost original documents and made deductions for bulk medicines and miscellaneous fees. The Ombudsman ordered payment of the deducted amount plus 8% simple interest due to inordinate delay by the insurer.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for Bilateral Maxillary and Ethmoidal Sinusitis. The insurer repudiated the claim under the two-year exclusion clause for sinus and nasal polyp conditions. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the hospitalization occurred within the initial two-year exclusion period.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for IHD, osteoarthritis, electrolyte imbalance, and UTI. The insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.1 for pre-existing ailments. The Ombudsman set aside total rejection and awarded 80% of expenses considering the long policy history and advanced age.

Insured underwent percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy for severe mitral stenosis and rheumatic heart disease. The insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based on a cardiologist's opinion. The Ombudsman noted lack of documentary proof of prior treatment and awarded 75% of the claim on an ex-gratia basis.

Insured claimed hospitalization expenses for angina pectoris and disputed partial cashless settlement by the insurer. The Ombudsman verified calculations under policy limits for room rent, doctor fees, and other charges, finding only a minor balance of Rs. 200 due.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was hospitalized for a renal mass and claimed under an enhanced sum insured. The insurer restricted the claim to the previous lower sum insured under clause 6.3 because the ailment was contracted during the previous policy period. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim was repudiated because the treatment involving injections for chronic HBV infection did not strictly require hospitalization and could be managed on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for treatment of frequent loss of consciousness was repudiated on the grounds that hospitalization was mainly for diagnostic purposes which could be carried out on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for ayurvedic treatments like massage, steam bath, and Sirodhara was repudiated under policy exclusion 4.24, which excludes specific ayurvedic procedures. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for coronary artery disease hospitalization was repudiated for pre-existing disease since hospital papers indicated illness duration of 6 to 10 months prior to hospitalization, predating the policy inception. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim was repudiated due to late submission of papers beyond the 30-day limit stipulated in policy condition 5.4. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for incisional and umbilical hernia surgery was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause due to a past acid peptic disease operation 30 years prior. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation, noting no medical nexus, and directed payment of the claim.

Claim for upper renal stone treatment was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing kidney ailments dating back to 1983. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the current condition was linked to long-standing history.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Personal accident claim was repudiated because post-mortem was not conducted and medical treatment was discontinued before death. The Ombudsman held that circumstantial evidence and hospital records were sufficient to prove accidental death and directed full payment.
Claim for chronic suppurative otitis media was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause. Through mediation by the Ombudsman, both parties agreed to a mutual settlement amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer paid 75% of the claim, deducting 25% for misstatement of age in the proposal form (stating 66 instead of 68 years). The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on material non-disclosure rules.

Insurer partially paid a cataract surgery claim, applying a sub-limit. The Ombudsman found the restriction unjustified based on policy continuation terms and directed the insurer to pay the deducted amount.

Insured claimed hospital cash benefit for hospitalization. Insurer repudiated claiming false hospitalization and misrepresentation without evidence. Complainant had received partial reimbursement from another insurer and sought the difference. Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay the remaining balance of Rs. 7,548.

Complainant contested short payment of claim. Insurer based payment on old sum insured before an increase at renewal. Treatment history showed a lump present prior to the increase. Insurer denied the enhanced portion under policy clauses for increased sum insured acting as a fresh insurance, which the Ombudsman upheld.

Claim was repudiated under clauses excluding diagnostic tests not incidental to a positive condition and psychiatric disorders. Investigation revealed the patient suffered from metabolic dementia due to vitamin B-12 deficiency, not a psychiatric disorder. Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay Rs. 16,775.

A group mediclaim reimbursement claim for accidental injury was rejected because hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours, violating policy clause requiring a minimum 24-hour stay except for specific treatments. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim was repudiated for pre-existing mediastinal mass and non-disclosure in the proposal form. Hospital records and chest X-rays proved the condition existed prior to inception and was not disclosed. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for angioplasty was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing heart disease. The insured argued previous chest pain was muscular and unrelated. Insurer failed to produce concrete evidence of pre-existing cardiac disease. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay Rs. 1,31,770 in full and final settlement.

Claim for acute myocardial infarction, CAD, hypertension, and diabetes was repudiated due to non-disclosure of hypertension and diabetes in the proposal form. Although the policy had continuity from a prior insurer, the non-disclosure of known risk factors was established, and the rejection was upheld.

Treatment for ureteric calculus was rejected under a policy clause excluding genito-urinary system treatments during the first two years of the policy. Since the claim occurred in the second policy year, the insurer's repudiation was upheld.

Claim for hysterectomy and multiple independent procedures including cystectomy and adhesiolysis was partially settled by limiting reimbursement to 20% of the sum insured under a golden policy. Ombudsman found independent procedures like cystectomy were unjustly denied and ordered payment of 50% of the claimed amount of Rs. 74,242.

Claim was repudiated solely due to a one-day delay in intimation beyond the 24-hour policy requirement. Ombudsman held that a one-day delay was not exorbitantly high and unjustified for total rejection, directing the insurer to pay the claim.

Claim for scar endometriosis and pelvic adhesion following a previous caesarean section was repudiated under pregnancy exclusion clauses and pre-existing condition rules. Medical confirmation established the condition stemmed from prior LSCS, so the insurer's rejection was upheld.

Cataract surgery expenses were rejected under a policy clause imposing a two-year waiting period for cataract treatments. The insured had reduced sum insured at renewal, which reset conditions like a fresh policy, making the claim during the second year ineligible. Rejection upheld.

Claim for acute fever and thrombocytopenia was repudiated on grounds of fraud and false statements based on an investigation report indicating no actual hospitalization. Ombudsman noted that proving fraud requires elaborate legal procedures beyond the forum's jurisdiction, and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for chest pain hospitalization was repudiated on the grounds that hospital confinement was not required as diagnostic tests revealed no positive disease or active treatment. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for brain cancer treatment via chemotherapy and radiotherapy was partially paid by capping it at Rs. 2 lakhs under a clause meant for cancer surgery. Ombudsman ruled that the clause did not apply to non-surgical treatments like chemotherapy and ordered payment of the remaining Rs. 49,568.

Complainant contested partial settlement after deductions for service charges and registration fees, realizing an advance deposit had been erroneously added. The complainant withdrew the complaint, requiring no formal award.

Cataract surgery claim was repudiated under an exclusion clause requiring a two-year waiting period. Since surgery occurred in the second year of the policy inception, the insurer's rejection was justified and upheld.

Claim for orthopedic trauma surgery was partially settled after deductions. Insurer erroneously clubbed nursing care charges with room rent. Ombudsman found room charges were within eligible limits and directed payment of an additional Rs. 38,804.

Claim was repudiated for late hospitalization intimation and late document submission. Records showed post-hospitalization treatment lasted 45 days and documents were submitted within the permitted timeframe after completion. Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay the claim.

Claim for acute pancreatitis was repudiated under a clause excluding illnesses caused by the use of alcohol. Hospital records confirmed the patient's history of alcohol use, justifying the insurer's rejection.
