The insurer repudiated a mediclaim for giddiness and headache invoking a one-year waiting period clause. Since the policy incepted years prior and the insurer produced no evidence to justify repudiation, the ombudsman ordered full payment.

Three claims for hospitalizations were delayed indefinitely without reason while being referred to a regional office. Finding deficiency in service, the ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the total amount of all three claims.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A hernia surgery claim was partially settled by deducting room rent and surgeon charges based on revised policy caps. The ombudsman noted dual standards were applied and ordered the balance amount paid.

Claims for accident hospitalization were repudiated due to a 69-day delay in submission caused by family trauma and a wedding. The ombudsman directed the insurer to pay 75 percent on a non-standard basis.
A fever hospitalization claim was rejected solely due to a 10-day delay during Diwali festivals. Finding no other infirmity, the ombudsman advised payment of the full claim amount.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for cardiac treatment was closed because additional requested documents were not submitted. The ombudsman found existing case papers sufficient and ordered full settlement.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for soft tissue sarcoma surgery was repudiated as a pre-existing disease based on CT scan lesion size. Finding no prior medical consultations before policy inception, the ombudsman allowed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Ureteric stone surgery claims were rejected under a two-year waiting period clause of a revised policy. Since new terms were never communicated at renewal, the ombudsman set aside the rejection and ordered payment.
Car accident hospitalization claims were repudiated for late submission by 69 days due to family trauma. The ombudsman directed the insurer to review and pay 75 percent on a non-standard basis.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A mediclaim was partially paid after deducting room and surgeon fees exceeding one percent of the sum insured under revised rules. Because total expenses were within the old sum insured limit, the ombudsman ordered the balance paid.
A personal accident claim for temporary total disablement was disputed regarding duration. Both parties mutually agreed during the hearing to a settlement amount for 3.5 weeks plus medical expenses.

A claim for ovarian cyst surgery was partially paid due to a waiting period restriction on increased sum insured. During proceedings, the parties mutually agreed to a compromise sum including cumulative bonus.

A hysterectomy and allied surgeries claim was partially paid, limiting hysterectomy to 20 percent of the sum insured. Based on expert medical opinions, the ombudsman upheld the hysterectomy limit but ordered 50 percent payment for additional complex surgeries.

A claim for intestinal perforation following medical termination of pregnancy was repudiated under policy exclusions for pregnancy complications. Independent expert opinion confirmed the perforation resulted from an erroneous MTP, so the dismissal was upheld.

A post-hospitalization claim for tuberculosis was rejected for late submission beyond seven days. Noting that treatment extended longer and actual submission was within 14 days of completion, the ombudsman set aside the rejection.

Claims for unstable angina hospitalizations were repudiated as pre-existing conditions without supporting documents. The insurer failed to justify its action, so the ombudsman set aside the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A maternity delivery claim under a group mediclaim policy was rejected due to a nine-month waiting period. Medical certificates indicated a caesarean was performed early due to a bad obstetric history, constituting a medical emergency, prompting the ombudsman to allow the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery claims across policy years were partially settled by deducting nursing charges under restrictive room rent clauses. The surgeon clarified the charges were part of operation theatre fees, leading the ombudsman to order full payment.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for knee replacement due to osteoarthritis was repudiated because medical records showed pain lasting three years prior to policy inception. Finding the pre-existing disease exclusion justified, the ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

A claim for calculus cholecystitis surgery was rejected under a two-year waiting period clause. Because the policy was a fresh contract without continuous prior renewal with the insurer, the rejection was upheld.

Claim for hospitalization expenses was partially settled due to prolonged stay and deductions for room charges and doctor visits based on TPA opinion. The forum found the charges commensurate with treatment and directed the insurer to pay the full amount.

Claim was partially settled by invoking policy exclusion clause for increased sum insured regarding prolapse intervertebral disc during the first two years of the policy revision. The forum upheld the insurer's partial repudiation.
Claims for cataract and age-related eye ailments were repudiated because they occurred within the two-year waiting period from policy inception. The forum dismissed the complaint.

Hospitalization reimbursement was partially settled based on internal company guidelines restricting surgeon and anesthetist fees. Since these guidelines were not part of policy conditions or communicated to the insured, the forum ruled in favor of the complainant.

A cataract surgery claim was partially paid up to the original sum insured plus bonus, while the recently increased sum insured was excluded under a two-year waiting period clause. The forum dismissed the complaint.

Claim was partially settled after applying deductions and incorrectly citing a waiting period for hypertension, even though the patient was an 11-year-old child treated for adenoids and sinus. The insurer was directed to settle the balance.

Hospitalization claim was repudiated on the grounds of lack of active treatment, despite the insured undergoing split thickness skin grafting surgery. The forum found the repudiation unjustified and directed settlement.
Claim for knee joint replacement due to degenerative conditions was repudiated because it fell within the four-year waiting period specified in the policy. The forum dismissed the complaint.

Claim for bilateral breast abscess developed after childbirth was repudiated under pregnancy and childbirth exclusions. The forum noted the condition resulted from infection rather than pregnancy and ordered the claim to be settled.
Claim was repudiated because the surgery was performed under local anesthesia and did not require hospitalization exceeding 24 hours. The forum dismissed the complaint.

Claim for ureteric calculus treatment was repudiated under a two-year waiting period clause for genito-urinary system treatments during the second policy year. The forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for knee replacement was partially settled after applying new policy caps following a sum insured increase. Because revised terms were not communicated or consented to, the forum ruled the claim should be processed under the old sum insured limits.

Claim was repudiated due to a 78-day delay in submitting the discharge summary. Considering the complainant's critical condition from tuberculosis, the forum directed the insurer to consider the claim.

Claim for hysterectomy was partially settled in accordance with policy clauses restricting reimbursement to 20 percent of the sum insured for surgery and 10 percent for pre and post-hospitalization. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Cataract treatment claim was repudiated because it occurred during the second year of a fresh policy, triggering a two-year waiting period exclusion. The complaint was dismissed.
Claim for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy due to morbid obesity was repudiated under a specific policy exclusion for obesity treatments. The forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for vaginal hysterectomy was repudiated on grounds of a pre-existing disease, but the insurer failed to produce concrete documentary evidence. The forum directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Claim for micro laryngeal laser surgery was repudiated on the grounds that all laser surgeries are excluded. The forum found the insurer misconstrued the policy wording, which only applied to eye and ear treatments, and ordered claim settlement.
Claim was initially repudiated due to investigation discrepancies. Through forum mediation, both parties agreed to a full and final settlement amount.
Claim was repudiated because treatment was given on an OPD basis rather than requiring hospitalization, and claim papers were submitted over 60 days late. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant expressed dissatisfaction with the forum proceedings before the award was pronounced. The ombudsman advised the complainant to approach appropriate courts or other forums. Complaint disposed of without any order favoring either party.

Claim was repudiated due to late submission of papers by 45 days. The ombudsman noted that post-hospitalization expenses are reimbursable up to 60 days, and directed the insurer to pay the full claim.
Insurer rejected the claim on the ground that admission was for less than 24 hours. Documents proved hospital stay was for 10 days. The insurer was directed to pay the admissible claim amount.

Insurer repudiated health claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary for transient loss of consciousness. The ombudsman held that a prudent person would follow medical advice to admit, set aside the repudiation, and ordered payment of Rs 13,000.

Insurer repudiated claim for low back pain citing pre-existing disease for 20 years. Treating hospital clarified in writing that '20 years' was a clerical error. Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay the claim.
Claim for father's treatment was repudiated on the ground of a pre-existing ailment mentioned as 20 years. The hospital clarified it was 2 years. Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay Rs 39,866.

Claim was repudiated stating the ailment was not covered. A medical specialist opined that the patient received conservative treatment for gall bladder without surgery, making the policy exclusion inapplicable. Insurer was directed to pay.
Claim for Sub-mucous Fibrosis was repudiated as pre-existing. The ombudsman noted continuous policy renewal with the same company for four years and ordered payment within one month.

Claim for hypertension treatment was repudiated as pre-existing. Since discharge summary did not specify onset and the policy had been continuously renewed since 2004, the ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the claim.

Insurer failed to settle group mediclaim citing non-submission of documents. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim within 15 days based on documents submitted to the forum, subject to the complainant submitting copies to the insurer.

Insurer repudiated emergency surgery claim on grounds of late intimation. Ombudsman held that rejecting a claim where delay was explained violates natural justice, and ordered payment based on bills produced.

Insurer repudiated five separate claims under multiple policies alleging they were exaggerated, stage-managed, and fraudulent. The ombudsman found no documentary evidence supporting the fraud allegation and ordered full payment for all claims.
For septicemia hospitalization, the insurer's fraud allegation was unsubstantiated. Ombudsman awarded Rs 40,601 for medical expenses plus Rs 22,500 for daily cash benefits.
For acute gastroenteritis treatment, insurer failed to prove fraud. Ombudsman awarded Rs 17,300 for hospital bills, medicines, and daily cash benefits.

Claims for Ritika and Preeti Jain were repudiated for alleged fraud without substantiation. Ombudsman ordered payments of Rs 6,000 and Rs 26,812 respectively, totaling Rs 147,094 across all five family claims.
Conclusive order directing payment of Rs 147,094 for five combined claims within 15 days, failing which 9% simple interest applies.

TPA repudiated Juvenile Diabetes claim under revised policy clauses requiring a 2-year waiting period. Although previous policy had a 30-day waiting period, renewal under the revised all-India policy terms governed the contract.

Claim for malaria treatment was repudiated based on investigator findings of medical discrepancies and unverified bills. Ombudsman found the claim inflated rather than bogus, allowing 70% of the admissible claim amounting to Rs 15,789.

Claim for endometritis and fever was rejected on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary. Treating doctor certified admission was essential, and insurer failed to substantiate rejection. Ombudsman awarded full claim of Rs 8,683.

Claim was repudiated due to delayed written intimation and document submission. Ombudsman noted the insured was hospitalized alone and unable to intimate timely, ordering settlement at 70% of the admissible claim.

The insured's father underwent CABG surgery. The claim was closed for want of documents after cashless was denied for alleged pre-existing disease. The ombudsman noted documents were submitted late and directed processing upon proper document submission.

Claim under a hospital cash policy for breast cancer treatment was repudiated as pre-existing since it manifested within 1.5 years of policy inception. Furthermore, the complaint was time-barred under the Redressal of Public Grievances Rules.

Claim for enteric fever and hepatitis was rejected because investigation revealed fabricated medical documents, including a USG report of a male patient containing female organ details and forged pathologist signatures.

The insured's wife underwent pacemaker implantation for cardiac conditions. The claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion based on hospital records showing a long-standing history of diabetes and hypertension.

Claim for hospitalization due to missed abortion was rejected by the insurer under policy exclusion clause 4.12 relating to pregnancy, miscarriage, and abortion expenses. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for paroxysmal vertigo was rejected because hospitalization was primarily for evaluation and diagnostic purposes without active medical treatment during the stay, falling under policy exclusion 4.10.

Claim for coronary angiography was rejected under pre-existing disease clause 4.1 of the revised 2007 policy. Since previous heart claims occurred within the last four years, the pre-existing exclusion had not yet lapsed.

Claim for intestinal obstruction surgery due to adhesions was rejected under pre-existing clause 4.1, as the patient had previously undergone colon cancer surgery and chemotherapy prior to the policy inception.

Claim for acute gastroenteritis was repudiated and the policy cancelled on allegations of inflated medical store bills. Since the insurer failed to provide concrete evidence of fraud, the ombudsman ordered full payment of the claim and refunded forfeited premium.

Claim for CABG was repudiated on the assumption of pre-existing disease following a policy break. The ombudsman noted the break was due to the insurer's negligence and no documentary proof of pre-existing heart disease existed, ruling the claim payable.

Under a hospital cash policy, the insured claimed double daily benefits for ICU admission. The insurer paid the standard daily benefit but rejected the ICU enhancement as it was never opted for or covered under the certificate.

The TPA partially settled a renal stone treatment claim by making proportionate deductions for room rent and associated charges based on general ward entitlement limits under the 2007 mediclaim policy. The ombudsman upheld the deduction.

Claim for coronary angiography was repudiated based on a doctor's certificate alleging 25 years of diabetes. The discharge summary indicated 15 years of diabetes, which fell within the policy coverage period. The ombudsman allowed the claim.

Claim for Ayurvedic treatment taken in a private hospital was rejected under revised policy exclusions permitting only Government or Medical College hospital treatments. The ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

The insurer partly paid a CABG claim, denying the portion attributable to an enhanced sum insured on the grounds that the heart ailment was pre-existing at the time of sum insured enhancement. The ombudsman dismissed the complaint.
Surgery for eye asthenopia (vision correction to avoid glasses) was rejected as cosmetic/aesthetic treatment under policy exclusions. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for CABG was rejected for pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Since the insurer failed to provide clinching evidence that coronary artery disease existed at inception, an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 50,000 was awarded.

Claim for back pain treatment was rejected on the grounds that it could be managed on an OPD basis. Noting that hospitalization was based on the treating doctor's advice, the ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 10,000.

Claim for knee injury hospitalization following a fall was rejected because the condition allegedly did not warrant hospitalization. Finding the admission was on emergency medical advice, the ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 9,000.

Kidney stone removal claim was initially partly paid via cashless, but the full balance was subsequently settled by the insurer upon submission of revised bills and documents. Finding no deficiency in service, the complaint was dismissed.
Insured claimed for road accident injuries treated with naturopathy after five months delay without FIR or proof of accident circumstances.
Angiogram and CABG claims rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman awarded partial amount as ex-gratia.
Insurer deducted amounts from ovarian cyst surgery claim based on room rent and proportionate caps. Ombudsman awarded ex-gratia.
Toe surgery claim rejected for pre-existing disease due to unproven continuity from past group policies. Ombudsman allowed claim considering prior employer proof.
Claims for diabetic complications and cataract rejected for pre-existing disease. Cataract claim allowed for continuous policy years, others dismissed.
Cholesteatoma ear surgery claim rejected for pre-existing condition. Expert opinion showed exact onset was unknown; insurer lacked clinching evidence, so claim allowed.
Hospitalization for phobic anxiety and depression rejected under policy exclusion for psychiatric disorders. Complaint dismissed.
Reimbursement cheque for respiratory illness sent to old address despite unrecorded address change notices. Complaint dismissed as payment was eventually received.
Emergency appendicitis surgery claim rejected for pre-existing condition on a two-month-old policy. Insurer failed to prove pre-existing nature; claim allowed.
Ureteroscopy claim delayed due to confusion between TPAs and agent errors. Ombudsman ordered 50 percent ex-gratia settlement.
Balance for post-menopausal bleeding refused due to revised policy cap on specific ailments. Renewal notices properly notified insured; complaint dismissed.
Ovarian cancer claim rejected treating the policy as fresh after insurer switch. Insurer proved no pre-existing disease, but insured changed insurer voluntarily; ex-gratia awarded.
Hospitalization for chronic constipation rejected for lacking active treatment/hospitalization necessity. Ombudsman ruled hospitalization was justified after failed OPD treatments.
Knee osteoarthritis day care treatment using RFQMR rejected because the facility did not meet policy hospital definitions and procedure was not covered. Complaint dismissed.
Tibial osteoma surgery claim rejected under first-30-days exclusion based on flawed hospital notes. No clinching evidence of early contraction; claim allowed.
Stroke claim rejected for pre-existing diabetes and hypertension before 3 completion years. Ombudsman awarded ex-gratia amount.
Stroke claim rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension within waiting timeframe. Ex-gratia awarded balancing medical risk facts.
Cardiac hospitalization claim rejected due to a single-day renewal gap treating policy as fresh. Ombudsman condoned the minor 15-hour gap and allowed claim.
Facial cyst surgery claim rejected because it was billed as OPD. Ombudsman ruled it was de-facto one-day hospitalization in an operation theater and allowed claim.
Kidney stone treatment claim rejected for pre-existing condition based on historical stone passage mentions. Insured lacked prior knowledge; claim allowed.

A mountaineer fell into a crevasse and died during an expedition. The insurer rejected the claim stating death was not directly caused by external violent and visible bodily injury. The Ombudsman discussed the interpretation of accident and bodily injury.

The policyholder was treated for an ulcerated inflamed adenomatous polyp. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing based on discharge summary notes mentioning symptoms for two years, but the Ombudsman found no specific medical proof of pre-existing disease.
Mediclaim was approved for Rs 17613 by the TPA but not paid by the insurer's head office. The Ombudsman directed payment to be made.

Claim for hospitalization diagnosed with moderate depression was rejected on the grounds of being solely for investigation. The Ombudsman noted investigations were incidental to the treatment of depression and allowed the claim.

Claim for Avascular Necrosis of the hip was rejected because the patient had past steroid therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. The Ombudsman ruled that subsequent conditions caused by side effects of treatment for past illness do not invalidate the claim.

Claim was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization for severe headache and vomiting was only for investigation. The Ombudsman held that investigations and minor medication constitute valid treatment.
Approved mediclaim amount was delayed due to inaction by the TPA. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to make the payment.

Hospitalization claim for breathlessness was repudiated because the discharge summary mentioned alcoholic liver disease. The Ombudsman noted the policy was over 4 years old and the exclusion did not apply, ordering payment with interest.

Claim was rejected on the grounds of non-disclosure of pre-existing Coronary Artery Disease. The Ombudsman noted the actual treatment was for a neurological disorder (infarct in brain) and not CAD, hence allowing the claim.
Mediclaim for dengue fever was refused due to marginal delays in hospital intimation and claim submission. The Ombudsman condoned the delay and allowed the claim.

Claim for fever and breathlessness was repudiated on the ground that there was no active treatment and it was only for evaluation. The Ombudsman ruled that evaluation and medical management constitute active treatment.
Claim for cancer treatment was severely restricted by the TPA based on obsolete policy option limits. The Ombudsman reviewed the dispute regarding sum insured enhancements.
Claim was repudiated because it was submitted slightly beyond the 60-day limit from discharge. The Ombudsman noted ongoing post-hospitalization treatment and condoned the minor delay.

Personal accident claim payout was delayed because no nominee was mentioned in the policy and a legal heir certificate was required. The Ombudsman awarded interest for the period of delay attributable to the insurer.
Non-settlement of mediclaim submitted to TPA. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Partial payment was made for a skin infection hospitalization claim without providing reasons for the deduction. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to review the disallowance and pay interest for delayed settlement.

Claim was rejected because hospitalization occurred within one month of the renewal policy start date. The Ombudsman ruled that since the bank debited premium on time, the policy was a continuous renewal and the initial waiting period clause did not apply.
Eye operation claim was delayed due to alleged non-submission of documents. The Ombudsman found requisitions were substantially complied with and ordered finalization.
Hospitalization claim for accelerated hypertension was rejected on the grounds of being solely for investigation. The Ombudsman held that prescriptions and cardiac tests constituted active treatment.

Knee injury hospitalization claim was disallowed on the ground that treatment was only for investigation and could have been done via OPD. The Ombudsman ruled that emergency hospitalization and subsequent diagnostic investigations formed part of active treatment.

Insured was hospitalized for Generalized Anxiety Disorder with panic attack. Insurer rejected the claim under the psychiatric ailment exclusion clause. Ombudsman noted the diagnosis was not explicitly psychiatric and allowed the claim of Rs.20415.

Insured was hospitalized for suspected Mediastinal Right Hilar Mass and underwent investigations including bronchoscopy. Claim was rejected on the grounds of lack of active treatment and that it could be done via OPD. Ombudsman held that diagnostic procedures are part of active treatment and allowed the claim.

Eye treatment claim was rejected stating it could be done via OPD and lacked active treatment. Ombudsman noted retinal dilation was done during hospitalization, constituting treatment, and directed the insurer to verify and pay the claim.
Claim was repudiated because original documents were not submitted, having been misplaced by the TPA. Ombudsman directed settlement on duplicate documents upon taking an indemnity bond.
Claim for breast tumor treatment was rejected as pre-existing due to a two-day renewal break. Ombudsman condoned the marginal delay, restored policy continuity, and allowed the claim of Rs.17568.

Insurer restricted mediclaim for diabetes treatment to the sum assured of the year diabetes was detected. Ombudsman held that the insured should also receive the benefit of accumulated bonus on the enhanced sum assured proportionally.

Insurer disallowed admission charges on the ground that treatment could be managed via OPD. Ombudsman held that admission charges cannot be disallowed once hospitalization has taken place and ordered payment.

Hospitalization claim and post-hospitalization medicine expenses for kidney transplant patient were rejected for lack of active treatment and unrelated medicines. Ombudsman held investigations constitute active treatment, and allowed hospitalization expenses and diabetes-related post-hospitalization medicines.
Claim was withheld because certain original documents were missing. Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim by obtaining hospital payment confirmation and an indemnity bond.

Mediclaim was treated as 'no claim' due to non-submission of VP shunt procedure details and legal heir certificate. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation as the insurer failed to justify the relevance of the documents, directing claim settlement.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz Gen. Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Personal accident death claim was repudiated for lack of documents and alleged signature mismatch on the proposal form. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation, noting police and postmortem reports established accidental death and signature mismatch was immaterial.

Claim for cervical dorsal disc disease was repudiated on the ground that only oral treatment and investigations were given without active indoor treatment. Ombudsman held medicines required strict medical supervision and allowed the claim of Rs.7080 with interest and cost.

Hysterectomy claim was paid only up to 20% of sum insured based on revised policy conditions. Ombudsman held that each annual renewal constitutes a distinct contract, making revised terms applicable, and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Ayurvedic treatment claim was partly repudiated, disallowing lab tests as routine check-ups and capping post-hospitalization expenses. Ombudsman held lab tests were necessary for ayurvedic medicines and allowed Rs.707 extra with interest and cost.

Surgery for thyroglossal cyst was repudiated on the ground that it is a congenital disease. Ombudsman held that only external congenital defects are excluded, whereas internal congenital anomalies are covered, and allowed the claim of Rs.11851.

Claim following hospitalization and death was restricted to the initial sum assured before policy enhancement on the ground of pre-existing illness. Ombudsman found no restrictive clause in the renewal policy and awarded the difference in sum assured of Rs.25000.

Claim for knee ligament injury was repudiated due to lack of 24-hour hospitalization and active treatment as treatment was pursued via OPD after initial discharge. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.
Headache treatment and scanning claim was repudiated because hospitalization was solely for investigation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

Periodontitis treatment claim was repudiated due to absence of 24-hour hospitalization, treatment at a dental clinic rather than a hospital, and aging wear-and-tear exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: CAD treatment claim was repudiated as pre-existing due to hypertension and a policy renewal break caused by a dishonoured cheque. Ombudsman held the cheque dishonour was not due to insurer's fault, but ruled that hypertension is not a heart disease and set aside the repudiation, awarding Rs.14723.

A claimant sought reimbursement for a CT scan bill not included in the original pre-authorization or hospital enhancement request. Since the hospital did not submit the proper bills for the scan to the insurer, the claim was rightly rejected by the company, and the complaint was dismissed.

An insured underwent treatments including EECP, which were repudiated for being pre-existing and using an unapproved method. The Ombudsman noted that policies crossing the waiting period cover pre-existing conditions, and FDA approvals validated EECP. The insurer was ordered to pay the claim with interest and costs.

A policyholder hospitalized for lower respiratory tract infection had their claim rejected on the ground of having no active line of treatment beyond tests. Records proved medicines were prescribed after diagnosis. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and awarded the eligible amount with interest and costs.

A policyholder underwent two hospitalizations for fatigue and illness, involving special tests and oral medicines, followed by lifestyle advice. The insurer rejected the claims as admission was merely for investigation and rest. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection and dismissed the complaint.

A policyholder underwent heart surgery eleven months after enhancing their sum assured. The insurer restricted payment to the pre-revised sum based on pre-existing hypertension and coronary artery disease. The Ombudsman found no record of pre-existing CAD before revival and ordered payment of the full enhanced sum assured.

A policyholder's wife underwent Cytotron treatment for osteoarthritis. The claim was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.13 regarding magnetic and magneto-therapy. Medical reports confirmed that Cytotron uses static electromagnetic fields, falling squarely under the excluded category. The complaint was dismissed.

An insured hospitalized for chest pain had their claim rejected because hospital records showed only diagnostic tests and medication for acidity, with no active treatment for chest pain. The Ombudsman concluded the hospitalization was merely for investigation and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for Ayurvedic treatment was rejected because it was allegedly doable on OPD basis and submitted after the 15-day window. The Ombudsman noted the treatment involved specialized massage requiring expertise, and the delay in filing caused no prejudice to the insurer, allowing the claim.

A reimbursement claim was initially repudiated due to the absence of a treating doctor's certificate to determine if the illness was pre-existing. During the hearing, the insurer agreed to settle for an eligible amount, which the complainant accepted.

An insured took inpatient Ayurvedic treatment for suspected rheumatic disease due to an allergy to allopathic medicines. The TPA repudiated the claim, but during the hearing, the insurer agreed to honour the eligible amount, to which the complainant consented.

An insured underwent treatment for renal failure and septicemia following ureteric calculi treatment days prior. The insurer repudiated the claim as a continuation of treatment for renal calculus, which is subject to a first-year exclusion. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for endometriosis treatment was repudiated on the grounds of treating infertility and the patient being a married, non-dependent daughter. The Ombudsman found the treatment was for dysmenorrhoea and cyst removal, and the policy terms did not define dependency or require a new proposal upon automatic renewal.

An insured underwent inpatient treatment for cervical encirclage due to a short cervix. The claim was repudiated under clause 4.12 as a treatment relating to pregnancy. The Ombudsman concurred that the surgical procedure was pregnancy-related and dismissed the complaint.

An insured's claim for 18 days of inpatient Ayurvedic treatment for joint and back pain was repudiated for lack of active treatment and lack of necessity for hospitalization. The Ombudsman noted admission in a government hospital coupled with active procedures warranted the claim, which was allowed.

A claim for hydrocele excision and circumcision for a minor child was repudiated under exclusion clauses 4.3 and 4.5, which exclude hydrocele and genitourinary treatments under revised policy conditions. The Ombudsman upheld the exclusion and dismissed the complaint.

A claim was repudiated solely on the technical ground that intimation was not given within the stipulated time, despite verbal intimation being made on the day of hospitalization. Finding the bills genuine and no prejudice caused, the Ombudsman allowed the claim.

A claim for inpatient treatment and physiotherapy for synovitis was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary and could be done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman noted that severe joint pain and restricted mobility made daily hospital visits impractical, thus setting aside the repudiation.

A cancer survivor hospitalized for fatigue underwent various diagnostic tests without active hospital treatment, leading to a repudiation under clause 4.10 for evaluation-only admissions. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for early-stage liver disease and diarrhea was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing illness and alcohol abuse. The Ombudsman found no clinical evidence of jaundice or alcohol-induced damage and noted the early stage of the disease, allowing the claim.

A claim for CABG surgery was repudiated because hospital records recorded a history of diabetes for 8 years and hypertension for 20 years, which are contributory factors to coronary artery disease. The Ombudsman ruled that the patient's admission of history held high probative value and dismissed the complaint.

Insured sustained serious spinal injuries while working abroad and could not submit claim within the one-month deadline due to being bedridden. The ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount of Rs. 25,000.

Insured was hospitalized for high blood sugar and cough. Insurer rejected the claim stating it was an OPD treatment. The ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered payment of Rs. 3,951 with interest and cost.

Insured underwent ayurvedic hospitalization including traction. The claim was repudiated on the grounds that traction is not approved in ayurveda and no investigation was done. The ombudsman set aside repudiation and ordered Rs. 4,450.
Insurer deducted Rs. 285 from a hospital claim towards utility charges, registration fee, RMO charges, and medicines. The ombudsman found these admissible and ordered a total payout of Rs. 2,010.
A cancer patient took oral chemotherapy at home without hospitalization. Insurer rejected the claim since policy requires inpatient hospitalization. The ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Multiple family hospitalizations were claimed, but insurer rejected them for lack of immediate intimation and failure to submit claim forms within 30 days. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Son was admitted for suspected kidney stone and evaluated with CT scan during a first-year policy period. Insurer repudiated due to first-year exclusion and diagnostic-only admission. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for umbilical hernia surgery was rejected under pregnancy complication exclusion because she had a previous cesarean section. Medical records showed hernia predated pregnancy; ombudsman awarded Rs. 56,755.

Claim for viral disease was closed by insurer requesting past ailment details for pre-existing conditions. Since the policy was running continuously for over 9 years, the ombudsman ordered full payment of Rs. 2,497.

Claim for cashless shortfall and pre/post-hospitalization was rejected due to unanswered TPA queries and missing documents. The forum directed the insurer to settle after receiving necessary documents.
Breast cancer treatment claim was left unsettled by the insurer without reason. The insurer failed to appear or defend. The complaint succeeded on its own merits.
Eye surgery claim was repudiated under a 24-hour hospitalization requirement. The ombudsman noted 24-hour stay is not mandatory for eye surgeries and allowed the complaint.
Claim was rejected due to a 16-day delay in intimation and submission caused by the treating doctor. The ombudsman found rejection harsh and awarded Rs. 8,500 on an ex-gratia basis.
Fibrocystic breast disease lumpectomy claim was incorrectly rejected assuming it was cancer treatment. Insurer failed to defend. The ombudsman directed full settlement with 8% interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization occurred on the day after policy inception. Insurer repudiated under the first 30 days exclusion clause. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Laser eye surgery claim was rejected for late submission of papers. Insurer offered 10% sum assured treating it like cataract. Ombudsman ruled cataract limits do not apply and ordered full payment of Rs. 41,073.
Claim was marked 'No Claim' due to late submission via agent. Through ombudsman mediation, both parties mutually agreed on a full and final settlement of Rs. 9,128.

Two claims were repudiated: one for wife's treatment due to fraudulent manipulation, and another for husband's nail removal which stemmed from a pre-existing fracture prior to policy inception. Repudiations upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Pacemaker installation claim was rejected for pre-existing cardiac conditions and misrepresentation. Since the policy ran since 2002 and previous exclusions were overlooked by the insurer, the ombudsman awarded Rs. 1,15,000 ex-gratia.
Cataract claim was partially settled due to late submission of documents. Through mediation, the parties mutually agreed on a settlement amount of Rs. 26,725.

The insured underwent a hysterectomy and the insurer deducted Rs.17,500 based on room rent limits under revised 2007 policy clauses. The ombudsman noted the policy incepted in 2001 and the actual expenses were well within the old sum insured limit, making the deduction unjustified. Full claim was ordered.

Mediclaim for cardiac and other ailments was repudiated for pre-existing disease under clause 4.1. The policy was in continuous renewal since 1996. The ombudsman noted pre-existing diseases are covered after 4 years and the insurer's rejection was unjustified, ordering payment of the original sum insured of Rs.37,500.

Claim for gall bladder stone treatment was repudiated because the insured did not disclose hypertension since 2002 upon migrating to the revised 2007 policy. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as justified due to non-disclosure.

A claim for typhoid treatment was repudiated on the grounds of fraud. The ombudsman held that deciding allegations of fraud requires elaborate legal procedures and oral evidence under oath, which is beyond the forum's jurisdiction, and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for breast cancer treatment was marked as no claim due to being cosmetic surgery, an exclusion. Through mediation by the forum, both parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement of Rs.83,124.
Claim for gynecological treatment was repudiated for late submission of intimation and papers. Through mediation, the parties agreed on a full and final settlement of Rs.9,841.
Claim for enteric fever and gastritis was repudiated because hospitalization occurred within the first 30 days of policy inception. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as justified.

Claim for kidney stone lithotripsy was repudiated for pre-existing history of lithuria. The ombudsman noted the insurer failed to prove nexus between lithuria and renal calculus, set aside the repudiation, and directed settlement.

A post-hospitalization claim for a fractured leg was delayed for over six months without response. As the insurer remained absent during the hearing, an ex-parte decision was taken directing payment of the claimed amount.
Claim for enteric fever was repudiated as fraudulent due to billing and signature discrepancies. The forum treated the matter as beyond its jurisdiction, and the complaint was resolved accordingly.
Goiter surgery claim was repudiated for late submission of claim papers. Through forum mediation, the parties reached a mutually acceptable full and final settlement.
Cataract operation claim was repudiated due to late submission of documents. Through forum mediation, both parties agreed on a mutually acceptable full and final settlement amount.
Cataract surgery claim was partially settled because the bill for the intraocular lens was missing. Through mediation, the parties agreed on payment of the deducted balance amount.

Claim for breast abscess surgery was repudiated on the grounds that it was a pregnancy-related complication excluded from the policy. The ombudsman noted the abscess occurred 40 days post-delivery due to bacterial infection, not pregnancy, and allowed the complaint.

Claim for intravitreal injection for eye treatment was repudiated based on an internal circular treating it as an excluded OPD procedure. The ombudsman noted it is a surgical procedure performed in an operation theater and internal circulars cannot override policy terms, allowing the complaint.

Claim for kidney stone and ureterorenoscopy was repudiated due to pre-existing history of lithotripsy within the two-year waiting period. The insurer produced medical evidence proving pre-existence, and the complaint was dismissed.

Claim for pancreatitis and gall bladder conditions was repudiated under a two-year waiting period clause for gall bladder stone removal. The ombudsman observed that no gall bladder surgery was actually performed, making the repudiation unjustified, and allowed the complaint.

Claim was partially settled after deductions were made under room rent caps and an internal circular restricting cash payments above Rs.10,000. The ombudsman found total expenses were within the policy limit and ordered the insurer to pay the deducted amount.

Cancer treatment claim was repudiated because the insured was an ex-gutkha chewer and tobacco exclusion applied. The ombudsman noted the exclusion was introduced in 2007 long after policy inception in 2000 and the insurer failed to prove tobacco use caused the cancer, allowing the complaint.

Claim for arthritis treatment was partially settled by applying a waiting period restriction. The ombudsman noted the policy had been in continuous force since 2005 and directed the insurer to pay the claim based on the 2006-07 policy terms.
Claim for enteric fever was repudiated for fraud and excessive billing proven by the attending doctor. The insurer's decision is upheld.
Hospitalization for renal failure was repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension and kidney disease since 2007. Insurer's decision upheld.
Claim was repudiated due to a 35-day delay in intimation. Through forum mediation, both parties agreed on a full and final settlement of Rs. 8500.
Claim for segmental double fracture tibia was rejected because knee POP treatment can be done on an OPD basis without hospitalization. Decision upheld.
Mediclaim repudiated on grounds that the hospital did not meet the minimum bed requirement, but investigation reports regarding bed counts showed inconsistencies.
Claim for pregnancy-related abdominal pain was rejected under clause 4.12. During proceedings, the representative agreed to compromise for Rs. 6225.
Claim was repudiated due to an exorbitant 89-day delay in submitting claim papers. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Accidental death claim resulting from a fall from a train was repudiated under suicide and self-inflicted injury exclusion, supported by police panchnama and SDM verdict.
Claim for sub retinal bleeding was partly rejected under clause 2.6 for hospital stays under 24 hours. The ombudsman ordered payment for earlier admissible claims.
Claim repudiated for late document submission by TPA guidelines. Ombudsman found the delay justifiable, set aside the repudiation, and ordered full payment.
Insurer partially settled the claim and disallowed costs for braces, ice bag, rib belt, walker, and salary loss under policy exclusions. Complaint failed.
Claims for cancer treatment were repudiated due to missing particulars from a 1997 settlement after TPA termination. Insurer directed to pay with interest.

Claims for intravitreal injections were repudiated as OPD treatment. Ombudsman noted hospitalization was advised by the treating doctor and circular classifying it as OPD came after treatment, setting aside repudiation.
Knee replacement claim was repudiated for late submission by 10 days. Both parties mutually agreed for payment during the hearing.
Jaundice hospitalization claim was partially settled. On forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed on an amount as full and final settlement.
Bariatric surgery for morbid obesity was rejected as cosmetic surgery. Based on medical references and surgeon opinion, the ombudsman ordered claim payment.
Complainant expressed dissatisfaction with the hearing proceedings after conclusion, so no formal order was issued.
Claim for diabetes mellitus and infective hepatitis was partially deducted for pre-existing diabetes. Parties mutually agreed on a settled amount during mediation.
Claim was repudiated for late submission because documents were first processed with another insurer. Ombudsman set aside rejection and ordered full payment.
Cancer claim was repudiated based on a doctor's note that the insured was a tobacco chewer, without proving it caused the cancer. Repudiation set aside.

Claim for post LSCS superior mesenteric artery thrombosis was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.12 for pregnancy-related treatment. The ombudsman noted the treatment was by a gastro enteric surgeon, not a gynecologist, making the repudiation unjustified.

Claim for spinal cord treatment was rejected for late submission of documents by 45 days. Since post-hospitalization continued, the delay should have been condoned. The insurer was directed to pay Rs 82,220.

Claim for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease was repudiated under clause 4.15 for genetic disorders and late submission. Literature proved it is a genetic disorder, so the insurer's decision was upheld.
Claim for obstructive sleep apnea was partially settled by excluding non-medical expenses like CPAP under group mediclaim policy clause 1(D)(c). The insurer's decision was found justified.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd
facts: Cataract surgery claim was rejected under exclusion C(3) for the first-two-years waiting period. The insured accepted the policy without accrued bonus and renewed it, making the exclusion operative.

Knee joint replacement claim of Rs 219,388 was partially settled for Rs 205,287 based on surgery caps. The insurer overlooked pre and post-hospitalization expenses up to 10% of sum insured, and was directed to pay an additional Rs 14,101.
Claim for ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and diabetes within two years of policy inception was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.3. The insurer's decision was upheld.

Cataract claim was partially settled by applying waiting periods and revised terms to an old sum insured. The ombudsman ruled that enhanced sum insured rules cannot apply to old continuous sum insured, setting aside the deduction.
Accidental death benefit claim due to tetanus following a crush injury was rejected because no police complaint or post-mortem report was produced to prove an accident.
Claim repudiated due to late submission was resolved through forum mediation, with both parties agreeing to a full and final settlement of Rs 86,590.
Claim repudiated under policy terms and conditions was resolved through forum mediation, with both parties mutually agreeing to settle for Rs 8,900.

Claim for CAD and IHD was rejected under pre-existing disease clause 4.1 due to diabetes history. As the insurer produced no concrete evidence connecting diabetes to coronary artery disease and the treating doctor denied connection, the repudiation was set aside.
Claim was repudiated for delayed intimation and late submission of documents. The ombudsman noted a minor delay of three days which should have been condoned, setting aside the repudiation.
Claim for acute viral hepatitis was rejected for lack of 24-hour intimation. Considering the insured was under tension and bills were genuine, the ombudsman directed payment on an ex-gratia basis.
Claim for malaria treatment was partially settled with deductions for room rent and unexplained visit charges. The insurer failed to provide satisfactory explanations, and was directed to pay Rs 900.

Claim for acute coronary syndrome was repudiated under pre-existing clause 4.1 for hypertension. Since the policy was issued after medical tests without specific exclusions and hypertension duration was unproven, the repudiation was set aside.

Claim amount was kept in abeyance pending legal heir determination following the insured's death. Upon submission of a will and bank passbook, the insurer was directed to deposit the amount into a trust bank account.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd
facts: Claim repudiation was resolved through forum mediation, with both parties mutually agreeing to a full and final settlement of Rs 5,000.
Claim repudiation under clause 4.12 was resolved through forum mediation, with both parties mutually agreeing to a full and final settlement of Rs 32,400.
Cataract surgery claim was rejected for lack of 24-hour intimation. Because discharge was on a Saturday and the TPA office had shifted, the delay should have been condoned, and payment was ordered.
Claim for lower back pain and PID treatment was repudiated by the insurer as it occurred within the two-year waiting period for prolapsed intervertebral disc.
The insurer failed to settle or respond to a mediclaim for cystoscopy treatment. The forum directed the insurer to settle the claim with interest.
The insurer neither settled nor replied to a claim for cystoscopy treatment. The forum ordered the insurer to settle the claim with interest as per regulations.
Insurer partially settled a claim by disallowing cash surgeon charges based on internal instructions not disclosed in policy terms. Forum ordered full settlement of the deducted amount.
Claim for viral hepatitis and liver failure was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.8 due to alcohol abuse. Evidence confirmed chronic alcoholism, and complaint was dismissed.
Dispute over mediclaim repudiation was resolved through forum mediation, with the insurer agreeing to pay a mutually agreed sum as full and final settlement.
During forum mediation for a repudiated claim, the insurer offered a compromised amount which the complainant accepted, leading to disposal of the case.
Claim for herniotomy was repudiated as a congenital condition. Based on medical principles regarding hernia acquisition in infancy versus later life, the repudiation was set aside.
Insurer improperly applied new policy conditions and room rent caps to a claim despite continuous policy renewal history. The forum directed payment of the balance amount.
Claim was repudiated because hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours. Records failed to establish discharge at midnight as claimed, justifying the rejection.
Insurer deducted surgeon fees based on internal guidelines not part of the policy contract. The forum ruled against arbitrary cuts and ordered payment of the deducted amount.
Repudiation of intravitreal injection treatment under OPD exclusion was set aside because expert medical evidence proved it is a surgical procedure requiring an operation theatre.
Insurer restricted hernia treatment reimbursement to 15% of sum insured as per policy clauses. The forum upheld the insurer's calculation and dismissed the complaint.
Dispute over short payment for joint replacement due to waiting period rules on enhanced sum insured. The forum upheld the insurer's application of the previous sum insured tier.
Claim for knee replacement surgery was repudiated due to pre-existing osteoarthritis history dating prior to policy inception. The forum upheld the rejection.
Angioplasty claim was repudiated because it occurred within the initial 90-day waiting period for critical illnesses under the policy terms. Complaint dismissed.
Dispute regarding short payment following sum insured enhancement. Insurer applied a two-year waiting period to the increased sum, which the forum found justified.
Claim was rejected for alleged non-submission of requirements. Since records proved all documents were duly submitted, the repudiation was set aside and settlement ordered.
Mediclaim for enteric fever was repudiated for fraud and misrepresentation after the attending doctor admitted preparing an inflated bill. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for tibia fracture treatment involving knee POP was rejected on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary as it is an OPD procedure. Insurer decision upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent treatment for pregnancy and abdominal pain. Respondent rejected the claim under clause 4.12. During proceedings, parties agreed to a compromise settlement of Rs. 6,225.
Claim repudiated due to late intimation and submission of papers by 35 days. Through mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement of Rs. 11,923.

Insured incurred Rs. 1,74,548 for CAD, HTN, and DM treatment. Respondent paid Rs. 1,25,000 based on restricted sum insured. Forum found insured was adequately covered for Rs. 3,00,000 since sum insured changes. Repudiation set aside for balance.
Mediclaim repudiated for late submission of papers by 53 days. Complainant stated continuous treatment caused the delay. Parties agreed to settle on compromise basis, setting aside repudiation.
Claim for infective hepatitis rejected alleging misrepresentation regarding health. Upon scrutiny showing no irregularities, parties agreed to compromise the claim for Rs. 10,700.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim rejected for non-submission of requirements. Insured underwent Ayurvedic treatment, where certain diagnostic reports were inapplicable. Ayurveda is covered up to 25 percent of sum insured. Repudiation set aside.
Claim repudiated stating insured did not cooperate during representative's visit. Hospitalization was established as justified. Parties mutually agreed on an amount of Rs. 6,000.
Insured hospitalized for Ischemic Seizure, incurring Rs. 49,915. Respondent partially repudiated Rs. 8,450 for medicines beyond 60 days. Upon scrutiny, papers were in order for Rs. 6,600.

Claim repudiated for hospitalization under 24 hours following an accident with a fracture. Referee doctor opined hospitalization was unnecessary. Overwriting on certificate required legal process beyond forum jurisdiction.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Partial repudiation for piles surgery invoking two-year waiting period. Respondent wrongly considered initial sum insured prior to 2007 renewal. Insured eligible for full claim amount.
Partial repudiation citing internal circular restricting cash payments to surgeons. Insured paid Rs. 26,000 in cash, well within the 25 percent sum insured limit. Partial settlement set aside.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for eye surgery involving intravitreal injection rejected as OPD treatment. Medical opinion established it as a surgical procedure requiring care. Repudiation set aside for full payment.
Claim repudiated because the hospital had only 7 beds and lacked appropriate registration, failing the 15-bed criteria. Respondent's decision upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Partial repudiation for uretic stone treatment under 2-year waiting period for enhanced sum insured. Earlier sum insured approved. Respondent's decision upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim repudiated because hospital lacked registration and bed count. Since insured met with an accident requiring urgent treatment and minor surgery, claim should be considered on non-standard basis.

insurer: IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for renal calculus and urethral stricture repudiated for pre-existing conditions across policy periods. Repudiation set aside for renal calculus and upheld for urethral stricture.
Claim for liver cirrhosis repudiated for late submission. Complainant stated papers were submitted on July 24, 2009. Respondent agreed to waive condition and mutually settled for Rs. 97,000.
Partial repudiation for Hysterectomy treatment. Policy prospectus allows 25 percent of sum insured, but respondent approved only 20 percent. Respondent directed to pay balance 5 percent.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for severe tonsillitis with high-grade fever repudiated invoking 2-year waiting period for first-year policy. Respondent's decision upheld.
Claim for uretic stone for Rs. 74,826 rejected due to cash payment irregularities to doctor. Through mediation, parties mutually agreed to full and final settlement of Rs. 40,000.

The insured's son received treatment for a lateral malleolus fracture on an OPD basis at a clinic without hospitalisation. The insurer repudiated the claim as OPD treatments are not covered under the policy terms. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

The insured's wife underwent cataract surgeries within seven months of policy inception. The insurer rejected the claim based on a two-year waiting period/exclusion for cataract and because the hospital did not meet the minimum bed requirement. The ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

The insured's son underwent LASIK eye surgery for myopia. The insurer repudiated the claim stating it was for cosmetic purposes and myopia less than 7 was excluded. The ombudsman observed the treatment was therapeutic as contact lenses were unsuitable, and ordered full payment.

The insured was hospitalised for a disc prolapse and the claim was repudiated on grounds of a pre-existing disease. The ombudsman noted the insured had held continuous mediclaim policies without break since 1998 and a similar claim had been paid in 2006, ruling the repudiation unjustified and ordering full payment.

The insured's daughter was hospitalised for viral pneumonitis. The insurer rejected the claim due to delayed submission and because the hospital lacked local authority registration and had fewer than 15 beds. The ombudsman noted the treatment was genuine and ordered 75 percent settlement as a special case.

The insured's wife was hospitalised for right dural AV fistula. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing conditions and a history of symptoms dating back 1.5 years based on an initial hospital report, which was later corrected by the treating doctor as 1.5 months. The case details ended before a final award was specified.

The insured's son received outpatient rabies injections following a dog bite. The insurer rejected the claim because outpatient treatments require no hospitalisation. The ombudsman noted it was an accidental injury that modern medicine does not require hospitalisation for, and recommended ex-gratia payment of the full amount.

The insured was hospitalised for evaluation of retrosternal pain and underwent complex diagnostic procedures like MRCP. The insurer rejected the claim stating it was solely for investigation and could be done on an outpatient basis. The ombudsman found the hospitalisation justified on medical advice and ordered settlement.

The insurer rejected a post-hospitalisation claim balance due to a three-month delay in submission. The ombudsman noted the delay was caused by continuous terminal illness and the patient's eventual death, making it eligible for waiver. The ombudsman ordered payment of the agreed balance amount.

The insurer rejected a cataract surgery claim because the discharge summary mistakenly mentioned a ten-year history of diabetes. The treating doctor later clarified this was a clerical error and the patient was non-diabetic. The ombudsman set aside the repudiation and ordered full payment.

The insured's father was hospitalised for heart conditions and ischemic heart disease. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing conditions and non-disclosure of a pacemaker implanted fifteen years prior. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

The insurer made arbitrary deductions from a mediclaim settlement and obtained a discharge voucher under full satisfaction. The ombudsman found no concrete evidence supporting the deductions and ordered payment of the balance amount after excluding non-payable registration charges.

The insurer deducted room rent and nursing charges based on an older lower sum insured, ignoring the current combined sum insured of one lakh rupees. The ombudsman ruled that the previous separate policies justified the higher sum insured and ordered payment of the deducted amount.

The insurer delayed processing and closed a claim due to a five-month delay in document submission, later offering a penalty-reduced settlement which was never formally executed. The ombudsman found fault with both parties and noted the claim warranted a compromise settlement.

The insurer partially paid a hospitalisation claim for chest pain, disallowing a costly medicine called Pipsor on the grounds that it was irrelevant to the diagnosis. The ombudsman noted the medicine was prescribed by a competent specialist and ordered full reimbursement of the disallowed amount.

The insurer delayed a pre and post-hospitalisation reimbursement claim submitted twenty-two months after treatment, while agreeing to pay the hospital deposit. The ombudsman upheld the rejection of pre and post-hospitalisation expenses due to severe delay violating policy conditions, but ordered payment of the hospital deposit.

The insured raised grievances regarding minor deductions in a first claim, rejection of outpatient chronic pancreatitis expenses claimed as post-hospitalisation for gastroenteritis, and delay in a third claim. The ombudsman noted the outpatient expenses were for a different ailment and upheld part of the insurer's stance while other claims were under process.

The insurer rejected hospitalisation expenses at one hospital on the grounds that the stay was unnecessary and for routine checks, prior to a subsequent nasal surgery. The ombudsman found the initial hospitalisation justified by doctor advice for acute symptoms, and ordered payment after deducting non-payable service charges.

A claim for a young child's urinary tract surgery was repudiated due to delayed document submission and because medical records indicated a congenital condition existing since birth, placing it under pre-existing disease and first-year exclusions. The text concludes with hearing rescheduling.

The insured's daughter was hospitalised for a planned surgery following an accident, and the claim was repudiated under a two-year exclusion clause. During the ombudsman hearing, the insurer's representative agreed to settle the claim upon receipt of documents.

Complainant's mediclaim claim for treatment at an ayurvedic center was rejected because the facility was not a government hospital. The ombudsman found that the center was duly registered and recognized by state authorities, thereby complying with policy conditions, and ordered the insurer to settle the claim upon receiving necessary documents.

Complainant underwent treatment for right-side hemorrhages at a medical college hospital and submitted the claim. The insurer withheld settlement alleging non-submission of prescriptions for four bills. The ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim based on submitted records without requiring a consent letter.

Complainant requested cancellation and a pro-rata premium refund upon receiving a health insurance policy. As the insurer processed the cancellation and refunded the premium to the complainant's credit card account during proceedings, the ombudsman ordered the complaint closed.

Insurer rejected a mediclaim on the grounds of a pre-existing disease. The ombudsman held that the treatment was not for a pre-existing condition since the policy was renewed without conditions and an earlier claim for the same ailment had been honored. The insurer was directed to pay the claim.

Insured's son was hospitalized, but the claim was rejected because the treating hospital was not on the insurer's list of 64 approved hospitals. The ombudsman found the treatment bonafide based on the discharge summary and ordered payment of the admissible claim amount.

Complainant incurred expenses for cataract surgery with a multifocal lens, but the insurer made a partial deduction claiming the lens should cost less. Upon verifying with the hospital doctor that the multifocal package cost was justified, the ombudsman ordered the balance amount paid with interest.

Claim for angioplasty due to fibro muscular dysphasia was rejected under first-year exclusions as a congenital or genetic disorder. The ombudsman noted it was a common middle-age disease, and giving benefit of doubt while acknowledging insurer's genetic exclusion, ordered a 70% non-standard settlement.

Insurer repudiated a hospitalization claim under pre-existing disease clause, alleging kidney-related issues. The ombudsman found records showed treatment was actually for Hepatitis C rather than kidney disease, and ordered payment of the admissible claim amount.

Insurer rejected a claim on the ground that hospitalization was solely for evaluation and diagnostic purposes without active medical management. The ombudsman upheld the rejection based on discharge summaries showing normal test results and no effective procedures performed.

Claim was rejected under maternity exclusion following the insured's recent abortion and subsequent death from pneumonia and cardiac arrest. The ombudsman held that death resulted from a separate hospitalization unrelated to the abortion, and ordered settlement of the claim.

Kidney stone surgery claim was repudiated because a 13-day renewal gap caused the policy to be treated as fresh, invoking a two-year waiting period. In the absence of a fresh proposal form or medical check-up, the ombudsman treated the policy as continuous and directed settlement.

Cashless health card was blocked and claim rejected because the insured's mother declared her age as 69 while official voter records stated 77, violating maximum age limits and utmost good faith. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Hospitalization claim for coronary angioplasty was repudiated because the insured had disclosed a prior angioplasty on the reverse side of the proposal form. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection since pre-existing heart disease was established and excluded.

Insurer repudiated a claim because the one-day hospitalization involved only investigations and an anti-anxiety tablet without active medical management. The ombudsman upheld the rejection, noting that the hospital stay was purely for diagnostic purposes.

Complainant's knee surgery claim was partially restricted based on historical sum insured levels and four-year waiting periods for arthritis. Finding that the insurer failed to communicate policy term changes, the ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount as full and final settlement.

Health insurance card was blocked due to an alleged age discrepancy affecting premium slabs. The ombudsman found that older electoral records supported the insured's stated age at policy inception, and directed the insurer to pay the admissible claim.

Insurer rejected a spinal surgery claim based on a discharge summary remark indicating 'Spinal Congenital'. The ombudsman noted clarifying letters from the treating surgeon and prior hospital records confirming no congenital condition, and ordered the insurer to settle the claim.

Insurer withheld claim settlement because bills were only submitted for treatment at one specific hospital. The ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim for the submitted bills and consider the remaining balance upon proof of further treatment.

Insurer repudiated a stroke treatment claim because documents were submitted after the 30-day deadline. The ombudsman directed the insurer to waive the delay, noting the claimant's extreme disorientation and isolated living situation following the stroke.

Insurer rejected a claim for an operation involving ovary removal during the initial two-year policy period under a hysterectomy exclusion. The ombudsman found ambiguity in the medical terms and policy conditions, giving the benefit of doubt to the complainant and ordering settlement.

Insured claimed reimbursement for pulmonary thromboembolism treatment. Insurer rejected it as a pre-existing disease based on a past history of seizure from 2001. Ombudsman noted a five-year gap without symptoms, rendering it invalid as pre-existing, and allowed the claim.

Complainant was hospitalized for one day and underwent angioplasty. Insurer repudiated the claim alleging the disease was pre-existing and not acute, without medical backing. Ombudsman gave benefit of doubt to the complainant and directed settlement.

Complainant underwent treatment for sleep apnoea under a group policy. Insurer paid hospitalization but denied the cost of a CPAP machine, classifying it as non-medical expenses. Ombudsman noted no specific exclusion existed in the policy and directed settlement.

Insured's wife was treated for CSF Rhinorrhea. Insurer restricted the claim to the previous lower sum insured, citing a policy break due to a bounced cheque and pre-existing rules. In the absence of the proposal form and clear proof of terms, the Ombudsman ordered processing under the renewed sum insured.

Complainant was hospitalized for uncontrolled diabetes with palm abscess and cellulitis following a knife injury. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman observed the proximate cause was the knife injury and directed claim settlement.

Insurer initially rejected a claim for a child's skin reaction on grounds of vitiligo exclusion and lack of hospital necessity, later conceding to hospitalization expenses. Ombudsman scrutinized pre and post-hospitalization bills, disallowed unsupported tests, and awarded partial payment.

Insured was treated for neuro cardio depressor. Insurer repudiated the claim alleging the symptoms arose from alcoholism, an excluded category. Ombudsman found no expert medical proof linking the condition to alcoholism and ordered settlement.

Insured claimed for cholelithiasis with DUB. Insurer rejected it as pre-existing based on hospital notes mentioning past abdominal pain and acid dyspepsia. Due to the absence of the proposal form and inconclusive evidence, the Ombudsman ruled in favor of the complainant.

Insurer rejected a mediclaim because the treatment took place in a hospital not included in the insurer's designated panel list. Ombudsman held that any medical institute meeting the policy's definition of a hospital qualifies, and directed settlement.

Complainant was treated for severe aortic stenosis. Insurer rejected the claim stating the severe condition could not develop in just one year of policy duration, implying pre-existence. Ombudsman found no expert medical opinion to support the insurer and ordered claim settlement.

Insurer rejected a claim for hemorrhoids and sinusitis invoking the two-year waiting period exclusion. Ombudsman noted the insured had continuous policies with another public sector insurer prior to porting, ensuring full continuity, and directed claim processing.

Insured underwent total knee replacement. Insurer restricted payout under a major surgery clause and treated an old fracture from four years prior as a pre-existing disease under a second policy. Ombudsman ruled the historical fracture fell outside the four-year threshold and ordered fresh processing.
Rectification of a prior award where the claim amount was incorrectly recorded as a lower figure. Ombudsman directed the insurer to process the correct higher claim bill subject to policy terms.

Insured underwent pacemaker surgery and submitted a claim. Insurer repudiated it citing pre-existing bypass surgery done years prior. Since the insurer failed to produce the proposal form or pre-acceptance medical records, the Ombudsman gave the benefit of doubt to the complainant and ordered settlement.

Insured underwent bypass surgery and the claim was partially cut based on a clause restricting major surgeries to 70% of the sum insured. Ombudsman found the insurer failed to attach the amended policy conditions and restrictions to the policy document, and directed full settlement.

Insurer limited a mediclaim payout to an older lower sum insured, arguing that an insurer-initiated mandatory hike under IRDA guidelines did not cover pre-existing conditions. Ombudsman held that since the enhancement was statutory and not requested by the insured, the full enhanced sum insured applies.
Complainant filed regarding non-settlement of mediclaim. During Ombudsman proceedings, the insurer settled the claim via cheque, leaving no further relief required.
Complainant challenged non-settlement of mediclaim. The insurer paid the claim amount during the Ombudsman's intervention, closing the dispute.
Dispute over non-settlement of mediclaim. The insurer resolved the matter by issuing a payment during the Ombudsman proceedings.
Complaint filed regarding inadequate settlement of a mediclaim. The insurer disbursed additional payments during the Ombudsman's intervention, satisfying the claim.
Insured filed a complaint regarding non-settlement of mediclaim. During proceedings, the insurer settled the claim for Rs.13,271 and the complaint was disposed of.

Complainant was hospitalized for severe headache diagnosed as chronic sinusitis. Insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.3 without medical evidence of pre-existing chronic sinusitis. Forum set aside the rejection and directed settlement.

Insured hospitalized for Spinal Canal Stenosis in the second policy year. Insurer and independent medical opinions confirmed the condition was a chronic degenerative affection existing prior to policy inception. Repudiation upheld.

Insured was hospitalized for acute ulcerative tonsillitis with pharyngitis in the second policy year. ENT disorders have a two-year waiting period under the policy, making the insurer's repudiation justified.
Insured underwent treatment for lumbar canal stenosis. Claim was delayed, and the insurer agreed to settle after disallowing certain expenses as per policy terms, which the forum found justified.

Complainant hospitalized for bilateral fracture of tibia fibula. Claim repudiated for alleged late intimation beyond 72 hours. Proof of delivery showed intimation was received within time, so complaint succeeded.
Complainant hospitalized for malaria and vitamin B12 deficiency. Claim repudiated for alleged late intimation. Complainant proved fax receipt showed timely intimation, making repudiation unjustified.

Insured hospitalized for urinary tract infection and gastritis. Insurer rejected claim alleging conversion of OPD into hospitalization without medical opinion. Treatment was taken on specialist advice, so complaint succeeded.
Insured underwent endoscopic septoplasty and sinus surgery. Claim was delayed and partially settled based on family floater group policy terms, which the forum upheld.
Insured underwent bilateral tibial knee replacement. Insurer offered 75% of the admissible amount under family floater group policy terms, which the forum found justified.
Insured underwent total knee replacement surgery. Insurer settled 75% of the admissible amount as per group policy terms, which the forum upheld.

Insured hospitalized for fever, cough, and cold. Claim rejected for a one-day delay in intimation. Insurer had discretionary power to condone delays up to 30 days but failed to exercise it, so rejection was set aside.
Complainant hospitalized for cataract surgery. Insurer limited payout to Rs.15,000 as per family floater group policy caps, which the forum upheld.
Insured underwent total knee replacement. Insurer paid 75% of the admissible amount as per family floater group policy terms, which the forum upheld.
Complainant hospitalized twice for respiratory and diabetic conditions. Insurer partially settled after disallowing certain items, which the forum found justified.
Insured hospitalized for cataract surgery. Insurer restricted settlement to Rs.15,000 as per family floater group policy caps, which the forum upheld.

Insured hospitalized for appendicitis. Insurer deducted amounts for cash surgeon fees based on an internal circular and miscalculated sum insured. Forum noted internal circular was not part of policy terms and allowed full claim.
Insurer partially settled mediclaim after disallowing Rs.5,099. Forum agreed with the insurer's revised liability of Rs.4,699 for full and final settlement.

Insured claimed Rs.2,10,065 for acute myocardial infarction and stenting. Insurer partially paid, invoking a waiting period for hypertension. Forum noted no evidence of hypertension or its link to the heart attack, and no waiting period for myocardial infarction, allowing the full claim.
Complainant hospitalized for colostomy surgery. Insurer limited payment to Rs.18,000 as per family floater group policy terms, which the forum found in order.
