Insured hospitalized for Pyrexia. Claim delayed over 4 months. Respondent agreed to settle after deducting admission fee.
Insured hospitalized for left knee joint replacement surgery. Claim delayed over 5 months. Respondent agreed to settle 75% of the admissible amount under group mediclaim policy.
Insured hospitalized for knee replacement. Claim repudiated due to overwriting on hospital documents suggesting fraud. Forum held it lacks jurisdiction to examine document corrections.

Insured hospitalized for knee replacement. Insurer repudiated claim alleging pre-existing knee pain. Forum noted group policy covers persons up to 80 years without medical checkup and pre-existing diseases are covered after 30 days, making repudiation unjustified.

Insured hospitalized for eye surgery and discharged same day. Insurer repudiated claim citing lack of 24-hour hospitalization. Doctor certified procedure did not require 24 hours due to medical advancements, making repudiation unjustified.

Claim made for removal of tibia implant. Insurer partially settled/repudiated by applying enhanced sum insured waiting periods. Forum held that old sum insured waiting period had long expired and revised terms could not apply to old sum insured.
Claim for prostate treatment partially settled with deductions including surgeon fees restricted to Rs 10000 based on internal instructions. Forum found restriction unjustified.
Claim unsettled for 9 months under dual policies. Another insurer settled fully. Forum directed respondent to settle in proportion to insured amount.
Claim repudiated for conversion of OPD into hospitalization without timely intimation. Complainant could not provide courier proof of intimation, so repudiation was justified.

Claim repudiated alleging continuous hospitalization was unjustified and intimation missing. Forum established treatment was continuous with proper intimation and no medical opinion was sought by insurer, making repudiation unjustified.
Claim repudiated as genetic disorder. Records showed patient suffered fracture from bicycle fall and underwent corrective osteotomy of tibia, not genetic disorder. Complaint succeeded.
Non-settlement claim for shoulder treatment resolved after respondent agreed to settle Rs 21125.
Claim for pre-existing disease resolved as both parties mutually agreed to a payment of Rs 4380.
Claim repudiated for late intimation, but resolved after parties mutually agreed to payment of Rs 22600.
Claim repudiated for being fraudulent, but resolved after parties mutually agreed to payment of Rs 6000.
Claim for hypertension settled after deducting enhanced sum insured due to two-year waiting period. Insurer's partial settlement upheld.
Claim for accidental injuries repudiated for late submission. Complainant had hand injuries and previous claims were settled on representation. Complaint succeeded.
Claim for ischemic heart disease repudiated for pre-existing chest pain of 3-4 years. Discharge summary and prior cashless denial confirmed pre-existing condition, justifying repudiation.
Claim repudiated for late intimation and document submission. Delay occurred due to children's exams and complainant's accident. Forum held delay should have been condoned.
Claim repudiated due to lack of indoor papers during investigation. Parties mutually agreed to settle for Rs 4500.

Complainant sought reimbursement for dengue fever treatment. Insurer repudiated claiming fraudulent documents, but discharge summary and consultation notes confirmed valid hospitalization and treatment.

Insured was hospitalized for an abscess and surgery. Insurer rejected claim under minimum 24-hour hospitalization clause. Records showed admission exceeded 24 hours, but the complaint ultimately failed to succeed on other policy terms.

Claim for cataract surgery was partially settled with deductions on room and surgeon charges. The ombudsman noted older policy terms applied without expense limits before sum insured enhancement and directed partial payment.
Claim was delayed for nine months without settlement. During the hearing, the insurer agreed to pay Rs 89501 as per policy terms, partially resolving the complaint.

Claim for ccf and uti was repudiated as pre-existing. Medical history confirmed diabetes, ischemic heart disease, and previous surgeries, making the current illness a complication of a pre-existing condition.
Claim for cystoscopy and DJ removal was rejected due to late submission of documents after 50 days without valid justification. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for hysterectomy and incisional hernia repair was partially rejected for hernia expenses. Previous caesarean sections decades prior were the proximate cause, making hernia non-admissible under policy exclusions.
Claim for infective endocarditis was repudiated as a complication of a pre-existing heart condition linked to prior ASD closure not disclosed or within the waiting period. Complaint dismissed.
Insurer rejected claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a settlement of Rs 10000.
Claim was rejected due to delay in document submission. Following mediation, both parties mutually agreed on a payment of Rs 20563.
Claim for enteric fever treatment was rejected for a three-day delay in document submission. The ombudsman condoned the short delay, and the complaint succeeded.

Claim for brain tumor in the second policy year was rejected under a first-year exclusion clause. Insurer argued symptoms began earlier, but the policy excluded diseases incurred, not merely symptomatic, in year one. Complaint allowed.
Cataract claim was settled based on the initial sum insured, restricting the increased sum insured due to a two-year waiting period. Insurer's deduction was upheld.
Claim for renal calculus was rejected because the policy was renewed after a 22-day break, triggering a fresh two-year waiting period clause. Insurer's decision was upheld.

Claim was repudiated for un-declared pre-existing disease based on a short history in the discharge summary. The policy covered pre-existing ailments after 30 days without mandatory pre-policy checkups, making rejection unjustified.
Claim was rejected because hospitalization was primarily for diagnostic purposes and could have been managed on an OPD basis with simple eye drops and tablets. Insurer justified.
Cataract surgery claim was rejected as it fell within the initial two-year exclusion period specified in the policy conditions. Rejection was justified.
Claim was rejected for alleged violation of policy terms. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to settle the claim for Rs 16144.
Claim for acute gastroenteritis was partially settled after disallowing certain doctor and procedure charges backed by informal cash receipts. Insurer's deductions were upheld.

Claim for anemia and viral fever was rejected under a general debility exclusion. Records showed the condition stemmed from accidental tooth extraction and bleeding, making the exclusion inapplicable. Complaint allowed.

The claimant sought reimbursement for hospitalization expenses for acute infective hepatitis. The insurer deducted certain doctor charges paid in cash, relying on an internal circular. The ombudsman found the internal circular was not part of the policy conditions, and the complaint succeeded.

The claimant sought reimbursement for polycystic kidney disease chronic renal failure. The insurer repudiated the claim under policy clause excluding genetic disorders. The ombudsman confirmed polycystic kidney disease is a genetic disorder, and the complaint failed.
The insurer repudiated a hospitalization claim due to abnormal delay in submitting claim papers. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a settlement amount of 5000.

The insurer repudiated a claim for viral fever and gastritis on grounds that the insured was not present during an investigator check and lacked indoor records. The ombudsman noted the investigation happened post-discharge and valid treatment papers were provided, so the complaint succeeded.

The claim was repudiated due to late intimation and late document submission. The complainant explained minor children and family hospitalization caused the delay. The ombudsman noted the insurer had discretionary power to condone delays on a non-standard basis, and the complaint succeeded partly.

The claim for diarrhea and vomiting treatment was repudiated because the hospital did not meet policy requirements of having fifteen beds and a fully equipped theater. The complainant could not submit hospital registration evidence, so the complaint failed.

The insurer made deductions on an eye operation claim stating amounts were on the higher side based on an MOU with doctors. The ombudsman ruled that the MOU did not form part of the policy contract and was not communicated, thus the complaint succeeded.

The claim for anal fissure and fistula treatment at an Ayurvedic clinic was repudiated under waiting period and Ayurvedic treatment clauses. The complainant failed to provide evidence of six years of continuous coverage, so the complaint failed.
The insurer repudiated a hospitalization claim due to abnormal delay in submission of claim papers. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a settlement of 4618.
The insurer made proportionate deductions for higher room rent under a revised 2007 mediclaim policy. The ombudsman found the insurer applied conditions correctly, and the complaint failed.

The insurer partially settled a hernia claim, denying the increased sum insured component because hernia has a two-year waiting period. The ombudsman found the two-year exclusion applied correctly to the recently increased sum insured, and the complaint failed.

The insurer deducted amounts on a cataract claim applying a two-year exclusion for increased sum insured while using revised policy conditions. The ombudsman found the insurer applied inconsistent standards under the same policy, so the complaint succeeded.
The claim for acute otomycosis ear surgery was repudiated because the policy excludes ear surgeries within the first two years. The ombudsman verified the clause applied, and the complaint failed.

The claim was repudiated due to late intimation past the 72-hour group MOU window. The ombudsman noted that while late intimation deprived inspection rights, the insurer should have exercised discretion to settle on a non-standard basis. The complaint succeeded partially.

The claim was repudiated because hospitalization was solely for investigation purposes and reports were within normal limits. The ombudsman found the insurer justified in repudiating, but recorded a partial allowance outcome.

The insurer deducted amounts from a prostate treatment claim including surgeon fees based on internal higher office instructions. The ombudsman found restricting surgeon fees to 10000 was unjustified, and the complaint succeeded.

The claim for ureteric stone was repudiated as fraudulent because the hospital bill was unpaid and paperwork incomplete. The ombudsman ruled that verifying the truth of hospitalization required court adjudication beyond forum jurisdiction, and the complaint was disposed.
The insurer repudiated the claim alleging concealment of facts regarding an accident. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to settle the claim for 65000.
The claim was repudiated due to late intimation after four days. The ombudsman found the insurer justified in rejecting the claim for delayed intimation, and the complaint failed.

The insurer deducted amounts for sinusitis treatment using internal office instructions and revised terms applied improperly to an initial sum insured. The ombudsman found the insurer's deductions unjustified, directing payment, and the complaint succeeded.

Claim for hypertension hospitalization repudiated due to pre-existing disease history of two years. Insured claimed history was only two days. Forum held that verifying conflicting medical history requires a competent court and is beyond its jurisdiction.
Claim not settled because no claim papers were submitted despite intimation. Insurer agreed to consider the claim on merits upon receipt of documents, resolving the issue.

Claim for stent removal repudiated under two-year waiting period clause. Insured had continuous coverage since 2002 without break, making the policy mature and the claim admissible under internal guidelines.

Claim for fistula operation partially settled after deductions under reasonable and customary charges. Insurer failed to provide supporting documents for standard packages, and the forum directed partial payment.

Claim for ureteric stone surgery partially settled due to cash payment deductions exceeding ten thousand rupees. Forum noted limiting cash fees is an internal circular and not a policy condition, ordering payment.

Claim for viral hepatitis partially settled. Insurer deducted twenty percent as co-pay under gold plus policy and rejected glucometer and post-hospitalization expenses beyond sixty days. Deductions found justified.
Claim for hemorrhoidectomy repudiated due to non-disclosure of pre-existing condition confirmed by discharge summary showing prior history of three years. Insurer decision upheld.
Claim for hospitalization left unsettled until hearing, where insurer agreed to pay eleven thousand two hundred sixty-one rupees. Complaint partially succeeded.
Claim for knee replacement rejected because group policy was cancelled with thirty days notice. Since hospitalization occurred prior to cancellation, insurer is liable and directed to pay.
Claim for finger fracture surgery repudiated for pre-existing injury dating back twenty-five years. Insurer's reliance on exclusion clause upheld.
Claim for scooter fall injuries repudiated due to unpaid bills and suspected fraud. Forum held it lacked powers and infrastructure to examine hospital authorities and verify payments.
Claim for hysterectomy partially settled due to limits on cash payments exceeding ten thousand rupees. Forum ruled internal circulars cannot override policy conditions and directed payment.
Claim for cataract surgery partially settled using revised policy terms. Forum noted old policy had no expense limits, and insurer applied inconsistent standards, directing partial payment.
Claim for pacemaker repositioning repudiated on grounds of physical comfort rather than illness. Medical records showed breathlessness and doctor's advice, making the repudiation untenable.
Claim for angioplasty partially settled by capping payment at seventy percent of sum insured under major surgery limits. Deductions justified.
Claim for myocardial infarction repudiated due to pre-existing ischemic heart disease recorded as six years. Forum noted resolving conflicting affidavits is beyond its jurisdiction.
Claim for congenital heart disease and atrial septal defect repudiated as internal congenital disease with permanent exclusion and pre-existing symptoms. Repudiation upheld.
Claim for knee replacement partially settled by capping expenses under revised policy terms. Forum ruled old policy terms applied without restriction, ordering balance payment.
Claim for bypass surgery left unsettled while insured sought reimbursement from government scheme first. Insurer guilty of deficiency in service; full payment with interest ordered.
Claim for cataract repudiated for late intimation and late submission with a minor delay. Given brief hospitalization and valid reasons, complaint succeeded.

Insured was hospitalized for lumbar stenosis and bladder urgency. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion as records showed low back pain history of 20 weeks and 7-8 years. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured hospitalized for Gilbert Syndrome with acute gastroenteritis and hemolytic jaundice. Claim repudiated as Gilbert Syndrome is a genetic disease excluded under policy conditions. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Complainant submitted a claim for reimbursement of hospitalization expenses. Following mediation by the forum, both parties mutually agreed on a settlement payment of Rs 9157.
Complainant filed a reimbursement claim for hospitalization expenses. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to resolve the grievance with a claim payment of Rs 18790.

Insured hospitalized for Ischemic Heart Disease with 95% LAD lesion on the 41st day of the policy. Insurer repudiated based on pre-existing condition and two-year waiting period. Ombudsman upheld the insurer decision.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for gastritis and dehydration treatment was repudiated alleging exaggerated bills and hospital discrepancies. Insurer failed to submit written statements or attend hearings. Ombudsman ruled the repudiation unjustified.
Reimbursement claim for hospitalization was repudiated invoking policy clause 2. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to settle the claim for Rs 7000.

Complainant submitted multiple claims for chemotherapy and surgery. The final claim was rejected because total benefits cannot exceed the sum insured during the policy period when hospitalization occurred. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for cataract surgery was partially settled after deductions for reasonable and customary charges, as the insured chose premium Crystalense lenses instead of aspheric IOL. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for laparoscopic gastric bypass surgery for morbid obesity was rejected as cosmetic surgery under exclusion 4.5. Ombudsman noted obesity is a disease and bariatric surgery was life-saving, setting aside the rejection.

Insured hospitalized for bronchitis and acid peptic disease. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing condition and heavy smoking history. Independent medical opinion supported the insurer's stand, and the complaint was dismissed.

Claim for viral fever and myositis repudiated for fraudulent claims and non-disclosure. Hospital records and independent medical opinion revealed actual admission was for psychiatric treatment and anxiety. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer partially settled claim by deducting Rs 25,000 because surgeon fees exceeded 25% of sum insured. Ombudsman ruled that valid hospitalisation expenses outside the main bill are fully reimbursable and set aside the deduction.

Insurer disallowed Rs 32,150 capping cataract surgery reimbursement at 10% of sum insured. Complainant claimed entitlement to a revised 25% limit, but failed to prove submission of a prescribed option form. Complaint dismissed.

Cataract surgery claim partially disallowed based on a 10% sum insured cap. Complainant argued a revised 25% limit applied, but consent was given after hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's deduction.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim partially disallowed by applying proportionate room rent limits under revised guidelines. Ombudsman noted total expenses were within old policy limits and cumulative bonus, rendering the deduction unjustified.

Cataract claim repudiated as pre-existing disease since surgery occurred 4 months after policy inception. Ombudsman observed the group policy covers all pre-existing diseases after 30 days without medical checkups, making the repudiation unjustified.

Knee replacement surgery claim repudiated as a pre-existing condition. Ombudsman noted the group policy covers pre-existing diseases after 30 days without medical checkups, rendering the insurer's repudiation unjustified.

Cataract surgery claim repudiated under pre-existing disease clause. Ombudsman noted the group policy covers pre-existing conditions after 30 days without prior medical checkup, setting aside the insurer's decision.

Claim repudiated for run-down condition resulting from a prolonged 45-day religious fast causing keto acidosis and hypokalemia. Ombudsman noted health policies indemnify natural illnesses, not self-inflicted voluntary deterioration, dismissing the complaint.

Insured underwent treatment for renal calculus, gastritis, and enteritis. Insurer repudiated citing hospital bed capacity and waiting period for renal calculus. Forum directed pro-rata settlement as bed criteria was met and other conditions were valid.
Cataract surgery claim for Rs. 68,576 settled partially using semi-special package charges. Forum adopted a golden mean by averaging deluxe package charges between semi-special and super deluxe.
Mediclaim repudiated due to one-day delay in hospitalization intimation. Forum held that insurer should have exercised discretionary power to condone the minor delay and ordered full payment.
Claim was delayed for over 6 to 7 months. During the proceedings, the insurer admitted the claims for settlement, resolving the disputes.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer partially settled claim invoking room rent limits and internal circulars restricting cash payments to doctors. Forum found total expenses within sum insured and ruled insurer unjustified in applying arbitrary internal circulars.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim partially settled after applying room rent limits based on old sum insured. Forum noted total expenses were within original sum insured and granted the full sum insured limit.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Prostate surgery claim arose in the second year of a revised policy. Because the condition has a two-year waiting period, the insurer considered the initial lower sum insured, which the forum upheld as justified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for Septoplasty in the second policy year. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion clause 4.3 excluding ENT disorders for two years, which the forum upheld.

Cataract surgery performed shortly after policy inception was repudiated as a pre-existing disease. Forum observed the policy covers pre-existing diseases after 30 days without medical check-ups, making repudiation unjustified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for Prolapse Intra-Vertebral Disc (PID) was repudiated due to a two-year waiting period. Based on independent medical opinion distinguishing PID from spondylosis, the forum upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for osteoarthritis of the knee occurred in the first policy year while subject to a four-year waiting period. Forum upheld the insurer's repudiation.
Mediclaim repudiated for late submission of claim papers after two months instead of 7 days. Forum directed payment of 60% of the claim amount on a non-standard basis.
Total knee replacement surgery claim repudiated because it occurred within the four-year waiting period. Forum found symptoms manifested during the fourth policy year and upheld rejection.
Claim for treatment under Magnetic Therapy was repudiated under policy exclusion for alternative medicine and unproven therapies. Forum upheld the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim partially repudiated based on room rent limits and proportional deductions. Forum noted total expenses were within previous sum insured plus cumulative bonus and ruled full claim payable.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer partially settled claim by capping cash payment towards surgeon fees at Rs. 10,000 based on internal guidelines. Forum held that surgeon fees formed part of hospitalization and internal guidelines were not part of policy terms.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer disallowed Rs. 13,419 under room rent capping and proportional scaling. Forum calculated correct deductions as Rs. 10,648 and ordered the insurer to pay the excess deduction amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer partially disallowed surgeon, anesthesia, and OT charges paid in cash based on internal instructions. Forum noted internal instructions are not policy conditions and ordered full payment.
Claim repudiated due to 14-day delay in submitting documents against a 7-day limit. Forum noted head office circular permitted delays up to 30 days and set aside repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for ventral hernia settled with deductions for room rent, consultation, and miscellaneous bills. Since the complainant consented to major deductions, forum recommended an ex-gratia amount.

Insured underwent hysterectomy and claimed Rs.44,784, but insurer partially reimbursed after applying internal guidelines and room rent caps. Ombudsman held internal guidelines invalid but upheld room rent and proportionate deductions, ordering partial payment.

Insurer repudiated claim due to delayed hospitalisation intimation and submission of claim papers. Ombudsman observed the delay was only by one day each and unjustified for total rejection, ordering the complaint to succeed.
Claim for cataract surgery was restricted to 10% of sum insured under old terms. Ombudsman noted failure to communicate revised terms violated good faith and awarded 25% of sum insured.

Insurer repudiated claim since cancer occurred within two years of policy inception, which falls under the waiting period. Hospital records confirmed cancer diagnosed within one year, making rejection justified.

Claim for intracranial hemorrhage with hypertension and diabetes was rejected as these conditions had a two-year waiting period following sum insured enhancement. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Insurer partially settled cataract claim based on old policy terms, arguing waiting period renewed. Ombudsman ruled the waiting period applies from initial policy inception, allowing the complaint.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz Life Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer delayed settling dental injury claim resulting from an accident without giving reasons or attending hearings. Ombudsman directed full payment with interest.
Claim for acute psychotic episode was repudiated under exclusion of psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders. Medical records and dictionary definitions supported the insurer's rejection.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was rejected due to discrepancies in age and conflicting accounts of how the injury occurred, alongside document tampering. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insurer rejected intravitreal injection claim on grounds of being an OPD procedure not requiring 24-hour hospitalization. Ombudsman found treatment required surgical operation theatre protocols and allowed the claim.
Insurer rejected claim for pre-existing conditions treated within the second year of a fresh policy after a break. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as continuity benefits did not apply.
Claim for hypertension and diabetes complications was repudiated because they fell within the policy's two-year waiting period. Ombudsman upheld the denial.
Insurer applied new capping terms for major surgery retrospectively to an older sum insured year. Ombudsman ruled older terms without capping should apply, allowing the complaint.
Dental treatment claim for chronic periodontitis was rejected as it did not result from an accidental injury. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's exclusion application.
Anti-rabies vaccination claim for dog bite was rejected as outpatient domiciliary treatment without hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.

Insurer partially settled claim based on third year policy limits after policy switch. Ombudsman established continuous renewal history but factored in a prior sum insured increase, granting partial relief.

insurer: Iffco Tokiyo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was repudiated because the treating hospital was registered under the Shops and Establishment Act rather than the Nursing Home Act and lacked 15 beds. Ombudsman ruled the hospital met policy definitions, allowing the complaint.
Insurer capped hernia surgery expenses. Ombudsman recalculated admissible amounts for hernia and cholecystectomy based on correct policy terms and issued a higher partial award.

Cataract surgery claim for a 5-year-old child was repudiated as a congenital external disease. Independent medical opinion disputed congenital classification, leading the Ombudsman to allow the claim.
Claim for urinary tract infection and fever was repudiated alleging document manipulation and fraud. Ombudsman found no evidence supporting fraud or misrepresentation, allowing the complaint.
Claim was repudiated because the insured underwent oral chemotherapy at home instead of parenteral chemotherapy and was not hospitalized.

Insurer rejected claim for Hiatus Hernia under congenital internal disease exclusion. An independent medical opinion confirmed it was not necessarily congenital, and forum ruled the insurer lacked proof.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension based on treating doctor records, despite being treated for pneumonia and ARDS.

Insurer deducted Rs. 7,663 for fissure in ano treatment citing a 2-year waiting period under revised 2007 policy rules. Forum held old sum insured applied without new waiting periods, allowing full payment.
Cataract surgery claim was partially settled applying new 2007 policy conditions and waiting periods. Forum ruled old sum insured and terms applied, directing payment of the difference of Rs. 6,050.
Cataract surgery claim of Rs. 31,314 was cut to Rs. 5,000 based on policy limits. Insurer failed to provide proof of proposal for revised policy terms, so full claim was awarded.

Claim was repudiated for withholding material information and issues regarding multiple policies and sum insured increases. Forum dismissed the complaint as it involved alleged fraud requiring legal trial beyond its jurisdiction.
Claim for infective Hepatitis was repudiated on the ground of fraud and doubtful treatment papers. Forum dismissed the complaint as proving fraud requires legal procedures beyond its jurisdiction.
Cataract surgery claim was rejected under clause 4.3 (two-year waiting period) because the policy was a fresh policy in its first year without continuous prior renewals with the insurer.
Road traffic accident claim had arbitrary deductions based on panel doctor opinion. Forum ruled treating doctor opinion carries more weight and awarded Rs. 19,230 for unjustified cuts.
Claim was repudiated because the hospital had 14 beds instead of the required 15. Resolved through mutual agreement via forum mediation.
Claim was repudiated due to late intimation of hospitalization. Resolved through forum mediation with a mutually agreed settlement.
Hysterectomy claim was partly paid via cashless facility, limiting it to Rs. 50,000. Forum noted revised policy entitled insured to higher limits, awarding a balance of Rs. 30,522.
Insurer disallowed pre- and post-hospitalization expenses for diabetes, HBP, and IHD during a prostate surgery claim, as they were unrelated to the primary hospitalization disease.
Claim for knee joint replacement surgery was delayed for over 7 months. Insurer agreed during proceedings to pay 75 percent of sum insured, and forum awarded Rs. 75,000.

Knee replacement surgery claim was rejected as pre-existing because it occurred within 3 months of policy inception. Forum held group policy covered pre-existing conditions after 30 days without medical checkups, making rejection unjustified.

Wife's knee replacement claim was rejected as pre-existing within 3 months of policy inception. Forum noted group policy covers pre-existing diseases after 30 days, invalidating the insurer's rejection.
Hip replacement claim was repudiated for late intimation to TPA beyond 72 hours. Complainant proved intimation was sent on time, so forum ruled in favor of the complainant.
Hospitalization claim was repudiated because intimation was not given to the TPA or insurer within 72 hours and no evidence of intimation was submitted.

Claim for Intra Ventricular SOL operation was settled based on old sum insured due to waiting periods on increased sum insured, with additional Zone-I deductions. Forum ruled zonal deductions unjustified and awarded an extra Rs. 7,250.

A claim for treatment expenses of the complainant's mother was repudiated as a congenital external disease. The forum noted the treatment was for a congenital internal disease, which was not excluded under the policy, and directed the insurer to pay Rs. 99,816.
A claim for reimbursement of treatment expenses of Rs. 29,654 was unsettled by the insurer. Through forum mediation, both parties amicably resolved and settled the dispute without a formal award.

A claim was rejected due to alleged lack of hospitalization intimation. The complainant proved intimation was given within 72 hours for cancer treatment. The complaint partially succeeded, and the insurer was ordered to pay Rs. 31,975 against the claimed Rs. 62,939.

A claim for daughter's treatment was repudiated due to a four-day delay in intimation caused by the complainant's educational backwardness. The forum noted the delay could be condoned on merit and ordered payment of Rs. 12,368.

The insurer deducted Rs. 37,450 from a Rs. 82,450 claim, citing higher hospital charges and potential pre-existing symptoms. The insurer failed to provide comparative charge lists, making deductions arbitrary. The complaint partially succeeded.

A claim was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary as diagnostic tests were normal and consultation occurred on an OPD basis just prior. The insurer's decision was upheld and the complaint dismissed.

A cataract surgery claim had deductions under room and miscellaneous charges based on new 2007 policy terms applied to an old policy. The forum ruled applying new conditions to an old sum insured was unjustified and the complainant was entitled to full payment.
A claim was marked as 'No Claim' due to late intimation of hospitalization. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to settle the claim for Rs. 27,000 without a formal award.

A claim for a son's treatment was repudiated under clause 4.4.16 for genetic disorders and stem cell therapy. Medical opinions confirmed the insured suffered from hereditary spherocytosis, a genetic condition excluded under the policy. The complaint was dismissed.

A claim under a group mediclaim policy was repudiated for pre-existing disease and fraud. The forum observed that the policy covered persons without medical checking and covered all pre-existing diseases after 30 days. The insurer's repudiation was unjustified and the complaint succeeded.

A partially settled claim involving deductions was brought to the forum, but because the complainant failed to submit necessary procedural forms (P-II and P-III), the matter was considered beyond the jurisdiction of the forum.

A claim was partially settled by deducting Rs. 7,825 due to room rent limits exceeding 1% of sum insured. The forum noted total expenses were within the old sum insured and cumulative bonus limit, rendering deductions unjustified. The complaint succeeded for Rs. 7,825.

A claim for USG guided fluid tapping and blood transfusion was rejected for lack of 24-hour hospitalization. The treating physician certified it as life-saving treatment requiring emergency admission. The forum held repudiation unjustified and ordered payment of Rs. 16,744.

A claim was not settled as the treatment could be done on OPD basis. Medical opinion obtained by the forum confirmed the procedure was performed under local anesthesia and hospital papers showed a deliberate date alteration to artificially extend hospitalization beyond 24 hours. The complaint failed.

A claim was repudiated because claim papers were submitted to the TPA nearly 50 days after discharge, violating the 7-day submission clause. The insurer's decision to repudiate was held justified and the complaint failed.

A claim for enteric fever treatment was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary as the condition is commonly treated orally on an OPD basis. The insurer's decision was upheld without relief.

A claim was repudiated under clause 4.2 because the insured contracted pneumonia and fever within 30 days of risk commencement. Evidence proved the illness began within the initial waiting period, justifying the insurer's decision.

A claim was partially settled with deductions made for late submission and missing blood sugar reports. Upon the complainant agreeing to submit the report, the forum directed the insurer to pay the deducted amount of Rs. 800.

Claims for cataract surgery were settled after deducting Rs. 20,000 each due to the use of multi-focal IOL lenses instead of standard aspheric lenses. The forum found a reasonable lens cost could be covered and ordered a partial payment of Rs. 14,000.

A claim for hormonal therapy expenses following breast cancer treatment was rejected on the grounds that hormonal therapy is not payable. The treating doctor certified it was necessary to prevent bone metastasis. The forum ruled the repudiation unjustified and the complaint succeeded.

Insurer settled mediclaim by deducting amount invoking room rent limits and proportionate scaling based on initial sum insured before enhancement. Ombudsman held room rent capping incorrectly applied to initial sum insured, but upheld pre-hospitalization deduction, partially allowing the complaint.

Insurer repudiated claim for iron deficiency anemia invoking exclusion clause 4.6. Ombudsman observed that anemia and hypothyroidism do not form part of exclusions under the policy and blood transfusion was not even given. Insurer's decision was unjustified and complaint succeeded.

Insurer deducted amount from cataract surgery claim based on old policy terms restricting cataract to 10% of sum insured. Insured claimed enhanced benefits. Ombudsman held that increased sum insured had a waiting period and old terms applied to initial sum insured, so insurer was justified.

Insurer repudiated claim alleging insured was absent during investigation and failed to submit indoor case and treatment papers. Ombudsman noted that verifying facts and examining evidence required legal processes beyond the forum's scope, hence complaint was deemed outside jurisdiction.

Insurer rejected osteoarthritis treatment claim invoking exclusion clause 4.3 for specified diseases having a waiting period of four years. Since the policy was incepted recently and treatment occurred in the first year within the waiting period, the insurer was justified.

Claim for cataract operation was delayed in intimation. Through mediation by the forum, both parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement amount, resolving the grievance without a formal award.

Claim lodged for acute pyelonephritis and fever was unsettled by the insurer. Through mediation, the parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement, amicably resolving the dispute without a formal award.

Claim was partially settled invoking limits on charges other than main hospital bill linked to room rent category. Through mediation, the parties mutually agreed on a balance payment for full and final settlement, requiring no formal award.

Claim was rejected due to variations in room charges and inflated bills. Through forum mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a specified amount for full and final settlement, resolving the dispute amicably.

Claim was settled based on capped No Claim Bonus (NCB) of 30% under the 2007 policy terms. Complainant argued for higher NCB based on long continuity. Ombudsman held insurer was justified in capping NCB at 30% per revised policy terms.

Claim was repudiated for fraud and misrepresentation regarding illness and treatment after hospitalization for acute gastroenteritis showed discrepancies in treatment pattern and fake receipts. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim repudiated because treating hospital failed to meet minimum bed criteria and hospital stay was unwarranted as patient remained afebrile with negative widal test. Insurer's decision was upheld.
Claim repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary for knee aspiration and plaster following a scooter fall. Consulting doctors had not advised hospitalization. Complaint failed.

Claim rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion based on degenerative meniscal injury. Evidence and medical certificates confirmed injury was post-traumatic resulting from a fall from stairs two months prior. Insurer produced no contrary evidence. Complaint succeeded.

Claim repudiated as hospitalization was unnecessary and treatment was an OPD procedure for high blood pressure and nose bleeding. Investigation report confirmed no need for admission. Complaint failed.

Claim for prostatitis was repudiated as it fell within the two-year waiting period. Insured argued continuous renewal from past insurers, but current insurer did not treat previous policy as continuous. Insurer's decision was justified.
Claim was repudiated due to late intimation and document submission. Through forum mediation, the parties mutually agreed to a settlement amount and signed an agreement, requiring no formal award.
Insurer paid 75% of claim invoking a special policy clause capping joint replacement surgery at 75% of sum insured. Actual claim was well within this limit of 75% of sum insured. Complaint succeeded.
Insurer deducted a large amount from hospital bills without providing any reasons or justification during hearings. Forum directed insurer to pay the deducted amount. Complaint succeeded.

Insurer deducted amount citing illness during 30-day lock-in and non-disclosure of past claim. Treating physician certified current fever had no relation to past illness. Insurer failed to prove documentary evidence of relation. Complaint succeeded for the disputed amount.
Circumcision performed to cure ballooning of prepucial skin was rejected under exclusion 4.4.2. Ombudsman found the surgery necessary for treatment of illness, not cosmetic, and allowed the claim.

Claim repudiated as investigator found patient absent from the hospital and admitted in general ward while special room charges were claimed, converting OPD treatment into hospitalization. Insurer justified in rejecting.
Claim repudiated due to exorbitant delay of more than three months in submitting intimation of hospitalization against policy requirement of 7 days. Insurer's decision upheld.

Insurer deducted Rs.12,026 citing waiting period for congenital internal disease. Treating doctor certified diabetes ketoacidosis is not congenital. Policy commenced in 2003, making the two-year waiting period inapplicable. Complaint succeeded.
Claim of Rs.3,10,159 was unsettled. Through mediation, both parties mutually agreed to a full and final settlement of Rs.1,05,000.
Insurer deducted Rs.3,200 because the consulting fee was paid separately in cash. Internal circular allows cash payments up to Rs.10,000 if part of hospitalization bills. Deduction found unjustified.
Insurer deducted Rs.4,400 for O.T Ultra strips as non-medical. Blood sugar tests required before perianal abscess surgery are payable. Complainant eligible for Rs.2,762 out of the disputed amount.
Reimbursement claim remained unsettled for over six months although Rs.13,066 was admitted as payable. Insurer directed to expedite preparation of the payment float.
Claim for liver transplantation due to Wilson's disease repudiated under clause 4.15 as Wilson's disease is a genetic/hereditary disorder causing copper overload. Repudiation upheld.

Ayurvedic treatment for fissure and fistula taken in the second policy year was rejected under waiting period exclusion and clause 2.1 requiring treatment in a government hospital. Complaint dismissed.

Surgery at an ayurvedic clinic for fissure and fistula in the second policy year excluded under clause 4.3 and clause 2.1. Complainant failed to produce previous policies to prove 6-year continuity. Decision justified.

insurer: Star Health And Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim rejected stating Ayurvedic treatment could be taken on an OP basis. Policy terms do not exclude Ayurvedic treatment from purview, hence rejection set aside and full claim ordered.
Claim for Tuberculosis hospitalization rejected under clause 1 as records proved insured suffered from pulmonary Kochi's for 3 years and PHO-RA for 5 years prior to policy inception. Decision upheld.

Claim partially settled by disallowing Rs.18,400 based on new revised terms linking benefits to room rent ceiling of 1% of sum insured. Since policy was continuously renewed from 2006 for initial sum insured of Rs.50,000, new terms could not apply. Insurer directed to pay full amount.

Claim under Janta Mediclaim policy partially settled by treating surgery as an intermediate surgery and paying according to fixed schedule of expenses for room, OT, anesthesia, and surgeon fee. Complaint dismissed.

Claim partially settled by restricting surgeon and anesthetist fees to internal guidelines not disclosed in policy terms. Insurer must inform insured of changes in terms and conditions. Complaint succeeded for deducted Rs.15,800.

First hospitalization claim rejected for lack of necessity and second for lack of intimation. Continuous treatment without break justified continuous intimation, and papers submitted within 30 days. Insurer directed to pay Rs.26,904.

Claim for blood cancer treated after sum insured was increased from Rs.15,000 to Rs.1,00,000 was settled only for original sum insured plus bonus. Revised policy terms excluded cancer treatment for the first policy year of increased sum insured. Complaint dismissed.

Pre and post hospitalization expenses for diabetes, high blood pressure, and ischemic heart disease disallowed because they were routine medicines not directly related to prostate surgery. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: Cataract surgery claim of Rs.25,109 settled for Rs.7,500 based on policy schedule C-6 limiting cataract treatments. Contention of unawareness of terms rejected. Insurer decision justified.

Insured was hospitalised for left knee osteoarthritis. The claim was submitted with all requisite documents but was neither settled nor rejected for months, constituting a deficiency in service due to inordinate delay.

Claim was partially settled by disallowing amounts under room charges and medical fees due to higher room rent selection under the revised 2007 policy. Ombudsman noted senior citizens cannot be forced to migrate to revised policies to their disadvantage, making old terms applicable.

Insured underwent CABG and claim was partially settled. Insurer disallowed increased sum insured portion because the insured suffered from diabetes prior to the sum insured increase in 2005 and 2009 without disclosure or extra premium.

Claim for right breast Gynecomastia surgery was repudiated under clause 4.5 alleging cosmetic purpose. An independent specialist opined it was a medical condition and removal was not cosmetic, so insurer was directed to pay.

Claim for reimbursement of oral chemotherapy and diagnostic tests was repudiated under clause 3.4 because oral chemotherapy without hospitalization is not covered, as the policy only covers parenteral chemotherapy without 24-hour hospitalization.
Claim for morbid obesity treatment was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.19 and the dismissal was upheld.

Dispute over non-consideration of cumulative bonus. The insurer explained that cumulative bonus is withdrawn on renewal if there was a claim in the preceding year, and it was kept on the policy bond by mistake.

Claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease prior to policy inception. The special master policy terms covered all pre-existing diseases after 30 days without needing declaration, making the repudiation unjustified.

Hospitalization claim for accidental knee injury was repudiated because treatment papers showed it was handled on an OPD basis with oral medicines, and required X-ray and CT scan reports were not submitted.

Total knee replacement claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing arthritis where discharge summary dates appeared altered. The forum noted verifying hospital records required legal procedures beyond its jurisdiction.

Claims under hospital cash and health policies were rejected and policies cancelled because investigation revealed gross discrepancies, fabricated nursing charts, and dates where the patient was not admitted, indicating a fraudulent claim.

Claim for treatment of fracture, paralysis, and hypertension was rejected because hospitalization was only for applying a plaster cast and nursing care/physiotherapy without active regular treatment, rendering hospitalization unnecessary.

Claim for acute gastroenteritis was repudiated because physical verification showed the patient was not in the hospital, records were missing, and medical opinion indicated discharge occurred before standard treatment duration, pointing to a fraudulent claim.
Chemotherapy claim for ovarian cancer was closed as 'no claim' due to non-submission of vital histopathology reports to verify pre-existing cancer history dating prior to policy inception.

Claim for urinary tract infection and cystitis was denied under pre-existing condition exclusions based on a past cystoscopy. The ombudsman found the insurer focused incorrectly on past unrelated tests and ignored treating doctor clarifications.

Claim for hysterectomy was repudiated because there was a policy break of over two months before renewal, treating the policy as fresh and invoking a two-year waiting period clause for genito-urinary surgeries.
Cataract surgery claim was partially paid, deducting expenses incurred prior to 30 days and miscellaneous hospital/medicine charges. Ombudsman ordered payment for unjustified deductions.
Claim for acute pancreatitis hospitalization within policy period remained unsettled. Insurer failed to attend hearing, and the ombudsman ordered settlement within 30 days.
Malaria hospitalization claim was initially delayed because the nursing home's criteria were doubted, but was later paid. Complainant's demand for interest for the delay was dismissed.

Complainant claimed a proportional refund of premium after mediclaim cards were supplied 11 months late and policy renewal was denied due to a change in corporate agent. The complaint was dismissed as the delay caused no financial loss.

Insured was hospitalized for severe abdominal pain and vomiting. The claim was repudiated on the ground that admission was primarily for investigations without active treatment. Ombudsman held that doctors decide hospitalization and ordered payment.

Insured suffered a heart attack abroad and claimed expenses under an overseas mediclaim policy. Insurer repudiated for non-disclosure of adverse medical history and alleged tampering of records by complainant. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as it required legal proceedings beyond its jurisdiction.

Group health claim for chronic renal failure hospitalization was closed by TPA due to non-submission of required documents. Complaint filed beyond the one-year limitation period after insurer's final reply, hence outside the forum's jurisdiction.

Minor sons met with a road accident while riding a motorcycle and sustained injuries. Claim was rejected because minors driving a motorcycle constituted an unlawful activity resulting in self-intentional injury.

Insured underwent Laproscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy for morbid obesity. Claim was rejected under the policy exclusion for obesity treatment. Insured contended it was life-saving due to cardiac risk, but records confirmed principal diagnosis was morbid obesity.

Insured claimed reimbursement for dental treatment following an alleged accidental fall from a staircase. Insurer rejected the claim stating treatment was for chronic abscess, dental hospitalization was unnecessary, and no accidental fall was mentioned in records.

Insured hospitalized for Acid Peptic Disease. Claim rejected due to discharge summary noting chronic alcohol consumption. Treating doctor certified ailment was unrelated to alcohol. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount.
Claim for daughter's thyroglossal cyst excision rejected by TPA and insurer on the ground that it was a congenital external disease excluded under policy terms.

Continuation of case where daughter's thyroglossal cyst was rejected as a congenital external disease. Ombudsman noted the cyst was internal and not external, and the policy had run for two years, making repudiation unjustified.

Claim for father's hospitalizations involving various neurological and gastrointestinal complaints rejected under pre-existing hypertension clause. Insurer claimed hypertension duration was four years, while family stated two years. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount.

Insured hospitalized for Acute Febrile Illness. Claim partially paid after insurer deducted amounts exceeding the room rent and nursing charges limit of 1.5% of the sum insured per day. Insurer's deduction upheld.

Senior citizen insured was diagnosed with T-cell Lymphoma and underwent chemotherapy shortly after policy inception. Insurer repudiated claim alleging intentional concealment of pre-existing cancer symptoms.

Continuation of case where senior citizen's claim for T-cell Lymphoma was rejected for non-disclosure. Records showed pre-authorization and medical history confirming cancer symptoms existed before taking the policy and answering negative in proposal form. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for abdominal hysterectomy rejected on the ground of a two-year waiting period, treating the policy as fresh due to a 10-day break during renewal.

Continuation of hysterectomy claim rejected due to a brief 10-day renewal gap. Ombudsman noted the policy explicitly marked the period as renewed, and the short break did not justify treating it as a fresh policy, ordering settlement.

Claim for pre-hospitalisation expenses partially disallowed because they were incurred beyond the 30-day limit permitted by the policy. Insured's contention that surgery was delayed due to uncontrolled blood pressure was unsubstantiated.

Claim for C5-C6 Anterior Cervical Disectomy rejected on grounds of pre-existing disease based on a case sheet noting a two-year history of neck pain. Since the discharge summary lacked this detail and insurer produced no clinching evidence, rejection was set aside.

Claim for inpatient admission to administer Remicade injections for ankylosing spondylitis rejected on the ground that it was a day-care procedure possible under OPD. Ombudsman ruled that inpatient admission was justified due to severe potential side effects requiring monitoring.

Claim for heart surgery due to Aortic Valve Disease restricted to 20% of sum insured because panel doctor opined bicuspid aortic valve with stenosis was a congenital internal disease, subject to specific policy limits after two years.
Claim for surgery for bilateral gynaecomastia in an 18-year-old rejected under policy exclusion for cosmetic or aesthetic treatments, as biopsy was not performed to establish malignancy.

Insured was hospitalized for elbow injury. Insurer restricted claim citing pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Ombudsman found no clinical evidence supporting the diabetes duration claim and directed full settlement based on current sum insured.
Insured hospitalized for giddiness and evaluation. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion clause for evaluation not followed by active treatment. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.
Insured claimed hospital cash for an extended 86-day stay following burn injuries. Insurer restricted payment to 12 days based on medical opinion. Ombudsman upheld insurer's restriction.

Wife of insured hospitalized for hysterectomy. Insurer restricted claim to 20% of sum insured based on revised policy terms introducing caps for specified ailments. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's application of policy terms.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS Gen Ins Co Ltd
facts: Insured's mother diagnosed with advanced stomach carcinoma shortly after policy inception. Insurer rejected claim under pre-existing/30-day exclusion clause due to prior symptoms of dyspepsia. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: Star Health Allied Insurance Co Ltd
facts: Insured's wife hospitalized for ankle fracture. Insurer deducted certain charges deemed excessive as reasonable and customary. Ombudsman noted lack of specific caps in policy terms and directed insurer to rework and settle balance.
Claim lodged for outpatient treatment of adenomyosis. Insurer rejected claim as minimum 24-hour hospitalization requirement was not met and treatment was on OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the dismissal.

Insured met with an accident in Belgium and underwent surgery. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing wound. Ombudsman noted local TPA gave prior approval for operation and applied principle of estoppel, directing full settlement.

Insured hospitalized for CAD and hypertension. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing condition based on high initial BP reading. Ombudsman relied on subsequent medical clarification that high BP was reactionary, directing claim processing.

Insured hospitalized for acute low backache and treated by orthopedic surgeon. Insurer rejected claim stating hospitalization was for investigation only and medicine bills were missing. Ombudsman found investigations part of treatment and awarded claim.
Insured alleged non-payment of cumulative bonus while settling claim. Insurer agreed during hearing to pay the accrued bonus. Ombudsman directed payment with penal interest.

Insured's daughter admitted for emergency headache and loss of consciousness. Insurer repudiated claim stating treatment could be taken as OPD. Ombudsman found hospitalization genuine under doctor's advice and ordered payment.

Insured treated for acute necrotizing pancreatitis with colonic leak. Insurer rejected claim under alcoholism exclusion based on investigator's report. Ombudsman reviewed medical expert opinion on records.

Policy lapsed after excessive premium increase. Complainant requested restoration for elderly mother insured since 1992. Ombudsman suggested issuing a fresh policy waiving waiting periods on payment of premium.
TPA approved claim but payment was not released due to administrative negligence. Ombudsman directed immediate payment with penal interest.
Claim repudiated due to delay in submission caused by TPA's change of address. Insurer admitted claim was medically admissible otherwise. Ombudsman directed payment with penal interest.

Claim rejected because hospital was removed from insurer's approved list after policy inception. Ombudsman held policyholder cannot be bound to specific hospitals and ordered payment with penal interest.

Claim closed by insurer due to non-compliance of information requested from insured. Ombudsman noted inordinate delay and lack of specific reason, ordering payment up to sum insured with penal interest.
Post-hospitalization expenses not settled despite hospitalization expenses being paid under cashless. Ombudsman found no justification and ordered payment.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for angioplasty and bypass surgery rejected on pre-existing hypertension and CAD grounds. Conflicting medical expert opinions regarding duration of arterial blockage.

Insured changed insurers after four continuous years without break. Hospitalized for chest pain and underwent coronary angiography and stent placement. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension and first-year policy status. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage since 2004 and ordered full payment with interest.

Hospitalized for cardiac condition and unstable angina. Claim was initially rejected due to late submission caused by bed rest and being the sole adult male. During proceedings, insurer paid most of the claim amount. Ombudsman directed payment of interest on the delayed settlement.

Patient hospitalized for bi-polar disorder. Insurer deducted amounts from hospital and post-hospitalization bills alleging excessive charges and tariff mismatches. During proceedings, insurer agreed to pay an additional amount based on panel doctor opinion. Ombudsman upheld deductions for post-hospitalization while allowing extra relief for consultation.

Complainant contested excess or wrong charging of mediclaim premiums over several years and disputed unrequested TPA charges. Insurer agreed to provide detailed computation and relevant circulars. Ombudsman disposed of the complaint with directions to provide the premium working details.

Policyholder's son was admitted for a knee injury at a nursing home listed in the insurer's brochure. Insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that the hospital was not authorized. Ombudsman held the repudiation unjustified since the hospital was in the approved list and awarded the full claim with interest.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Hospitalized for acute intestinal obstruction caused by a fibrous band. Insurer rejected claim under permanent exclusion for congenital illnesses. Treating doctor clarified the band could have developed recently. Ombudsman held that congenital illness was not conclusively proven and ordered full reimbursement with interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Insured suffered sudden unconsciousness and was treated for CVA and neurogenic bladder. Cashless facility and reimbursement were denied based on a hospital record stating a three-year history of hypertension and seizures, recorded from an attendant's statement while patient was unconscious. Ombudsman found pre-existing hypertension was not established and ordered payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim remained unsettled for an extended period. During the hearing, it was verified that original payment receipts were indeed submitted. Insurer conceded the claim was admissible. Ombudsman directed immediate settlement of the claim with interest.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insured was treated for lesion and infection in the left breast. Insurer repudiated the claim claiming it was treatment for breast lumps within the initial two-year waiting period. Ombudsman noted the patient was treated for abscess and infection, not lumps, and ordered full payment with interest.

Father of the policyholder was hospitalized in an emergency at a hospital listed in the TPA's approved list. Insurer rejected the claim stating the hospital was not on their approved list. Ombudsman held the rejection was based on technical grounds and ordered full payment with interest.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Wife of the complainant was operated for bladder outlet obstruction. Insurer denied reimbursement alleging non-disclosure of a prior surgery for the same condition under a previous policy year. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage from 2005 across insurers and ruled the repudiation unjustified.

Wife of the complainant underwent hysterectomy. Insurer rejected the claim applying a two-year waiting period clause, treating the policy as fresh. Ombudsman observed the policy had been in continuous force since 2001 across various public insurers with accumulated benefits and ordered full payment with interest.

Complainant underwent hysterectomy. Insurer rejected the claim stating it was the second year of the policy and hysterectomy is excluded during the first two years. Ombudsman found the insurer had accepted continuity from a previous insurer without requiring a fresh proposal or medical tests, making the treatment fall into the third policy year, and ordered payment.

Son of the complainant suffered a dental injury from an accident and received outdoor treatment resulting in loss of teeth. Insurer rejected the claim because treatment was taken in OPD without hospitalization. Ombudsman noted hospitalization is not required for accidental dental treatments in OPD and ordered payment.

Claims for the treatment of the policyholder and his wife remained unsettled despite submission of requisite documents. Insurer failed to issue any formal decision. Ombudsman ordered payment of the claimed amounts along with penal interest.

Complainant underwent an eye operation after four years of continuous policy coverage and cumulative bonus accrual. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diminished vision based on hospital records. Ombudsman ruled the pre-existing disease clause inapplicable due to four years of continuous coverage and ordered payment with interest.

Insured was hospitalized for a fracture following a fall at home. Insurer repudiated the claim under pre-existing disease clause citing a history of post-polio residual paralysis from childhood. Ombudsman noted the hospitalization was due to an accidental fall and unrelated to polio, ordering full payment with interest.

Claims for hospitalization of the policyholder and his daughter were rejected because treatment was taken at a nursing home not on the insurer's approved network list. Ombudsman held that taking treatment outside networked hospitals is not a valid ground for rejection if treatment is genuine, and ordered payment with interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Complaint was filed regarding non-settlement of a mediclaim. During the proceedings, the insurer settled and paid the claim in full. Ombudsman disposed of the complaint as resolved.
Complaint was filed regarding non-settlement of a mediclaim. During the proceedings, the insurer paid the balance amount of the claim. Ombudsman disposed of the complaint as resolved.
Complainant filed a mediclaim grievance against the insurer. During the proceedings, the insurer settled the claim for Rs.9199, leaving no further relief to be granted.

Complainant sought reimbursement for son's hospitalization due to impending paralysis from possible disc prolapse. The insurer rejected the claim stating admission was only for investigation. The Ombudsman held the doctor's advice on admission is final, ordering payment of Rs.13842 with interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Complainant's wife sustained multiple and head injuries in an accident. Due to priority treatment for head injury, dental injury treatment was delayed beyond 60 days. The insurer rejected the claim based on the 60-day post-hospitalization limit. The Ombudsman ruled the delay was justified, ordering Rs.23652 plus interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for treatment and filed a claim. The insurer repudiated it on the ground that admission was for investigation only. The Ombudsman held the treating doctor is the best judge for admission and ordered payment of Rs.51048 with interest.

Complainant suffered severe accident injuries including fractures and unconsciousness, leading to delayed claim submission. The insurer closed the claim for late filing. The Ombudsman found sufficient reasons for the delay and ordered payment of Rs.41194 with penal interest.

Complainant sought reimbursement for pre and post hospitalization expenses. The insurer rejected the claim alleging documents were received beyond 90 days. The Ombudsman noted documents were actually submitted within the stipulated 90 days and ordered payment of Rs.4760 with penal interest.

Complainant's wife was treated for right sacroilitis and discogenic pain in the fifth year of continuous health cover. The insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing. The Ombudsman ruled that continuous insurance from prior insurers negated the pre-existing clause and ordered payment of Rs.31627.

Complainant was treated for pilonidal abscess and hospitalized. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 3 relating to fistula in anus. The Ombudsman held that pilonidal abscess is not specifically excluded and ordered payment of Rs.35352 with interest.

insurer: Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Complainant raised a grievance regarding non-settlement and policy errors. Upon intervention, the insurer corrected the policy endorsement as desired, and the complaint was closed.

Complainant's wife was treated for anxiety neurosis and pus. The insurer repudiated the claim citing exclusion 4.8 for anxiety disorder. The Ombudsman noted anxiety neurosis was not explicitly excluded under the policy and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

Insured was hospitalized and diagnosed with anxiety neurosis with panic attack and nasobronchial allergy. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clauses for psychiatric disorders and diagnostic examinations. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Future Generali India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for status epilepticus after a previous attack prior to policy inception, which was not disclosed in the proposal form. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion 3.1 and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman upheld the denial and closed the complaint.

Complainant was hospitalized for pus with malaria. The claim was closed due to insufficient documents regarding previous treatment and prolonged hospitalization justification. The Ombudsman found settlement process irregularity and directed a fresh decision within 15 days.

Complainant incurred Rs.805404 for cardiac treatment against a sum assured of Rs.500000. The insurer partially settled the claim at Rs.300000 without justification. The Ombudsman found the deduction unjustified and directed the insurer to reconsider and settle the claim afresh.

Complainant was treated twice for alcoholic hepatitis. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.4.6 relating to alcohol-related diseases. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as regular and closed the complaint.

Complainant lodged a claim for Rs.85803, of which hospital bills worth Rs.23958 were paid as cashless. The balance was pending due to non-submission of original USG report, final bill, and money receipt. The Ombudsman directed completion of settlement upon document submission.

Complainant's wife underwent angioplasty. The insurer rejected the claim because she had hypertension for 15 years and diabetes for 5 years, and heart diseases had a 5-year waiting period. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife underwent surgery for piles in the second year of the policy. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing disease based on a discharge summary note. The Ombudsman found no corroborative medical evidence for long-standing piles and allowed the complaint.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant paid premium for an employee's health policy to an unverified person via debit card and cheque. The insurer had no record of the transaction. The Ombudsman held the insurer had no liability for transactions with an imposter and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant claimed Rs.192031 for hospitalization and Rs.44840 for pre/post hospitalization for cancer treatment. The TPA restricted settlement to Rs.127000 by applying group capping and limits. The Ombudsman ordered re-processing by splitting the IMRT package expenses across groups.

A claim for hysterectomy was rejected due to a short renewal gap, which the Ombudsman found was caused by administrative delays within the insurer's office. Relief was granted as the policy had long continuity since 2004.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A senior citizen policyholder sought treatment for Metabolic Encephalopathy and seizures. The insurer repudiated the claim under the pre-existing disease clause, which was upheld by the audio evidence establishing non-disclosure at inception.

The insured underwent Urethroplasty and submitted a bill. The insurer rejected it alleging fraud due to conflicting hospital bills. The Ombudsman found the reasonable treatment cost was 40000 and ordered partial payment.

A claim for D&C procedure was rejected because it was purely for evaluation and diagnostic purposes without an active line of treatment requiring 24 hours hospitalization. The insurer's decision was upheld.

The insured underwent bilateral cataract surgeries and claimed actual expenses. The insurer applied the policy's monetary cap of 7500 per policy period for cataract. The complaint against the fixed limit was dismissed.

A claim for renal problem and dialysis was rejected as pre-existing hypertension. The Ombudsman noted the insured was unaware of mild hypertension during policy inception and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

A claim under an Arogyadaan policy for a 70-year-old dependent was rejected on age eligibility and pre-existing grounds. The insurer agreed to settle during the proceedings, leading to an allowed outcome.

A claim for CABG surgery was repudiated on the ground that Coronary Artery Disease was a complication of pre-existing hypertension. Medical evidence supported the absence of prior hypertension, and the claim was allowed.
Hospitalization for loss of consciousness involving diagnostic MRI tests was rejected due to policy break and lack of active medication. The Ombudsman awarded MRI charges as ex gratia.

Claims for acute coronary syndrome were rejected due to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Due to discrepancies in proposal filling and lack of policy endorsement, an ex gratia amount of 15000 was awarded.

Multiple claims for diabetic foot amputation, kidney problems, and heart angioplasty were delayed and contested. Pre-existing diabetes was established, but an ex gratia award was granted for the heart treatment.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for hysterectomy due to ovarian cyst was rejected as a pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman ruled that continuous prior insurance from 2005 nullified waiting periods and exclusions, ordering full payment.

After paying 70% of the sum insured for a major cardiac surgery ceiling limit, the insurer rejected a second major surgery claim within the same policy year. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's limit interpretation.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Quantum Magnetic Resonance Treatment for osteoarthritis was rejected for pre-existing disease and lack of 24-hour hospitalization. An ex gratia award was granted because the insurer failed to reply to pre-treatment queries.
A fracture claim was rejected due to a four-month delay in submission, lack of discharge summary, and contradictory statements regarding the accident cause. The dismissal was upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder treatment was rejected under policy exclusions for psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization for abdominal pain resulting in a diagnosis of mild fatty liver was rejected because it involved only evaluation and oral medication without an active line of treatment.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Surgery for Gastric Outlet Obstruction was repudiated as a complication of prior chronic pancreatitis surgery. Due to ambiguity regarding direct nexus, an ex gratia amount was awarded.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for Quantum Magnetic Resonance therapy taken on an outpatient basis for knee and back pain were rejected as the policy mandates a minimum 24-hour hospitalization.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for spinal canal stenosis surgery was rejected under a two-year waiting period/exclusion clause for spinal disorders in the first renewal policy. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured daughter hospitalized twice for ovarian cyst complications. Insurer rejected claims citing policy exclusions and pre-existing disease due to past surgeries, and lack of active treatment. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as hospitalizations were for evaluation and related to past ovarian cyst problems.

Policyholder underwent CABG surgery and claimed reimbursement. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman noted evidence of PED was inconclusive and awarded Rs. 10,000 as ex-gratia.

insurer: Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's mother hospitalized after a road accident. Insurer repudiated daily cash claim alleging extended stay post discharge summary. During proceedings, parties agreed on settlement for 17 days, and Ombudsman allowed the complaint accordingly.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent brain tumour surgery. Insurer restricted settlement to original sum assured, ignoring the enhanced amount, claiming brain tumour was pre-existing. Ombudsman found tumor was detected after sum enhancement and ordered full settlement on enhanced sum.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent nasal surgery at a non-network hospital. Cashless was denied and reimbursement was partially cut for surgeon, OT, and laser charges. Ombudsman noted deductions were arbitrary but the bill was slightly excessive, awarding Rs. 25,000 as ex-gratia.

Insured underwent hernia surgery and claimed Rs. 63,394. Insurer restricted payment to 15% of sum insured (Rs. 30,000) as per policy condition for hernia. Ombudsman held the insurer applied policy terms correctly and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's mother underwent total knee replacement for osteoarthritis. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing disease based on hospital record. Ombudsman found lack of substantial evidence for PED and awarded Rs. 1,00,000 as ex-gratia.

TPA proportionately reduced hospital expenses because the insured occupied a room above his entitled category. Ombudsman ruled proportionate cuts on charges not varying with room rent were unjustified and ordered payment of deducted amount minus room rent difference.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's mother underwent cytotron therapy for osteoarthritis during hospitalization. Insurer repudiated claim under unproven treatment exclusion. Ombudsman noted treatment was not proven to be unproven/experimental and ordered full payment with interest.

Insured was hospitalized and diagnosed with chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalization was solely for diagnosis/evaluation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured hospitalized for treatment within 105 days of previous illness. Insurer repudiated claiming sum assured was exhausted under previous policy terms. Ombudsman held enhanced sum assured was not available for same illness within 105 days, allowing partial claim under previous balance.

Insured took treatment for duodenal ulcer at home and raised domiciliary hospitalization claim. Insurer repudiated as patient's condition did not warrant domiciliary treatment per policy conditions. Ombudsman upheld repudiation and dismissed complaint.
