Insured hospitalized for osteoporosis with compression fracture. Claim rejected as hospitalization was primarily for investigations/evaluation without active treatment. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.
Insured hospitalized for ovarian cystectomy within 30 days of policy inception. Insurer rejected claim under initial 30-day waiting period exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for cancer chemotherapy and medications were partially rejected due to missing prescriptions, bills not in patient's name, and expenses exceeding pre/post hospitalization limits. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant filed against partial settlement of mediclaim. During proceedings, the TPA approved and agreed to pay the balance claim amount, closing the complaint.

Insured underwent Enhanced External Counter Pulsation (EECP) for IHD on an outpatient basis. Claim rejected as unproven treatment and lack of 24-hour hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld rejection of EECP charges but directed insurer to reimburse other admissible investigation expenses.

Insured hospitalized for chest pain for less than 24 hours. Claim repudiated for lack of 24-hour stay and alleged unnecessary hospitalization. Ombudsman noted valid cardiac treatment and allowed 85% of hospitalization expenses plus post-hospitalization costs.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Limited
facts: Complainant challenged partial settlement of right eye cataract surgery. Following Ombudsman's direction, the insurer settled both eye surgery claims in full.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Limited
facts: Insured's wife diagnosed with breast cancer shortly after sum insured was enhanced. Insurer restricted claim to original sum insured plus bonus, treating breast lump as pre-existing at enhancement. Ombudsman reviewed case regarding policy enhancement terms.

Insured underwent surgery for calculus and urinary tract infection during the first year of the group policy. Insurer rejected the claim based on a two-year waiting period clause. Due to an administrative error in supplying old policy terms, the Ombudsman awarded a 50% ex-gratia payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife underwent laparoscopic myomectomy in the second year of the policy. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.3 for diseases contracted within the first two years. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured sought reimbursement for intravitreal injections administered for eye treatment, which the TPA rejected as an OPD procedure not requiring hospitalization. The Ombudsman evaluated medical evidence supporting that such eye injections require an operation theatre environment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Limited
facts: Complainant claimed for hospitalization due to acute pelvic inflammatory disease in the second year of a renewed policy following a previous policy cancellation due to a bounced premium cheque. The insurer rejected the claim based on a two-year waiting period exclusion, which the Ombudsman upheld.

Insured with a history of an old leg injury and implant removal suffered a new fracture from an accidental fall. The insurer rejected the claim based on policy exclusions. The Ombudsman awarded 50% of admissible expenses giving the benefit of doubt regarding pre-existing conditions.

Insured was hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction with severe coronary artery stenosis. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension and a two-year waiting period. The Ombudsman noted hospital records confirming long-standing hypertension.

Insured's daughter underwent LASIK surgery for high myopia. The insurer rejected the claim as a cosmetic or aesthetic procedure. The Ombudsman noted medical evidence showing high myopia constituted a severe visual disability rather than mere cosmetic correction.

insurer: Royal Sundaram General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant treated for hypertension and memory loss after holding a policy continuously for over six years. The insurer rejected the claim for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman allowed the claim based on IRDA guidelines covering pre-existing conditions after four claim-free years.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent a hysterectomy and cyst removal. The insurer rejected the claim citing treatment for infertility as an excluded disease. The Ombudsman observed the surgery was unrelated to infertility and ordered full payment with interest.
Complainant hospitalized for a leg injury resulting from an accident and incurred expenses. The insurer delayed payment of the claim. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay the claim amount.

Complainant was hospitalized for menorrhagia with lower abdominal lump and uterine fibroids. The insurer repudiated the claim on the ground of pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman held that continuous policy renewal since 2006 precluded the pre-existing disease argument.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for acute thigh pain due to herpes infection and claimed expenses. The insurer rejected the claim under a clause excluding diagnostic or laboratory investigations. The Ombudsman held that since hospitalization was for treatment rather than tests, medicine costs were payable while diagnostic charges were excluded.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant underwent bypass surgery after previously undergoing angiography, following which the insurer had endorsed the policy to exclude heart disease. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection since the complainant accepted the policy with the exclusion.

Insured hospitalized for myocardial infarction and claim was rejected due to alleged pre-existing hypertension of 8 years. The Ombudsman noted continuous prior insurance coverage and lack of proof of pre-existing hypertension, ordering claim payment.

Complainant underwent surgery for hernia and filed a claim that was initially closed. During proceedings, the insurer settled the claim for the full sum insured, leading to dismissal of the complaint.

Two claims for a son's bone fracture treatment were rejected, the first for delayed document submission and the second due to rejection of the first. The Ombudsman noted treatment continued post-discharge and ordered both claims to be paid.

insurer: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co Ltd.
facts: Insured employee hospitalized for gall stone disease and claimed expenses. The insurer repudiated the claim citing an exclusion for the first policy year, but settled the claim prior to the Ombudsman hearing.

Insured's son hospitalized for persistent diarrhea. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing malnutrition and anemia. The Ombudsman found no evidence of prior treatment and ordered payment with interest.

Insured's daughter underwent LASIK laser treatment for myopia. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 4.3 as cosmetic and aesthetic surgery. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured with four years of continuous policy renewal had a claim rejected on grounds of pre-existing alcoholism and self-medication. The Ombudsman ordered claim payment as the insurer failed to provide evidence of prior treatment.

insurer: United India General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent knee replacement surgery incurring Rs. 3,80,000. Insurer paid Rs. 2,00,000 based on the policy clause capping major surgeries at 70% of sum insured subject to a maximum of Rs. 2,00,000. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as justified under policy terms.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insured's husband hospitalized for brain hemorrhage and passed away, incurring Rs. 3,37,356. Insurer repudiated claim citing history of heart ailment seven years prior. Complainant argued the brain hemorrhage was a sudden and new disease unrelated to past conditions.

Insured's wife underwent hip surgery following a car accident. Insurer repudiated the claim under duty of disclosure and fraudulent claims clauses, stating the policy was made effective prior to the date the proposal was received by the branch.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insurer repudiated a claim on the ground of late filing. Ombudsman noted the claim was filed within 30 days of the MRI test date and ruled the rejection was on flimsy grounds, awarding Rs. 3,000 with penal interest.

Insurer repudiated mediclaim because treatment was taken in an emergency at a hospital outside the approved list. During the hearing, the insurer's representative agreed the claim is payable. Ombudsman ruled rejection on technical grounds was unjustified and awarded Rs. 45,701 with interest.

Insurer rejected cataract surgery claim because the hospital was outside the approved list. Ombudsman held that treatment in a government-registered hospital cannot be denied on technical grounds and awarded Rs. 18,300 with penal interest.

Claim for cancer treatment was repudiated due to delayed submission beyond 30 days and initial cashless denial. Ombudsman found delay justified as the insured was busy with funeral ceremonies following his wife's demise and awarded Rs. 1,39,119 with interest.

Motor vehicle accident claim repudiated because the driver's license was reported fake. Complainant provided verification from RTO Agra showing the license was valid. Ombudsman ruled the insurer was not justified and ordered payment as assessed by the surveyor.

Mediclaim repudiated under two-year waiting period for gall bladder stones. Ombudsman observed that although diagnosed with cholecystitis, the patient was not treated for stones and expenses were mainly for investigations, making the claim admissible. Awarded Rs. 20,238 after deducting consumables.

Claim for enteric fever treatment repudiated under fraudulent claim clause due to alleged variations in documents and patient statements. Ombudsman found no evidence of misrepresentation and awarded Rs. 24,765 with penal interest.

Complainant alleged delay in settling mediclaim. Insurer stated cheque was issued earlier, but later issued a fresh cheque in January 2010 as the first became stale. Ombudsman awarded penal interest for delayed payment from September 2009 to January 2010.

Mediclaim for urinary tract infection and dehydration treated in an emergency at a nearby hospital was repudiated because the hospital was outside the approved list. Ombudsman ruled rejection on technical grounds unjustified and awarded Rs. 24,964 with penal interest.

Reimbursement for cataract surgery rejected because treatment was taken at a hospital not on the insurer's panel. Ombudsman ruled technical rejection invalid and directed payment of Rs. 20,654 with penal interest.

Insurer withheld claim settlement demanding original bills, while complainant had already submitted originals and later provided duplicates. Ombudsman held duplicate bills are as authentic and ordered payment of Rs. 1,77,000 with penal interest.

Insurer partially settled a mediclaim, cutting diagnostic charges, miscellaneous fees, and registration charges, and citing unlisted hospital. Ombudsman held diagnostic charges and fees were payable and awarded Rs. 2,660 plus interest.

Emergency mediclaim for son's treatment at a Delhi government-registered nursing home was treated as no claim because the hospital was not on the insurer's list. Ombudsman held rejection on technical grounds unjustified and awarded Rs. 8,558 with interest.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for acute renal failure, dengue, and dialysis was closed by TPA for want of treating doctor certificate and OPD papers. Insurer agreed to settle during hearing. Ombudsman directed payment of Rs. 71,291 plus post-hospitalization consideration.

Claim for scalp injury treatment requiring stitches after a fall was repudiated on the ground that 24-hour hospitalization was not required (minor surgery). Ombudsman held the claim was admissible and awarded Rs. 5,728 with penal interest.

Claim for hospitalization due to severe arm pain, dizziness, and numbness was repudiated on the ground that treatment could be done on OPD basis. Ombudsman held that the insurer has no role in deciding treatment mode against treating doctor's advice and awarded Rs. 60,386 with interest.

Cashless and reimbursement claims for bypass surgery and TVD were repudiated on pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of hypertension since 2005. Complainant contended continuous coverage since 2000 across insurers without break.

Insured was hospitalized for chronic liver disorder. Insurer repudiated the claim alleging pre-existing cirrhosis of liver and alcohol intake. Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existing disease or alcohol abuse and ordered full payment of Rs. 45563/-.

Insured met with an accident and incurred expenses for treatment at multiple hospitals. Insurer partially settled the claim by paying Rs. 60962/- out of Rs. 139690.77/- without valid reasons for deductions. Ombudsman directed payment of the balance Rs. 78732/- with 8% interest.

Claim for cataract surgery was repudiated on the ground that it fell within the 2-year waiting period of the new policy, ignoring continuity from previous insurer. Ombudsman held that continuity benefits apply and ordered payment of Rs. 28207/- with 8% interest.

Claim for treatment of MCA Infarct with Hemorrhage was denied because it occurred in the first year of the policy. Ombudsman held there is no waiting period for this disease and ordered payment of Rs. 300000/-.

Claim was repudiated solely because treatment was taken at a hospital not on the insurer's approved list. Ombudsman held the hospital met requisite conditions and ordered payment of Rs. 36223/- with 8% interest.
Claim was repudiated because the treating hospital had 7 beds instead of the required 15. Ombudsman noted the hospital was registered with the State Government and ordered payment of Rs. 23986/-.

Group mediclaim was repudiated because treatment was taken at a hospital not on the panel list for Delhi. Ombudsman held the hospital was registered and ordered payment of Rs. 33786/- with 8% interest.

Claim was denied because treatment was taken at a hospital outside the approved list. Ombudsman held that a registered hospital's treatment cannot be denied on technical grounds and ordered payment of Rs. 21598/- with 8% interest.
Claim was repudiated due to late intimation and late submission of documents. Ombudsman noted continuous policy history since 2004 and ordered payment of Rs. 26977/- with 8% interest.

Claim was repudiated because treatment was taken at a nursing home outside the approved list. Ombudsman ruled that valid treatment at a registered hospital cannot be rejected on technical grounds and ordered payment of Rs. 20751/- with 8% interest.

Cataract surgery claim was rejected because the hospital was not empanelled for cashless treatment. Ombudsman held reimbursement is permissible at any registered hospital and ordered payment of Rs. 10750/- with 8% interest.

Claim was repudiated because treatment was taken outside the approved list of hospitals. Ombudsman held the claim is payable at any registered hospital and ordered payment of Rs. 21918/- with 8% interest.

Claim was repudiated because treatment was not taken in a network hospital. Ombudsman held the claim cannot be denied on technical grounds for a registered hospital and ordered payment of Rs. 28491/- with 8% interest.
Claim for son's hospitalization was rejected for want of documents. Ombudsman noted documents were already submitted and ordered payment of Rs. 8268/- with 8% interest.

Claim for brain surgery was repudiated as pre-existing because symptoms arose prior to the Reliance policy inception. Ombudsman held continuity from previous insurer since 2004 applied and ordered payment of Rs. 56318/- with 8% interest.

Insurer restricted claim to Rs. 1500/- arguing hospitalization was solely for investigation and unnecessary. Ombudsman noted admission was on doctor's advice for over 24 hours and ordered payment of the balance Rs. 20704/- with 8% interest.

Claim for cardiac treatment was repudiated on the ground that necessary documents were not submitted. Ombudsman found documents were submitted and continuous insurance existed since 2000, ordering payment of Rs. 178800/- with 8% interest.

Insurer deducted part of the claim relating to dental and nose treatment following an accident. Ombudsman held that treatment was part of accident injuries on doctor's advice and ordered payment of the balance Rs. 6250/- with 8% interest.
Insurer made deductions from cataract surgery claims for insured and spouse under policy clause 2. Ombudsman found deductions unjustified and ordered payment of the balance Rs. 25025/-.

Claim for hepatitis treatment was rejected because the hospital was not on the panel list. Ombudsman held rejection on technical grounds for an emergency inadmissible and ordered payment of Rs. 24158/- with 8% interest.

Insured underwent gall bladder surgery and other treatment at a hospital outside the insurer's approved list and intimated the claim late. The ombudsman held that repudiation on technical grounds of non-approved hospital is not justified and ordered settlement with interest.

insurer: IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Insured claimed penal interest for delayed settlement of mediclaim policies by over a year. The ombudsman found the delay unjustified and awarded penal interest at 8% on the already paid amounts.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Motor vehicle theft claim was repudiated due to late intimation, failure to safeguard, and failure to deposit both keys (only one received from previous owner). The ombudsman found the reasons unjustified and awarded IDV with interest.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Father of complainant was hospitalized for chronic liver disease in the second month of a comprehensive parental medical policy. Insurer repudiated on pre-existing grounds. The ombudsman noted the policy covered pre-existing conditions without waiting periods and ordered full sum insured payment.
Insurer partially settled a mediclaim and withheld a balance amount citing delayed submission of documents. The ombudsman held the entire claim payable and directed payment of the balance amount.

Twin children were born during the policy year and notified for inclusion under a family group health plan. Insurer repudiated the newborn's hospitalization claim citing the 30-day waiting period from formal inclusion. The ombudsman ruled that coverage applied from birth and ordered reimbursement.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Mediclaim reimbursement for OPD consultation was rejected due to late submission. The ombudsman held that the claim cannot be denied merely for minor delay in filing and awarded the claimed amount.

Spouse of complainant was hospitalized for brain tumor (meningioma). Insurer repudiated claim under first-year exclusion of benign tumors. The ombudsman noted the tumor was malignant/meningioma and not benign, hence payable, and ordered reimbursement with interest.

TPA partially approved cashless hospitalization for kidney stone treatment, forcing the patient to pay the remainder and sign a no-claim letter. The ombudsman held the full hospital cost payable and ordered reimbursement of the out-of-pocket amount with interest.

Insurer partially paid a mediclaim, rejecting expenses for a CPAP machine, pulse oximeter, and a sleep study bill lacking proper receipt. The ombudsman upheld deductions for equipment but allowed the sleep study cost since a valid bill was produced.

Mother of complainant was hospitalized, but TPA closed the claim file without notice due to delayed document submission while policyholder was studying abroad. The ombudsman found the closure improper and ordered payment with interest.

Mediclaim was repudiated because treatment was taken at a nursing home outside the insurer's approved list. The ombudsman held that claims cannot be rejected on technical grounds of non-network hospitals and awarded the amount with interest.

Cataract surgery claim was rejected because treatment was taken at a nursing home not on the insurer's newly introduced approved list. The ombudsman ruled against technical rejections and awarded the claim with interest.

Son of complainant underwent surgery at a hospital outside the approved network list. Insurer repudiated the claim. The ombudsman held that rejection on technical non-network grounds is unjustified and ordered payment with interest.

Coronary angioplasty claim under Parivar Mediclaim policy was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.3 for chronic diseases. The ombudsman held that successfully treated conditions are not chronic and ordered full reimbursement.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
facts: Child's hospitalization claim for back pain investigation was repudiated on the grounds that treatment could have been managed via OPD. The ombudsman held that attending doctors are the best judges for admission and ordered payment with interest.

insurer: IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Limited
facts: Mediclaim was treated as 'no claim' with vague reasons regarding the duration of knee stiffness and pre-existing ailments. The ombudsman held the claim payable up to the sum assured including bonus.

Hospitalization claim for acute myocardial infarction was repudiated for alleged suppression of diabetes history. The ombudsman held that the insurer failed to substantiate suppression with evidence and awarded the claimed amount with interest.

Employer-provided mediclaim was closed by insurer on the grounds that hospital admission was not required. The ombudsman held that admission is based on doctor's prescription and ordered payment excluding pre-hospitalization costs.

The insured incurred pre and post hospitalization expenses which were repudiated for late submission beyond 30 days. The Ombudsman held that minor delay does not justify rejection and ordered full payment with interest.

Claim was repudiated alleging fraudulent hospitalization and inflated bills without concrete evidence. The Ombudsman noted that treatment at a network hospital during the policy period was undisputed and ordered full payment with interest.

Claims for the insured's wife were repudiated citing clause 4.1. The Ombudsman observed that the policy was in continuous force for over 12 years without break, making the clause inapplicable, and awarded the claimed amount subject to verification of a prior cheque.

The insurer rejected a claim for surgical treatment of an infected toe on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary as it could be done on the same day. The Ombudsman ruled that the insured followed medical advice and allowed the full claim.

The insurer made deductions under various expense caps while settling a mediclaim. The Ombudsman held that such caps were introduced after the policy inception and were not applicable, ordering payment of the balance amount.

A claim for Multiple Myeloma chemotherapy treatment was rejected because there was no 24-hour hospitalization. The Ombudsman held that day-care chemotherapy for cancer does not require 24-hour hospitalization and allowed the claim.

The insurer repudiated the claim because treatment was taken at a hospital outside the approved list. During the hearing, the insurer's representative conceded the claim was payable. The Ombudsman ordered full payment.

The insurer rejected the claim on the grounds of a pre-existing disease assuming the policy started in 2001. Evidence showed the policy was active prior to 2001 with cumulative bonuses. The Ombudsman ordered full payment with interest.
The claim was rejected because the treating hospital was not in the approved list. The Ombudsman held that admissible claims cannot be rejected on technical grounds and ordered payment with interest.

Initially rejected for non-approved hospital, the insurer later made a partial payment without explanation. The Ombudsman held the technical ground invalid and ordered payment of the balance amount with interest on both parts.
Post-hospitalization expenses claim was rejected for being filed a few days after the 7-day post-treatment submission window. The Ombudsman held the claim admissible and ordered payment.
Claim in the third policy year was repudiated for pre-existing disease without supporting evidence. The Ombudsman ruled that the policy was in continuous force since 2007 and ordered full payment.
The insurer deducted non-medical items during claim settlement. The Ombudsman reviewed the items and allowed reimbursement for admissible items while upholding deductions for items like thermometers.
The complainant sought post-hospitalization expenses, admitting a minor portion was spent outside the treating doctor's prescription. The Ombudsman allowed the admissible portion of the claim.

Cashless claim for angioplasty was rejected citing a 2-year waiting period for hypertension complications. The treating doctor clarified it was an emergency life-saving procedure for CAD and not related to prior hypertension. The Ombudsman ordered full payment with interest.

The insurer restricted the claim to a lower sum insured based on waiting periods and prior policy limits. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's limit of Rs. 40,000 and ordered payment of the remaining balance upon submission of a discharge voucher.

Due to agent error, a renewal payment resulted in a new policy issuance causing a break and claim denial. The Ombudsman granted continuity benefits as the premium was paid in time, ordering full payment.

The claim was rejected under a 2-year waiting period clause, ignoring prior continuous coverage with another insurer. The Ombudsman held that continuity benefits must apply and ordered payment with interest.
The insurer repudiated the claim because treatment was taken in a non-listed hospital. The Ombudsman ruled that valid claims cannot be rejected on technicalities and awarded payment with interest.
The mediclaim was settled belatedly months after document submission. The Ombudsman awarded penal interest for the delayed settlement.

Insured claimed reimbursement for wife's treatment of septicemia with URTI. Insurer repudiated claiming the hospital lacked a ventilator and registration, and alleged fraud. Ombudsman found no evidence of fraud and that the hospital was registered, awarding the full claim of Rs. 84,474 with interest.

Complainant sought reimbursement for pancreatic cancer treatment expenses. Insurer partially paid, restricting amounts based on a 50% sum insured cap for chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Ombudsman found caps were misapplied and awarded an additional Rs. 1,18,750 with penal interest.

Insured's hospitalization claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing diabetes and non-disclosure. Ombudsman noted diabetes was detected after policy inception and the illness was caused by bacteria, ruling the repudiation unjustified and awarding Rs. 1,03,051 with interest.

Claim was repudiated because there was an 18-day break in policy renewal, treating it as a fresh policy where pre-existing complications were excluded. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to the continuity break and lack of proof that the disease developed during the active period.

Complainant underwent angioplasty and claimed Rs. 4,43,849. Insurer settled for Rs. 2.00 lacs applying a sub-limit cap of 70% or Rs. 2 lacs for major surgeries. Complainant encashed the cheque despite protest. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as the settlement was accepted voluntarily without fraud.

Insured underwent cardiac operations and had claims restricted based on revised policy terms and conditions introduced in 2007. Insured argued unilateral changes were invalid. Ombudsman held that the insurer applied terms approved by IRDA correctly and dismissed the complaint.

Pre-authorization and reimbursement for angioplasty were rejected on grounds of pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of hypertension and heart history. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as the insured failed to disclose material facts.

Reimbursement for hospitalization due to swollen feet was rejected because treatment involved only oral medications and evaluation without an active line of treatment. Ombudsman found hospitalization was primarily for evaluation but awarded an ex gratia of Rs. 5,000 for pain management.

Claim for coronary angioplasty within two months of policy inception was rejected under the 30-day waiting period and pre-existing disease clauses. Ombudsman held that 100% arterial blockage must have existed prior to policy inception and dismissed the complaint.

Hospital cash insurance claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes noted in hospital records. Complainant submitted altered/notarized discharge summaries to change the duration of diabetes. Ombudsman found evidence inconclusive regarding tampering but awarded an ex gratia of Rs. 1,500.

Claim for CABG surgery was rejected because the policy was shifted from another insurer with a break in renewal, causing loss of pre-existing disease coverage. Ombudsman upheld the rejection under policy exclusion clauses.

Post-hospitalization claims for oral chemotherapy tablets taken at home and diagnostic scans without subsequent hospitalization were rejected. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as policies do not cover oral chemotherapy or outpatient diagnostics without hospitalization.

Claim for treatment of fever leading to a hysterectomy and ovarian mass removal was rejected under a first-year policy exclusion for cysts and hysterectomy. Ombudsman upheld the exclusion for gynecological procedures but allowed expenses related to fever treatment and appendicectomy.
Claim for bilateral ovarian cysts surgery was rejected under the pre-existing disease clause, as hospital records indicated past hysterectomy and cystectomy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for enhanced sum insured following incisional hernia surgery was rejected because the waiting period for hernia and rules for enhanced sum insured applied as a fresh policy. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for spinal cord AVM embolisation was rejected as a congenital disorder, and the policy was subsequently cancelled for non-disclosure of hypertension and filariasis. Ombudsman upheld both the rejection and policy cancellation.

Claim for QMR therapy for osteoarthritis of both knees was rejected because the treatment was administered on an outpatient basis without 24-hour hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's rejection.

Claim for Total Knee Replacement was paid only up to the old sum insured, while the enhanced sum insured portion was rejected based on waiting periods for joint replacements and fresh policy rules. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim for outpatient treatment of facial lacerations due to a road traffic accident was rejected because the policy requires hospitalization exceeding 24 hours. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Complainant sought reimbursement for RFQMR therapy for knee osteoarthritis. Claim was rejected under policy exclusions.

The insured underwent QMR therapy on an out-patient basis with no indoor admission or 24-hour hospitalization. The insurer rejected the claim because the treatment did not involve hospitalization, and the Ombudsman upheld the decision as terms of the policy strictly require in-patient hospitalization.

The insured enhanced the sum insured of the mediclaim policy, but the insurer restricted settlement to the original sum insured following a Total Knee Replacement surgery, citing restrictions on pre-existing diseases and unauthorized enhancement. The Ombudsman ruled that the insurer could not arbitrarily restrict the sum insured after accepting the higher premium and directed full settlement.

The insured filed two claims for abdominal pain hospitalizations. The insurer rejected both, claiming admissions were solely for diagnostic evaluation rather than active treatment. The Ombudsman allowed the first claim considering the patient's critical condition and need for diagnosis, but dismissed the second hospitalization claim since it involved only diagnostic tests like a colonoscopy.

The insurer rejected the first claim for late submission and the second claim because hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman found the delay for the first claim justified and awarded it as ex gratia, but upheld the rejection of the second claim due to the minimum 24-hour hospitalization requirement not being met.

The insured was hospitalized for severe headaches, but the insurer rejected the claim stating there was no active line of treatment and admission was primarily for diagnostic tests. The Ombudsman observed that hospitalization was largely for investigation but awarded an ex gratia amount.

The insured was hospitalized for fluctuating blood pressure and blood sugar levels. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that admission was for evaluation rather than active treatment. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection under the policy exclusion for evaluation, but awarded token ex gratia because the TPA had misled the insured with an initially issued and later withdrawn pre-authorization.

The insured underwent bypass surgery shortly after obtaining the policy and undergoing a medical check-up. The insurer rejected the claim as a pre-existing disease based on pre-medical ECG findings. The Ombudsman noted the insurer had technical justification for repudiation, though the insured had no prior knowledge.

The insured claimed reimbursement for total knee replacement surgeries for his wife. The insurer rejected the first surgery claim because the hospitalization predated policy inception, and the second surgery claim as a pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint due to lack of proof for the initial premium payments and valid policy terms.

The insured's wife and daughter were hospitalized for food poisoning, and the insurer short-settled their reimbursement claims without reasons. During proceedings, the insurer re-evaluated the claims and offered additional amounts. The Ombudsman allowed the complaint based on the revised settlement agreed by the complainant.

The insured's daughter was treated for typhoid fever at a center. The insurer rejected the claim stating that the facility lacked in-patient infrastructure and treatment was administered on an out-patient basis without 24-hour hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

The insured was hospitalized for GB Syndrome shortly before the policy premium was realized and the policy formally commenced. The insurer rejected the claim because the hospitalization occurred prior to inception. The Ombudsman upheld the decision as cover only began upon premium receipt.

The insured's wife underwent incisional hernia surgery, which the insurer rejected under a general pregnancy exclusion because it traced back to a prior caesarean section. The Ombudsman ruled that specific time-bound waiting periods for hernia applied, and general exclusions could not override specific policy provisions after continuous renewal, allowing the claim.

The insured contested short-settlement of his bypass surgery expenses by the insurer. The Ombudsman reviewed various disallowed deductions, upholding package-rate limits for angiograms and weight-control exclusions for specific diagnostic tests, but directed the insurer to make good shortfalls regarding restricted day counts and unjustified room rent deductions.

The insured's wife underwent a total thyroidectomy after long-standing neck swelling and hypothyroidism. The insurer repudiated the claim for non-disclosure of material facts at the time of proposal. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection because pre-existing hypertrophy and hypothyroidism were undisclosed.

The insured underwent treatment for end-stage renal disease and a solitary kidney. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension and chronic kidney failure dating back years. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the current illness was a continuation of a pre-existing condition.

The senior citizen insured underwent laser treatment for an enlarged prostate gland, and the insurer limited payout to the policy cap for benign prostatic hyperplasia. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's liability restriction as per the specific policy terms, dismissing the complaint.

The insured was hospitalized with severe chest pain, and the insurer rejected the claim stating the admission was only for evaluation without active treatment. The Ombudsman noted that modification of medications constituted active treatment and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

The insured's father suffered a cardiac event, underwent bypass surgery, and passed away shortly after. The insurer repudiated the critical illness benefit claim because the insured survived for only 13 days, failing to meet the mandatory 30-day survival period condition. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

The insured was hospitalized for severe knee joint pain, but the TPA rejected cashless treatment alleging treatment for morbid obesity. The Ombudsman found that the patient was treated for osteoarthritis rather than obesity and that the insurer had wrongfully rejected the reimbursement claim, directing full settlement with interest.

The insurer partially settled a hospitalization claim but disallowed an advance payment made to the hospital because a pre-numbered receipt was not provided. The Ombudsman ruled that demanding a separate advance receipt when the local hospital did not issue one was unjustified and ordered payment of the disallowed amount.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for intestinal obstruction. Insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing disease due to a previous LSCS surgery in 2003. Ombudsman noted no evidence of symptoms or treatment within 48 months prior to policy inception, held the repudiation unjustified, and allowed the complaint.

Complainant sought reimbursement for hospitalization due to severe low back pain. Insurer repudiated the claim stating there was no active line of treatment and hospitalization was merely for evaluation and investigation. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Policyholder raised claims for ulcer burst treatment. Insurer repudiated the claims citing pre-existing illness and alcohol-related complications based on a 2007 discharge summary mentioning chronic alcoholism and smoking. Ombudsman concluded the current ailment was related to pre-existing conditions and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for CAD and underwent CABG. Claim was rejected because medical history showed 14 years of diabetes and 12 years of hypertension, which were suppressed in the proposal form. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's justification for repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insurer rejected a surgical reimbursement claim citing a pre-existing ailment and alleged correction in the discharge summary duration from 2 years to 2 months. Ombudsman found the correction bona fide by the treating doctor and directed the insurer to pay Rs.10,025 with 9% interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim under group mediclaim policy was repudiated because treatment was taken in a private ayurveda hospital instead of a government hospital. Ombudsman noted policy amendments permitting registered private hospitals up to 25% of sum insured and directed partial reimbursement.

Complainant underwent a full body check-up and claimed Rs.4,500, but insurer paid only Rs.1,000 citing a 1% sum insured restriction. Ombudsman found no such restriction in the issued policy contract and directed the insurer to pay the balance of Rs.3,500 with interest and costs.

Complainant sought reimbursement for hospitalization for severe low back pain. Insurer repudiated the claim citing no active line of treatment and mere evaluation/investigation. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

insurer: HDFC Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured suffered a back injury from an accidental fall and underwent surgery. Insurer repudiated under first two years exclusion and alleged suppression of pre-existing back pain and osteoporosis. Ombudsman found clear evidence of accidental fall and directed reimbursement of Rs.44,783 with interest.

Claim for hysterectomy was rejected by the insurer under the one-year exclusion policy period. Ombudsman verified that hysterectomy falls under the policy's exclusion clause for the initial period and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for benign ovarian cyst surgery was repudiated because it occurred within two years of policy inception, violating clause 4.3. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant alleged partial payment of mediclaim bills. Insurer stated balance amount was withheld pending supporting medical reports and doctor's prescriptions. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand due to missing documents and dismissed the complaint.

Insured was hospitalized for angina within four months of policy inception. Medical records indicated illness duration of six months and diabetes for a year, falling under pre-existing exclusion clause 4.1. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim was initially rejected under the pre-existing disease clause. During the hearing, the insurer expressed willingness to settle the claim up to eligibility if bills were submitted. Ombudsman allowed the complaint directing settlement upon bill submission.

Insurer rejected a hospitalization claim for severe headache, vomiting, and leg swelling on the ground that only oral medication was administered. Ombudsman noted hospitalization was required for observation and MRI under doctor's advice, allowing the claimed amount of Rs.7,870.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim under employee group mediclaim was rejected because the employee ceased employment prior to hospitalization. Ombudsman noted premium was retained and coverage cancellation was only communicated later, rendering the denial invalid. Complaint allowed.

Claim for incisional hernia treatment was denied on grounds of a previous alleged surgery 1.5 years prior. Ombudsman found no proof of such prior surgery and ruled the insurer unjustified in denial, allowing the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant submitted a bill for Rs.1.51 lakhs after enhancing sum insured from Rs.15k to Rs.1L, but insurer settled only Rs.15k due to pre-existing heart ailment treated in 2004. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's limitation to the original sum insured and dismissed the complaint.

Claim for intravitreal injection for eye hemorrhage under local anesthesia in operation theatre was rejected on the ground that it could be done on OPD basis. Ombudsman held that TPA cannot arbitrarily decide on hospitalization need against medical advice and allowed the complaint.

Claim was rejected because only oral medicines were given during a five-day hospitalization for severe ear and shoulder pain. Ombudsman noted observation was justified based on MRI scan findings and directed the insurer to settle the claim.

The complainant's wife underwent surgery for fibroid uterus. The insurer partially paid hospital cash but repudiated major surgical benefit claiming fibroid uterus was not a major surgery. The Ombudsman noted it fell under major surgeries and allowed 50% surgical benefit.

The insured submitted hospital claims which were rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing liver cirrhosis with portal hypertension and diabetes prior to policy inception. Medical records proved prior illness. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim was repudiated on the grounds that hospital admission was for investigation only and not medically necessary. The Ombudsman observed that the patient was admitted on doctor's advice for severe hypertension and set aside the insurer's decision.

Claim for fibroid uterus surgery was rejected under 2-year waiting period clause since it arose in the second year of the policy. The Ombudsman referred the case back to the insurer to check continuity benefits from a previous policy.

Claim for congenital hip dysplasia (DDH) surgery was rejected as a pre-existing congenital condition. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision since bilateral flat foot and limping gait were congenital and existed prior to policy inception.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for diabetes and UTI treatment was repudiated for pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman noted the policy was over 3 years old and previous claims for diabetes were honored without objection, setting aside the repudiation.

Complainant contested partial settlement for angioplasty after sum insured enhancement. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision to restrict the claim to the previous lower sum insured because the heart condition was diagnosed before enhancement.

Complainant sought review of partial deductions on pre and post-hospitalization claims for breast cancer treatment. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to provide bill-wise disallowance reasons quoting policy conditions.

insurer: Apollo Munich Health Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim was partially disallowed for items like external halo brace appliances, private nursing charges, and day care MRI. The Ombudsman upheld the exclusion of the halo brace as an external equipment rather than an internally implanted device.

Claim for pacemaker implantation due to sick sinus syndrome was repudiated for pre-existing hypertension and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman found no medical evidence of long-standing hypertension and set aside the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim was partially settled after disallowing doctor fees due to lack of numbered money receipts. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to pay additional amounts as per revised policy clauses allowing doctor fees paid by cash.

Complainant alleged delay in settlement for gastroenteritis and cardiac treatment. It was revealed that the cheque had already been encashed prior to filing the complaint. The complaint was dismissed as false.

Claim for respiratory distress was repudiated on the ground that hyperventilation was a psychosomatic illness excluded under the policy. The Ombudsman held that psychological origin was not conclusively established and set aside the repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for laminectomy surgery was partially disallowed for cash doctor fees and missing bills. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to settle the claim based on a newly submitted revised bill and awarded interest for delayed processing.

Claim for angioplasty was heavily cut by the TPA under capping limits. The complainant submitted a detailed expense break-up during the hearing, and the Ombudsman directed the insurer to resettle the claim based on the new break-up.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for stroke (CVA) treatment was rejected due to pre-existing hypertension of 10 years. Initial hospital forms recorded a 10-year history, and echocardiography showed left ventricular hypertrophy indicative of chronic hypertension. Repudiation was upheld.

Claim for breast cancer treatment was repudiated because the policy had a break in continuity and had not run continuously for the mandatory 4 years with the current insurer. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Claim for incisional hernia and hysterectomy in the second policy year was repudiated under the 2-year waiting period clause for specified diseases. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for electrolyte imbalance and associated symptoms was repudiated as treatment for psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders (anxiety neurosis). The Ombudsman found the treatment matched psychiatric medication and upheld the dismissal.

Claim for exploratory laparotomy was repudiated as a pre-existing condition based on long-standing abdominal pain history. The Ombudsman noted the policy rolled over from a continuous previous policy and directed the insurer to reconsider continuity.

Insured was hospitalised for acute myocardial infarction in the second policy year. The insurer repudiated the claim invoking the two-year waiting period for ailments related to pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for left inguinal hernia was repudiated because the insured had a history of past right-sided hernioplasty and ailment duration prior to policy inception, which was not disclosed in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Claim for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy for metabolic syndrome/obesity was repudiated under exclusion for cosmetic or aesthetic treatment. Ombudsman decision text is incomplete in the snippet.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for hospitalisation and death due to post-operative complications following hemicolectomy was closed as no claim due to non-submission of hypertension history and indoor papers. The Ombudsman set aside the closure and ordered settlement.

First-year claim for carotid artery aneurysm was repudiated as a congenital anomaly and pre-existing condition subject to waiting periods. The Ombudsman ordered an independent medical specialist review.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for facial cellulitis was closed as no claim for want of investigation reports proving staphylococcus infection and indoor case papers. The Ombudsman found the nursing home had faxed papers and ordered settlement.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Maternity claim was repudiated under a 9-month waiting period clause. The Ombudsman noted continuity benefits applied from a previous policy with another insurer and directed full settlement.

Claim for hospitalisation diagnosed as neurolept syndrome was repudiated because treatment was primarily for psychiatric disorders and obesity-related pain manageable at home. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for laparoscopic cholecystectomy for calculus cholecystitis in the first policy year was repudiated under the two-year waiting period for gall bladder surgery. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Partial repudiation of claim for replacement of loose acetabular component following an accidental fall, where enhanced sum insured restrictions for pre-existing arthritis were applied. Ombudsman decision text snippet cuts off.

Complainant alleged partial settlement and non-payment of multiple chemotherapy bills across two policy periods for colon carcinoma. The Ombudsman referred unaddressed bills back to the insurer for payment according to policy terms.

Claim for short hospitalisations for administering Decapeptyl injections for multiple fibroid uterus was rejected on the ground that treatment could be done as an outpatient. The Ombudsman set aside the decision and ordered payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Claim for pacemaker replacement was repudiated on the ground that the pacemaker was implanted before policy inception. Without the original proposal form to prove non-disclosure, the Ombudsman gave the benefit of doubt to the insured and ordered ex-gratia payment.

Claim for coronary angioplasty was repudiated alleging non-disclosure of past chest pain based on a hospital history note. The Ombudsman found no irrefutable evidence or corroborating medical reports and set aside the repudiation.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insurer paid 50% of hospital expenses, disallowing coronary angiography costs on the ground that normal ECG made it unnecessary. The Ombudsman held that treatment decisions rest with the treating doctor and ordered full payment.

Claim for green stick fracture reduction under general anaesthesia was repudiated because hospitalisation was less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman ruled it qualified as day care treatment and instructed the insurer to honour the claim.

Claim for emergency respiratory disorder and nose bleeding was repudiated because treatment was taken in a non-network hospital. The Ombudsman noted the emergency admission and directed the insurer to honour the claim.

Travel insurance claim for overseas treatment of spinal stenosis, haemorrhoids, and lipoma was rejected on pre-existing grounds based on symptom duration. The Ombudsman ordered 50% reimbursement as a borderline case.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for hysterectomy was short-settled due to room rent caps, OT charge proportions, and cash payment limits for surgeon and anesthetist fees. The Ombudsman ordered additional payment for anesthetist fees and OT charges.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Personal accident death claim following an accidental head injury slip was repudiated because death was due to renal and heart failure without post-mortem. The Ombudsman granted partial relief noting the fall contributed to complications.

Insured underwent Ossiculoplasty with Titanium Chain Prosthesis. The insurer partially settled the claim by disallowing the cost of the titanium prosthesis under exclusion 4.4.4. The Ombudsman held that internal prosthetics are admissible and ordered full payment.

Insured claimed for Total Knee Replacement surgery. Insurer restricted surgeon fees to 25% of the basic sum insured, omitting the cumulative bonus. The Ombudsman ruled that cumulative bonus must be added to the sum insured for calculating limits.

Spouse of the complainant was hospitalized for vertigo. Insurer repudiated the claim stating treatment was on OPD basis. The Ombudsman held that given the patient's age and symptoms, hospitalization was justified and directed settlement.

Maternity claim under a group policy was denied due to lack of prior intimation of hospitalization. The Ombudsman noted that claim papers were submitted on the third day after discharge and held the denial unjustified.

Overseas mediclaim for mother who died abroad was rejected on the ground that her heart failure was a complication of pre-existing hypertension. The Ombudsman found no medical connection established to hypertension and awarded medical and funeral expenses.

Child underwent cochlear implant for sensorineural hearing loss. Insurer repudiated the claim under an exclusion for hearing aids. The Ombudsman noted that cochlear implant is a surgical internal device, not an external hearing aid, and set aside the repudiation.

Claims for gall bladder stone surgery within the first two years of the policy were rejected under specific waiting period exclusions. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as the policy had no continuous prior coverage.

Claim for wide excision of soft palate lesion was partially settled with major deductions in surgeon and anaesthetist fees. The Ombudsman awarded an additional amount for surgeon fees and directed coverage of pre-existing conditions after long continuous policy years.

Claim for retinal detachment surgery was repudiated because the insured had previously undergone cataract surgery, which is explicitly excluded along with related problems. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on policy exclusions.

Laptop damage claim under a Portable Electronic Equipment Policy. Insurer incorrectly offered settlement on constructive total loss. The Ombudsman ordered settlement on repair basis plus a penalty for improper handling.

Mediclaim was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing cancer. The Ombudsman held that cancer was detected after taking the policy and no evidence showed it existed prior, ordering payment of the claim.

Mediclaim for train accident injuries was rejected because documents were submitted past the stipulated date. The Ombudsman noted documents were initially submitted to the insurer instead of the TPA and directed payment.

Group mediclaim for Ayurvedic treatment was denied under policy clause excluding Ayurvedic treatment. The Ombudsman noted treatment was taken at a recognized hospital under therapy and directed payment.
Claim for daughter's knee injury hospitalization was severely cut by the TPA due to room rent restrictions. The Ombudsman held the restrictions unjustified and awarded the balance amount.
Inadequate settlement of mediclaim due to room rent and registration charge deductions. The Ombudsman recalculated the payable amount according to policy terms and awarded the balance.
Partial settlement of mediclaim with a balance withheld for missing test reports. The Ombudsman found all documents were submitted and awarded the balance with interest.
Overseas mediclaim for treatment of hyponatraemia in Canada was repudiated for pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman found symptoms appeared weeks after policy inception and ordered payment.
Mediclaim for hospitalization was delayed due to allegations of missing documents. The Ombudsman found requisite documents were submitted and ordered full payment of the claim.
Mediclaim was repudiated because treatment was taken at a hospital outside the approved list. The Ombudsman held that admissible claims cannot be declined on technical grounds and ordered payment.
Heart attack and angioplasty claim was rejected on grounds of non-disclosure of past history. The Ombudsman found the insurer's rejection unjustified and ordered payment.

The insured's wife was hospitalized twice for treatment. The insurer repudiated the claims invoking exclusion clause 4.8. The Ombudsman found the exclusion inapplicable and ordered full payment of the claim.

The insured claimed reimbursement for dental injuries sustained by his daughter due to trauma. The insurer rejected the claim stating the establishment was not a hospital and hospitalization was not required. The Ombudsman held that trauma injuries do not require hospitalization and ordered full payment.

The insurer rejected a mediclaim for the insured's daughter on the ground that the treatment was conservative and could be done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman noted the patient was admitted due to prolonged recovery and family distress, and ordered the insurer to pay the full claim amount.

The insured sought settlement of a hospital bill following a leg injury due to a fall. The insurer delayed and failed to settle the remaining balance due to bill cuttings. The Ombudsman found the claim payable, deducting prior cashless payments and registration charges.

The insured was admitted to the hospital under doctor's advice due to continuous pain for evaluation. The insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary and for evaluation only. The Ombudsman held the claim payable as tests were advised by a doctor to ascertain illness.

Following an accidental fracture and surgery, the insured claimed post-hospitalization expenses. The insurer only paid a partial amount. The Ombudsman directed payment of the balance amount excluding doctor's home visit charges.

A senior citizen policyholder was hospitalized for excess bleeding through stool. The insurer rejected the claim because hospitalization was less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman held that the 24-hour stay requirement was unnecessary for this condition and awarded the claim.

The insured sought reimbursement under an overseas mediclaim policy for emergency diarrhea treatment in the USA. The insurer repudiated the claim due to delayed intimation. The Ombudsman ruled the claim payable as the insured had shared policy details with the foreign hospital and expected cashless settlement.

The insured met with a motorcycle accident causing a leg fracture and was treated at a clinic without 24-hour hospitalization due to remote location. The TPA denied the claim for lack of 24-hour admission. The Ombudsman ruled that hospitalization is not mandatory for accident injuries and awarded the claim with interest.

The insured's wife underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy. The insurer repudiated the claim because there was a 7-day break in policy renewal when shifting from another company's individual policy to a Swasthya Bima policy. The Ombudsman condoned the delay caused by the bank and directed full payment.

The insured's wife was hospitalized following a road traffic accident resulting in an elbow fracture. The TPA partially paid and repudiated the balance due to non-submission of documents and disallowed expenses related to pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. The Ombudsman held that accident treatment papers suffice and ordered the balance payment including pre-existing condition expenses.

The insured was hospitalized and treated for depressive psychosis, which the insurer rejected under exclusion clause 4.8. Conflicting medical records showed initial treatment for acute amoebic hepatitis and subsequent psychiatric diagnosis. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision technically but awarded an ex-gratia amount for the hepatitis treatment.

The insured's wife was hospitalized for a lower lumbar spine ligament injury. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion 4.10 for evaluation/diagnostic admissions without active treatment. The Ombudsman noted excessive investigation costs but awarded 50% on an ex-gratia basis since admission was on doctor's advice.

The insured's wife underwent surgery for a large ventral hernia. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion 4.12, claiming it was a complication of a past caesarean section. The Ombudsman gave the benefit of doubt to the insured based on the treating gynecologist's opinion that the hernia was unrelated to pregnancy, setting aside the repudiation.

The insured sought reimbursement under an overseas mediclaim policy for mouth ulcer treatment in the USA. The TPA rejected the claim as time-barred, misreading the US date format (MM/DD/YYYY). The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim with penal interest for delayed settlement.

The insured's son underwent surgery for painful gynaecomastia. The insurer restricted the claim to the original sum insured of Rs. 50,000, arguing non-disclosure of a 5-year pre-existing condition when enhancing the sum insured. The Ombudsman upheld restricting the sum insured but directed recalculation including cumulative bonus.

The insured's son was hospitalized for abdominal pain and vomiting, initially diagnosed with cholelithiasis. The insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion 4.4.11 for investigation-only admission since later tests showed no gallstones. The Ombudsman upheld the exclusion for cholelithiasis but awarded partial payment for antibiotic treatment of other acute symptoms.

The insured was hospitalized for NSTEMI and underwent PTCA and stenting. The insurer offered a partial settlement of Rs. 77,230, which the complainant rejected as insufficient. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to review calculations, correct discrepancies, and include cumulative bonus.

The insured underwent an intravitreal Avastin injection for BRVO with macular edema. The insurer repudiated the claim based on an internal circular excluding Avastin for ARMD/eye treatments. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's policy terms but awarded an ex-gratia amount due to a service lapse in omitting the exclusion stamp on the policy document.

The insured's wife underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy. The insurer delayed settlement and subsequently lost the submitted claim documents due to office repairs and staff changes. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim based on photocopies of documents provided by the complainant.

Claim was closed by the TPA due to delayed submission of documents. The insured had experienced postal delays in receiving the deficiency letter and submitted all papers subsequently. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to re-open the file and settle the claim.

Claim for sigmoid colon treatment was repudiated on the ground of pre-existing disease based on a doctor's remark of six months prior duration. The insurer failed to produce conclusive clinical evidence of prior onset. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation and allowed the claim.

Partial payment was made for bilateral ovarian cyst surgery, and the balance for surgeon fees was disallowed for un-numbered receipts. The complainant submitted proper bank statements and numbered registrations proving payment. The Ombudsman ordered full payment of the disallowed balance.

Claim for hernia repair was repudiated under pre-existing clauses because a three-day delay in paying service tax during renewal caused a policy break. The Ombudsman held that premium was paid on time and service tax is not premium, condoned the short delay, and allowed the claim.

Claim for obstructive sleep apnoea investigation involving a CPAP machine was rejected as non-admissible since it was for investigation rather than active treatment. Considering the advanced age and financial condition, the Ombudsman granted an ex-gratia amount.

Claim for total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for endometriosis was partly paid by applying a capping limit applicable to hysterectomy. The Ombudsman noted additional procedures were performed and granted an ex-gratia amount over previous settlements.

Claim for mastoidectomy operation was partly settled with deductions for room rent, doctor advice, and nursing charges. The Ombudsman instructed the insurer to pay the balance based on revised calculations adhering to policy limits.

Claim for road accident right elbow fracture surgery was partly disallowed due to capping limits on doctor fees across multiple receipts. The Ombudsman ruled that ceilings apply per doctor's bill and granted partial relief.

Claim for surgical removal of impacted wisdom teeth requiring two days hospitalization was repudiated under dental exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman held that the exclusion applies only to non-hospitalized dental treatments and allowed the claim.

Claim for intravitreal lucentis injections for subretinal neovascular membrane was rejected because the hospitalization was under 24 hours. Although technically correct under older administrative rules, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment given the medical necessity to prevent blindness.

Claim for severe hypertension and acute left ventricular failure was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension. Since hospital case history records were illegible and inconclusive, the Ombudsman gave the benefit of doubt and ordered a 50% settlement.

Hospital cash claim for viral fever leading to acute tonsillitis was repudiated under first-year exclusions for tonsil treatments. The Ombudsman noted the primary admission was for viral fever and ordered a 50% payout.

Claim for strangulated incisional hernia repair was repudiated because insurers linked it to a past caesarean section scar from decades prior. The Ombudsman found the hernia arose from a recent laparotomy scar as per discharge records and allowed the claim.

Claim for coronary artery disease and diabetes treatment was rejected due to a policy break caused by a dishonored renewal cheque and subsequent delay. Recognizing faults on both sides regarding communication, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount.

Claim for fatal septicemia related to lupus was partly paid because the sum insured was recently enhanced. The Ombudsman ruled that the four-year waiting period was satisfied since the condition was first diagnosed five years prior, making the enhanced sum insured applicable.

Claim for total hip replacement due to avascular necrosis was partly denied on the basis of a four-year waiting period for degenerative conditions on enhanced sum insured. The Ombudsman found the cause was idiopathic rather than degenerative and allowed the full claim.

Claim for total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy was capped at 20% of the sum insured. The Ombudsman observed that additional non-hysterectomy organ removals were performed as emergency life-saving procedures and granted an ex-gratia amount.

Hospital cash claim for post-operative wound infection following hysterectomy was denied due to pre-existing fibroids. The Ombudsman concluded the hospitalization resulted from surgical stitching failure rather than the pre-existing condition, and granted an ex-gratia payment.

Claim for severe abdominal pain and intestinal colic was closed as 'No Claim' due to alleged non-submission of documents. The Ombudsman found delays were compounded by ordinary post communications by the insurer and directed them to settle the genuine claim.

Claim for surgical excision of a mucous cyst on the lip was repudiated because the procedure could be done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman held that the patient followed direct medical advice for nursing home admission and set aside the repudiation.

Insured underwent implant removal following cervical spine surgery and a known history of renal cell carcinoma. The insurer repudiated under pre-existing disease exclusion clause 4.1. The Ombudsman noted continuous coverage since 2002 exceeded the 48-month waiting period, set aside the repudiation, and ordered full settlement.

Wife of the insured underwent cataract surgery and claimed reimbursement. The TPA repudiated the claim due to non-submission of specific documents such as the biometry report, discharge summary in proper format, and lens invoice. The Ombudsman found all necessary documents were submitted, held the repudiation unjustified, and ordered full payment.

Claim under group health policy was repudiated for delayed submission of documents. The insured explained the delay was due to her father's sudden death and subsequent illness. The Ombudsman condoned the delay, finding the reasons satisfactory, and directed the insurer to admit and pay the claim.

Insured was hospitalized for macular degeneration and administered Macugen injections. Cashless and reimbursement were denied based on a head office circular treating ARMD as an OPD procedure. The Ombudsman noted the circular post-dated policy renewal but allowed an ex-gratia payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for Avastin injections for CNVN/ARMD was repudiated based on a head office circular classifying it as OPD treatment. The Ombudsman noted the circular was issued before policy renewal making the rejection technically correct, but granted an ex-gratia award considering available treatments and fairness.

Insured was hospitalized for obstructive sleep apnoea and treated conservatively. The insurer repudiated under clauses relating to external devices and evaluation/diagnostic admission without active treatment. The Ombudsman found active treatment was administered, rejected total repudiation, and awarded an ex-gratia amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for laparoscopic cholecystectomy was rejected as pre-existing under the third-year policy on the erroneous assumption of a 4-year waiting period. The Ombudsman noted the correct waiting period for gall stone surgery is 2 years, acknowledged the insurer's error, and ordered claim settlement.

Insured was hospitalized following syncope attacks and treated for hyponatremia and depression. The claim was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was primarily for evaluation and diagnosis without active treatment. The Ombudsman noted mixed problems and awarded an ex-gratia payment.

Claim for appendectomy and myelodysplastic syndrome was partly settled, deducting costs for disposable kits and blood cross-matching on the ground they were not organ donations. The Ombudsman found the interpretation too narrow and awarded an ex-gratia payment due to financial hardship.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for low back pain treatment involving Ozone therapy was repudiated on the ground that the therapy was not authorized by the Indian Medical Association and constituted unproven treatment. The Ombudsman noted it was a recognized non-surgical procedure though primarily for pain relief, and granted an ex-gratia payment.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Travel insurance claim for compassionate visit due to mother's cancer diagnosis was rejected because documents were submitted months after policy expiry and past the one-month post-return deadline. The Ombudsman found the insurer's rejection valid under contract terms, despite sympathetic circumstances.

Claim for pulpectomy of multiple teeth due to alveolar abscess was repudiated under a clause excluding dental treatments unless caused by an accident. The Ombudsman found the insurer relied on a non-existent clause while the applicable policy terms permitted specific dental surgeries without a 24-hour stay, ordering settlement.

Claim for cervical disc prolapse following a fall was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was for diagnostic purposes only without active treatment. The Ombudsman found admission for trauma and pain management was justified and awarded an ex-gratia payment for the accidental injury treatment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for anti-rabies injections administered in OPD without hospital admission was repudiated for lack of 24-hour hospitalization. The Ombudsman noted the insurer was technically correct under policy terms but allowed the claim on ex-gratia basis due to the child's age and meager claim amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claims for hospitalizations related to respiratory and cardiac issues were closed by the TPA because historical pre-existing disease records for the past 4 years were not provided. The Ombudsman held that closing the file without independent inquiry was unfair and ordered claim admission.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for intravitreal Lucentis injections for CNVM was repudiated on the ground that it is an OPD treatment not requiring inpatient admission. The Ombudsman noted the insurer was technically correct due to an existing circular, but awarded an ex-gratia payment given the medical necessity and lack of alternative cures.

Claim for Lasik surgery diagnosed as myopia with astigmatism was repudiated on the ground that the condition was pre-existing and occurred in the first policy year, ignoring prior continuous coverage and treating the ailment as pre-existing solely via panel doctor opinion. The Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment.

Claim for forehead cut injury repair was repudiated because the hospital stay was less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman found the insurer's decision sustainable under basic policy terms, but granted an ex-gratia payment considering the child's tender age.

Claim for trigger thumb release surgery was repudiated because hospital stay was less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman held the insurer's decision was sustainable under policy conditions, but awarded an ex-gratia payment considering the child's tender age.

Claim for epistaxis treatment involving endoscopic cauterization was repudiated because hospitalization lasted less than 24 hours. The Ombudsman noted the insurer was technically correct but granted an ex-gratia payment given the emergency admission and long-standing customer history.
Insured underwent intravitreal injections for ARMD. Insurer repudiated based on circular excluding ARMD drug injections as OPD treatment. Ombudsman granted an ex-gratia payment of Rs.40,000.

Group mediclaim for chronic kidney disease was partially rejected due to non-submission of investigation reports. Ombudsman found reports were already in the discharge summary and ordered payment of the balance.

Claim for acute pancreatitis hospitalization was repudiated on grounds of admission being solely for investigation. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision under clause 7.7 but awarded an ex-gratia payment of Rs.5,000.
Insured underwent hernia surgery and was charged 20% co-payment instead of 10%. Insurer admitted the mistake, and Ombudsman ordered refund of difference plus interest.

Repudiation of claim for intravitreal Macugen injections for ARMD under company circular. Ombudsman held rejection was technically correct but awarded an ex-gratia of Rs.30,000 due to senior citizen status and lack of prior claims.

Claim for hospitalization due to nausea and spondylosis was rejected as admission was for investigation only. Ombudsman upheld rejection under exclusion clause 4.10 but awarded Rs.5,000 ex-gratia on humanitarian grounds.

Partial repudiation of cerebral infarction claim where TPA disallowed high specialist consultation fees and visit charges. Ombudsman upheld disallowance of excessive specialist fee but allowed home/hospital visit charges.

Claim for excision biopsy of scalp ulcer was repudiated because surgery was performed under local anesthesia as an OPD-type procedure. Ombudsman set aside rejection, stating treating doctor's judgment on hospitalization prevails.

Partial repudiation of perineal abscess claim based on an unsubstantiated internal survey of package charges. Ombudsman rejected insurer's arbitrary reduction and ordered full settlement of surgeon fees.

Claim for hysterectomy due to fibroid uterus was rejected as pre-existing. Ombudsman found policy had been continuously renewed since 2007 (exceeding the 24-month waiting period for pre-existing conditions under Gold Plan) and set aside repudiation.

Claim for hoarse voice treatment was repudiated as pre-existing based on a medical history noting symptoms for 7-8 years. Ombudsman ruled that mere symptom history does not constitute a pre-existing disease and set aside rejection.
Complaint regarding inordinate delay in settling a claim for intravitreal Macugen injection. Ombudsman found all policy conditions were satisfied and directed verification and payment.
Claim for pneumonia treatment was repudiated due to late intimation (beyond 30 days) and submission of fake medical bills confirmed by the shop owner. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.
Insurer partially paid fracture claim applying a misunderstood co-pay rule to the company liability limit rather than the claim amount. Ombudsman corrected the interpretation of the policy condition.

Cashless authorization for spinal tumor treatment was cancelled mid-treatment, forcing patient to shift hospitals. Ombudsman clarified that denial of cashless authorization does not bar reimbursement claims under policy terms.

Claim for endocervicitis surgery was repudiated under sterility exclusion clause based on an indefinite panel doctor opinion. Ombudsman preferred the treating doctor's clear opinion that endocervicitis is not sterility and set aside rejection.
