Ombudsman held that the continuity endorsement waived pre-existing disease exclusions, making the claim payable.

Insurer rejected claim for surgical removal of a rapidly growing forehead lump under cosmetic exclusion and lack of trauma. Ombudsman noted the tumor was growing rapidly and needed medical correction, setting aside the insurer's decision and directing settlement.

Insurer closed claim for maxillary bone surgery due to non-submission of misplaced x-ray plate and report. Ombudsman observed that other documents like doctor prescription, discharge summary, and hospital bills were submitted and the hospital lost the x-ray. Insurer directed to settle.

Insurer repudiated claim for malarial hospitalization due to delayed submission beyond 7 days. Ombudsman noted elderly couple were weak and advised rest with no help at home, holding the delay justifiable and directing claim settlement.

Insurer repudiated claim for malarial hospitalization due to delayed submission beyond 7 days. Ombudsman noted elderly couple were weak and advised rest with no help at home, holding the delay justifiable and directing claim settlement.

Insurer repudiated cholecystitis claim under waiting period exclusion, ignoring previous continuous policy with another insurer. Ombudsman noted continuous renewal and disclosure, setting aside repudiation and ordering settlement.

Insurer repudiated hernia claim alleging non-disclosure of a hernia operation done 13 years prior. Ombudsman held that a successful operation 13 years ago without complications does not constitute a pre-existing disease under policy definitions.

Insurer repudiated heart surgery claim citing pre-existing hypertension. Complainant produced medical records proving blood pressure medications were years prior for a different condition and hypertension was recent. Ombudsman set aside repudiation.

Insurer delayed/closed claim requiring certificates for pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage for over 6 years with no-claim bonus, meaning waiting periods for pre-existing ailments already elapsed, and ordered settlement.

Insurer restricted knee replacement claim to sum insured prior to enhancement due to pre-existing osteoarthritis. Ombudsman upheld sum insured restriction based on policy terms but found calculation errors and awarded an additional amount.
Additional amount of Rs. 12,000 awarded under various heads for a knee replacement claim where the insurer had improperly calculated deductions.

Insurer repudiated inferior turbinates surgery claim as an after effect of chronic sinusitis under waiting period. Treating doctor confirmed no definite relation to sinusitis. Ombudsman set aside repudiation and ordered settlement.

Insurer repudiated total hip replacement surgery for osteoarthritis under 4-year waiting period. Ailment arose 4 months short of 4 years following an accident. Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 50,000.

Insurer repudiated claim for colitis and subsequent heart failure leading to death, citing pre-existing disease without evidence of origin date. Ombudsman held insurer failed to establish grounds and ordered claim settlement to the claimant.

Insurer repudiated hernia surgery claim based on a hospital admission form mentioning 10 years of pain (treated as clerical error by hospital). Ombudsman noted lack of sound documentary evidence and previous higher plan coverage, setting aside repudiation.

Insurer rejected ARMD treatment claim because hospital stay was under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted head office circular relaxed norms for such treatments retrospectively from approval date and ordered claim settlement.

Insurer repudiated coronary artery disease claim alleging diabetes complications based on a post-hospitalization anti-diabetic prescription. Treating doctor certified patient was not diabetic. Ombudsman set aside repudiation.

Insurer repudiated peripheral vascular surgery claiming pathogenesis was related to CABG done 7 years prior. Treating doctors certified no relation. Ombudsman held insurer's stance was unsubstantiated and ordered settlement.

Insurer repudiated renal tumor surgery claim alleging non-disclosure of past CABG and hypertension from 2002. Ombudsman noted past heart issues had no direct link to kidney tumor and no fraudulent intention was proven, setting aside repudiation.

Insurer disallowed extra room rent and proportionately reduced visiting surgeon fees because a higher room category was used due to unavailability. Ombudsman upheld room rent limit but ruled proportional surgeon fee reduction unjustified without ascertaining entitled rates, directing reconsideration.

Insured underwent CABG/PTCA and claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease and missing original money receipt. Ombudsman found receipt was submitted and repudiation was erroneous, directing settlement.
Dispute over non-consideration of Cumulative Bonus (CB) in settlement. Insurer agreed during hearing to pay additional amount on account of CB.

Claim for necrotizing fascitis due to insect bite was rejected under 30-day waiting period exclusion treating it as viral infection. Ombudsman noted all medical opinions favored insect bite and set aside rejection.

Claim for lumbar disc prolapse was repudiated on the ground that hospitalization was for investigation only. Ombudsman held treatment was valid for age 66 and allowed specific charges totaling Rs. 28,555.
Personal accident temporary total disablement claim partially settled. Insurer argued disability was not total as patient was improving. Text cuts off before final decision.
Claim for CABG repudiated under tobacco exclusion due to 30-year smoking history. Ombudsman granted partial relief of 20% considering co-existing diabetes and hypertension.
Claim pending due to unsubmitted original money receipt and investigation reports. Complainant agreed to submit remaining documents.
Critical illness claim for PTMC procedure for Mitral Stenosis repudiated as balloon techniques are excluded under policy definition of heart valve surgery. Complaint dismissed.
Dengue claim repudiated for alleged misrepresentation and suspicious hospital relationship. Insurer failed to prove allegations. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 20,000 on ex-gratia basis.

Knee replacement claim for osteoarthritis partially paid by restricting sum insured to initial year amount. Ombudsman ruled restricting sum insured defeats enhancement purpose and ordered balance payment.
Radiotherapy claim for prostate cancer rejected solely due to delayed submission of papers. Ombudsman ruled delay did not alter claim nature and directed settlement.
Lucentis injections for age-related macular degeneration denied as unapproved OPD procedure. Ombudsman noted advancements in medical technology and ordered equal sharing of expenses.
Lap sleeve gastrectomy for sleep apnoea and obesity repudiated because obesity treatment is excluded. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision as obesity necessitated the surgery.
Short-settlement due to deduction of 20% hospital surcharge. Hospital clarified surcharge was abolished. Ombudsman held deduction based on internal circular unjustified.

Claim for Type II Odontoid fracture rejected as hospitalization was for investigation only. Ombudsman noted fracture was positively diagnosed and treated conservatively, directing claim entertainment.
Hepatitis C treatment claim rejected under pre-existing disease clause during first policy year. Ombudsman upheld repudiation as symptoms like mild fever predated policy inception.
Claim for interstitial lung disease lodged in first policy year rejected as pre-existing chronic condition. Request for removal of cataract exclusion also addressed with option to migrate policies.
External Counter Pulsation (ECP) treatment expenses denied on the ground that it was an unproven/experimental treatment in India. Ombudsman discussed validity but noted summary nature of proceedings.
Dispute over failure to collect diabetes loading premium for one year leading to loss of continuity benefit. Ombudsman directed insurer to collect premium and grant continuity.
CABG claim in first policy year denied due to pre-existing advanced coronary artery disease. Ombudsman upheld technical validity of insurer's stance but awarded ex-gratia due to young age.

Insured's spouse was treated for Ca Ovary stage IV. The insurer restricted the claim to the original sum insured of Rs. 4 lakhs citing pre-existence of the disease before taking an enhanced floater policy of Rs. 8 lakhs. The Ombudsman took a compassionate view and granted a lumpsum amount.

Complainant was hospitalized for ischemic heart disease and TVD. The claim was repudiated due to a recorded prior history of hypertension. The Ombudsman noted that pre-existence was not conclusively proved and ordered payment of 50% of admissible expenses.

Complainant was treated for Hepatocellular carcinoma. The claim was repudiated under policy exclusion for alcohol abuse. The Ombudsman held that the alcoholic etiology was not substantiated by conclusive evidence and partially allowed the claim up to 50% of the sum insured.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for right eye 3rd cranial nerve partial paresis. The claim was repudiated on the grounds that treatment could be managed on an OPD basis and was for evaluation only. Considering the symptoms, the Ombudsman allowed 50% of the claim.

Complainant's wife underwent angioplasty, and the TPA deducted costs based on stent capping limits under a SAIL tender. The insurer failed to provide requested underwriting details to substantiate the capping, leading the Ombudsman to allow an ex-gratia payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife was treated for Ca Breast. The TPA deducted 25% towards co-payment based on claim ratios. The Ombudsman observed that co-payment was not mentioned on the policy schedule for that year, rendering the deduction unjustified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife was treated for Ca Pancreas. The insurer rejected a second claim under a separate membership certificate on the ground of multiple covers and limits per illness. The Ombudsman ruled that restrictions in an internal MOU not known to the insured could not be used to deny the claim.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Limited
facts: Insured underwent surgery for PIVD. The claim was repudiated due to a two-year waiting period for the ailment and non-disclosure of past psychiatric treatment. The Ombudsman found the insurer's decision valid.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant submitted claim papers 43 days after discharge instead of the required 30 days. The insurer rightly deducted 20% of the claim amount, and the complaint failed.
Complainant was hospitalized for bypass surgery, and the claim was partially settled according to policy maximum limits. The Forum upheld the insurer's decision.
Complainant's son was treated for abdominal pain. Post-discharge lab tests and medicines were treated as OPD expenses and not covered. The insurer's partial repudiation was upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for renal failure and gastroenteritis was initially repudiated under an exclusion clause. During the hearing, parties agreed the treatment was for acute gastroenteritis, and a mutually settled amount was accepted by the complainant.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for knee osteoarthritis. The claim was repudiated as the tailor-made group policy applied a 4-year waiting period condition, and the complaint failed.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife was hospitalized for viral fever and the claim was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 7. The insurer's decision was found valid.
Complainant's wife underwent laparoscopic salpingectomy and tubal ligation. The claim was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.13 of the happy floater policy, and the complaint failed.
Complainant claimed operation expenses for sub-retinal bleeding treated in a daycare hospital on an OPD basis, which was not payable under policy conditions.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's son was hospitalized for acute gastroenteritis with dysentery. The claim was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 7, and the Forum upheld the decision.

Complainant was hospitalized for hypertension and chest pain across two hospitals. The insurer paid the first claim and rejected the second under an exclusion clause. The Forum directed the insurer to pay an additional amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife was treated for an infected sebaceous cyst. After shifting from another insurer, there was a gap of five days, making the policy a fresh contract and attracting the initial waiting period exclusion.
Claim for injuries after a fall was repudiated because treatment was on an OPD basis with hospitalization under 24 hours, and alcohol involvement was suspected.

Complainant's father was hospitalized for multiple ailments. The claim was partially settled because one of the policies was a Super Top-up policy excluding pre-existing diseases within 48 months, while the individual policy was partially paid. The Forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for treatment of anemia and lower respiratory tract infection was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 4.1 as the patient had pre-existing hypertension and hypothyroidism within six months of taking the policy. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant hospitalized for chest pain in the first year of the policy. Due to a three-month break from the previous insurer, continuity benefits were denied, and the insurer repudiated the claim under a two-year exclusion clause. The Forum upheld the decision.
Claim for viral hepatitis occurred within 30 days of taking a fresh policy. Despite previous coverage elsewhere, the fresh policy terms applied, and the insurer's repudiation was upheld.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for accidental injury treatment was partially paid based on reasonable and customary charges. Upon document scrutiny, the Forum denied the balance amount and dismissed the complaint.
Claim for renal colic was repudiated due to delayed intimation and late submission of papers by 16 days under a group policy. The Forum found no grounds to interfere with the insurer's decision.
Cataract surgery claim under a group policy was partially paid as per a clause restricting expenses to Rs. 15,000. The Forum upheld the insurer's partial settlement.
Claim for acute appendicitis treatment was repudiated because the treatment was taken at a delisted hospital based on high court orders and company circulars. The Forum upheld the repudiation.

Cataract surgery claim was partially paid under family floater group policy limits. Additionally, the complainant failed to produce concrete evidence of being insured, leading to dismissal of the complaint.
Claim for carbuncle treatment was partially settled at 90% of the claimed amount per policy terms. The complainant failed to prove insurance under the policy, and the complaint was dismissed.

Osteoarthritis treatment expenses were partially settled via cashless service. Additional pre- and post-hospitalization claims exceeding the sum insured were partially paid based on policy terms, which the Forum upheld.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Fibroid treatment claim was partially settled based on reasonably and necessarily incurred clauses. The complainant failed to attend the hearing, and the Forum agreed with the deduction.
Coronary artery disease claim was repudiated under exclusion clauses because available papers proved the insured suffered from hypertension and diabetes for 20 years. The complaint failed.
Knee replacement claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease. A 20-day break between previous and new policies rendered it a fresh policy, upholding the insurer's rejection.
Claim for medical expenses was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.4.6 because primary records proved the treatment was taken on an OPD basis. The decision was upheld.
Knee replacement claim was partially settled, but the insurer noted the group policy was cancelled before hospitalization and the matter was sub judice in civil courts, making it unentertainable.

Vaginal hysterectomy claim was repudiated under a 2-year exclusion clause during the first year of the policy. Frequent renewal breaks of 45 days justified treating it as a fresh policy, and the repudiation was upheld.
Claim for haematuria and doubtful PU valve was repudiated under clause 4.1. Medical papers indicated the condition was genetic, meaning the insurer's rejection could not be interfered with.

Stenosis disc prolapse and laminectomy claim was partially settled after deductions for reasonable and customary charges under policy condition 13. The complainant remained absent, and the Forum upheld the decision.

Piles treatment claim was initially repudiated due to hospital name discrepancies in investigator reports. Following mediation by the Forum, both parties mutually agreed to settle the claim without a formal award.

Father of the complainant was hospitalized for knee replacement surgery. The claim was repudiated because the disease falls under a one-year exclusion clause of the newly issued group mediclaim policy. The ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant claimed expenses for wife's cataract surgeries. Insurer partially deducted amount under policy clause 3.13. Through forum mediation, parties mutually agreed to settle for an additional amount.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized and maternity benefits were claimed under an unconventional group mediclaim policy. Insurer paid 10% of sum insured as per policy rules, and the partial settlement was upheld.
Complainant hospitalized for hysterectomy surgery and claim was partially settled by invoking policy conditions limiting expenses based on customary and reasonable charges.
Complainant treated for knee injury and claim was rejected on the grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Through mediation, parties agreed to settle the claim.
Complainant underwent high cost cataract surgery for both eyes. Insurer partially settled the claim based on policy limits and terms. The insurer's decision was upheld.
Wife of the complainant hospitalized for uterus fibroid treatment. Insurer made deductions based on specific policy conditions and notes. The complaint failed to succeed.
Complainant's wife hospitalized and claim for hospitalization and post-hospitalization was repudiated under policy conditions for an unconventional group insurance policy without insurable interest.
Complainant hospitalized for abdominal pain and gastritis. Claim was rejected as 'No Claim' based on panel doctor opinion and medical records.

Husband of the complainant hospitalized for cardiac asthma. Claims were repudiated under exclusion clauses and because cardiac diseases have a 4-year waiting period during the first year of policy inception.
Complainant hospitalized in a private hospital instead of a government hospital as required under the micro policy, and intimation was delayed by 29 days. Complaint failed to succeed.
Cataract surgery expenses were partially settled using an old sum insured. Through forum mediation, the insurer agreed to pay an additional amount accepted by the complainant.
Complainant treated for coronary artery disease. Claim was repudiated on the ground of pre-existing disease under exclusion clause 4.3. Insurer's decision was upheld.
Car damage claim was repudiated because the vehicle was used for commercial purposes at the time of the accident, violating policy limitations.
Wife of the complainant hospitalized for hysterectomy. Claim was partially settled based on customary and reasonable charges. Insurer's deduction was justified.
Complainant's wife operated for tumor removal and claim was repudiated under sterility exclusion. During hearing mediation, insurer agreed to pay an amount as full and final settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for Para Umbilical Hernia, incurring Rs.2,41,426/-. The claim was partly settled for Rs.56,925/- with deductions made according to policy conditions and PPN MOU rates. The Forum upheld the insurer's deductions and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant sought reimbursement of Rs.12,500/- and Rs.1,400/- for treatments including Left Shoulder Supraspinatus Tendiopathy. The insurer rejected the claim under clause 2.3 as the treatment could have been done on an OPD basis without 24 hours admission.
Complainant incurred Rs.2,67,913/- for Prostactomy treatment, which was partially settled for Rs.1,54,300/- with deductions under clause 3.12 of the policy. The Forum upheld the partial settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant incurred Rs.13,790/- for Polycystic Kidney disease treatment, which was repudiated as it was a genetic disorder excluded under policy condition No.4.4.16.
Complainant's father was hospitalized for Coronary Artery Disease with claims of Rs.1,87,228/-, which was repudiated due to pre-existing hypertension and diabetes under exclusion clause 4.1.

Complainant filed two claims for Knee Haemarthrisis. The first claim of Rs.58,433/- was partly settled for Rs.54,334/-, and the second claim of Rs.51,825/- was settled for Rs.20,586/- because it occurred within 105 days for the same illness. The Forum upheld the insurer's decision.

Complainant's wife incurred Rs.50,000/- for Rt. Ovarian Cyst treatment, repudiated because admission was in a declined hospital list. Since the policy was a tailor-made Group Floater Mediclaim, the Forum held it was beyond its scope.
Complainant's hospitalization expenses were rejected under pre-existing disease clause 4.1. The policy was a tailor-made Group Floater Mediclaim, which the Forum found to be beyond its jurisdiction.
Complainant incurred Rs.17,146/- for Ischemic Heart Disease and Diabetes Mellitus, which was repudiated as a pre-existing disease within the first year of the policy under exclusion clause 4.1.

Complainant's mother incurred Rs.50,000/- for Varicose Vein treatment, repudiated under clause 2.3 for lack of hospitalization necessity. Additionally, the policy was a group mediclaim issued to a charitable trust, falling outside the Forum's scope.

Complainant incurred Rs.23,823/- for acute fissure in ano and sphincterectomy, which was denied because allopathic surgical treatment was administered by an Ayurvedic doctor (BAMS) in violation of policy clause 31.

Complainant incurred Rs.11,350/- for UTI, Hypothyroidism, and diabetes treatment, which was denied due to pre-existing conditions (diabetes and hypertension) that were not disclosed in the proposal form.

Complainant's wife incurred Rs.38,260/- for Umbilical Hernia, which was repudiated because the condition was caused by obesity, and obesity-related treatments are excluded under policy condition No.4.19.

Complainant incurred Rs.2,72,207/- for CAD and unstable angina under a family floater policy. The insurer settled only Rs.1.00 Lac due to pre-existing hypertension and waiting periods, and the Forum dismissed the complaint.
Complainant claimed Rs.1,68,686/- for knee joint replacement, which was settled for Rs.1,17,934/- after deductions based on PPN MOU rates. The Forum denied further relief.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant incurred Rs.66,000/- for cataract surgery, which was settled for Rs.44,000/- with a deduction of Rs.22,000/- under policy condition No.3.13. The Forum upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's son incurred Rs.42,901/- for Hepatitis, which was settled for Rs.23,673/- based on PPN hospital rates. A post-hospitalization claim of Rs.9,234/- was also partly paid as Rs.5,680/-, leading to the dismissal of the complaint.

Complainant incurred Rs.8,281/- for Plantar Fasciitis and Dyslipidemia, which was repudiated under clause 19 because the insured was treated with oral medicines only and no injectable medicines were provided, making hospitalization unnecessary.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant incurred Rs.29,702/- for Cirrhosis of Liver and related conditions during the first policy year. The claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of material facts regarding pre-existing illness in the proposal form.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant hospitalized for malaria and claimed Rs.16,350/-, which was partially settled for Rs.12,050/-. Additional Rs.2,700/- agreed to be sent, and Rs.1,600/- deducted for non-medical items. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant hospitalized for stroke with expenses of Rs.25,745/-. Insurer settled Rs.21,495/-, deducting Rs.4,250/- under policy clauses for non-hospital bill expenses. Insurer's decision upheld and complaint dismissed.

A 4-day-old newborn hospitalized multiple times with claims totaling around Rs.92,000/-. Insurer repudiated claim citing permanent policy exclusions for congenital ailments and genetic disorders under a group floater policy. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.1,35,855/- for acute cholecystitis was settled for Rs.1,20,053/- after deductions of Rs.15,802/- under policy conditions. Insurer's deductions found proper and complaint dismissed.

Claim of Rs.1,87,303/- for heart attack rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion clause since the policy had been incepted for only 13 months against a 36-month waiting period requirement for pre-existing conditions. Complaint dismissed.

Mitral valve replacement claim of Rs.2,32,877/- partially settled for Rs.1,05,000/-, calculating payout based on older sum insured due to pre-existing disease limits. Forum upheld decision and complaint dismissed.

Piles treatment expenses of Rs.36,676/- partially settled for Rs.33,176/- with Rs.3,500/- deducted. Lack of proper discharge summary, original files, and doctor's signatures led to the insurer's decision being upheld and complaint dismissed.
Pregnancy-related hospital expenses of Rs.56,590/- repudiated due to late intimation and late submission under a tailor-made group master policy without insurable interest. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization expenses of Rs.25,881/- for anal rectal polyps repudiated invoking the 2-year waiting period clause, as treatment occurred within the first year of policy inception. Complaint dismissed.

Coronary artery disease expenses of Rs.1,71,296/- partially settled for Rs.24,500/-, calculated on old sum insured. Complainant failed to produce past proposal forms to claim higher cumulative bonus. Complaint dismissed.
Back pain hospitalization claim of Rs.39,157/- rejected because hospital stay was less than 24 hours, alongside severe age discrepancies across medical records. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.22,503/- repudiated for late intimation and late submission by 53 days. Investigation revealed forged signatures on claim forms, indicating a fabricated claim. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization claim of Rs.17,479/- for enteric fever repudiated due to inordinate delay in filing the complaint and original files being untraceable after over two years. Complaint dismissed.

Mediclaim rejected due to late intimation and late submission of claim papers. Intimation for first hospitalization was delayed and no intimation was given for the second hospitalization. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Mediclaim for back pain repudiated as treatment was taken on an OPD basis and medical papers did not suggest any clinical need for hospitalization. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for viral fever repudiated invoking policy conditions regarding false statements at inception, as consultation records showed no prior notation of illness and claim bills appeared fabricated. Complaint dismissed.

Claim of Rs.1,21,789/- for hemiparesis partially settled for Rs.78,584/- after deducting home doctor visit charges during pre and post hospitalization periods under policy exclusions. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.77,806/- for chronic liver disease partially settled for Rs.53,000/- with deductions made under customary and reasonable charges as non-hospital bills were produced. Complaint dismissed.
Viral treatment expenses of Rs.17,360/- partially settled for Rs.9,910/-, with deductions made according to Preferred Provider Network (PPN) fixed rates agreed via MOU. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.1,08,379/- for hysterectomy partially settled for Rs.51,625/- by capping payment at a maximum percentage of sum insured for the specific procedure. Complaint dismissed.
Insured was hospitalized for Malaria and anemia and lodged a claim. The insurer rejected it citing discrepancies in claim papers and a blacklisted hospital. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for atypical febrile seizure and epilepsy. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing disease since the condition arose prior to policy inception. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was admitted for convulsions with Dandy-Walker Variant, a congenital brain malformation specifically excluded from coverage. The claim was rejected and complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent treatment for umbilical hernia which developed at the site of a previous LSCS surgery. The insurer invoked permanent exclusion for conditions traceable to pregnancy. The complaint was dismissed.

Insured was hospitalized for CAD. The claim was repudiated due to a 2-year waiting period applicable to a known case of diabetes mellitus during the first year of the policy. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for a finger dislocation due to an accident took treatment at a declined hospital. The insurer's rejection was held proper and the complaint was dismissed.
Insured hospitalized for Bronchial Asthma. Claim was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease. Upon examination, the ombudsman admitted the claim for 75 percent of the admissible amount.

Complainant was hospitalized for acute bronchial allergy. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing bronchial asthma. The ombudsman noted bronchial allergy is not pre-existing and ordered settlement.

Insured son was hospitalized shortly after policy renewal. Insurer denied the claim citing a 5-day gap making it a fresh policy subject to initial waiting periods. The ombudsman held the denial unjustified as the premium cheque was delivered in time to the agent.

Insured took a travel health policy for a trip that was delayed by a year. After shifting policy periods once without charge, a second change required a fresh policy and premium. The insurer's action was held justified.

Hospitalization claim of a member's daughter-in-law under a group policy was declined because the primary member's age in the voter list exceeded 75. The ombudsman used the matriculation certificate to prove eligibility under 75 and allowed the claim.

Hospitalization claim was rejected because the insurer argued only investigations were conducted without active treatment. The ombudsman held it payable as discharge summary prescribed post-hospitalization medicines and follow-up.

Claim for renal stone treatment was rejected on the grounds of a two-year waiting period in the first year. The ombudsman noted continuous renewals since 2008 and awarded the full claim amount of Rs. 51,640.

Claim for mother's hospitalization was denied because the policy was newly taken with the current insurer. The ombudsman granted continuity benefits from the previous insurer and awarded Rs. 29,147 with interest.

insurer: Star Health & Allied General Ins. Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant contested partial settlement of a CVD claim and introduction of a co-pay clause. The ombudsman found the hospital bill settlement correct according to policy terms but awarded an unpaid post-hospitalization expense of Rs. 5,143.

Claim was rejected because the patient was admitted within days of taking the policy and did not give prior intimation. The ombudsman held rejection on technical grounds unjustified and awarded Rs. 17,400.
Claim was partially settled because a few reports were missing. The ombudsman held that the insurer should have paid up to the full sum insured of Rs. 1,00,000 and awarded the balance of Rs. 15,985.

Wife underwent a breast surgery and the claim was rejected for being the first year under a 2-year waiting period. The ombudsman noted continuous insurance since 2001 and awarded the claim of Rs. 83,123.

Complainant treated for CAD was denied cashless and claim settlement under waiting period clauses. The ombudsman granted continuity benefits for five years of continuous policies and awarded Rs. 1,90,702.

Insured underwent coronary angiography and received partial payment based on a pre-enhanced sum insured from an illness years prior. The ombudsman ruled that the claim should be paid against the enhanced sum insured and awarded an additional Rs. 83,750.
Insured claimed reimbursement for daughter's medical treatment. The TPA closed the file after raising queries. The Ombudsman found the claim payable and directed the insurer to pay Rs. 17,987.

Claim for hospitalization of insured's mother was rejected citing pre-existing disease and that the policy was only one year old. The Ombudsman noted continuous coverage since 2003 with no proof of prior existence of the disease and awarded Rs. 4,24,230.
Cashless facility and claim for septicemia treatment were delayed. The TPA and insurer raised maternity exclusion issues incorrectly as the treatment was unrelated. The Ombudsman awarded Rs. 61,600.

Insured was admitted for an emergency ENT condition. Insurer repudiated the balance claim citing a two-year waiting period, ignoring prior continuous policy benefits. The Ombudsman awarded Rs. 30,006.

Claim was rejected because intimation and documents were submitted late due to the insured rushing to his village for his seriously ill father. The Ombudsman held that claims should not be declined on technical grounds and awarded Rs. 12,013.

Claim for emergency hospitalization after throwing blood from the mouth was rejected on the ground that it was only for investigation purposes. The Ombudsman found the admission justified and ordered payment of the admissible amount.

Reimbursement for cataract surgery was denied due to a gap in policy renewal caused by the insurer misplacing the renewal cheque. The Ombudsman held the insurer at fault, waived the gap, and awarded Rs. 44,200.

Motor theft claim was settled as per consent for a lower amount than IDV. The Ombudsman denied extra claim amount based on consent but ordered a refund of the renewal premium since the vehicle was stolen on the last day of the policy.

Motor theft claim was repudiated alleging gross negligence because ignition keys were left inside the unattended vehicle. The Ombudsman held the insurer unjustified and awarded Rs. 8,39,000 for total loss.

Insurer applied a 15% co-payment clause which was not stipulated on the face of the policy schedule due to a software change. The Ombudsman ruled against the co-payment deduction and awarded Rs. 3,68,574.

Claim for a procedure done under anesthesia was rejected as an OPD treatment since the patient did not stay for 24 hours. The Ombudsman ruled that the case fell under day-care surgery definitions and ordered payment.

Claim was repudiated solely due to lack of prior intimation of hospitalization. The Ombudsman held that valid claims cannot be rejected on technicalities and awarded Rs. 21,256 with 9% panel interest.
Insurer made arbitrary deductions on a gall bladder surgery claim. Finding no sufficient reasons for deductions, the Ombudsman awarded an additional Rs. 3,226.

Claim for viral fever and vitamin deficiency was rejected on the grounds that treatment was primarily for psychiatric purposes under exclusion 4.8. The Ombudsman found the hospitalization genuine and awarded Rs. 30,438.

Claim for spinal tumor surgery was rejected under a two-year waiting period clause. The Ombudsman noted continuous policy renewal across different insurers since 2004, granted continuity benefit, and awarded Rs. 1,83,469.
Insurer partially settled a claim by arbitrarily restricting hospital stay to 7 days. The Ombudsman found the restriction unjustified and awarded a total of Rs. 91,677 minus previous payments.
Insurer made unauthorized deductions during claim settlement for emergency hospitalization. The Ombudsman reviewed the assessment sheets and ordered an additional payment of Rs. 2,215.
Claim for carcinoma upper alveolus was rejected under clause 4.8 because the patient was a known tobacco chewer. The Ombudsman found the exclusion inapplicable to the facts and awarded Rs. 2,10,000.

Insurer partially settled claims related to breast carcinoma treatment over a ten-year policy history. During the hearing, the insurer admitted further liability, and the Ombudsman awarded an additional Rs. 96,934.

Claim was repudiated citing pre-existing coronary artery disease and hypertension in the second policy year. The Ombudsman held that the specific illness treated during hospitalization did not pre-date the policy and awarded Rs. 53,893.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for severe headache, incurring expenses of Rs.25,769. The insurer partially settled the claim for Rs.3,627, claiming it was the maximum permissible amount. The Ombudsman found the deduction unjustified and ordered payment of the remaining amount.

insurer: New India General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for a serious cardiac condition and incurred expenses of Rs.54,925, of which the insurer paid Rs.28,059, making proportionate deductions due to higher room rent. The Ombudsman held that diagnostic charges do not depend on the room occupied and awarded Rs.13,948.

Complainant filed a mediclaim bill for Rs.13,793 for hospitalization due to paralysis/domiciliary treatment which the insurer delayed and denied, arguing the admission was only for investigation. The Ombudsman ruled the treatment valid and ordered payment of Rs.12,613.

Wife of the complainant was hospitalized for post-menopausal bleeding and underwent surgery during the 4th year of continuous policy coverage. The insurer repudiated the claim citing pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman held the claim payable since it was filed in the 4th year and awarded Rs.26,656 with interest.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for acute myocardial infarction and diabetes during the 4th year of continuous group mediclaim coverage. The insurer rejected the claim due to pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman found the rejection unjustified as the policy was in force for 4 years and awarded Rs.1,63,500.

insurer: Star Health & Allied General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent treatment for a compression fracture. The insurer partially settled the claim, deducting amounts under 'reasonable and necessary' and non-payable items including physiotherapy charges. The Ombudsman found the complainant entitled to a further sum of Rs.7,811 with interest.

Insured was hospitalized for angioplasty and diagnosed with hypertension and CAD. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds of pre-existing hypertension since previous years. The Ombudsman noted the treated condition was different from past history and awarded the balance claim amount of Rs.94,865.

Complainant was hospitalized for pneumonia and chest pain. The insurer declined the claim on the ground that hospitalization was unnecessary. The Ombudsman ruled that since the insured was admitted and treated, the claim is payable and awarded Rs.23,510.

Complainant underwent a kidney transplant and sought critical illness double sum insured benefits. The insurer settled partial amounts citing a 95-day delay in document submission. The Ombudsman held that late document filing does not negate critical illness benefits and awarded Rs.2,00,000.

Complainant's wife underwent emergency eye surgery to save her sight after suffering from eye-flu. The insurer rejected the claim under cosmetic and refractive surgery exclusions citing a past procedure done 6 years prior. The Ombudsman found the surgery was an emergency to save vision and awarded Rs.49,845.

Complainant submitted a reimbursement claim of Rs.1,03,243 for bilateral eye surgery, but the TPA restricted payment to Rs.80,000 based on reasonability. The insurer admitted there was no policy capping. The Ombudsman ruled the full expenses reimbursable and awarded Rs.1,03,146.

Complainant's daughter was hospitalized for recurrent urinary tract infection and incurred Rs.47,727. The insurer repudiated the claim alleging misdisclosure and fraudulent claims after verification of hospital records. The Ombudsman found the repudiation baseless and awarded Rs.45,727.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured suffered a fall from a height requiring two surgeries across different hospitals with total expenses exceeding Rs.2.4 lakhs. The insurer made deductions based on reasonability. The Ombudsman held deductions unjustified and awarded a further payment of Rs.65,975.

Insured's spouse was treated for renal stone and hypertension. The insurer repudiated the claim citing non-disclosure of pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman found that the insured had continuous policy coverage for 9 years, rendering pre-existing disease exclusions inapplicable, and awarded Rs.83,625.

Complainant sought reimbursement of Rs.1,23,957 for hospitalization, but the insurer paid only Rs.75,066 after arbitrary deductions linked to room rent. The Ombudsman noted the lowest available room rent justified the charges and awarded an additional Rs.35,755.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's son was hospitalized in an emergency for stomach pain. The insurer rejected the claim alleging prior anti-tuberculosis treatment despite negative tests. The Ombudsman held the ground untenable and awarded Rs.23,627 with 8% interest.

Insured underwent treatment for coronary artery disease and unstable angina. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.3, refusing to acknowledge continuity benefits from prior insurers. The Ombudsman ruled that the clause did not apply to the condition and awarded Rs.2,00,000.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Motor insurance theft claim for a two-wheeler was rejected due to alleged gross negligence (leaving keys) and delayed intimation. The Ombudsman noted delay was due to the father's paralytic stroke and awarded total loss compensation of Rs.39,570 with interest.

insurer: Apollo Munich Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for severe abdominal pain and diagnosed with UTI. The insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could have been done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman held the hospitalization was on doctor's advice and awarded Rs.28,898.

Insured underwent treatment for renal stone and hydronephrosis in the second policy year. The insurer rejected the claim citing a two-year waiting period and refusing continuity benefits from the previous insurer. The Ombudsman ruled continuity applied and awarded Rs.34,660.

The insured underwent shoulder surgery and filed a claim for Rs. 55,303. The insurer made deductions based on room rent limits. The Ombudsman found that since the hospital granted a room rent subsidy, the full claim was payable, awarding an additional Rs. 16,200.

The insured was hospitalized under a group medical policy and submitted the claim in time, but intimation was delayed beyond 24 hours. The insurer repudiated the claim on this ground. The Ombudsman held that an otherwise admissible claim cannot be denied solely for delayed intimation and awarded Rs. 40,386 with 8% interest.

The insured filed claims under a family health policy for Rs. 91,919, out of which the insurer paid Rs. 84,738 after deductions. The Ombudsman observed that the claim was not fully and reasonably settled, and awarded a further payment of Rs. 6,714.

The insured was hospitalized for a sudden heart condition (CAD/HT/ACS). The insurer rejected the claim alleging non-disclosure and pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman found no evidence that the disease was pre-existing at policy inception and ordered payment of Rs. 105,000.

The insured's son was hospitalized and sadly passed away. The insurer rejected the reimbursement claim under exclusion clause 4.9, claiming he was an alcoholic. The Ombudsman noted the death summary did not support this, and awarded Rs. 58,240.

The insured suffered a sudden heart attack and underwent coronary stenting. The insurer rejected the claim under a 2-year waiting period for pre-existing conditions. The Ombudsman ruled that CAD does not attract a waiting period under the policy and awarded Rs. 350,600.

The insured underwent surgery at a heart institute and claimed Rs. 89,895, but received only Rs. 65,900 without proper reasons for deductions. The Ombudsman found the settlement incomplete and awarded a further payment of Rs. 10,745.

The insurer declined a mediclaim on the grounds that the treating hospital was blacklisted. The Ombudsman held that the insured had a bonafide belief and the hospital was not on the blacklisted list at the time of treatment, awarding Rs. 40,100.

The insurer repudiated a claim for cerebral palsy under exclusion clause 11, alleging a congenital external defect. Based on the treating doctor's certificate, the Ombudsman found it was not a congenital defect and awarded Rs. 57,818.

The complainant submitted a hospitalization claim of Rs. 20,433 and post-hospitalization claim of Rs. 8,799 for his wife's treatment, which the insurer settled partially for Rs. 17,348 and Rs. 7,674 respectively. The Ombudsman awarded an additional payment of Rs. 4,210.

The insured suffered a heart attack and underwent bypass surgery after exhausting his primary individual policy. The insurer rejected claims under a super top-up policy citing a 2-year waiting period for hypertension. The Ombudsman found no proof of prior heart disease and noted the insurer failed to submit a written reply.

The insured fell ill while visiting his hometown and filed a claim. The insurer declined the claim citing delay in intimation and non-submission of documents. The Ombudsman ruled that valid claims cannot be declined on technicalities and awarded Rs. 9,587.

The insured was hospitalized for Hernia and incurred Rs. 1,29,771. The insurer settled the claim using a lower historical sum insured of Rs. 3.5 lacs and made proportionate deductions. The Ombudsman upheld the sum insured limit but ruled proportionate deductions incorrect, awarding Rs. 21,474.

The insured's wife was hospitalized in critical condition, and intimation was sent via fax after a few days. The insurer rejected the claim for late intimation. The Ombudsman ruled that valid claims cannot be denied on technical grounds and awarded Rs. 75,000 with 8% interest.

The insured's family member was diagnosed with cancer and received prolonged treatment at multiple hospitals, leading to a delayed claim submission. The insurer rejected the claim due to late filing. The Ombudsman held there was sufficient cause for the delay and awarded Rs. 1,00,000 with 8% interest.

The insured's wife was hospitalized suddenly and passed away. The insurer repudiated the claim based on a pre-existing condition from 1995. The Ombudsman noted the death was due to unrelated reasons and ordered payment of Rs. 1,25,996.

The life assured died in an accident in Dubai. The insurer rejected the death claim because the named nominee had predeceased the policyholder. The Ombudsman held that the insurer cannot escape liability to the legal heir, awarding Rs. 10 lacs to the widow.

Against a total claim of Rs. 3,28,903, the insurer arbitrarily paid only 35% (Rs. 1,11,983) without providing valid reasons. The Ombudsman found no rationale for the restriction and awarded a further payment of Rs. 2,16,250.

The insured underwent major surgeries after suffering a brain bleed. The insurer deducted Rs. 1,70,804 from the total claim of Rs. 5,26,671. The Ombudsman found the deductions unjustified and awarded an additional sum of Rs. 17,687.

A claim for heart valve surgery was filed under a policy continuing since 2007. The insurer closed the file alleging non-submission of bills. The Ombudsman accepted that documents were provided and awarded the claim amount of Rs. 1,20,000.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: The insured was hospitalized for chest and stomach problems. The insurer rejected the claim stating that hospitalization was not necessary and was only for investigation. The Ombudsman found the treatment valid and ordered payment of Rs. 16,123.

The insured was treated for carcinoma breast with bone metastasis. The insurer rejected the claim citing a pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman noted no evidence of pre-existence prior to policy inception and awarded Rs. 1,73,027.

The insured filed two claims for hysterectomy/ovarian cyst and intestinal obstruction. The TPA rejected them under waiting period and wrong diagnosis claims. The insurer failed to appear. The Ombudsman found the continuous policy covered the claims and awarded Rs. 1,71,042.

Motor insurance claim where vehicle suffered engine damage due to water logging. Insurer paid a minor amount citing consequential loss. Ombudsman directed the insurer to consider engine overhauling and pay admissible amount.
The insured was hospitalized for treatment at Holy Family Hospital. The insurer repudiated the claim without submitting any reply. The Ombudsman held the claim payable and awarded Rs. 21,326.

insurer: Apollo Munich General Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insurer made deductions for room rent during hospital stay. The Ombudsman found no room rent capping in the policy and ordered payment of Rs. 8,000 for the deduction made.

The insured was hospitalized for Chronic Ischaemic Heart Disease during the second year of the policy. The insurer rejected the claim under waiting period. The Ombudsman held that heart diseases have no waiting period and awarded Rs. 34,409.
The insurer settled a hospitalization claim based on the pre-enhanced sum insured of Rs. 1 lakh instead of the enhanced sum insured. The Ombudsman awarded an additional Rs. 2,146.

The insurer rejected a mediclaim for varicose veins surgery on the ground of delayed submission of documents beyond 30 days of discharge. The Ombudsman held that valid claims cannot be denied on technical delays and awarded payment with interest.
The insurer rejected the hospitalization claim due to a delay of 40 days in document submission. The Ombudsman held that an admissible claim cannot be declined solely on delay and awarded Rs. 38,743.

The insurer repudiated a claim for head injury treatment due to delayed submission. The Ombudsman ruled that admissible claims cannot be declined solely due to delay and awarded Rs. 20,596 with interest.

The insurer partially settled a mediclaim, paying Rs. 1,40,000 against a claim of Rs. 2,70,800. The Ombudsman found the insured was entitled to 70% of the sum insured and awarded an additional Rs. 70,000.

The insurer settled angioplasty treatment using an older sum insured period instead of the current policy period. The Ombudsman held that the current year sum insured applied and awarded an additional Rs. 53,000.
The insured faced severe delays and lack of response for cancer treatment reimbursement claims. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to process and pay Rs. 4,03,225 based on the correct sum insured.
The insurer repudiated a chest pain hospitalization claim on the ground of pre-existing disease without evidence. The Ombudsman held the claim payable and awarded Rs. 80,000.

The insurer heavily deducted amounts from a cataract surgery reimbursement claim. The Ombudsman found no justification for withholding hospital stay and professional charges and awarded an additional Rs. 3,200.

The insurer repudiated a heart blockage treatment claim under the waiting period for hypertension and alleged misrepresentation. The Ombudsman held that heart treatment has no waiting period and awarded Rs. 1,87,700.
The insurer failed to decide a mediclaim filed following the death of the insured during treatment. The Ombudsman held the claim payable and awarded Rs. 1,50,000.

The insurer repudiated an accident hospitalization claim on the ground of late intimation and delayed filing. The Ombudsman ruled that valid claims cannot be denied on technicalities and ordered payment.
The insurer failed to settle hospitalization claims under a happy family floater policy citing non-submission of documents. The Ombudsman found documents were submitted and awarded Rs. 67,144.

Complainant claimed for wife's paralysis and self's cataract surgery. Insurer rejected paralysis claim citing two-year waiting period for hypertension complications, and delayed payment on cataract. Ombudsman held paralysis has no waiting period, awarding Rs. 26,897 for it while noting cataract claim was already settled.

Insurer repudiated cancer/duct ectasia treatment claim citing pre-existing condition and past mammography advice. Ombudsman noted cancer was detected years after policy inception and previous mammography was negative, making the pre-existing disease argument unjustified. Awarded Rs. 56,090.

Insurer settled breast cancer claim based on pre-enhanced sum insured of Rs. 1 lakh instead of enhanced Rs. 4 lakhs. Ombudsman found cancer was detected when the higher sum insured was active, invalidating deductions. Ordered additional payment of Rs. 3,200.

Insurer partly settled hospitalization claim for Rs. 3,166 out of Rs. 10,091 on grounds of missing consultation papers. Ombudsman found all necessary documents were submitted, rendering deductions unwarranted. Awarded balance of Rs. 6,565.

Complainant sought pending claims for mother-in-law's pneumonia treatment, father's injury treatment, and mother's cancer treatment. Insurer failed to represent or settle claims. Ombudsman directed payment of Rs. 37,308 for pneumonia treatment and Rs. 8,998 for father's treatment.

Complainant alleged inadequate settlement and failure to consider cumulative bonus. Ombudsman found cumulative bonus was correctly factored into a Rs. 2.5 lakh limit, but half-day room rent worth Rs. 1,250 was wrongly deducted. Awarded Rs. 1,250.

Insurer repudiated father's hospitalization claims citing history of CVA, HTN, and DM under clause 4.3. Ombudsman held that the policy had continued for years from a group scheme to individual policy, making pre-existing clauses inapplicable. Awarded Rs. 39,462.

Insurer repudiated back pain surgery claim citing pre-existing disease under clause 4.1. Ombudsman found no evidence that the insured suffered from back pain when the policy started in 1997. Awarded Rs. 40,394.

Motor insurance claim for an accident vehicle was denied due to overloading. Ombudsman held that overloading alone does not prove it was the sole cause of the accident, and surveyor's assessed loss must be paid. Awarded Rs. 1,21,685.

Insurer rejected father's chest pain and CAD hospitalization claim citing a two-year waiting period for hypertension complications. Ombudsman ruled that the treated condition had no waiting period and ordered full payment of Rs. 3 lakhs.

Insurer denied emergency cardiac hospitalization claim under clause 4.1, arguing admission was unnecessary. Ombudsman held admission was justified due to emergency heart palpitations, awarding Rs. 22,999.

Insurer settled knee replacement claim based on base sum insured of Rs. 1 lakh, omitting cumulative bonus. Since the insurer agreed in written reply to honor cumulative bonus, Ombudsman awarded an additional Rs. 30,000.
Complainant alleged short payment for motor claim regarding theft of CNG kit, glass, and stepney. Insurer failed to attend or submit defense. Ombudsman modified assessment and awarded Rs. 24,884.

Critical care policy claim for myocardial infarction was repudiated because treating doctor stated patient suffered from unstable angina and diabetes rather than myocardial infarction, falling outside policy scope.

Insurer rejected CABG claim under clause 4.1 for pre-existing CAD and hypertension. Medical records proved history of CAD and hypertension for four years, while policy had only run for four years with a four-year exclusion period. Claim dismissed.

Insurer rejected cervical spine surgery claim citing a two-year waiting period for prolapsed intervertebral disc under clause 4.3. Ombudsman noted diagnosis was cervical myelopathy, a distinct condition not subject to that waiting period. Claim allowed.
Insurer denied cashless for gallbladder stone surgery under a two-year specific waiting period clause. Since policy inception was less than two years prior, complaint was dismissed as justified.

Insurer repudiated vertigo hospitalization claim because patient had a background history of hypertension during the first year of the policy, which carries a two-year waiting period under clause 4.3. Complaint dismissed.

Insurer rejected epididymitis treatment claim claiming admission was solely for diagnostic evaluation under exclusion 13. Ombudsman held admission was doctor-advised and conservative treatment was provided, allowing the complaint with 8% interest.

Insurer partially settled bilateral hip replacement for rheumatic arthritis by restricting sum insured due to recent enhancement and two-year waiting period rules for enhanced amounts combined with single illness rules. Matter detailed in incomplete text.

Insured was admitted for Periarthritis Shoulder following an accident. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.10 alleging lack of active treatment and hospitalization necessity. The Ombudsman found evidence of active treatment including physiotherapy and medication, ruling the hospitalization necessary and awarding Rs. 4032 with interest.

Complainant's wife underwent Ayurveda treatment for Lumbar Disc Prolapse. The claim was rejected alleging hospitalization was unnecessary. The Ombudsman noted the treatment course was certified by the treating doctor and rejected the insurer's reliance on allopathic expert opinion, awarding Rs. 115000 with interest and costs.

Complainant's wife diagnosed with Chronic HCV infection and admitted to start PEG-interferon injection. Claims were denied on the ground that no hospitalization was required. The Ombudsman held that severity and medical advice justified inpatient care, awarding Rs. 77380 with interest and costs.

Insurer repudiated a claim for daughter's hospitalization under psychiatric exclusion clause 4.4.6. The Ombudsman found the patient was treated solely by a neurosurgeon for head injury manifestations from a prior road accident, and awarded Rs. 20394 with interest.

Complainant's wife was admitted for Osteoporosis treatment. Insurer rejected the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary and for evaluation only. The Ombudsman observed that intravenous infusion and diagnostics were consistent with active treatment, and awarded Rs. 14200 with interest.

Complainant claimed daily hospital cash benefit for 17 days of Naturopathy treatment for unstable angina. Insurer rejected the claim citing lack of medical necessity and offered an arbitrary goodwill amount. The Ombudsman upheld the validity of Naturopathy treatment under the policy and awarded Rs. 48000 with interest.

Complainant underwent inpatient Ayurveda treatment for low back pain at a private medical college hospital. Claim was rejected because treatment was not in a Government hospital. The Ombudsman interpreted the policy wording to include medical college hospitals regardless of private or government status, awarding Rs. 17000 with costs.

Complainant suffered stroke and claim was partially settled by applying a waiting period following enhancement of sum insured. The Ombudsman found that the pre-existing hypertension waiting period had already expired and the acute stroke occurred during the current policy year, awarding Rs. 34375 with interest.

Complainant's son hospitalized for Pneumonia. Insurer partially settled after cashless deduction, citing pre-existing Cerebral Palsy. The Ombudsman verified that the TPA had authorized Rs. 30000 cashless but only disbursed Rs. 27000, and awarded the balance of Rs. 3000 with interest.

Claim for thyroid removal surgery was rejected for falling within the initial 30-day waiting period. The Ombudsman determined that the diagnosis and knowledge of the ailment occurred beyond 30 days from policy inception, and awarded Rs. 60189 with interest.

Multiple claims for eye treatment were rejected due to a two-year waiting period for cataract complications and missing documents. The Ombudsman upheld closure for the missing document claim and one cataract-related claim, but allowed claims concerning corneal rupture and ulcer treatments not linked to cataract, awarding Rs. 33860.

Insurer denied reimbursement for gallbladder surgery balance based on Preferred Provider Network (PPN) package tariff agreements. The Ombudsman held that private tariff agreements between insurer and hospital are outside the policy scope, and awarded Rs. 25959 with interest.

Claim for aortic valve replacement surgery was partially paid after insurer alleged the heart condition was a pre-existing complication of dyspnoea. The Ombudsman found no medical evidence supporting pre-existence and awarded Rs. 270404 with interest and costs.

Bypass surgery claim was rejected on the ground of pre-existing coronary artery disease based on past retrosternal pain. The Ombudsman noted the lack of substantiating medical proof of prior treatment and awarded Rs. 182834 with interest.

Claim for prostate surgery was rejected as a pre-existing disease. The Ombudsman ruled that pre-existing ailments are covered after one claim-free year and no prior treatment proof existed, but later reviewed the award to limit liability to Rs. 20000 based on policy caps.

Complainant's claims for hospitalization and post-hospitalisation expenses related to Parkinsonism were partially deducted by the insurer. The Ombudsman found no valid grounds for deductions under the policy terms and awarded Rs. 6446 with interest and costs.

Appendicitis claim for complainant's daughter was repudiated under clause 4.2 for hospitalization within 30 days of policy inception. The Ombudsman clarified that the exclusion applies to hospitalization within 30 days, whereas actual hospitalization occurred after 180 days, and awarded Rs. 32904 with interest.

Ayurveda hospitalization claim for Cervical Spondylosis was rejected on grounds of outpatient treatability and claim delay. The Ombudsman ruled that supervised inpatient procedures constituted an active line of treatment and procedural delay caused no prejudice, awarding Rs. 12817 with interest.

Claim for daughter's eye protrusion investigation and treatment was rejected as admission was allegedly only for diagnostics. The Ombudsman found investigations were consistent with the diagnosis and awarded Rs. 5140 with interest.

Claim for abdominal pain hospitalization and post-hospitalisation was partially paid. The insurer applied a 7% limit on post-hospitalisation expenses. The Ombudsman verified correct calculations under policy caps and awarded Rs. 6198 inclusive of costs.

The policyholder sought restoration of cumulative bonus. The insurer issued a revised policy in August 2009. The complaint was filed in November 2012, which is beyond the one-year limitation period under the rules. The complaint was dismissed.

The insured underwent surgery for sebaceous cyst in the scrotum. The claim was initially rejected on the ground of no active line of treatment during hospitalization. The insurer later agreed to pay Rs. 7,235. The ombudsman directed the insurer to pay the amount with 9% interest.

The insured slipped, suffered severe back pain, and was hospitalized for two days. The claim was rejected claiming only investigations were done without active treatment. The ombudsman noted that MRI and physiotherapy were conducted, rendering hospitalization justified, and ordered payment of Rs. 8,432 with interest.

The insured's minor daughter was treated for mesenteric adenitis as an in-patient. The insurer rejected the claim stating no hospitalization was necessary. The ombudsman found medications were administered and investigations were consistent with the diagnosis, ordering payment of Rs. 2,578 with interest.

The insured's enhanced sum assured claim was partially settled on pre-existing ailment grounds. The ombudsman ruled that the 48-month waiting period runs from the inception of the first policy in 2005, not the enhancement date. The insurer was directed to pay the balance of Rs. 25,000 with interest.

The insured underwent angioplasty for CAD. The claim was partially settled citing pre-existing hypertension for the enhanced sum assured. The ombudsman calculated the total sum insured including cumulative bonus and ordered an additional payment of Rs. 12,625 with interest.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured's husband was hospitalized for shoulder pain, and the claim was rejected due to pre-existing diabetes which was not disclosed in the proposal form. The ombudsman upheld the repudiation due to suppression of material facts regarding diabetes.

Claims for two hospitalizations (son's fall and wife's headache) were rejected. The ombudsman upheld the rejection for the son as no fracture or active treatment occurred, but allowed the wife's claim since she underwent investigations and received medications for urinary infection and headache, awarding Rs. 3,281.

The insured underwent ear surgery for CSOM. The claim was rejected as pre-existing based on an unsupported statement in the discharge summary. The ombudsman held that unsupported statements cannot validate repudiation and ordered payment of Rs. 58,667 with interest.

The insured's wife underwent a myomectomy for a fibroid uterus. The insurer restricted the claim to 25% applying a clause meant for hysterectomies. The ombudsman noted myomectomy is distinct from hysterectomy and ordered an additional payment of Rs. 19,759 with interest.

Two claims for urinary tract infection hospitalizations were rejected citing diabetes and lack of necessity. The ombudsman ruled that the treating doctor's decision to admit was valid, though bulk medicine purchases should be deducted. An award of Rs. 14,984 was granted.

The insured was hospitalized for Lucentis injections for an eye condition. The claim was rejected on the ground that treatment could be done on OPD basis. The ombudsman noted medical guidelines recommend hospitalization for this procedure, and ordered full payment of Rs. 50,000.

The insured's respiratory tract infection claim was partially settled after initial rejection. The ombudsman found further deductions of Rs. 3,184 were reimbursable and awarded this amount with interest and costs.

The insured was hospitalized for chest pain and ischemic heart disease. The claim was rejected under exclusion clause for evaluation/diagnostic purpose. The ombudsman noted active medical treatment was provided during hospital stay and ordered payment of Rs. 9,483 with interest.

The insured underwent surgery for acute emphysematous cholecystitis. The claim was closed due to non-production of investigation reports. The ombudsman ruled that once hospitalization and surgery are admitted, missing investigation reports do not warrant claim closure, and ordered payment of Rs. 29,663 with interest.

The insured's daughter underwent surgery for contracture following an accident after a policy break of 72 days. The insurer rejected the claim as pre-existing under a fresh cover. The ombudsman held that the injury was not pre-existing at the original inception, and ordered payment of Rs. 24,099.

The insured underwent cataract surgery, and the insurer settled cashless at tariff rates for a standard lens. The reimbursement for balance amount was denied. The ombudsman upheld the lens tariff payout, but ordered payment of undisputed pre-hospitalisation expenses of Rs. 2,075.

The insured's son was treated for fever, meningism, and sinusitis. The claim was repudiated due to a policy break and waiting period for sinusitis. The ombudsman observed that while sinusitis was inadmissible in the first year, expenses for fever and meningism were admissible, ordering payment of 50% of the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: The claim for convulsion and seizure disorder treatment was delayed and pending due to non-submission of documents including a money receipt. The ombudsman noted the documents were already submitted and reflected in hospital bills, and directed the insurer to settle and pay the claim.

The insured's wife underwent excision of a sebaceous cyst. The claim was initially repudiated on the ground that no active line of treatment was received and stay was for dressing. Since the insurer later agreed to admit and settle the claim, no further intervention was needed.

Insured was admitted for severe vertigo and investigations, but insurer repudiated under exclusion 4.8 for lack of active hospitalization and routine evaluation. Ombudsman noted some positive illness (mild cerebral atrophy) and allowed 50% of the admissible claim.

Insured hospitalized for dengue in Bangalore and delayed intimation and claim submission due to being alone. Insurer rejected for violating time limit conditions. Ombudsman found the delay genuine under IRDA guidelines and directed full settlement.
Claim for tympanoplasty was repudiated for non-submission of specific consultation papers already provided or covered by discharge summary. Ombudsman found compliance adequate and ordered settlement.

Insurer treated policy as fresh and invoked pre-existing disease exclusion due to 10-day bank premium receipt delay. Ombudsman noted bank was authorized agent and ordered continuous policy renewal and settlement.
Partial deduction made on cancer surgery claim including room rent/SCU charges. Ombudsman found SCU eligibility was higher and awarded an additional Rs. 1,700 for bed charges.

Insured hospitalized for accelerated hypertension and ischemic heart disease. Insurer repudiated as diagnostic/OPD case under exclusion 4.10. Ombudsman noted very high BP and CCU advice, ordering payment.
Claim repudiated due to delay in intimation while caring for hospitalized mother. Ombudsman accepted waiver petition reasons and ordered claim settlement.

Insured underwent aortic valve surgery opting for a closed package. Insurer rejected closed OT package charges and settled under open package. Ombudsman upheld package shift but awarded unpaid extra ICCU stay charges.
Gastritis treatment claim partially deducted for room rent, misc items, and doctor fees. Ombudsman upheld most deductions but ruled professional fee deduction incorrect, awarding Rs. 2,700 extra.
Claim for malaria treatment repudiated for delayed submission by 29 days without issuing a proper repudiation letter. Ombudsman directed insurer to admit and settle.

Claim for multiple pre-existing chronic conditions in 3rd policy year was validly rejected under PED, but newly detected severe hypothyroidism and lumbar canal stenosis were admissible. Ombudsman allowed 50%.
Angiography claim rejected for pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Ombudsman noted policy was in its 4th year under Silver Plan which covers PED after 2 years, and ordered settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insurer settled surgery claim excluding doctor's fee because the surgeon provided a hand-written numbered receipt. Ombudsman found insurer's insistence on printed receipt unjustified and ordered full settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: MRI claim repudiated for 15-day delay in document submission due to year-end work pressure. Ombudsman condoned marginal delay and ordered settlement.

PTCA claim repudiated for non-submission of past history documents. Ombudsman verified that doctor certificates had been submitted establishing hypertension and diabetes duration outside pre-existing exclusions, and ordered settlement.
Chemotherapy claim for lung cancer rejected under PED/non-disclosure. Ombudsman noted cancer was detected recently and TPA had previously approved cashless cycles, ordering claim settlement.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Hysterectomy claim partially paid after capping surgeon fee paid in cash. Ombudsman ruled that caps apply per bill rather than clubbed bills, and ordered extra payment for anesthetist and RMO fees.

insurer: Bharti AXA General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cancer claims repudiated for non-disclosure of past hernia surgery and hypertension. Ombudsman noted hernia surgery was 8 years prior with no bearing on liver cancer, and hypertension pre-existence was unproven, ordering full settlement.

Claim for acute LRTI and sepsis partially paid after deducting doctor visit caps, ambulance, and emergency fees. Ombudsman upheld doctor caps but found ambulance and emergency charges payable, awarding extra.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery claim settled at maximum senior citizen policy limit of Rs. 10,000. Ombudsman found pre and post-hospitalization expenses were omitted and awarded additional amounts.

A 75-year-old insured was hospitalized for acute respiratory disorders due to COPD. The insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalization was under 24 hours and lacked an active line of treatment. The Ombudsman noted the marginal time shortage, advanced age, and active treatment, setting aside the repudiation and ordering settlement.

The insured underwent an intravitreal injection of Avastin for age-related macular degeneration. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds that it was an OPD procedure and excluded under internal guidelines. The Ombudsman found no specific policy exclusion and that internal guidelines came later, setting aside the repudiation and ordering settlement.

A claim for hemicolectomy hospitalization expenses was delayed by 59 days in submission. During proceedings, the insurer stated the competent authority condoned the delay and agreed to settle the claim. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim as per policy terms upon document compliance.

Following a knee injury and surgery, the insured claimed hospitalization and post-hospitalization expenses. The insurer partially settled, deducting amounts for room rent proportion, non-medical items, and physiotherapy. The Ombudsman found certain surgical fees and physiotherapy charges wrongly disallowed and ordered additional payment.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for hydronephrosis and urothelial carcinoma treatment under a senior citizen policy was repudiated for non-disclosure of a pre-existing condition. During the hearing, the insurer agreed to admit and settle the claim upon receiving original documents. The Ombudsman directed the insurer to settle the claim.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured underwent surgery for carpal tunnel syndrome. The insurer partially settled the claim and deducted amounts for inadmissible items and room rent proportionality. The Ombudsman found errors in clubbing doctor fees and proportionate deduction calculations, directing the insurer to verify hospital variable room rates and reprocess.

The insured claimed expenses for cyst treatment hospitalization. The insurer partially settled, disallowing separate bills for surgeon and doctor fees because they were not part of the hospital bill, alongside room rent proportionate deductions. The Ombudsman ruled that hospitalization includes all relevant treatment expenses and ordered additional payments.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: The insured underwent hernia surgery and claimed reimbursement for post-hospitalization and miscellaneous expenses. The insurer partially settled the claim, deducting room charges and unprescribed medicines or missing bills. The Ombudsman upheld most deductions but ordered payment for validly supported consultation and RMO charges.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: A claim for intravitreal injection of Lucentis for ARMD was repudiated based on a head office circular excluding such treatments from mediclaim scope. The Ombudsman noted the policy lacked the exclusion endorsement and the circular contents were not communicated to the insured, awarding an ex-gratia payment for service deficiency.

The insured's wife was hospitalized for stress urinary incontinence treatment. The claim was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 19 due to pregnancy complications and lack of previous treatment papers. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insured claimed hospitalization expenses for thrombosis surgery. The insurer partially settled the claim, deducting amounts for separately paid surgeon, doctor home visit, and anesthetist charges not shown in the hospital bill. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial settlement and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for laparoscopic hysterectomy was repudiated because records showed the condition and prior consultations existed before the policy inception, falling within the 48-month waiting period for pre-existing diseases in the first-year policy. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

The insured underwent robotic prostatectomy at a distant hospital. The claim was repudiated on the grounds that robotic prostatectomy is unproven and lacking clearance, and no referral letters or prior consultation papers were submitted. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

The insured claimed expenses for plastic surgery following a leg injury from a fall. The insurer rejected the claim under policy terms, noting monsoon-delayed healing was not believable. The Ombudsman upheld the rejection and dismissed the complaint.

A claim for retinal detachment surgery was partially settled with deductions applied under policy condition 1.2. The complainant argued full payment due to long-term policy holding with a lower sum insured. The Ombudsman found the insurer's deductions proper and dismissed the complaint.

A knee replacement claim was partially settled on a non-standard basis due to non-compliance with required documents within the stipulated timeframe, which the complainant had accepted. The Ombudsman noted the insurer was fully discharged from liability and dismissed the complaint.
A claim for acute dysentery and gastroenteritis was repudiated by the insurer under policy terms. Reviewing available documents, the Forum also found the claim deniable and dismissed the complaint.
