A dengue fever hospitalization claim was partially settled based on preferred provider network rates and reasonable and customary charges. The insurer explained deductions, and the complainant failed to submit required proformas. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

A claim for dental treatment following a bike accident was repudiated because the hospitalization period was less than 24 hours, classifying it as OPD treatment outside policy scope. The Ombudsman upheld the dismissal.

A claim for BPH and stricture urethra treatment was partially settled with deductions for reasonable and customary charges, missing policy details on the claim form, and discrepancies in discharge summaries and doctor receipts. The Ombudsman upheld the partial settlement and dismissed the complaint.
Wife was hospitalized for back pain. Insurer rejected claim under clause 4.4.13 as treatment was related to pregnancy. Complainant failed to prove otherwise.
Claim for CAG+PTCA treatment was repudiated because hospitalization occurred during a policy break period, although renewed within the grace period.
Eye surgery done on OPD basis and claim papers submitted late. Complaint dismissed.
Partial settlement for laparoscopy and appendectomy after deductions under policy conditions. Forum denied remaining amount.
Hospitalization benefit for chronic gastritis with gall bladder rejected under pre-existing disease due to past symptoms.
Eye surgery claim partially settled after valid deductions under policy conditions.
Acute bronchitis claim repudiated due to discrepancies in date, time, and patient age.
Cervical epidural claim rejected as hospitalization was less than 24 hours.
Partial settlement for chronic myositis agreed by complainant after hearing, closing the case.
Metastasis ER neck claim partially settled under policy condition 2.3.
Cataract surgery claim repudiated because hospital had only 2 beds and policy was renewed after a break making it a fresh policy.
Knee replacement claim settled correctly as per sum insured plus cumulative bonus minus per-claim deduction.
Coronary angioplasty claim partially settled based on old sum insured due to pre-existing condition waiting period.
Hip fracture claim repudiated due to late intimation, late submission of papers, missing signature on discharge summary, and no consultation paper.
Head, lip, and teeth injury claim partially settled, with dental treatment cost excluded as per clause 4.4.5.
Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura claim rejected due to 4-year waiting period cap for pre-existing disease.
Trigeminal neuralgia claim partially settled as treatment papers created suspicion of OPD treatment without surgery.
PTCA claim partially settled based on old sum insured; enhanced sum insured denied due to nondisclosure of DM and HTN.
Viral fever claim rejected as hospitalization was not required and treatment could be managed on OPD basis.
Cataract surgery claim partially settled with deductions for reasonable and customary charges. Complaint succeeded based on policy limits.

Complainant was hospitalized for Cardio Embolic Infarct LV Myxoma. The insurer repudiated the claim invoking pre-existing disease clause, stating the claim occurred in the first year of a fresh policy due to a cancelled cheque endorsement. The forum dismissed the complaint.

A baby girl was hospitalized for excision of bony growth. The claim for Rs.25,285/- was rejected under exclusion clause 4.8 for congenital external disease. The forum found the insurer's decision in order and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant underwent knee joint replacement surgery incurring Rs.3,54,036/-, partially settled for Rs.2,27,500/- with deductions made because the treating surgeon was the patient's son and the assistant surgeon's name was missing. The complaint was dismissed.

Hospitalization for vertigo and vomiting costing Rs.18,443/- was rejected as the admission was solely for investigation purposes and could have been managed on an OPD basis. The complaint was dismissed.

Complainant incurred Rs.54,272/- for tibia and fibula treatment, partially settled for Rs.44,819/- with deductions under clause 1.2. The insurer agreed to release a pending post-hospitalization amount, but penalty demands were rejected and the complaint was dismissed.

Hospitalization expense of Rs.16,846/- for acute appendicitis was repudiated under clause 5.4 due to lack of timely intimation, as the fax copy provided to the TPA was illegible and no concrete evidence of timely notice was presented.
Claim of Rs.26,227/- for right inguinal hernia surgery was settled for Rs.17,669/- based on PPN MOU rates under reasonable and necessary policy conditions. The complaint was dismissed.

Treatment for ring finger injury costing Rs.19,080/- was partially settled for Rs.5,937/- with deductions under clause 1.2 due to unacceptable altered hospital bills submitted later. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim of Rs.2,59,806/- for incisional hernia with septicemia was rejected because case papers indicated treatment related to grade-II obesity, far exceeding standard hernia treatment costs. The complaint failed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.65,026/- for left eye intra vitreal avastin injection was rejected as the procedure can be performed on an OPD basis, which is excluded from coverage. The complaint was dismissed.
Abdominal pain treatment costing Rs.20,512/- was rejected because it stemmed from a complication of an LSCS performed in 2008, falling under permanent exclusion clause 4.12. The complaint failed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.94,399/- for fracture treatment was partially settled for Rs.72,347/- with deductions under clauses 2.1, 2.3, and 2.4, alongside discrepancies in patient age and undisclosed pre-existing conditions. The complaint was dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hysterectomy claim of Rs.47,827/- was settled for Rs.26,076/- with valid deductions under policy conditions. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim for CAD and HTN treatment amounting to Rs.1,93,837/- was rejected as it occurred within the first year of policy inception, invoking waiting period clauses alongside non-disclosure of tobacco use and obesity treatment. The complaint was dismissed.
Cataract surgery claim of Rs.98,400/- was partially settled for Rs.61,400/- with deductions for reasonable and customary expenses. The insurer's decision was upheld and the complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.68,819/- for two simultaneous operations (mesh hernioplasty and TURP) was partially settled for Rs.54,938/- with deductions applied since the second surgery performed under a single OT session was paid at 50%. The complaint was dismissed.

Viral hepatitis treatment claim of Rs.25,487/- was partially settled for Rs.14,038/- based on PPN rates and MOU. The insurer had publicly notified the PPN list in newspapers, and the complaint was dismissed.

Urethra stricture treatment claim of Rs.35,348/- was repudiated due to non-disclosure of material facts regarding prior TURP operation and solitary kidney in the proposal form, despite extra premium paid for hypertension and diabetes. The complaint was dismissed.

Knee replacement claim of Rs.1,45,000/- was partially settled for Rs.35,000/- with deductions applied because the enhanced sum insured was subject to a 4-year waiting period. The complaint was dismissed.

Claim of Rs.65,157/- for ischemic heart disease and rheumatoid asthma was partially settled for Rs.20,164/- based on PPN rates and MOU, which were duly published in newspapers. The complaint was dismissed.
Complainant incurred Rs.31,288 for viral fever treatment, partially settled for Rs.16,291 based on PPN rates. The forum upheld the insurer's deductions and dismissed the complaint.
Claim of Rs.42,814 for stricture urethra and hernia was repudiated because the insured exceeded the maximum age limit of 65 years under the policy guidelines. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant claimed Rs.44,256 for viral fever and septicemia treatment, which was partially settled for Rs.35,500 due to limit exhaustion. Complaint dismissed as settlement complied with policy terms.
Claim of Rs.25,442 for naturopathy treatment was repudiated under policy clauses excluding unproven and alternative treatments like naturopathy and acupuncture. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery claim of Rs.18,538 for acute allergic bronchitis treatment was partially settled by deducting Rs.6,637 for exceeding eligible room category limits. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Kidney transplant expenses of Rs.6,95,947 had an erroneous cashless payment of Rs.2,33,000 made by TPA. The forum upheld the denial of the remaining claim amount and dismissed the complaint.

Cataract surgery claim of Rs.50,000 was partially settled for Rs.38,260 due to non-submission of original papers. Insurer agreed to pay an extra Rs.7,000 upon production of originals. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant incurred Rs.21,459 for urinary tract infection treatment, partially settled for Rs.11,929. Separately, an 82-year-old's renal failure claim was restricted to the Rs.50,000 heart disease limit. Complaints dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Treatment expenses of Rs.80,210 for ovarian cyst and fibroids were partially settled at Rs.48,634 after deductions as per policy clauses. The forum dismissed the complaint.
Claim of Rs.5,70,713 for morbid obesity treatment was repudiated under policy exclusion clause 4.19. The forum upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.
Claim of Rs.36,244 for umbilical hernia and hypertension was repudiated because the surgery resulted from morbid obesity, which is permanently excluded under the policy. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Tympanoplasty surgery claim of Rs.30,786 was partially settled for Rs.15,787 with deductions made according to policy terms. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.49,920 for pneumonia treatment was repudiated as the insured received treatment at a hospital included in the insurer's declined list. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization expense of Rs.69,360 for acute appendicitis was partially settled for Rs.25,238 based on PPN rates and MOU. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.98,038 for hysterectomy surgery was repudiated because the treatment took place at a hospital on the declined list of public sector insurers. Complaint dismissed.

Claim of Rs.39,942 for vaginal hysterectomy was repudiated under the pre-existing disease/waiting period clause since portability procedures were not completed for the fresh policy. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Fever treatment expenses of Rs.16,746 were partially settled for Rs.12,346 based on PPN rates and MOU. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Dental treatment claim of Rs.26,706 following an accidental fall was repudiated because the procedure was performed on an outpatient basis without hospitalization. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.1,45,409 for carcinoma mucosa buccosa treatment was repudiated because treatment papers established a 10-year history of tobacco chewing. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Dengue fever hospitalization expenses of Rs.28,772 were partially settled for Rs.17,500 based on policy terms and PPN rates. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant was hospitalized for enteric fever and claimed Rs.16,150, which was partially settled for Rs.8,283 based on room category conditions. A modified bill submitted was deemed bogus, leading to dismissal of the complaint.

Claim for abdominal hysterectomy and appendectomy amounting to Rs.79,332 was partially settled for Rs.44,849, deducting Rs.34,483 as per PPN MOU rates and reasonable and customary expenses. Complaint was dismissed.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Mediclaim for enteric fever was repudiated as fabricated records were submitted for a fraudulent claim when the policy was not in force. Complaint dismissed.
Two claims for calculus treatment and microdisectomy were repudiated under policy condition 4.3 as they fell within the first two years of the policy where specified diseases are excluded.
Claim for EECP therapy sessions totaling Rs.90,302 was rejected because treatment was taken on an OPD basis without the mandatory 24-hour hospitalization required under the policy.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for inguinal hernia surgery was partially settled, deducting Rs.15,325 for non-medical items and pre/post expenses under senior citizen policy exclusions. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for epididymo-orchitis amounting to Rs.14,725 was repudiated because it was a second-year policy and the condition was excluded for the first two years.
Mediclaim was rejected because the insured failed to produce the hospital discharge summary. Insurer's decision was upheld.
Mediclaim was partially rejected and settled according to PPN MOU rates under the reasonable and necessary clause. Decision upheld.
Cataract claim was rejected during the second year of the policy as it falls under a 2-year exclusion clause. Decision upheld.
Mediclaim was partially rejected under the reasonable and necessary clause of the policy. Insurer's decision was upheld.
Hernia claim arising from obesity was repudiated as obesity-related claims are not payable under policy clause 4.9. Decision upheld.
Mediclaim was partially rejected because separate receipts for anesthetist fees and other charges fell outside the main hospitalization bill as per policy terms.
Mediclaim was rejected due to late intimation and late submission of claim files, violating policy clauses 5.3 and 5.4.
Mediclaim on increased sum insured was repudiated in accordance with the pre-existing disease clause of the policy. Decision upheld.
Post-hospitalization claim of Rs.7,979 was repudiated due to a 16-day delay in document submission. Furthermore, the complaint approached the forum beyond the permitted jurisdiction timeline.

insurer: The Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Mediclaim was repudiated after investigation revealed fraudulent hospitalization papers. Decision upheld.
Claim for neurological deficit and hypertension amounting to Rs.87,269 was settled for Rs.675 as the condition was pre-existing and occurred within the first two policy years. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for nutritional anemia was denied under general debility exclusion. Another claim for inguinal hernia was partially settled after room rent deductions since the insured opted for a room category higher than eligibility.

insurer: The HDFC Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for myocardial infarction/angina following a bike accident was repudiated as heart conditions were specifically excluded under policy section III. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for CAD and Unstable Angina was rejected under waiting period for pre-existing diseases. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Femur fracture claim for Rs. 43,412 was partially settled with proper deductions. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Parotid tumor surgery claim was rejected due to 2-year waiting period as previous insurance details were not submitted. Complaint dismissed.
Newborn congenital disease claim was rejected under maternity and newborn child cover exclusion. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Cataract surgery claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of prior eye surgery in the proposal form. Complaint dismissed.
Acute bronchitis claim during the first 30 days of the policy was rejected as continuity benefit was not given. Complaint dismissed.
Dialysis claim for Polycystic Kidney Disease was rejected as it is a genetic disorder falling outside policy scope. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Circumcision surgery claim was partially settled based on PPN rates and permanent exclusion of non-payable items. Complaint dismissed.
Craniotomy for glioma claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause during the fourth policy year. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Personal accident temporary total disability claim was reduced due to lack of accident proof like FIR or MLC. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for brain lesion excision was rejected under pre-existing disease clause within the first four years. Complaint dismissed.

insurer: The United India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for foot swelling admission was rejected as admission was solely for diagnostic purposes without active treatment. Complaint dismissed.
Health checkup reimbursement claim was wrongly rejected based on another family member's claim. Ombudsman ruled each insured is a separate entity and awarded reimbursement.
Abscess treatment claim was partially settled according to PPN rates. Complaint dismissed as settlement was proper.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Encephalitis claim was partially settled after giving prior policy benefits, but remaining amount was cut due to waiting period. Complaint dismissed.
Claim for paralysis and hypertension treatment was repudiated due to non-submission of previous medical history documents. Complaint dismissed.
Abdominal adhesion surgery claim was rejected under exclusion clause as it related to a past caesarean section. Complaint dismissed.
Shoulder fracture hospitalisation claim was partially settled with proper deductions under policy conditions. Complaint dismissed.
Post-hospitalisation claim for sinus treatment was partially repudiated due to missing supporting documents. Complaint dismissed.
Cataract surgery claim was partially settled as bills other than hospital bills were non-payable. Complaint dismissed.

Insured claimed Rs.46,762 for hernioplasty. Insurer partially settled for Rs.18,750 based on old sum insured and a two-year waiting period for the increased sum insured. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Complainant incurred Rs.88,011 for umbilical hernia treatment, partially settled for Rs.30,065. Insurer cited improper cash receipts and discrepancies in discharge certificate. Ombudsman upheld the partial settlement and dismissed the complaint.

Claims for stone removal and asthma totaling Rs.60,197 and Rs.91,695 were partially settled. Complainant sought full amount plus interest. No hospital papers were produced, and the insurer did not attend the hearing. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.11,068 for urinary cyst treatment was repudiated under clause 4.3 due to a two-year waiting period in the first-year policy. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.50,000 for eye laser surgery was repudiated because vision correction surgery is excluded under policy condition 4.6. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.
Claim of Rs.14,135 for fever and headache was partially settled for Rs.11,515 after deductions for reasonable and customary charges under clause 3.13. Ombudsman upheld the decision.
Claim of Rs.51,823 for fibromyoma of uterus was rejected under clause 4.3 as a two-year exclusion and due to late premium payment treating it as a fresh policy. Complaint dismissed.
Knee replacement claim of Rs.2,18,534 was partially settled after a deduction under customary and reasonable charges. Insurer applied tie-up hospital package rates. Complaint dismissed.
Dengue treatment claim of Rs.24,117 was partially settled for Rs.17,904 based on PPN network rates with the hospital. Complaint dismissed.
Gastroenteritis claim of Rs.16,573 was offered at Rs.15,773, but lack of required documents created doubt about claim genuineness. Complaint dismissed.

Hospitalization expenses of Rs.24,061 for vertigo and hypertension were rejected under permanent exclusion clause 4.4(11) as admission was solely for investigation without active treatment. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.9,910 for a child's prepusal skin and zip injury was rejected under permanent exclusion clause 4.8 as a congenital external condition. Complaint dismissed.
Post-hospitalization claim of Rs.7,286 was rejected because papers were submitted after 66 days, violating policy timelines. Complaint dismissed.
Fibroid uterus claim of Rs.50,008 was rejected for pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of 5-year abdominal pain history. Complaint dismissed.
Eye surgery claim of Rs.26,481 for a child was rejected under clauses 4.1 and 4.8 because the condition was a congenital squint. Complaint dismissed.
Hospitalization claim of Rs.20,000 for anemia was repudiated under permanent exclusion clause 11 of the policy. Complaint dismissed.
Claim of Rs.24,446 for benign prostatic hypertrophy was rejected because it occurred during the first policy year, falling under exclusion clause 4.3. Complaint dismissed.

Cataract surgery claim of Rs.54,973 was partially settled after deducting Rs.14,000 towards multifocal lens charges exceeding standard limits under reasonable and customary expense clause 3.12. Complaint dismissed.
Heart disease treatment claim of Rs.2,12,634 was settled for Rs.1,70,000 with deductions applied as per policy limits on stents and implants. Complaint dismissed.
Gastroenteritis claim of Rs.17,476 was rejected because treatment was taken at a debarred hospital and due to discrepancies in medical records regarding duration of illness. Complaint dismissed.

Insured underwent left knee ACL surgery incurring Rs. 69334, and insurer partially paid Rs. 60247, deducting Rs. 7500 for operation charges under reasonable and customary expenses. Ombudsman upheld the deduction based on comparative hospital package rates.

Insured was hospitalized for eye treatment of superior temporal branch vein occlusion with macular oedema. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.19. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured was hospitalized for fissurectomy and haemorroidectomy, but the treatment was administered by an Ayurvedic doctor while holding an MBBS distinction or similar context. Claim was rejected under policy exclusion clause 2.7.

Claim of Rs. 69,146 for accidental elbow injury was partly paid at Rs. 59,331. Deductions of Rs. 9,815 were made for excessive surgery charges and IITV charges under reasonable and customary clause. Ombudsman upheld the partial payment.
Insured was admitted for eye treatment involving intra ocular avastatine injection which can be done on an OPD basis. Claim was rejected because hospitalisation was not necessary as per policy terms.
Insured claimed Rs. 16007 for infective hepatitis treatment. Claim was rejected due to non-submission of claim intimation, preventing the TPA from verifying inpatient treatment genuineness.

insurer: The New India Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured claimed Rs. 69511 for right eye vitreous haemorrhage surgery. Insurer paid Rs. 41511 and deducted Rs. 28000 for procedural, equipment, nursing, and disposable items under permanent exclusions clause 4.4.4. Ombudsman upheld the deductions.
Female insured hospitalized for uterine prolapse treatment. Claim was rejected under exclusion clause 4.11 due to past instrumental delivery in 2007. Ombudsman found the repudiation valid.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for damage to a telescope during surgery under an Office Protection Shield Insurance policy for doctors was repudiated based on warranty conditions under section VII. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim of Rs. 1,82,000 for knee replacement was settled for Rs. 52,500 because sum insured enhancements over the years required calculation based on an older sum insured of Rs. 75,000 for major illnesses. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's calculation method.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs. 95,830 for lower uretric calculus was partly settled at Rs. 71,033. Deductions of Rs. 24,797 were made for surgery and OT charges under reasonable and customary basis by comparing with network hospitals. Ombudsman upheld the deductions.
Two claims for dengue and UTI were rejected due to age discrepancies and non-disclosure of material facts regarding ages stated in proposal forms versus treatment papers.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs. 33,941 for renal stones was partly settled at Rs. 23,049, deducting surgeon fees billed separately from the hospital bill exceeding policy limits. Ombudsman found the deduction genuine and reasonable.

Insured hospitalized for internal haemorrhoids and underwent ayurvedic treatment in a private hospital. Claim was rejected under clause 2.1 since ayurvedic treatment expenses are only admissible in government hospitals.

Claims for bilateral cataract surgery were partly settled by deducting Rs. 14,000 from each claim under customary and reasonable expenses due to extensive lens costs for better vision without glasses. Ombudsman upheld the deductions.

Claim for coronary angiography under a group floater policy was delayed due to non-submission of original discharge card, itemized bill breakup, and hospitalization intimation reason. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim of Rs. 45268 for vaginal hysterectomy was repudiated because it occurred during the second policy year, falling under the exclusion clause 4.3 prohibiting certain disease treatments during the first two policy years. Ombudsman upheld the decision.

Claim for coronary angiography was unsettled due to pending requirements including original discharge card, itemized bill breakup, and explanation for delayed intimation. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim of Rs. 45577 for dental treatment following an accident was repudiated because dental treatments generally require hospitalization and the receipts indicated OPD treatment. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Claim of Rs. 37264 for right uretha stone treatment was partly paid with a deduction of Rs. 4500 for endoscopy camera charges under exclusion clause 4.16 regarding durable medical equipment. Ombudsman upheld the deduction.
A mediclaim for laparoscopic surgery was rejected because the insured did not disclose a previous insurance policy and the disease fell within a two-year exclusion period.

insurer: The New India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insurer partially repudiated a cataract surgery claim because the insured paid premium in Zone III but took treatment in Zone I, applying a 20% deduction as per policy conditions.

insurer: The New India Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: The insurer partially rejected a claim for femur fracture treatment because treatment was taken from a relative, fees were exorbitant, and physiotherapy twice daily was unjustified.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for brain hemorrhage treatment was rejected because the patient had accelerated hypertension at admission, and the condition developed within the waiting period for specified diseases.
The insurer partially repudiated a knee replacement claim, capping payment at 70% of the sum assured as per policy norms for individual health insurance.
A claim for squamous cell carcinoma was rejected because the insured had a history of tobacco chewing, which falls under policy exclusions for diseases caused by intoxicating substances.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: A claim for a patient treated as an outpatient who died on the same day was rejected because hospitalization did not meet the mandatory minimum 24-hour requirement.

insurer: The United India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A householder policy claim for a damaged TV picture tube due to voltage fluctuation was repudiated due to non-disclosure and misrepresentation.
A claim for cataract surgery under a group mediclaim policy was rejected based on the two-year waiting period exclusion clause.
A knee replacement claim under a group policy was settled only up to the previous sum insured limit of 2 lakh because the increased sum insured was subject to a two-year waiting period.
A claim for umbilical hernia treatment was partially rejected because deductions were made based on preferred provider network (PPN) hospital rates.
Claims under mediclaim and personal accident policies for surgical treatment following a fall were wrongly rejected as pre-existing based on an older 2008 injury; the ombudsman ordered settlement.
Deductions made for room rent limit and missing x-ray report in a senior citizen mediclaim policy were found unjustified since the policy had no capping and the report was provided.
A claim deduction for a cancer test conducted outside the hospital was contested because hospital registration number sufficed for identification, and the foreign test report was accessed online.
The insurer incorrectly restricted a cataract surgery reimbursement to Rs. 10,000 under a senior citizen policy, ignoring the policy document stating a limit of Rs. 24,000.

The insurer restricted a claim to basic cataract package limits after complications required advanced retinal treatment in Delhi; the ombudsman ruled the complication required separate treatment and ordered full payment.
An overseas mediclaim claim for high altitude sickness during a Mount Everest expedition in Nepal was validly rejected under general exclusions for hazardous activities.
The insurer incorrectly settled a hospitalization claim based on an older sum insured of 3.5 lacs instead of 4.5 lacs, prompting an order for additional payment.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Gen. Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: The insurer inadequately settled a claim for cardiac treatment at a hospital, leading the ombudsman to order an additional payout.
Rejection of a menorrhagia treatment claim on grounds of a pre-existing disease was overturned because the condition did not exist before the policy inception.

Complainant was hospitalized for chest pain. Cashless facility and reimbursement claim were rejected citing policy exclusion clause 4.3. During hearing, the insurer admitted the claim was payable and promised settlement, but failed to pay. The Ombudsman ordered payment with penal interest.

The insured's son suffered severe injuries after falling from a height and was hospitalized for less than 24 hours. The TPA repudiated the claim on the grounds of hospitalization being under 24 hours. The Ombudsman held the claim payable and awarded the claimed amount.

insurer: ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant submitted all requisite documents, which were returned without settlement. During the hearing, original documents were handed over to the insurer's representative. The insurer stated the claim would be settled upon receiving originals, but failed to report back. The Ombudsman ordered payment.

Complainant regular policyholder had his claim rejected on flimsy grounds regarding alcohol or smoking habits, which the complainant denied. The insurer failed to submit the file. The Ombudsman ruled the repudiation unjustified and awarded the claim amount.

Hospitalization claim was denied due to a delay in submitting documents. During the hearing, the insurer acknowledged two pending claims, one of which had an unsent cheque, and promised to settle both. The Ombudsman ordered payment for both claims with penal interest.

Claim was rejected due to lack of policy continuity when the insured switched from Reliance to United India in 2009. The Ombudsman held that the insured was under a bonafide belief of continuity from 2007 and had no pre-existing disease, directing the insurer to pay the claim.

insurer: Star Health & Allied General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant underwent Hernia surgery. Claim was repudiated for non-disclosure of past medical history from 2006 under policy condition 7. The Ombudsman found condition 7 inapplicable as the claim was not fraudulent and Hernia was certified not to be a PED complication.

insurer: Star Health & Allied General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent pacemaker replacement surgery and claims were partially rejected on the grounds of pre-existing disease and co-pay conditions. The Ombudsman calculated the entitled amount per policy terms and awarded the remaining balance.

Post-hospitalization claim was repudiated due to late submission of documents caused by a family member's accident. The insurer admitted the claim was otherwise valid on merits. The Ombudsman awarded the claim amount with penal interest.

Insurer settled a claim for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm referencing a lower sum insured from 2007-2008 instead of the current higher sum insured of Rs. 3,25,000 for 2010-2011. The Ombudsman found no justification for reducing the sum insured and awarded the difference.

Insured underwent angioplasty and was paid 70% under an individual policy, but the insurer failed to consider the accompanying Super Top-up policy. The Ombudsman held that the insured was entitled to the benefits of both policies and ordered payment of the balance.

Insurer failed to make any decision on a reimbursement claim for depression treatment despite continuous renewals. The Ombudsman reviewed the discharge summary and found the claim payable, awarding a partial amount.

TPA approved a pre-authorization request for cataract surgery but excluded the assistant surgeon's fee of Rs. 7,138. The Ombudsman noted that policy terms do not exclude assistant surgeon fees and awarded compensation.

Insurer closed two hospitalization claims after demanding information that was allegedly not provided. The Ombudsman found the closure unjustified and directed the insurer to pay the admissible amounts.

Claim for knee joint pain surgery was rejected under clause 4.3 (4-year waiting period). The insured had continuous coverage since 1997, switching from another public sector insurer in 2009. The Ombudsman held that continuity benefits applied and awarded the full claim.

Claim for treatment following a fall was repudiated under clause 4.1 for pre-existing hypertension and diabetes. The Ombudsman noted the insurer brought no evidence that the insured suffered from the treated condition at policy inception, and awarded the claim.
Cataract surgery claims for both eyes were left undecided due to a 2-day gap in policy renewal and a 2-year waiting period. The Ombudsman found the 2-day gap negligible and ordered payment.

Claim for loss of valuables under an unicare policy was ignored by the insurer despite document submission. The bank had paid part of the loss, and the Ombudsman ordered the insurer to cover the remaining balance up to the sum insured.

Six claims relating to chronic kidney disease and kidney transplant were denied on grounds of pre-existing disease and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman held that the insurer produced no evidence of pre-existence at policy inception and awarded the full amount.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz Gen. Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Hospital cash allowance for fever was denied on the grounds that the illness was a complication of declared diabetes. The Ombudsman found the repudiation unjustified and awarded the hospital cash as per policy terms.

Insured underwent an eye operation and filed a claim for Rs. 6,878. The insurer repudiated the claim solely on the ground of late submission. The Ombudsman held that an otherwise payable claim cannot be declined for late filing and directed the insurer to pay the full amount.

Insured's wife was diagnosed with cancer and underwent surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy in Mumbai. The claim was repudiated due to late filing. The Ombudsman noted the insured was busy treating a deadly disease and set aside the repudiation, directing payment of the maximum sum incurred of Rs. 1 lac.

insurer: Star Health & Allied General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent surgery for a CBD stone in 2012. The insurer rejected the claim under pre-existing disease citing a previous surgery in 2009. The Ombudsman found both surgeries independent with no evidence of pre-existence and directed payment of the admissible amount.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was admitted for acute abdominal and breast pain, underwent investigations, and was treated conservatively. The insurer repudiated stating admission was for investigation only and could be managed on OPD basis. The Ombudsman set aside the repudiation as the patient received active treatment.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for an acute stomach problem. The insurer closed the file as 'No Claim' due to non-submission of first consultation history certified by the doctor. The Ombudsman held it was the insurer's duty to investigate previous particulars and directed claim settlement.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized and treated for lung carcinoma within the second year of the policy. The insurer repudiated the claim under a two-year exclusion clause for carcinoma. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured's father was hospitalized for COPD with acute exacerbation. Cashless was denied and claim repudiated on the ground that the patient was a smoker and the ailment was related to smoking under clause 4.8. The Ombudsman noted smoking was not in clause 4.8 and ordered full payment.

Complainant underwent surgery for removal of ovarian cyst within the first year of the policy. The insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.3(ii) which specifies a one-year waiting period for polycystic ovarian diseases. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint as the waiting period had not expired.

Complainant's mother was hospitalized for ischemic heart disease. The insurer repudiated under a two-year waiting period for hypertension. The attending doctor certified she was never hypertensive and blood pressure records were normal. The Ombudsman directed payment of the claim.

Complainant was hospitalized for CIDP treatment. The insurer repudiated stating treatment could be done on OPD basis under clause 4.10. The Ombudsman found active treatment and steroids were given, making hospitalization necessary, and directed payment.

Complainant's wife was hospitalized for a grade II ankle sprain. The insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could have been taken on OPD basis. The Ombudsman found the hospitalization justified and ordered payment of the claim.

Complainant underwent peritoneal dialysis procedures where a catheter reinsertion attempt was abandoned/unsuccessful. The insurer paid only 50% for the second admission. The Ombudsman found no policy condition supporting a 50% cut and ordered full reimbursement.

Hospitalization claim for balanoposthetis with secondary phimosis was not settled due to delay in submission and unanswered clarifications. The Ombudsman held that the insurer suffered no prejudice and ordered payment of hospital and pre-hospitalization expenses.

Insurer partially settled a treatment claim from an Ayurvedic hospital, doubting certain bills. The Ombudsman found no justification for the unpaid balance except for non-payable registration and service charges, and ordered payment of the remaining amount.

Complainant took treatment at a private NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospital. The insurer repudiated the claim based on policy terms requiring treatment in a government hospital or medical college. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Chola MS General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for family hospitalization was repudiated for delay and non-production of original discharge summaries. The Ombudsman found the delay was explained and routing through the bank was proper, ordering full reimbursement.

insurer: Apollo Munich Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's son suffered a knee injury with hemarthosis and was hospitalized. The insurer repudiated stating treatment could be done on OPD basis. The Ombudsman held that the treating doctor's advice for hospitalization was valid and ordered claim payment.

Hospitalization claim for necrotizing skin and soft tissue infection of the foot was repudiated because the insured had pre-existing Diabetes Mellitus. The Ombudsman noted the infection was independent of diabetes and ordered full claim payment.

Carcinoma treatment claim spanning policy renewal was only partially settled, with the insurer refusing to apply the renewed policy's higher sum insured. The Ombudsman held that continuous hospitalization entitles the insured to the renewed sum and ordered balance payment.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's wife underwent hernia surgery and abdominoplasty during the first policy year. The insurer rejected the claim under exclusion clause 3.5 for first-year hernia surgeries. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured's wife had undergone treatment for an ailment. Insurer repudiated the hospitalization claim citing pre-existing disease under exclusion clause 4.1 based on an earlier 2007 claim. Ombudsman found no evidence that the illness existed prior to the first policy inception, noting earlier judicial orders, and ordered payment of Rs. 68,316 with interest and cost.

Complainant's son was hospitalized for severe fever, cough, and respiratory infection. Insurer rejected the claim claiming no active line of treatment and conservative management. Ombudsman noted the treating doctor's advice and active treatment provided, ruling hospitalization was necessary, and awarded Rs. 2,266 with interest.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for Carpel Tunnel Syndrome. Insurer claimed the amount of Rs. 4,073 was settled and credited to a Bank of India account. Complainant stated he held no such account. Ombudsman noted the insurer failed to prove payment to the correct account and ordered payment of Rs. 4,073 with interest and cost.

Insured was hospitalized for intermittent fever and underwent various investigations without a final diagnosis or active treatment. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4.10. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision that investigations without diagnosis and active treatment do not warrant hospitalization reimbursement.

Insured was hospitalized for stomach discomfort and diagnosed with GERD, gastric erosions, and a history of hypertension for 8 years. Insurer rejected the reimbursement claim and terminated the policy for non-disclosure of material facts regarding pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the dismissal due to non-disclosure vitiating the contract.

Insured underwent surgery for bilateral internal carotid aneurysm. Insurer repudiated the claim stating it was a complication of pre-existing hypertension. Ombudsman observed treating doctor's opinion that the aneurysm was unrelated to hypertension, ruled hypertension was not pre-existing under policy definitions, and awarded Rs. 1,74,828 with cost and interest.

Insured underwent treatment for acid peptic disease. Insurer repudiated the claim on grounds of pre-existing Type II diabetes mellitus and non-disclosure of material facts at policy inception. Ombudsman found the present ailment was not pre-existing, but upheld the dismissal due to suppression of material health facts regarding diabetes at inception.

Insured's wife was hospitalized for breathlessness and diagnosed with COPD and severe pulmonary hypertension. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.10 for lack of hospitalization necessity. Ombudsman found investigations were followed by active treatment, set aside the repudiation, and awarded Rs. 3,490 with interest.

Insured's wife took inpatient treatment for lumbar disc prolapse and cervical spondylosis at a private ayurvedic center. Insurer rejected the claim based on a special policy condition restricting ayurvedic treatment to government hospitals. Ombudsman held that a new restrictive condition introduced upon renewal without notice is invalid, and awarded Rs. 28,060 with cost and interest.

Insured was treated for carcinoma of the tongue. Insurer rejected the claim under clauses 4.1 and 4.2 for pre-existing disease and disease contracted within 30 days. Ombudsman noted that the disease was first detected after the policy inception and clauses 4.1 and 4.2 were mutually exclusive, awarding Rs. 64,825 with interest.

Insured's husband underwent treatment for liver cirrhosis. Insurer rejected the claim under clause 4.8 assuming the condition was caused by alcohol consumption. Ombudsman found no positive evidence establishing a nexus between alcohol and the cirrhosis, and awarded Rs. 62,009 with cost and interest.

Insured's mother underwent cancer treatment including parenteral chemotherapy and oral tablets. Insurer partially settled the claim by reimbursing parenteral chemotherapy injections while denying oral tablets under hospitalization criteria. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's partial settlement as oral consumption does not meet parenteral exception rules.

Insured submitted a claim for son's meniscus injury treatment which was initially repudiated under clause 4.10. Insurer subsequently admitted inpatient treatment necessity and agreed to pay. Ombudsman awarded the full claim amount of Rs. 9,575 with interest.

Insured suffered major motor vehicle accident injuries and claimed reimbursement along with hospital cash benefit. Insurer partially disallowed deductions and hospital cash. Ombudsman found the insurer could only deduct a minor amount, and awarded an additional Rs. 31,479 including hospital cash and cost with interest.

Insured was hospitalized for submandibular abscess/submental space infection. Insurer repudiated the claim under clause 4.3 citing a 2-year waiting period for skin disorders. Ombudsman found medical evidence proved the infection was not a skin disorder, and awarded Rs. 10,824 with interest.

Insured underwent surgery and received partial settlement for his claim. Insurer offered an additional amount during proceedings due to split-up bill clarifications. Ombudsman reviewed denied items and determined total liability at Rs. 53,782, awarding the balance amount with interest.

Insured's daughter underwent laparoscopic surgery for a left paraovarian cyst. Insurer repudiated the claim under exclusion clause 4/5.4 as treatment for internal cysts is excluded during the first two policy years. Ombudsman upheld the dismissal as strictly based on policy conditions.

Insured underwent a hysterectomy under a group welfare policy. Insurer partially settled the claim based on a retrospective package rate reduction. Ombudsman ruled that benefits already provided cannot be reduced retrospectively without notice, and awarded the balance amount of Rs. 5,000 with interest.

Insured enhanced sum insured from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 1 lakh and later incurred high treatment costs for a severe heart condition (MVR) contracted in 2008. Insurer paid out based on pre-enhancement limits due to pre-existing disease restrictions on enhanced sums. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's settlement in accordance with policy conditions.

Insured's wife underwent Sequential Programmed Magnetic Field therapy for knee osteoarthritis. Insurer rejected the claim under clauses 4.13 and 2.3 for unproven/naturopathy therapy and lack of 24-hour hospitalization. Ombudsman upheld the dismissal as SPMF therapy lacked recognized status and mandatory hospitalization conditions were not met.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured was hospitalized for Diabetes Mellitus and Hypertension. The insurer repudiated the claim on the grounds of non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation due to evidence of prior duration of the ailment, dismissing the complaint.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured daughter was treated for Young Onset Parkinsonism. The insurer rejected the claim alleging non-cooperation and misrepresentation for failing to provide treatment records from certain medical facilities. The Ombudsman found that no such treatment records existed and ordered the insurer to pay the claim with interest and costs.

The insured was hospitalized for chest and back pain, diagnosed with vertigo and ischemic stroke. The insurer repudiated the claim claiming hospitalization was for investigations only and lacked active treatment. The Ombudsman noted active treatment and investigations were consistent, ordering full reimbursement.

The insured was hospitalized for stroke and incurred expenses which were partially settled by the insurer. The Ombudsman evaluated the policy clauses regarding room rent caps and proportionate deductions, and directed the insurer to pay a slightly revised eligible amount.

The insured underwent chemotherapy for ovarian carcinoma. The insurer repudiated the claim under the clause requiring 24 hours hospitalization. The Ombudsman held that chemotherapy is specifically excluded from the 24-hour hospitalization rule and ordered payment with interest and costs.

The insured underwent renal transplantation and nephrectomy for kidney disease. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing hypertension and kidney failure and missing proposal forms. The Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existing knowledge prior to 2004 and noted that even if pre-existing, it was covered after four years of continuous insurance.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insurer delayed settling the balance claim amount of Rs. 20,000 for over three months until after the complaint was filed. The Ombudsman ordered the insurer to pay interest for the delay period along with costs.

The insured took chemotherapy in tablet form as an outpatient after being treated for astrocytoma. The insurer repudiated the claim because there was no 24-hour hospitalization. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation, noting that oral chemotherapy via the alimentary canal does not qualify under the parenteral chemotherapy exception.

The insured's wife was admitted for knee osteoarthritis and treated with traction and physiotherapy. The insurer rejected the claim stating treatment could be done on an OPD basis. The Ombudsman found that traction and strict bed rest necessitated hospitalization, ordering full reimbursement.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured was hospitalized for low back pain caused by intervertebral disc prolapse. The insurer rejected the claim under clauses excluding mere investigations without active treatment. The Ombudsman ruled that inpatient care, observation, and medications constituted valid active treatment, awarding the claim.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured's pregnant wife was hospitalized for a lower respiratory tract infection. The insurer partially settled the claim, making deductions for room rent and assuming pregnancy treatment. The Ombudsman upheld room rent caps but found respiratory treatment distinct, awarding a partial additional sum with interest.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The senior citizen insured was treated for obscure gastrointestinal bleeding. The insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, and hemorrhoids. The Ombudsman found no evidence that the bleeding was related to those conditions and awarded the claim with a 20% non-network hospital deduction.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured's mother-in-law underwent an angiogram for atypical chest pain. The insurer repudiated the claim alleging pre-existing angina and non-disclosure. The Ombudsman found no evidence of prior cardiac diagnosis or treatment, and awarded the claim subject to co-payment.

The insured was hospitalized for severe neck pain caused by cervical spondylolisthesis and treated with analgesics and muscle relaxants. The insurer rejected the claim alleging only investigations were done. The Ombudsman ruled that observation and treatment constituted active treatment, awarding the claim.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured's son was treated for a sacral pressure sore. The insurer rejected the claim stating it was a complication of a congenital disease (spina bifida). The Ombudsman held that the insurer failed to prove the exclusion, and awarded hospitalization expenses and benefits.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured's daughter was treated for Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. The insurer repudiated the claim claiming treatment was for infertility under an exclusion clause. The Ombudsman noted the treating doctor certified no infertility treatment was given, and awarded daily hospital cash benefit.

The insured and his wife underwent ayurvedic treatment at a private hospital. The insurer rejected the claim based on an amended policy clause restricting ayurvedic reimbursement to government hospitals. The Ombudsman ruled that the restriction introduced after policy inception without notice was not binding, and awarded the claim.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd
facts: The insured underwent tonsillectomy for chronic tonsillitis. The insurer repudiated the claim as a pre-existing condition based on history of recurrent throat pain for three years. The Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as symptoms existed prior to policy inception within the waiting period.

The insured suffered from Herpes Zoster and took domiciliary treatment because other patients objected to his admission due to the contagious nature of the disease. The insurer rejected the claim. The Ombudsman ruled that domiciliary hospitalization conditions were met and ordered reimbursement.

The insured underwent total knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis and claimed pre and post-hospitalization expenses. The insurer partially rejected certain medical bills. The Ombudsman reviewed the bills and ordered payment for a specific missed doctor consultation fee supported by prescription.

Complainant contested partial repudiation of wife's heart surgery claim. Insurer applied pre-existing disease exclusion based on policy enhancement clauses, restricting settlement to pre-enhanced sum insured. Ombudsman upheld insurer's stand on pre-existing hypertension but granted cumulative bonus that was inadvertently ignored by TPA.

Claim was initially rejected due to delay in submitting claim documents following the death of insured's father during hospitalization for septicemia. During proceedings, the insurer's competent authority condoned the delay and the TPA settled the claim, subject to submission of bank details.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co Ltd
facts: Insured challenged partial settlement where deductions were made for doctor fees and nursing charges after availing a higher room category. Ombudsman found no variable rates for doctor fees existed based on room category, making proportionate doctor fee deduction unjustified, while nursing charge deduction was upheld as per policy terms.

Complainant challenged partial settlement of hospitalization claim for chest pain, pneumonia, and pleural effusion, which was restricted due to pre-existing diabetes. Ombudsman noted lack of medical evidence supporting renal failure or that present ailments were directly caused by pre-existing diabetes.

Group mediclaim beneficiary sought balance payment for surgical and hospitalization expenses following an accidental fracture of patella. Verification of disallowed items revealed certain expenses were wrongly deducted by the TPA. Insurer and complainant agreed on recalculated payable amount.

Complainant challenged disallowance of surgeon fees and consultation charges for cataract surgery because they were paid directly and not included in the main hospital bill. Ombudsman ruled that surgeon fees are an essential part of hospitalization and ordered full payment since genuineness of surgery was undisputed.

Insurer repudiated hospitalization claim for Wegners Granulomatosis and newly detected diabetes under pre-existing disease exclusion clauses. Ombudsman found acute infection required immediate hospitalization and ordered settlement of 40% of admissible amount for non-pre-existing ailments treated concurrently.

Insurer repudiated claim for adenoidectomy under waiting period clause meant for sinusitis. Ombudsman observed that adenoiditis and sinusitis are medically distinct, with adenoidectomy having a one-year waiting period which had been completed, making the claim admissible.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim was repudiated because final diagnosis included Obsessive Compulsive Disorder, a psychiatric ailment excluded under the policy. Ombudsman noted the patient was also treated concurrently for gastritis, and allowed 35% of the admissible amount towards gastric treatment expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant challenged proportionate deductions applied to doctor, OT, and investigation charges following a hysterectomy because a higher room category was chosen. Ombudsman held that proportionate deductions require variable room tariff structures, which must be verified with the hospital.

Claim for mother-in-law's conservative treatment of obstructive jaundice and chronic cholecystitis was closed by TPA due to alleged non-submission of documents. Ombudsman found original documents were duly submitted and directed the insurer to process and settle the claim.

Insurer made severe proportionate deductions and disallowed surgeon and anesthetist fees for an ophthalmic operation because bills were not part of the hospital invoice. Ombudsman ruled that direct surgeon and anesthetist payments supported by receipts are valid hospitalization expenses and must be reimbursed.

Claim for intravitreal injection administered for retinal detachment was rejected because the patient was discharged on the same day, categorizing it as an OPD treatment. Ombudsman granted an ex-gratia payment of Rs. 3,000 in the interest of justice.

Insurer restricted claim settlement to pre-enhanced sum insured under the argument that cerebellar haematoma was pre-existing. Ombudsman found no medical evidence supporting pre-existence and directed settlement based on the enhanced sum insured of Rs. 5 lakh.

Pre and post hospitalization claim for cataract surgery was partly disallowed for right eye OCT charges since surgery was for the left eye, and for a missing consultation prescription. Ombudsman upheld right eye OCT disallowance but allowed the consultation fee since prescription was available.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insurer applied proportionate deductions across hospital charges because insured stayed in a room exceeding entitled limits. Ombudsman noted specific tariff rates were available and insurer admitted additional amounts were payable under OT charges, medicines, and investigations.

Claim for neck stiffness and leg numbness treatment was repudiated because the patient was not hospitalized for the mandatory 24-hour period. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision as outpatient treatments do not qualify under policy coverage rules.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insurer withheld wife's accident hospitalization claim because original bills and cash memos were missing. Ombudsman noted it was unproven whether documents were misplaced by insured or insurer, gave benefit of doubt to the insured, and awarded the full claimed amount.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hospitalization following retrosternal pain was repudiated on grounds of excluded psychiatric disorder and lack of emergency warranting inpatient admission, as treatment involved only oral medications and investigations. Ombudsman found hospitalization was essentially for diagnostic evaluation.

Insurer denied fistula-in-ano surgery claim due to misrepresentation and anomalies concerning nursing home records and lack of anesthetist documentation. Ombudsman closed the complaint, noting that resolving disputed third-party evidence requires cross-examination outside the forum's summary powers.

Insured underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute calculous cholecystitis. Insurer rejected the claim under the pre-existing illness clause based on notings in medical papers mentioning similar episodes two years prior. Ombudsman noted experiencing generic symptoms does not equal a diagnosed past illness and directed the insurer to pay admissible expenses.

insurer: Apollo Munich Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for viral diarrhea and treated by a BAMS doctor. Insurer rejected the claim stating the treating doctor did not meet the policy definition of a medical practitioner registered with the Medical Council of India. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Insured sought reimbursement for the balance amount of hospital bills for cataract surgeries after cashless payment was made based on preferred provider network rates. The insured had opted for a higher category package and signed an undertaking. The text cuts off before a final conclusion.

Insured claimed short-settlement for inguinal hernia treatment expenses. Insurer provided a break-up of deductions including administrative charges, sundry medical supplies, and lab medicine. Insurer expressed willingness to settle the lab test charges amounting to Rs. 2,310 while other deductions were found in order.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for cataract surgery was repudiated because a previous renewal cheque bounced leading to policy cancellation and a fresh policy issuance with a break in continuity, placing the claim within the two-year waiting period for cataract surgery. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand.

Claim for hospitalization due to acute gastritis was repudiated on the grounds that evaluation and treatment could have been managed on an OPD basis without indoor admission. Complainant failed to attend the hearing or submit substantiating evidence, so the insurer's decision was upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for ESRD and related conditions was initially rejected due to alleged non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension since 1998. Following submission of service records and health reports, the insurer reconsidered and settled the claim for Rs. 49,191 after making proportionate and room rent deductions.

Claim for cataract surgery under a group mediclaim policy was closed as 'no claim' because the insured failed to provide documentary evidence proving they were an existing customer of the master policyholder. The text cuts off before final orders.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim for acute gastritis treatment was short-settled after insurer excluded charges for a PET scan done to investigate chronic breathlessness and weight loss, noting the test was unrelated to the acute admission and could be done on an OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the disallowance of the PET scan charges.

Claim for acute gastroenteritis was repudiated due to major discrepancies in indoor case papers, lack of vital charts, and suspicious medical entries. The complainant failed to provide contradictory documentary evidence, leading to the dismissal of the complaint.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for L4-L5 disc bulge was repudiated under clause 4.4.11 on the grounds that hospitalization was primarily for investigation and could be managed as an outpatient. Ombudsman noted the patient had severe radiating pain and inability to walk, and directed the insurer to settle admissible expenses.

Hospitalization claim for liver disease resulting in death was repudiated under the pre-existing disease exclusion since hospital papers mentioned a history of liver cirrhosis. The text cuts off during the procedural details.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for endometriotic ovarian cystectomy was repudiated under clause 4.4.6 as treatment related to infertility. Treating doctor clarified surgery was for pelvic pain from an endometriotic cyst, not fertility evaluation. Text ends mid-sentence.

Claim for lumbar disc prolapse was short-settled with MTP expenses disallowed under maternity and pregnancy exclusions. Ombudsman observed MTP was necessitated as a medical emergency due to doctor negligence in performing an MRI during early pregnancy, and directed ex-gratia payment along with outside test bills.

Claim for back pain treatment was repudiated due to lack of required hospitalization records proving treatment could be on OPD basis. Complaint dismissed. Another claim for cancer esophagus was dismissed due to non-disclosure of tobacco chewing habit under exclusion clause 4.8.

Claim for carcinoma of thyroid was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause since treatment was taken four months prior to policy inception. Another claim for vomiting and HTN was dismissed as OPD treatment. A third claim for Ureteric stone had partial deductions upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Piles treatment claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease and two-year waiting period in the second policy year without proof of continuity benefit. Another partial settlement dispute for knee joint treatment had deductions upheld as proper.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for sinusitis and hysterical behavior was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.4.6 because the complainant failed to produce first consultation papers and indoor case papers, making the claim suspicious for OPD treatment. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for fibroid uterus was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause since investigation reports showed the insured was advised hysterectomy 6 to 8 years prior to policy inception. Complaint dismissed.

Multiple complaints involving partial repudiations and rejections for cataract under waiting periods, sum insured limits, hospital parameter non-compliance, and room rent caps. All complaints were dismissed as insurer decisions were found proper.
A claim for fibroid and hysterectomy was partially settled by the insurer based on policy conditions and deductions were found to be proper.
Claim for piles treatment taken in an ayurvedic hospital was repudiated as ayurvedic treatments are not covered under the policy.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Hospitalization for ischemic brain disease and epilepsy was repudiated due to lack of additional premium for pre-existing disease despite a long-standing policy.
A claim for aortic aneurysm treatment was lodged within the first year of the policy, falling within the 3-year waiting period for pre-existing diseases.
Claim for a 2-year-old son's treatment of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome was rejected because it was lodged in the first policy year, violating the pre-existing disease waiting period.
Hospitalization expenses for right ear treatment in the second policy year were rejected under the 3-year waiting period clause for pre-existing diseases.
Claim for prolapsed disc was denied because treatment papers showed only injections and medicines were prescribed which could have been managed on an OPD basis.
Coronary artery disease treatment claim lodged after two years and seven months was rejected as it fell within the three-year waiting period for pre-existing conditions.
Claim was repudiated because investigation reports and staff members confirmed the patient was not present in the hospital during visits.
Claim for ischemic heart disease was repudiated because medical papers proved the insured had diabetes mellitus for 5-6 years prior, which was not disclosed in the proposal form.
Hospitalization claim for a son's treatment was rejected based on specialist opinion confirming treatment for a congenital disease falling under policy exclusions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Partial settlement was upheld as the treatment occurred in a different zone than the policy origin and an increased sum insured had a 4-year waiting cap.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Heart treatment claim for a senior citizen policy was rejected because medical reports proved treatment for a long-standing pre-existing ailment before inception.
Claim for liver disease was partially settled after lawful deductions under policy conditions, leading to dismissal of the complaint.
Coronary angioplasty treatment in the second year of the policy was rightly repudiated under the two-year waiting cap for specific diseases.

Claim was dismissed because the insured failed to submit original documents in time and did not inform the insurer within the stipulated period, despite having a personal accident policy paid elsewhere.
Fistula treatment claim was partially settled after applying policy deductions which were supported by sufficient evidence from the insurer.
Knee replacement claim was partially settled under hospitalization benefit clauses with proper explanation of deductions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant demanded interest for delayed mediclaim payment, but the forum dismissed the complaint as there is no policy provision to pay such interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Group insurance claim for hospitalization was partially settled by deducting reasonable and customary expenses properly justified by the insurer.
Complainant claimed Rs.5,975/- for mother's ureteric stone treatment within the first policy year, but the policy imposed a two-year waiting period for this treatment.
Complainant claimed Rs.55,725/- for wife's hospitalization due to high risk pregnancy and pancreatitis, which was rejected under policy clauses excluding pregnancy-related diseases.

Complainant sought Rs.22,323/- for hospitalization due to fever, vertigo, and gastritis. The claim was rejected as it was deemed an OPD treatment converted into IPD for investigation without active treatment.
A group mediclaim of Rs.39,000/- for cardiac treatment was repudiated, and the son represented the claim two years after repudiation, making the case time-barred.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant incurred Rs.23,856/- for diabetes complications, partially settled by the insurer. During the hearing, the insurer agreed to pay an additional Rs.1,400/- for an RBS report.
Complainant sought Rs.24,820/- for malaria and gastroenteritis treatment, but the claim was rejected as the forum found the claim suspicious.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's father underwent prostate surgery for Rs.52,947/-. The insurer deducted Rs.8,041/- because the patient had undisclosed long-standing hypertension and diabetes.
Complainant claimed Rs.1,55,853/- for unstable angina and single vessel disease in the second policy year, which was rejected due to a pre-existing history of diabetes and hypertension.

Complainant's mother underwent cataract surgery costing Rs.32,000/- in the second year of the policy, but the claim was rejected due to a two-year waiting period and lack of continuity proof from a previous insurer.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought Rs.1,07,438/- for wife's treatment and death. The claim was partially settled after deducting 25% because total previous payouts had exhausted 94.23% of the sum insured under policy limits.

Complainant's wife underwent a caesarean delivery costing Rs.39,138/- under a group policy. The claim was rejected because the insured had not completed 9 months of the policy period due to late premium payment.
Complainant sought Rs.46,361/- for ureteric stone treatment, but the claim was partially settled for Rs.18,000/- after applying PPN network and reasonable charge limits.
A group mediclaim file was closed and rejected due to non-compliance with required document submissions and a 12-month claims reporting limit.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant claimed Rs.44,927/- for cerebral infarct and hypertension treatment in the first policy year, but the claim was rejected for non-disclosure of previous medical history.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought Rs.46,064/- for a staff member treated in the complainant's own hospital, which was partially settled for Rs.33,074/- based on customary and reasonable charge limits.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant incurred Rs.2,16,577/- for myocardial infarction. The claim was partially settled for Rs.69,000/- because the insured had pre-existing hypertension without paying additional premium after a sum insured increase.

insurer: Max Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought Rs.1,02,000/- for post-hospitalization dental treatment following an accident. The claim was rejected because post-hospitalization papers were submitted after the 60-day time limit.
Complainant sought Rs.10,734/- for cardiac and anxiety treatment, but the claim was rejected due to suppression of material facts regarding age leading to an incorrect policy issue.
Complainant claimed Rs.26,346/- for chest pain treatment, which was rejected because treatment papers indicated a known history of hypertension subject to a two-year waiting period.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought Rs.1,86,197/- for central retina vein occlusion treatment, but the claim was rejected due to inordinate delay in submitting claim intimation and documents.
Complainant claimed Rs.22,000/- for URI treatment, but discrepancies in admission time and disease name led the insurer to repudiate and the forum to dismiss the fraud claim.

Claim of Rs.45,585/- for carcinoma was partially settled, but 9 prior claims totaling Rs.3 Lakhs had already been paid for the same treatment. The complainant was not the policyholder, and the complaint was dismissed.
Claim for Rs.25,424/- for head injury under a group policy was repudiated due to late submission of papers by 48 days, and the complaint was time-barred.
Claim of Rs.19,091/- for fever and vomiting was rejected due to late intimation and suspicious lab report dates without consultation papers.
Claim of Rs.50,516/- for hemiplegia was rejected because hospital papers showed a 15-year history of HTN/DM that was not disclosed in the proposal.

Multiple cases reviewed. First case for Rs.5,563/- for epilepsy was rejected as excluded. Second case claimed Rs.81,835/- and was partially paid. Third case claimed Rs.81,407/- and was partially paid after valid deductions.
Claim of Rs.66,153/- for giddiness and walking imbalance was repudiated because no active line of treatment was given during hospitalization.
Group mediclaim for Rs.20,804/- for heart attack treatment was rejected on pre-existing disease grounds, and the petition filed in 2013 for 2011 expenses exceeded the time limit.
Claim of Rs.74,236/- for laparoscopic cholecystectomy was rejected and policy cancelled because previous health history was not disclosed.
Claim of Rs.20,823/- for diabetic neuropathy was rejected due to non-submission of required documents despite TPA correspondence.
Claim of Rs.5,704/- for hydrocele and undescended testicle surgery in a toddler was rejected on the ground of congenital disease.
Claim for pneumonia with respiratory distress was rejected because investigation proved treatment was on an OPD basis.
Claim of Rs.2,02,222/- for femur fracture was partially settled for Rs.88,535/- after deductions, and the complaint was dismissed as documents looked fabricated.
Claim of Rs.83,000/- for vehicular accident hospitalization was rejected due to late intimation and treatment reports showing OPD care.
Claim of Rs.25,685/- for inguinal hernia surgery in an infant was rejected based on expert opinion that the condition was congenital and non-payable.
Claim of Rs.64,295/- for cataract surgery was partially settled for Rs.29,720/- per policy terms, and the complaint was dismissed.
Complainant incurred Rs.3,74,975/- for treatment. Rs.1,93,750/- was paid under individual policy, and the rest was rejected under super top-up policy due to pre-existing disease.
Claim of Rs.2,34,502/- for brain hemorrhage was repudiated under exclusion clause as the policy incepted only two months prior and medical records indicated a chronic prior ailment.
Claim of Rs.45,893/- for prostate abscess and UTI in the first year of the policy was repudiated due to non-disclosure of prior history of prostate issues and DM.
Claim of Rs.16,201/- for chest pain was partially settled for Rs.10,151/- after proper deductions, and the insurer's decision was upheld.

Complainant was covered under a group policy until 2011, then switched to an individual policy. A subsequent hospitalization claim was rejected based on the policy exclusion clause, and the complaint was dismissed.

A claim for a child's tonsil and nasal treatment was repudiated due to non-availability of required documents despite reminders. The complainant's excuses regarding rural residence and doctor availability were rejected by the forum.

A claim for vaginal hysterectomy was rejected under policy clause 4.3. The policy was issued to bank account holders, and continuity benefits from a previous insurer were not applicable as the claim arose in the first year of the current policy.
A claim for tongue cancer treatment was repudiated under policy condition No.4.8. Upon scrutiny of documents, the forum upheld the insurer's decision and dismissed the complaint.

insurer: Universal Sampo Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims were rejected because hospital stay was less than 24 hours, or the hospitalization was solely for investigation purposes with no active line of treatment, or due to congenital conditions not covered under group policies.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims were dismissed either due to being fraudulent according to investigation reports, or because deductions for hernia and cataract lenses under specific policy clauses were found to be right and proper.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims for accidental injuries and post-hospitalization expenses were partially paid by the insurer. The forum found the deductions under the policy terms and conditions to be detailed and proper, hence dismissing the complaint.

Cataract and seizure treatment claims were partially settled by insurers after deducting amounts for treatments deemed inadmissible, such as OPD-based cancer treatments. The forum upheld the deductions and dismissed the complaints.
A claim was partially settled in 2011, and the complainant filed a case in 2013. The forum dismissed the complaint as being time-barred under the Redressal of Public Grievances Rules 1998.
A claim for laser eye surgery for a child was repudiated because correction of eyesight surgery is not payable under clause 4.3(c) and was considered a pre-existing congenital internal condition.
A cataract surgery claim was partially paid, with deductions made on the grounds that treatment for cosmetic purposes is not payable under the policy terms.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A claim for mitral valve replacement was settled via cashless payment and partial reimbursement, with minor deductions made correctly according to policy clauses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
