facts: Claims were repudiated or partially settled because hospitalization was under 24 hours for angiography, or because deductions for hernia treatment were correctly applied according to policy clauses.

insurer: Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A daily hospitalization benefit claim for stomachache and weakness was rejected as the insurer determined hospitalization was not medically necessary based on treatment records and medical opinions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claims were rejected either due to the 4-year waiting period for osteoarthritis treatment not being completed, or due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension linked to a transient ischemic attack.
A claim for treatment was partially settled with deductions made for expenses not deemed reasonable and necessary. The forum upheld the insurer's decision.
A claim for fibroid removal surgery was partially settled after deducting amounts exceeding reasonable and customary expenses. The forum denied the remaining amount.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: A hospitalization claim for a patient with diabetes, hypertension, and renal failure who passed away was repudiated because the illness was pre-existing and occurred within the first year of the policy.
A claim for liver cirrhosis treatment was repudiated under the 2-year waiting period clause. Continuity benefits were denied because a fresh proposal form was obtained when switching insurers.
A chemotherapy claim for chest cancer was repudiated due to non-submission of required documents and because the claim form was unsigned by the policyholder.

Insured treated for Neuroendocrine Cancer. Claim of Rs.59,000/- was submitted under a family floater policy incepted in 2009. Repudiated as there is a 4-year waiting period cap for this treatment and it was only the third year of the policy.
Daughter underwent dental treatment due to accidental injury. Claim for Rs.4,000/- was repudiated due to late submission after 60 days and lack of required consultation papers or proof of accident.
Son underwent surgery for Left Congenital Hernia with expenses of Rs.7,962/-, which was repudiated under policy exclusion clause No.4. Insurer failed to attend the hearing or provide original papers.

Insured underwent cataract surgery incurring Rs.41,392/-, settled for Rs.23,792/- with Rs.17,600/- deducted under reasonable and customary clause. Forum upheld the insurer decision and dismissed the complaint.

Insured treated for Fistula incurring Rs.16,198/-, which was repudiated under exclusion clause 4.3 as policy coverage with current insurer started recently in 2010 after switching from another insurer.

insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured hospitalized for bypass surgery costing Rs.1,82,595/- and claim was rejected under pre-existing disease exclusion due to history of smoking and non-disclosure in the proposal form.

Insured hospitalized for Inguinal Hernia incurring Rs.69,941/-, partially settled for Rs.44,206/- based on old sum insured of Rs.1,75,000/-. Sum insured increased in 2013 and treatment taken in same year is subject to a two-year exclusion period.
Wife hospitalized for Urinary Tract Infection with expenses of Rs.41,800/- under a group mediclaim policy, repudiated due to a 32-day delay in submitting claim documents.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Seven-year-old son hospitalized for Dengue with expenses of Rs.18,655/- partially settled for Rs.10,455/-, with Rs.8,200/- deducted for doctor visit charges, admission charges, and room rent as per policy terms.
Father treated for Acute Infarct and other conditions with expenses of Rs.53,287/-. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause No.4.1, and the forum upheld the decision.
Hospitalization claim of Rs.29,063/- for son's finger injury from glass was repudiated on the grounds of late intimation and failure to follow advance intimation conditions.
Insured treated for severe anemia and abdominal pain incurring Rs.50,377/-, settled for Rs.21,459/-. Claim form was unsigned and anemia treatment falls under policy exclusions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured treated for spontaneous osteonecrosis of knee incurring Rs.57,742/-. Repudiated because panel doctor opined that hospitalization was not necessary for the subject treatment.
Insured treated for IHD and Myocardial Infarction. Claim rejected under policy condition 4.1 for pre-existing diabetes mellitus diagnosed 6 years prior, within the 3rd year of the policy.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured treated for Myocardial Infarction with expenses of Rs.11,124/-, rejected under policy condition 4.1 due to pre-existing diabetes of 10 years within the 2nd year of the policy.

Insured treated for Fistula in ano at a private Ayurvedic hospital incurring Rs.27,704/-. Claim was rejected because Ayurvedic hospitalization expenses are only admissible if treated in a Government Ayurvedic hospital.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Senior citizen hospitalized for coronary artery disease with claim of Rs.1,42,952/- settled partially for Rs.71,476/- under pre-existing disease exclusion clause restricting payment to 50%.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complaint filed regarding denial of cumulative bonus and improper premium loading. Insurer argued policies were renewed in one go. Ombudsman directed the insurer to allow cumulative bonus for claim-free years.

insurer: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd.
facts: Claim of Rs.92,865/- for OSA treatment was settled for Rs.31,750/- after excluding the cost of a CPAP machine. Ombudsman held that outright denial without explicit policy conditions was unjust and ordered partial payment.

Insured's son treated for Leukemia. Insurer denied normal coverage under the renewed policy after paying a critical illness claim. Ombudsman held denial unjustified and directed settlement restricting liability to Rs.1,00,000/-.

Hospitalization claim was denied after an investigation revealed cuttings and over-writings in the hospital attendance register, indicating a fake claim, and the insured could not provide a satisfactory explanation.

Hospitalization claim for treatment of Hydatidiform Mole resulting from abnormal conception was rejected because the policy permanently excludes treatments arising from or related to pregnancy and childbirth.

Claim for kidney transplant was partially settled and the donor spouse's claim was denied because the insured had chronic kidney disease since 2001, and enhanced sum insured benefits for pre-existing ailments only apply after 48 continuous months.
Claim for accident injuries was rejected because the insured persons were hospitalized for less than 24 hours, failing the mandatory 24-hour inpatient stay requirement under the policy.

Critical illness claim for brain stroke was repudiated and the policy terminated because the insured failed to disclose a pre-existing condition of loss of consciousness dating back to 2010 in the proposal form.

Claim for brain hemorrhage was rejected under the pre-existing condition exclusion clause because there was a 38-day break in policy renewal, treating it as a fresh policy, and the insured had a history of hypertension and diabetes.

Insurer restricted a cataract surgery claim by disallowing pre and post hospitalization expenses on the grounds of no 24-hour stay. The Ombudsman held that 24 hours is not required for eye surgery and pre/post expenses are payable.

Chemotherapy claim for cancer treatment was withheld because the insured did not produce a certificate showing the duration of the ailment. The Ombudsman ruled that the 48-month pre-existing waiting period had already passed, making duration irrelevant.

Claim for low back pain and spinal canal stenosis was repudiated on the grounds of pre-existing CVA. The Ombudsman held that the ailment was not related to CVA, and even if it were, the 18-month waiting period had long expired.

Insurer partially settled a claim for lumbar disc prolapse based on specific limits. The Ombudsman found that traction charges, procedure charges, and X-ray expenses were improperly deducted and ordered full payment.

Claim for heart disease occurring in the second policy year was repudiated based on a two-year waiting period clause. The Ombudsman rejected the insured's argument of policy continuity from a prior insurer and dismissed the complaint.

Claims for rabies vaccination and immunoglobulin following a dog bite were repudiated for lack of 24-hour hospitalization, while the son's identical claim was paid. The Ombudsman ruled this discriminatory and ordered payment.

Insurer restricted settlement for knee surgery to an arthroscopy package rate. The Ombudsman noted that major surgical procedures like ACL reconstruction and meniscectomy were also performed alongside diagnostic arthroscopy, making package restriction improper.

Claim for hospitalization was repudiated and the policy cancelled due to non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension, prior hysterectomy, and back pain in the proposal form. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.
Continuation of previous rulings regarding policy cancellation and non-disclosure where the cancellation of the renewed policy was set aside for one of the insured persons.
Critical illness claim for surgical removal of a kidney due to a tumor within 90 days of policy inception was repudiated based on the initial 90-day waiting period clause.

Claim for Ayurvedic inpatient treatments for neck and joint pain was repudiated on the grounds that it could be done on OPD basis. The Ombudsman held that the required complete bed rest prescribed by the doctor justified hospitalization.

Claims for husband's COPD treatment and son's septoplasty were repudiated under pre-existing and first-year exclusion clauses. The Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existing COPD or sinusitis linked to septoplasty, ruling in favor of the complainant.

Claims for acute on chronic pancreatitis and coronary artery disease were repudiated alleging alcohol-induced illness and that a second admission was only for investigations. The Ombudsman found no medical evidence supporting alcohol abuse and confirmed active treatment.

Claim for intracerebral hemorrhage resulting from a fall was repudiated due to a pre-existing hypertension history and policy breaks. The Ombudsman ruled that the claim arose in the third year of coverage and the hemorrhage was caused by an accidental fall, not excluded.

Insured underwent mastectomy and chemotherapy for breast carcinoma. Insurer repudiated the claim alleging pre-existing disease and non-disclosure of an earlier benign lump. Ombudsman observed that previous biopsy showed no malignancy and carcinoma was diagnosed after policy inception, hence ordered full payment with interest.

Complainant underwent pacemaker change in 2012. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing heart ailment from 2002. Ombudsman noted prior treatment was beyond 48 months before first policy inception, hence not a pre-existing disease under policy terms. Claim allowed with interest and cost.

Insured suffered facial and dental injuries from a fall, requiring inpatient treatment followed by outpatient dental care. Insurer partially settled but denied post-hospitalisation dental expenses under OPD exclusion. Ombudsman held that post-hospitalisation OP treatment following valid inpatient admission is covered, directing payment.

Complainant sought reimbursement for Ayurvedic treatment. Insurer rejected the claim citing a newly introduced exclusion clause for naturopathy/alternative therapies. Ombudsman noted lack of proper notice to the insured regarding policy changes and that Ayurvedic treatment was not explicitly excluded, ordering full payment.

Wife of complainant was hospitalized for Intra Vertebral Disc Prolapse with sciatica. Insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalisation was only for diagnosis and could be managed on OPD basis. Ombudsman held that treatment depends on medical advice and gravity, ruling the hospitalisation valid and awarding the claim.

Complainant's wife underwent appendicectomy and hysterectomy in 2008. Claim remained unsettled for five years, with insurer citing waiting period for hysterectomy. Ombudsman found hospitalisation occurred after the waiting period elapsed, directing payment with interest and cost.

Complainant underwent angioplasty after cashless facility was denied by TPA, though subsequent reimbursement claim was fully settled. Complainant sought compensation for mental agony due to cashless denial. Ombudsman held that cashless is an added service and not an absolute right, dismissing the compensation claim.

Insured hospitalized for carbuncle with pre-existing diabetes. Insurer repudiated claim under pre-existing disease exclusion. Ombudsman noted that three consecutive claim-free policy years had passed, making the exclusion inapplicable, and ordered payment with cost.

Complainant's mother-in-law admitted to an Ayurvedic hospital for back pain. Insurer rejected claim alleging excluded panchakarma and heat therapy. Ombudsman found medical records showed different specific treatments not listed under exclusions, ordering reimbursement.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant suffered disc prolapse from an accidental fall at work. Insurer rejected claim under waiting period exclusion for disc prolapse. Ombudsman verified accident reports and noted exceptions to waiting periods for accidental injuries, awarding the claim.

insurer: Max Bupa Health Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought cancellation and full premium refund of health policy after claims were rejected due to pre-existing disease waiting periods. Ombudsman observed request was made beyond free-look and 180-day cancellation terms offering zero refund, dismissing the complaint.

insurer: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent coronary artery bypass graft surgery. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing heart condition from 1993. Ombudsman noted that the condition was contracted long before the standard pre-existing definition window and policy inception, ordering payment with interest.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Senior citizen underwent bypass surgery in 1990 and suffered cardiac events in 2011, making claims under a 2010 policy. Insurer rejected claims for non-disclosure of past bypass surgery in proposal form. Ombudsman upheld repudiation citing concealment of material facts.

Complainant's mother hospitalized for cardiac syndrome and diabetes. Insurer repudiated claim under pre-existing disease clause due to policy break. Ombudsman noted continuous coverage for over three claim-free years made the exclusion inapplicable, awarding full sum insured with interest.

Insured underwent polypectomy under general anesthesia. Insurer initially rejected claim for lack of 24-hour hospitalization, later citing two-year exclusion for genito-urinary procedures. Ombudsman upheld dismissal based on the applicable genito-urinary waiting period exclusion.

Complainant hospitalized for acute cervical disc prolapse. Insurer repudiated claim for delayed submission and lack of active treatment. Ombudsman ruled that technical delay should not override genuine claims and medical necessity justified hospitalisation, awarding reimbursement.

Complainant's wife underwent cataract surgery. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing cataract and a break in continuity from previous group policy exceeding allowed limits. Ombudsman upheld the rejection as a new policy with pre-existing exclusions applied.

Insured treated for metastatic adenocarcinoma until death. Insurer repudiated claims as pre-existing under a 2007 individual policy. Ombudsman found continuous coverage existed from 2005 and diagnosis occurred after policy inception, ruling pre-existing clause inapplicable and awarding claims.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant hospitalized for cardioembolic stroke and atrial fibrillation. Insurer repudiated claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension. Independent medical opinion confirmed hypertension as a key risk factor, leading the Ombudsman to uphold the insurer's decision.

Complainant underwent chelation therapy for ischaemic heart disease. Insurer rejected claim stating chelation therapy is non-payable under naturopathy exclusion. Ombudsman noted policy text only excluded naturopathy while medical opinion classified it as allopathic/alternative, prompting further re-examination.

Complainant underwent PTCA and sought reimbursement for balance hospitalization expenses. Insurer restricted the claim to the sum insured from the year prior to pre-existing symptoms, invoking the pre-existing disease exclusion. The Ombudsman examined records and noted ambiguity in the duration of the pre-existing history.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant underwent CABG and filed a claim. Insurer settled only 50 percent of the sum insured citing pre-existing diabetes and policy conditions for the third year of coverage. The Ombudsman reviewed the case regarding complications arising from pre-existing conditions.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife was hospitalized for viral fever with gastritis. Insurer repudiated the claim stating hospitalization was unnecessary and an attempt to convert domiciliary treatment into an inpatient claim. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision due to lack of justification for hospital admission.

Complainant was hospitalized for an ACL tear and faced deductions from his claim. Insurer disallowed surgeon fees based on PPN rate lists and various non-medical expenses. The Ombudsman found surgeon fee deductions and certain material charges unjustified and ordered partial payment.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalized for a cerebrovascular accident and a femoral fracture after a fall. Insurer restricted the claim to the basic sum insured, citing pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. The Ombudsman upheld the restriction as conditions were pre-existing to the enhanced sum insured.

Complainant underwent corneal reshaping surgery for eye sight correction and lodged a claim. Insurer repudiated it under the policy exclusion for correction of eyesight. The Ombudsman found the rejection valid as refractive error corrections are excluded.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for mother's hospitalization for ischemic heart disease and hypertension was rejected due to pre-existing conditions and a break in policy continuity caused by delayed premium transmission through a cooperative credit society.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Limited
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for malaria and later underwent a medical termination of pregnancy. Insurer paid the malaria claim but rejected expenses for the second hospitalization under pregnancy exclusions. The Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant underwent CABG surgery and filed a claim, which was repudiated for non-disclosure of pre-existing hypertension and diabetes in the proposal form. Medical records supported the prior history, leading to the rejection.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant's son underwent radiofrequency ablation for an osteoid osteoma. Insurer repudiated the claim, erroneously treating it as an excluded quantum magnetic resonance procedure without expert backing. The Ombudsman granted the benefit of doubt to the complainant.

Complainant underwent endovenous laser therapy for varicose veins. Insurer rejected the claim citing eye and ear laser surgery exclusions and arguing it was an OPD procedure. The Ombudsman ruled that the procedure required inpatient care and was wrongfully denied.

Complainant was hospitalized for brain aneurysm and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing heart ailments and hypertension after migrating policies. The insurer failed to trace the proposal form and ignored prior continuous coverage.

Claim for breast cancer treatment was rejected because the breast lump symptoms manifested within thirty days of policy inception and pre-existing diabetes and hypertension were not disclosed. Hospital records confirmed prior medical history.

insurer: Bharati Axa General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Complainant was hospitalized for enterocolitis, urinary tract infection, and suspected malaria. Insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing diabetes and hypertension. Hospital admission notes and regular prescription data confirmed the pre-existing conditions.

Complainant's son was hospitalized following a road accident for soft tissue injuries. Insurer repudiated the claim claiming hospitalization was unnecessary. The Ombudsman noted the accident circumstances and ordered settlement on an ex-gratia basis.

Complainant contested the reduction of his daughter's sum insured from a higher amount back to the primary insured's level. Insurer cited a 2006 internal circular requiring identical sum insured for primary and dependent members, though it was implemented late.

Claim for bacterial meningitis hospitalization was rejected due to severe discrepancies, lack of ICU facilities at the hospital, and uncooperative hospital authorities refusing verification. The Ombudsman dismissed the complaint due to lack of cooperation and evidence.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
facts: Complainant sought reimbursement for a CT coronary angiography undergone on an outpatient basis. Insurer denied the claim as the policy covers only hospitalization expenses. The Ombudsman upheld the denial since the test is a non-invasive outpatient diagnostic procedure.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for urinary tract infection and myositis hospitalization was rejected due to anomalies in medical management, inflated bills, and lack of necessity for prolonged inpatient stay. The Ombudsman directed the complainant to submit hospital clarifications for re-evaluation.

Claim for road accident injuries and prolonged hospitalization was repudiated for alleged manipulation of medical records and inflated stay. Investigation photos showed minimal scarring inconsistent with deep wounds, prompting further document review.

Insured claimed for transcatheter ASD closure. Insurer deducted surgeon and anesthetist fees paid directly outside the main hospital bill. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's stand as per policy terms since no consolidated bill was provided.

insurer: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for severe bodyache hospitalization was rejected because inpatient admission was not medically necessary and treatment could have been managed on an OPD basis. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Travel policy claim for syncopal episodes during a US visit was repudiated due to non-disclosure of pre-existing diseases. The text is incomplete.
Complainant alleged short-settlement for diverticulitis hospitalization. Discrepancies found in bills; TPA directed to re-process and pay admissible balance expenses.

insurer: The New India Assurance Company Ltd
facts: Claim for CABG rejected due to pre-existing diabetes without premium loading after a short break in policy renewal. Ombudsman ruled that since the insurer knew of the condition, they could not penalize the insured, and ordered full settlement with interest.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd
facts: Senior citizen sought continuation under older policy terms instead of migrating to the revised 2007/2012 policy. Complaint became infructuous as renewal under new terms had already occurred without timely objection.

insurer: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Travel insurance claim for respiratory distress in Australia was rejected due to pre-existing conditions and non-disclosure. Text is incomplete.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for neuroma excision surgery rejected as it could be done on OPD basis. Ombudsman noted no fault in insurer's stand but awarded 50% on ex-gratia to avoid injustice.

insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for bilateral fallopian tubal blockage (infertility treatment) rejected as infertility is excluded under the group policy. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

Short-settlement claim for transcatheter ASD closure where surgeon and anesthetist fees paid directly outside hospital bills were disallowed. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision as no consolidated bill was provided.

insurer: Star Health & Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for leptospirosis with enteric fever under a specific Diabetes Safe policy (which only covers certain diabetic complications) was rejected. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for CABG in the first year of policy was rejected because it stemmed from pre-existing hypertension subject to a 4-year waiting period exclusion. Ombudsman upheld the rejection.

insurer: Bharti Axa General Insurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for External Counter Pulsation (EECP) therapy for ischemic heart disease was largely disallowed as unproven/experimental treatment. Text is incomplete.

Short-settlement for R.F. Ablation due to disallowing surgeon fees paid separately. Ombudsman noted policy did not explicitly require fees to be in the main bill, but hospital refused a consolidated bill, leaving no grounds to overturn.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for hemiplegia was restricted to pre-enhanced sum insured due to a 2-year waiting period for hypertension. Ombudsman upheld the restriction but ordered interest for delayed part-payment.
Short-settlement of claim for diverticular disease where insurer paid 50% proportionally across dual policies and deducted surcharges and non-medical items. Text is incomplete.
